reading: The poet calls the body a house walled with flesh and blood and framed with bones, and himself caught in the prison of the craving that says 'a little for me, a little for you', fallen into birth, bewildered in sleep and dream and suffering the states of the soul; he asks whether he will rather wander singing the power and fame of Murugan's lotus feet. The praise names Siva of the red crescent and matted hair, who loves the green creeper at his side, the brother of the big-bellied wishing tree Ganesa, the lord of the cock banner, the vel that gives raw flesh to the drum-beating ghosts, at Kachi.
nuance: உறக்கச் சொப்பனத்து உற்றுத் திகைக்கப்பட்டு அவத்தைப்பட்டு: the states of sleep and dream are named as part of the soul's suffering. The last line (படுக்கைக் கச்சபத்து இச்சைப்படு கச்சி) may name the tortoise (கச்சபம) of the Kachchapesvara shrine, linked with Vishnu, but the division is uncertain.

reading: The poet confesses that he took the body as his own, delighted in women with fish-eyes and painted breasts, fell into their arts, cried out and grew weary in the waves of their false words; before, when he dies, they carry him to the drums, lay him on the logs, set the fire and the kin give him up and go, he asks whether he will join in devotion, hold the kadamba-adorned feet and wander singing their fame in Tamil. The praise tells of Surapadman driven into the sea and struck down, the mango pierced, and Valli of the millet field embraced, at Kachi.
nuance: கடத்தைப் பற்று எனப் பற்றி: the first error is clinging to the pot of the body as one's own. The funeral is told quickly (எடுத்துக் கொட்டிடக் கட்டைப்படத் ... அனல் ... கொளுத்தி), and the kin let go (பற்றற்றவர் போமுன்) before the poet does.

reading: The poet traces a life from the womb, growing, falling to earth and taking form, caught by things seen, until Yama counts its days, quarrels, rushes in, rages, throws the noose and seizes the breath, and the kin burn the false corpse and go home; he asks that birth and its clinging end and he be given the kadamba-adorned feet. The praise names Murugan dear to Valli of the millet field, the one who taught the Madman who burned the cities and gave his foes his golden feet, the hero who fought the mango and the boar-like demons, at Kachi where pure Tamil of the three kinds is spoken.
nuance: Yama's coming is given as a string of verbs (கணக்கிட்டு, பிணக்கிட்டு, கதித்திட்டு, கொதித்திட்டு, கயிற்றிட்டு, பிடித்திட்டு), counting, quarrelling, rushing, raging, noosing, seizing. பித்தனைக் கற்பித்தருள்வோனே names the teaching of Siva (the பித்தன்) without naming Om. த்ரயச் சித்ரத் தமிழ் is the threefold Tamil of verse, music and drama.

reading: The poet describes women who darken their teeth with betel, laugh, frown and turn their eyes, bind young men by the neck, press their breasts on them, melt them and spoil their virtue, and unite on gold-adorned beds, and asks whether, avoiding such unions, he will gain the golden feet to guard him. The praise names the vel that pierced the mango and the golden mountain, Brahma, son of the discus-bearer, fettered, and the ghosts tearing raw flesh on the battlefield, and Murugan of the kadamba garland and the fierce sakti, at Kachi.
nuance: சக்கரிக்குப் புத்திரற்கு உற்றுத் தளைபூண: Brahma, son of Vishnu, put in fetters, the Om story told only by its outcome. The courtesans' arts are listed but money is not named.

reading: A four-line song: the poet asks whether he will gain the attachment that does not suffer, seeking each day's food and clinging to wealth. The praise names the victorious vel, the one who pierced the mountain, the wisdom known by learning and experience, at Kachi.
nuance: தவியாத பற்று: the cure for the clinging that suffers is another clinging, to the Lord; the line can also be divided to ask for freedom from the clinging that seeks food and wealth. கற்று உற்று உணர் போதா: Murugan as the wisdom reached by learning and by experience.

reading: A short song: the poet, who wanders stumbling through every birth for many days, colliding and whirling, asks whether Murugan will not think to take hold of him a little. The praise names the holy feet fit to be placed on the round flower, the one who gives grace to those whose bonds are cut, at Kachi.
nuance: கதிதோறும் ... சுழல்வேனை: கதி here is each birth or state the soul passes through. வட்டப் புட்பத் தலம் may be the lotus of the heart where the feet are set.

reading: The poet asks not to worship the feet of those who give wealth, cherishing the body-hut, learning worthless words and dying and dying to be born again, but to be given Murugan's green kadamba-adorned feet to praise. The praise names the vel that struck the mango, the one sweet to Valli, the one who pierced the golden mountain, at Kachi.
nuance: அத்தத் தத்தத் தருவோர் தாள் அர்ச்சித்து: worshipping the feet of patrons who give gold is set against worshipping the Lord's feet, the confession of 310 in brief. செத்துச் செத்துப் பிறவாதே: repeated death and birth. The doubled syllables of the rhythm make the division of the first lines uncertain.

reading: The poet asks whether, not joining the pure devotees of pure mind, seeking crooked words, caught in the madness of women who bring sickness, he will be trapped in their snare, fall behind and languish. The praise names Murugan adorning Valli with the kadamba garland, sending the sakti against the mango, at Kachi of the chaste and beautiful Sakti.
nuance: பிணிமாதர் பெட்டிற் கட்டுத் தட்டுப்பட்டு: the women are a sickness and a box that traps. Several lines, especially the praise of the fruit given (பலம் ஈவாய்), are too dense to read confidently.

tamil: கொக்குக் கொக்கத் தலையிற் பற்றுச் சிக்கத் தளகக்
குக்கிக் கக்கிக் கடையிற் பற்றத் துற்றுக் கழலக்
திக்கித் திக்கிக் குளறிச் செப்பித் தப்பிக் கெடுபொய்ச்
சிக்கற் றுட்குக் கருணைச் சுத்தச் சித்தித் தமிழைத்
அக்கிட் டிக்கிட் டமருக் கொட்டிக் கிட்டிட் டெதிரிட்
அச்சுக் கெட்டுப் படைவிட் டச்சப் பட்டுக் கடலுட்
தக்குத் திக்குத் தறுகட் டொக்குத் தொக்குற் றதுகட்
சத்திக் குத்தித் துடியிற் சத்திக் கக்கைச் சமர்செய்ச்
reading: The poet pictures himself old, hair white as a crane, its tufts falling, diseased, coughing and vomiting, learning crooked speech and stammering in many languages, carrying the false, rubbish shirt of a body-hut; he asks whether, free of that tangle, he will gain grace to speak with conviction the pure Tamil of siddhi. The praise, in drum syllables, tells of Surapadman who lost his strength, threw down his arms in fear and entered the sea as a tree, the ghosts clapping and dancing, and the sakti, at Kachi.
nuance: The cure for the old man's stammer (திக்கித் திக்கிக் குளறி) is pure Tamil spoken firmly (சுத்தச் சித்தித் தமிழைத் திட்டத்துக்குப் புகல). செற்றைச் சட்டைக் குடில்: the body is rubbish, a shirt and a hut at once. Sura in the sea as a tree (துருமம்) is the mango.

reading: Spoken for a girl sick with love for Murugan: the speaker asks that the painted creeper not be maddened and perish because of the roaring dark sea and the crescent caught by the serpent, and that Murugan give his kadamba garland. The praise names the vel that pierced the mountain and fought in the ten directions, the one sweet to the hunter girl Valli, the hero who ends the sorrow of pure devotees, at Kachi.
nuance: This is akam poetry in another's voice, a mother's or friend's plea for a girl, not the poet's confession. The sea's roar and the crescent are the classical torments of the lovesick; சர்ப்பத்து அத்திற் பட்டு, the moon seized by the serpent, is the eclipse. The garland asked for is the lover's token.

reading: The poet asks not to whirl in sorrow, tending this hollow sack of skin, a false and lying hut, learning crude and obscene speech and caught in the grief of women with hill-like breasts in golden bodices, but to join the pure devotees of pure mind and worship a little. The praise names the vel that fought the mango, Murugan who adorns Valli with the kadamba cluster, the great one, at Kachi.
nuance: பொக்குப் பை ... தொக்குப் பை: the body is a hollow bag of skin. The plea asks only to worship 'a little' (சற்று அர்ச்சிக்க), among the devotees. The line beginning கக்கக் கைத்தக்க is unclear.

reading: The poet describes women whose eyes are vel, fish and poison, breasts like mountains, hair like dark clouds, who lie with many words and melt a man's heart, so that he staggers, loses sleep and action, grieves and tires, and asks whether, not whirling so for bangled women, he will hold and worship the kadamba-adorned feet that are the golden meaning of the Vedas. The praise names the hero of the arms that embraced Valli, the pearl of the millet field, the lord of the cock banner, the one at Kachi, and the vel that destroyed the mango in the sea.
nuance: துயில்விட்டுச் செயல்விட்டுத் துயர்வுற்றுக் கயர்வுற்று: infatuation as sleeplessness, inaction, grief and exhaustion. சுருதிப் பொற்பொருள்: the feet are the Vedas' golden meaning. The line on Kailasa (கயிலச் சுத்த ரதத்துச் சயிலத்து) is unclear.

reading: Spoken for a girl sick with love: wounded by the flowers of Kama with his fish banner and by the moon that rose to fright from the poison sea, her heart is maddened and she grows weak, which is no small thing; the speaker asks Murugan to give his kadamba garland tucked with fresh jasmine. The praise names Murugan dwelling at Kachi, which green Uma desired, the vel that fights to end the faults and enemies of those who cling to him, the chest Valli embraced, and the one who cut the eight great mountains to dust.
nuance: Akam in another's voice, as in 334: இவள் உளம், 'her heart', is spoken by a mother or friend. Kama's arrows and the moon born with the poison of the churned sea are the torments; the cure is the god's garland.

title: காஞ்சீபுரம்
theme: Last songs at Kanchipuram (காஞ்சீபுரம், 3 of 3): the poet confesses infatuation with women and courtesans who take his wealth, the body's old age and death, and his own trade of praising unworthy patrons for money, and asks for the feet, a truth beyond the quarrelling sects, and a place among the devotees; the praise dwells on Uma's penance at Kanchi by the Kampa river, Krishna in the Bharata war, and Murugan as Siva's teacher.
structure_note: Songs on women and courtesans (338, 340, 342, 345, 346, 348, 349, 351); old age and death (341); songs of doctrine against the sects and toward the wordless truth (339, 343, 347, 350); a love-lament in another voice (344); and the poet's confession of praising patrons for gold (352). The Kanchi legend of Uma's penance and the Lord melting toward her recurs in 338, 350 and 352.
source_issues: Song 343: one corrupt character in புலி஧வ்ளுர் (line 21), probably புலியூர் (Chidambaram).
Song 351: one corrupt character in லு஡ர்ந்து (line 3), probably ஊர்ந்து.
Song 349: heading variant '( காஞ்சீபுரம் )' recorded by the source.
Song 347: possible unflagged garble வெருபம் (line 15).

reading: Struck by Kama's flower arrows and taken by a woman whose kohl-dark, intoxicated eyes drew out his life, the poet asks to give up the experience of infatuation with her and be granted the lotus feet that are the substance of the house of supreme bliss taught in Vedanta. The praise names Siva Ekambara clothed in the directions, and Uma who joined him at Kanchi of the dharmas, and Murugan who embraced the huntress, let Indra's city live, and drew the vel that dried the sea and uprooted the night-walkers.
nuance: வேதாந்த பரமசுக வீடாம் பொருள் இதவிய பாதாம்புயம்: the feet are themselves the Vedantic goal, the bliss of release, set against the அநுபோகம் of the woman. ஏகாம்பர names Siva of the Kanchi temple. The epithets of Siva in lines 12 to 14 (அமகர, அதுலன நீலாம்பரம் அறியாத, அநகர நாளாங்கிதர்) are hard to divide.

reading: The poet sets aside the quarrelsome, ill-natured followers of the sects, who find no single way to end karma-born birth and stagger among the doubts and contradictions of their many texts, and asks Murugan to tell him, so that he does not perish, the true form filled with silence that the mind cannot reach. The praise is of Krishna, refuge of the five Pandavas, who drove the chariot through the eighteen days on the field of the Kurus until the kshatriyas died, and calls Murugan his nephew at Kachi.
nuance: கலக காரண துற்குண சமயிகள்: the sects are not merely wrong but causes of quarrel, and their many-class texts breed விகற்பம் and விபரீதம். Against them the goal is மவுன பூரித சத்திய வடிவு, a truth filled with silence. நாளோர் பத்தெட்டு, eighteen days, and தேர்கடவு அச்சுதன, Achyuta driving the chariot, name the Kurukshetra war, told at unusual length for a praise section.

tamil: கனதன பொற்பிட் டோ ங்கு மார்பொடு ...... வடமாடச்
reading: After a long picture of women with ringing anklets, gem-hung breasts, rolling sword-eyes, pearl smiles and cloud-dark hair who speak flirtatious words, the poet asks whether kinship with them is fitting. The praise is mostly of Uma, the golden lady who kept her grace on him and ruled him, Parvati joined in Siva's form, Sivakami, the dancer who saw the three worlds, Sambhavi, and of Murugan her son, whose vel burned the asura clans and who loves Devayanai and the wise huntress, at Kanchi.
nuance: எனையருள் வைத்திட்டு ஆண்ட நாயகி: the poet claims the goddess's grace on himself, not only on Murugan. The many names of Uma (சிவை, சுடர், சத்தி, சாம்பவி, அமை) make the praise a hymn to the Shakti of Kanchi, as in 32. The plea itself is only a rhetorical question; தூவையர் is unclear.

reading: The poet pictures old age and death: teeth fall like clusters, the ruined coat of the body stops working, the man turns white as a crane, bent over a stick, yawning, his breath going out, and then the kin cry 'he is dead, I am ruined, ah, oo', burn him, leave and go; he asks whether that bewilderment will not end. The praise calls Murugan the eternal Kumaresa of Kachi who stands for the peacock, who fought Sura in the long sea, and the unending, pure, released lord of release.
nuance: The song is set in hard, clipped syllables, and the kin's wailing is given as sound (அஆ உஉ). குப்பாயம், a coat, is the body worn and thrown off. The last line runs epithets of release (முற்றா நித்தா அத்தா சுத்தா முத்தா முத்தி). The close of the plea (அப்பேதுத்துக்கு அமறாதோ) is unclear in division.

reading: A short song: the poet asks not to wander clinging to what suits sin, the women with coral lips and bodice-bound breasts, but to be given a heart of devotion so that he may sing. The praise names the vel that pierced the mango tree, Murugan sweet to the parrot of the ruby heaven, with the cock in his golden hand, lord of Kachi and emperor of the gods' heaven.
nuance: பாடப் பத்திச் சித்தம்: devotion is asked for as the condition of song. The mango (மா) is Sura in his tree form.

reading: The poet seems to rebuke himself ('fie!') for having tasted jivanmukti and experience, burning the three cities to ash and uprooting the sheath of sleep, and yet, not knowing how to stay settled in grace, having run off and let go; he asks Murugan to hold him so he does not end on the ruined road and to grant the lotus feet. The praise names Siva with trident, deer and axe and Uma at his side, whose golden guru Murugan is, and lists the shrines where Murugan receives worship three times a day: Kasi, Madurai, the seven hills, Kovalur, Vedaranyam, Kazhi, Arur, Puliyur, Kalatti, Chiramalai and Kanchi.
nuance: சீவன் முத்தியிற் கூடவே களித்து அநுபூதி சேர: the plea speaks of liberation in life and அநுபூதி, the direct experience of the Lord, as something reached and then lost. The three cities (முப்புரம்) and the sheath of sleep (நித்திரைக் கோசம்) seem to be inner, not mythic. The list of shrines in the praise is a small map of Tamil and northern holy places.

reading: In the voice of one who watches over a lovesick girl, the singer asks that this child, who came to desire without yet knowing desire, not waste away under the stained moon the serpent seeks and the sea roaring with its conches and waves, and that Murugan come and say 'do not fear'. The praise names him with the green peacock, the green hunter maid and the green hills, the one whose anklets his devotees serve, the Kachi lord of the shining vel who freed the bound hands of the gods of the kalpaka grove.
nuance: The whole song is built on doubled words with different senses (நச்சரவம், பச்சை, பத்தி, கச்சி, கற்பக): a யமகம். இச்சையுணர்வின்றி இச்சையென வந்த இச்சிறுமி: the girl is too young to know what she feels. This is akam, not the poet's confession.

reading: The poet confesses that with deceitful conduct and a foolish heart he gave much real wealth to the quick-talking jesting women to please them until his life withered, and now lives in poverty that burns like the undersea fire; he asks that, his cunning gone, hell left behind and the two deeds cut, he be given the feet. The praise names Murugan who embraced the huntress at Kachi, his chest hung with kuravu, vetchi, lotus and kuvalai flowers, guru to Siva who burned the cities with his long bow, and the one who crushed the nirudas' army by the sea.
nuance: மிடியெனப் பெரு வடவை சுட்டிய விதனம்: poverty is the வடவை fire under the sea, the result of what he gave the women, so the courtesan's charge is told from its end. மெய்ப்பொருள் may be wealth or 'true substance', a pun on what he threw away.

reading: The poet describes ornamented women with cuckoo voices who speak Kama's words and jesting talk, then talk money and send go-betweens, impure of heart, greedy for many men's leavings, and asks whether such company befits him. The praise, after a drum passage of battle, names Kandavel who angrily struck on the head the Veda-learned god of the lotus, child of the one with the discus, and who married the guardian of the millet field, at Kanchi.
nuance: பணமெத்தப் பேசித் தூதிடும் ... பலர் எச்சிற்கு ஆசைக் காரிகள்: money and many men, the two stock charges. The praise alludes to the punishment of Brahma (மறைகற்ற புத்தேள், the lotus-dweller born of Vishnu) but does not say here that it was for not knowing Om.

reading: The poet asks for That which is hard to tell people, cannot be reached by learning, has no likeness, cannot be measured by the mind or caught in the chain of tattvas, which was the meaning taught to the three-eyed Siva, the cause of release, out of fools' reach, and which the four Vedas say they cannot reach even at their height. The praise names the vel that pierced the great Sura's chest, Vishnu's admiration, and Murugan who played before the mother whose chastity holds although she bore all seven worlds, at the Kachchalai of Kachi.
nuance: The plea is built of negations (முடியாதது, ஒவாதது, படாதது, எட்டாதது): a way of speaking of the Absolute rather than the poet's own state. முக்கண் ... அருசாவிய அர்த்தக்குப் போதகம்: the meaning Siva asked to hear is the teaching of Siva, without Om named. கற்பு தப்பாது உலகேழையும் ஒக்கப் பெற்றாள்: the virgin mother of all worlds. One word in the praise (வெருபம்) may be garbled.

reading: The poet asks whether he, Murugan's servant, should swoon, his mind destroyed and wasted, by a woman's dull infatuation, her deceitful words, deer and spear eyes, moon forehead, swan gait and bangled hands. The praise names Kumaresa who once circled the world on the peacock in an instant, the Murugesa given by the mountain daughter who shares Siva's side, at Kampai city of tall jewelled mansions.
nuance: அறிவே அழிந்து அயர்வாகி நைந்து: the harm named is to understanding, not to wealth. The circling of the world is the contest for the fruit; கம்பை is Kanchi by the Kampa river.

tamil: முத்து ரத்ந சூத்ர மொத்த சித்ர மார்க்கர்
முத்து திர்த்த வார்த்தை யொத்த பத்ர வாட்கண்
எத்தர் குத்தி ரார்த்தர் துட்ட முட்ட காக்கர்
எக்கர் துக்கர் வாழ்க்கை யுற்ற சித்த நோய்ப்புண்
தித்தி மித்தி மீத்த னத்த னத்த மூட்டு
திக்கு மக்க ளாக்கை துக்க வெற்பு மீக்கொள்
கற்பு ரத்தை வீட்டி நட்ட மிட்ட நீற்றர்
கற்கு றிச்சி வாழ்ப்பெ ணொக்க வெற்றி வேற்கொள்
reading: The poet lists the courtesans, priced women decked in pearl and gem strings, sinful, tricky, cheating, with leaf-like sword eyes and smiles, whose way of life brings sickness of mind and sores, and asks whether he must wander on that path. The praise, after drum syllables, names the vel that sank the enemies and their mountain of sorrow in the red sea, Murugan as guru to Siva the dancer smeared with ash, and the husband of the girl of the hill village, at Kachi.
nuance: விலைமாதர், women with a price, is named outright, and சித்த நோய்ப் புண் joins the mind's sickness to the body's sores. கற்புரத்தை வீட்டி is unclear: perhaps Siva destroying the stone (or triple) cities.

reading: The poet praises those who leave behind the mischievous, wave-loud sects and their hard mass of learning, who with minds free of attachment, by grace, without distraction, know Murugan, melt and reach his golden lotus feet, and asks whether he will not think of placing him too with love in their company. The praise names the twelve-armed hero whose vel broke a mountain and Sura, and Murugan of Kachi by the Kampa river, where the Mother did penance so that her chastity toward Siva's arms would not fail.
nuance: தங்குழாத்தினில் என்னையும் வைக்க: the request is not for release directly but for a place in the gathering of devotees. கம்பையாற்றினில் அன்னை தவம்புரி: the Kanchi legend of Uma's penance by the Kampa river is named. கன்னமிடும் (housebreaking) in the first line may charge the sects with robbing minds; the division is uncertain.

reading: After describing women's carp-like eyes that dart, rival arrows and reach the ears, the poet says that even if he falls at their feet and goes on in this way, he will not forget the one word. The praise, through drum syllables, names Murugan as guru to the dancing Siva at the time of the great flood, the great one, and the lord of famed Kanchi who sang in Tamil that the bond is like magnet and needle.
nuance: ஓர் மொழி மறவேனே: the plea is turned into a vow; the one word may be the Lord's name or a mantra. காந்தக் கல்லும் ஊசியுமே என ஆய்ந்து தமிழ் ஓதிய: the magnet and the needle is the Saiva image of the Lord drawing the soul. The flood (பெருநீர் வெள்ளம்) may be the Kampa flood of the Kanchi legend. Several lines of the praise are hard to divide.

tamil: அறிவிலாப் பித்த ருன்ற னடிதொழாக் கெட்ட வஞ்சர்
அவலர்மேற் சொற்கள் கொண்டு கவிகளாக் கிப்பு கழ்ந்து
சிறிதுகூட் டிக்கொ ணர்ந்து தெருவுலாத் தித்தி ரிந்து
திரியுமார்க் கத்து நிந்தை யதனைமாற் றிப்ப ரிந்து
இறைவர்மாற் றற்ற செம்பொன் வடிவம்வேற் றுப்பி ரிந்து
இருளைநீக் கத்த வஞ்செய் தருளநோக் கிக்கு ழைந்த
குறவர்கூட் டத்தில் வந்து கிழவனாய்ப் புக்கு நின்று
குணமதாக் கிச்சி றந்த வடிவுகாட் டிப்பு ணர்ந்த
reading: The poet confesses that he made poems praising senseless, ungrateful, deceitful men who never bow to Murugan's feet, wandered blessing them in search of wealth, gathered a little, and poured it out on women while roaming the streets; he asks that this disgrace be removed and that release be given clearly. The praise tells how Uma came on the bull to Kachi to do penance and remove her darkness and the Lord melted toward her, and how Murugan, whose words Siva hears, entered among the hunters as an old man and embraced the girl who chased the birds, at Kumarakottam.
nuance: The confession is of the poet's own trade: praising unworthy patrons (அவலர் மேல் சொற்கள் கொண்டு கவிகள் ஆக்கி) and spending the gain on women. இருளை நீக்கத் தவஞ்செய்து அருள நோக்கிக் குழைந்த: the Kanchi legend of Uma's penance and Siva's melting toward her. குமரகோட்டம் is the Murugan shrine at Kanchi.

title: திருவானைக்கா
theme: Songs at Thiruvanaikka (திருவானைக்கா), the elephant forest by the Kaveri: the poet confesses bondage to courtesans who sell love by the measure of wealth, the body as a hut of filth, his faults and his trade of begging patrons, rejects the breath-holding yogi who would make the body last, and asks for the feet, Siva-knowledge beyond the stages of practice, and service; the praise names Ganesa, Uma as Akhilandeswari, the Ramayana, the spider and the jambu tree of the shrine, and Murugan as the Tamil child who won at Madurai.
structure_note: Courtesan and desire songs (353, 354, 356, 357, 360, 361, 364, 366); the body and the poet's faults (362, 365, 367); songs of doctrine (355 against the false yogi, 359 on the Absolute beyond chariyai and kiriyai); the poet's confession of begging patrons (358); and a short song for a wise life (363). Song 367 names Arunai, not Thiruvanaikka.
source_issues: Song 356: one corrupt character in மடலு஡ர்வித் (line 3), probably மடலூர்வித்.
Song 358: one corrupt character in பொற்று஡செடுப்பா (line 7), probably பொற்றூசெடுப்பாய்.
Song 359: one corrupt character in வயலு஡ரா (line 18), probably வயலூரா.
Song 364: one corrupt character in தேனு஡றல் (line 1), probably தேனூறல்; also ஜநமுத (line 3), perhaps for ஜலமுத.
Song 366: one corrupt character in காயத்஡ணசெப (line 15), probably காயத்ரீ செப (஡ண for ரீ).
Song 361: line 6 (காமக் ரோத லோப மப மிவை) seems garbled; the fourth vice is perhaps மதம்.
Song 367 is grouped under திருவானைக்கா but names only Arunai (அருணை) and ends without a shrine.

reading: The poet lists the arts of women who call with kohl-dark eyes, smile to melt, loosen their hair, show nail-marks on their palms, kindle the fire of desire in young men, bind them with idle talk, bewilder them by dancing in the hall, and take their wealth without blame, and asks whether a day will come when, the bond at these clever hands cut, Murugan grants service at his feet. The praise is first a hymn to Ganesa, elephant-faced, with goad and noose, one tusk and great belly, who cuts the deeds of those who bow, and then names Murugan his younger brother, the six-faced lord of the six syllables who cherished the three Tamils, at the elephant forest by the Jambu tank.
nuance: எவரேனும் நிந்தை செய்யாது பொருட்பறிக்கவும்: the courtesans rob without anyone blaming them. The remedy is சேவை, service at the feet. The long praise of Ganesa (விக்கிநப்ரபு, கணராஜன், எங்கள் விநாயகன்) is unusual. கஜாரணியம் and சம்பு தடாகம் name Thiruvanaikka; சுந்தர மாறன் மதில் appears to be a wall built by a Pandya king.

tamil: அம்புலி நீரைச் சூடிய செஞ்சடை மீதிற் றாவிய
அன்புட னாவிற் பாவது சந்தத மோதிப் பாதமு
வம்பணி பாரப் பூண்முலை வஞ்சியர் மாயச் சாயலில்
கொம்பனை நீலக் கோமளை அம்புய மாலைப் பூஷணி
கொஞ்சிய வானச் சானவி சங்கரி வேதப் பார்வதி
செம்பவ ளாயக் கூரிதழ் மின்குற மானைப் பூண்முலை
செந்தமிழ் பாணப் பாவலர் சங்கித யாழைப் பாடிய
reading: The poet asks whether, without singing on his tongue with love and without worshipping the feet with flowers in his hand, he, a wretched sinner, must perish, dimmed in the deceptive charm of women with heavy breasts, bee-hovering hair and blue looks that reach both ears. The praise is a string of names of Uma, the blue tender one, Kundali, Abhirami, Sankari, Parvati of the Veda, and names Murugan her son who embraced the hunter girl, at Thiruvanaikka where Tamil poets and panars sing to the yazh.
nuance: The plea defines the loss by what is left undone: பாதமும் அங்கையின் நானில் பூசையும் அணியாமல், the worship of the feet with flowers. ஆலப்போசனி, she who ate the poison, gives Uma Siva's deed.

tamil: அனித்த மான வூனாளு மிருப்ப தாக வேநாசி
தவத்தி லேகு வால்மூலி புசித்து வாடு மாயாச
செனித்த காரி யோபாதி யொழித்து ஞான ஆசார
செகத்தி யாவும் வேறாக நிகழ்ச்சி யாம நோதீத
தொனித்த நாத வேயூது சகஸ்ர நாம கோபால
சுவர்க்க லோக மீகாம சமஸ்த லோக பூபால
மனித்த ராதி சோணாடு தழைக்க மேவு காவேரி
மணத்த சோலை சூழ்காவை அனைத்து லோக மாள்வாரு
reading: The poet asks not to become a foolish yogi of desire and illusion who, thinking this impermanent flesh will last, holds the breath so it does not leave the nostrils and withers in austerity eating herbs; he asks instead that, with malam, maya and their adjuncts removed, devoted to the conduct of knowledge, knowing 'I am other, my body is other, the whole world is other', he be ruled as a yogi of Siva's own form beyond the mind. The praise names Gopala of the thousand names who plays the flute as uncle, Murugan of Vayalur, and the grove-circled Kavai watered by the Kaveri's flood, which all world-rulers revere.
nuance: அனித்தமான ஊன் நாளும் இருப்பதாகவே ... அசட்டு யோகி: the target is breath-holding and herbs used to keep the body, not yoga itself, since the plea ends asking to be a சிவச்சொரூப மாயோகி. யான் வேறு என் உடல் வேறு செகத்து யாவும் வேறாக: release is described as disidentification from body and world.

reading: The poet speaks of women whose breasts, smeared with camphor and sandal, burst their bands and make men wither and even ascetics ride the palmyra horse of desire, with carp-like eyes reaching to the ears, and asks whether, on the day Death comes seeking to throw down his body, he will call on Murugan without forgetting his feet. The praise names Murugan on the dark-plumed peacock, the little one younger than the elephant with flowing musth, plunderer of Sura's city, guardian of the gods, servant of the peacock-girl of the millet field, the light of the Tamil Veda, at Kavai.
nuance: துறவோரை ஆசை மடல் ஊர்வித்து: the classical madal, the spurned lover's ride on the palmyra horse, is forced even on renouncers. காலைமறவாமல்: the feet are what must be remembered at Death's hour. Some lines of the praise (பாய்மத கபோலத்தானொடு இகலாம் முற்பாடி) are hard to divide.

reading: The poet says that, infatuated with women of poison eyes skilled in Kama's arts, who act out desire exactly as far as the money goes even if a thousand measures of gold are paid for their breasts, he suffered weakness, trembling and madness as fate wrote on his head, and asks grace for himself who has built a house that is a worm-filled cave of filth. The praise shows the battle with the giants, ghouls clapping and vultures dancing, says that Murugan gives whatever those who tell of his vel desire, and names him the son of the three-eyed Siva of the white jambu where seven-note Tamil found its fruit.
nuance: ஆசை அப்பொருள் ஒக்க நடிப்பவர்: the desire is acted in proportion to the payment. தலையிட்ட விதிப்படி: the poet lays his ruin on the fate written on his head, a rare appeal to fate in these confessions. புழுக்கொள் மலக் குகை வீடு: the body as a house of filth. வெண்ணாவல், the white jambu, is the tree of Thiruvanaikka.

reading: The poet voices the begging poet's speech to a patron, 'I am first in the rules of prosody; shall I sing you a madal or a kovai? Fetch palm leaf and stylus; I have seen no one your equal on earth; bring this king of poets gold in a bundle, jewels and gems', and asks whether he must wither in the trouble of such talk. The praise names Murugan who at Tamil Madurai, against those who wear no waist-cloth, put the palm leaf into fire and water and won the name of father of dharma, and the light of the shrine on the Kaveri bank where the spider meditating on Siva wove a canopy.
nuance: The confession is of the court poet's begging flattery, quoted in his own voice, including the genres he offers (மடல், கோவை). அரைக்காடை சுற்றார் are the naked Jains, and the leaf put into fire and water (அனற்கே புனற்கே வரைந்த ஏடு) is Sambandar's contest at Madurai: Murugan is identified with Sambandar. சிலந்தி நூல்செய் திருக்காவணம் is the Thiruvanaikka story of the spider that sheltered the linga.

reading: The poet describes the One the Vedas proclaim, the supreme light in the upper space, beyond those who practise chariyai and kiriyai, beyond turiya, formless knowledge mingled with world, flesh and life, seen by those with Siva-knowledge, full without lack, without caste or clan, the space the devotees speak of, the true house and sea of bliss, and asks whether, the senses' torment ended, he will gain the feet. The praise names Murugan as the child Guha who removed Indra's sorrow, and the son of the Mother, first of the world, daughter of the Himalaya, Gauri, Kundali, the form of nada, spouse of the lord of the white jambu.
nuance: சரியை க்ரியையும் புணர்ந்தவர் எவராலும் ஓத அரிய: the rites of the first two stages cannot reach it, and துரியம் கடந்தது puts it beyond the fourth state. சாதி குலமும் இலது: it has no caste or clan, a pointed phrase. The goddess's names close the song at Thiruvanaikka, where she is Akhilandeswari.

reading: The poet calls the women of cloud-dark hair and moon faces thieves of love, total cheats, who take the lives of lustful men ignorant of the higher path, who make arrows their eyes and sing for greed of wealth, and asks grace for himself who perishes by them. The praise names Murugan the bridegroom of the hunter girl, the vel that pierced the two hills while the sea cried out, and the peacock rider whose valour Siva, whose head and feet Vishnu on the serpent bed could not find, admires, at Thiruvanaikka.
nuance: பரநெறி உணரா அக்காமுகர் உயிர்பலி கொளும்: the women take the lustful as a sacrifice, and their victims are those who do not know the higher path. The search for Siva's head and feet is given to Vishnu alone here.

tamil: காமக் ரோத லோப மப மிவை ...... சிதையாத
reading: The poet speaks of women's poison-blue eyes and illusory bodies, and of lust, anger, greed and pride that are not destroyed in him, and asks whether Murugan will not think to rule him at his anklet feet, so that from now on he may love the path of knowledge that the masters of breath praise, and yoga, japa and tapas. The praise has the cock crying 'long live', the peacock dancing and ghoul armies playing in the sky, the vel that ended Sura, Murugan of Vayalur, and Thiruvanaikka where women sing and dance.
nuance: காமக் ரோத லோப ... இவை சிதையாத பாவி: the inner enemies are named, though the fourth word is garbled. Unlike 355, here breath practice (வாயு வலம் வரல்) and yoga are part of what the poet hopes for. The division of lines 9 to 11 is uncertain.

reading: The poet describes the body as a hut packed with blood, flesh, bone, sinew, worms, bile, phlegm, gut, fat, hair and brain, in which the five senses run into the forest and drive him to the five great sins, so that he never tries the Vedas, Puranas, Agamas, chariyai, kiriyai, worship or meditation; he asks that this fault be removed so he may see the house of bliss. The praise names the single vel that broke Krauncha, the giants, the mango and the sea, Murugan the nephew of Ranganatha of Srirangam whom Brahmins of the six limbs praise as Hari and Govinda, and the son of Sambhunatha of the elephant forest.
nuance: The inventory of the body (குருதி புலால் என்பு தோல் நரம்புகள் கிருமிகள் ...) is the same device as the Naladiyar's, but here it explains why the poet's senses ran wild, not why a woman should not be desired. சீரங்கராசன் names Srirangam, across the river from Thiruvanaikka.

reading: A very short song: the poet asks whether he must wander apart from those who seek and worship Murugan, and asks to be given the wise life of Madurai of mansions. The praise names him the lover of songs, gracious as milk and honey, sweet to the dancing peacock, at Thiruvanaikka.
nuance: மாடக் கூடற் பதி ஞான வாழ்வு may point to the Sambandar episode at Madurai, as in 358, or simply mean wisdom at that city. நானத்தாக is hard to divide.

reading: The poet compares a woman's lips to honey, her eyes to poison, her breasts to Meru, her waist to empty space, and describes lovemaking in which his life wanes and his clothes slip, then asks whether he must roam like a clown's monkey for women who give an illusory life, and when he will reach the stilling of mind. The praise retells the Ramayana at length: Rama's message to the forgetful Sugriva that the arrow that killed Vali is not spent, the bridge across the sea and Ravana's fortress broken, and names Murugan the brother-in-law of Kama, Narayana's son.
nuance: குரங்கை ஒத்து உழல்வேனோ: the poet sees himself as a performing monkey; the image leads, perhaps by design, into the monkey-king of the praise. மனோலயம் என்று சேர்வேன்: the goal named is the dissolution of mind. The speech to Sugriva is hard to divide, and ஜநமுத in line 3 may stand for ஜலமுத, cloud.

reading: The poet heaps names on himself: the wretch proud of running errands at fragrant-haired women's feet, trickster, fool, boaster, worthless, unlearned, all anger, stupid, a sinner of unchanging deeds whose speech fails, fallen into hell, and asks whether a day will come when Murugan asks after him and rules him kindly. The praise is of Uma as Narayani who held the mountain bow to burn the cities, the girl of Kanchi, mother of the sea-girt world, Akhilanda Nayaki of the elephant forest, and names Murugan the nephew of Vishnu who twisted off Ravana's heads.
nuance: வினவி முன் அருள்செய்து பாங்கின் ஆள்வது: the hope is that the Lord will take the first step and inquire. The praise gives the burning of the three cities to Uma (மலைசிலை ஒருகையில் வாங்கு நாரணி), and names her as the goddess of both Kanchi and Thiruvanaikka (அகிலாண்ட நாயகி).

reading: The poet lists courtesan epithets, women who bewilder with spear eyes, breed lust and anger, roam the streets, send their breasts into battle, speak like cuckoos, drive out men without money, paint their skin and call anyone to bed, plunderers, and asks whether he will escape the net of sorrow. The praise names Rama, the sea of compassion who killed Tataka to guard the sacrifice of sages who bathe at dawn and offer to the sun and recite the Gayatri, as uncle, Murugan of the cane and paddy fields of Vayalur, and the beloved of the Father at Thiruvanaikka.
nuance: காசற்றாரை இதத்தில் ஒழிச்சிகள்: the women gently put out those without money. காம க்ரோதம் விளைத்திடு: they breed anger as well as lust. The praise sets Vedic morning rites (தர்ப்பணம், காயத்ரீ செபம்) beside the confession.

reading: The poet calls himself cruel, wretched and foolish, one who never melts crying 'Kumara, Guru, Saravanabhava, Muruga, refuge', who falls into the pit of beautiful women who give embraces in measure with wealth, and vows that he will not forget, waking or dreaming, the lotus feet with anklets which once at Arunai came with the compassionate devotees and the Vedas at their side to rule him. The praise names Vishnu who churned the sea with Vasuki and Meru so the gods' hunger ended, the dwarf who measured the worlds, as uncle, and Murugan who, in prattling speech, taught Siva that the meaning is to know the knower.
nuance: அருணையில் ஒருவிசை ... வரும் இருபரிபுர கமல மலரடி: the feet came once at Arunai (Tiruvannamalai), apparently the poet's own experience of grace, so the vow rests on memory. அறிவை அறிவது பொருளென அருளிய: the teaching to Siva is given as 'know that which knows', without Om. The courtesans who give union by the measure of wealth (பொருளளவளவு) appear again.

title: திருவருணை
theme: First songs at Thiruvannamalai (திருவருணை, 1 of 6): the poet renounces women, sects, patron-poetry and birth, vows not to forget the word and the feet given him at Arunai, sees each charm of a woman as Death's weapon, and pictures the funeral and Yama's noose; three songs are laments of a lovesick girl tormented by the moon, the flute and the town's talk. The praise dwells on Arunai's tall tower, Murugan as teacher of Siva, and his love for Valli.
structure_note: Renunciation and longing for silence (368, 370), the quarrelling sects (369), the word and feet given at Arunai (371, 373), women's charms seen as their dangers (372, 374), courtesans who sell (373, 375, 377), death and Yama's noose (376, 378), the akam laments (379 to 381), and 382, which asks to be taken into service before death. 376 to 381 name the tower (கோபுரம்) of Arunai.
source_issues: Song 371: unflagged garble நிற்முசும் (line 3).
Song 372: unflagged garble யென்முவா (line 3), probably என மூவா.
Song 375: unflagged garble ளித்ழுறல் (line 9), probably இதழூறல். In this chapter the source seems to write ்மு and ்ழு where மூ and ழூ are meant (also துன்ப்முழ்கி in 382).
Song 381: one corrupt character in லு஡டு (line 1), clearly ஊடு.

Song 382: unflagged garble துன்ப்முழ்கித் (line 6), probably துன்பமூழ்கி. Its last two lines (பாதமலர் மீதிற் போதமலர் தூவிப் பாடுமவர் தோழத் தம்பிரானே) are identical to song 383's; one may have been copied into the other.
Songs 377 and 378: the last two lines are identical (அடவியிற் றோகைபொற் றடமுலைக் காசையுற் றயருமச் சேவகப் பெருமாளே); possibly a copying error.

reading: The poet says 'enough, enough' (அலம் அலம்) to lovemaking with women, to the learning that likens men of the world to the wish-tree, to form and youth, to the arts of perverse sects, to the bewildering life of deeds and to births like writing on water, and asks now for his feet and for silence, to walk one way with his devotees. The praise tells at length of Siva's burning of the three cities, the chariot breaking under his foot and the cities blazing at his laugh, and names Murugan his son, who melted with the hunter girl and roams on a peacock over the peak of Arunai with its seven-tiered towers.
nuance: The refrain அலமலம் sweeps away not only women but the poet's own trade: உலகோரைத் தருவை நிகரிடு புலமை is the art of praising patrons as the kalpa tree. சலில லிபியன சனனம், births like letters written on water, is a striking image of impermanence. The Tripura story is told in its full details (Meru as bow, the serpent king as string, sun and moon as wheels, Brahma as charioteer, the Vedas as horses), and the three spared devotees appear as ஒருவரும் இருவரும் அருள்பெற.

reading: The poet sets against the pitiless, hair-plucked night-wanderers, flesh-eaters and many quarrelsome sectarians who wail broken scriptures till the path is lost, the reality without rising or death which the Vedas drum is easily gained in knowledge when the eyes stream, the words falter, the heart melts, craving, worldly bonds, speech, act and feeling end, the two deeds fall away and 'mine' is shaken off; he asks when that day of grace will come. The praise is a long litany of the Goddess, Gauri, Bhairavi, Tripurai, the faithful wife who bore all worlds, and names Murugan her son and Ganga's, the guru brighter than countless suns, who gave the forest girl and the gods' daughter their place beside him at Arunai.
nuance: பறிதலை நிசிசரர், the hair-plucked night-wanderers, likely means Jain monks, who pluck their hair; பிசித அசனர், flesh-eaters, may be another group. The conditions are stacked as a chain of 'if' clauses (விடில், கெடில், அறில்) ending in எனது எனும் மலம் அறில், 'if the impurity called mine ends'. The Goddess's names in the praise are partly Sanskrit compounds whose divisions are uncertain.

reading: The poet pictures the women without bounds who sell their sweet lovemaking at a price in every street, their hair and garments loosening, breasts swaying, eyes speaking Kama's scripture, so that men, gods and sages run after them, and asks when his life, tossing in the sea of pleasure they give, will plunge instead into the sea of silent Siva-bliss. The praise paints Arunai, its areca palms tearing the sky so that clouds, moon and the sun's horses stumble, its fields, tanks, moat and walls, and the hill stream carrying agil, flowers, gems, goats, elephants and lions, where Murugan bowed melting at the feet of the hunter girl born of a sage.
nuance: The song is built on two seas: the சுக சலதி the women give and the மவுன சிவசுக சலதி the poet longs for. வரைவில் அரிவையர் and விலைகூறும் use the very terms of the Kural's chapter on women who draw no line. முநி தரு புனிதை, the pure one born of a sage, points to the story of Valli's birth.

reading: The poet says that even if he melts at women's eyes, hair, smile, lips, waist, gait and feet, speaks their names, runs their errands, strays from the path, jests with them and loses himself in the sea of passion on their bed, he will not forget the one supreme word and the two feet that Murugan gave him with compassion at Arunai. The praise shows the vel trampling the seven hills, breaking Meru's peak and tearing the old mango tree in the sea, names Murugan Siva's son and Ganapati's brother, and has him, for the hunters' salvation, write a lone madal out of longing for the doe of the millet field.
nuance: அருணை நகர்மிசை கருணையொடு அருளிய பரம ஒரு வசனமும் இரு சரணமும் மறவேனே: the poet speaks of a word and the feet given to him at Arunai, apparently his own initiation; the vow is not to be pure but not to forget, even in the midst of desire. தனி மடல் எழுதிய makes Murugan the lover who takes the desperate madal for Valli. முதுசூதம், the old mango, is Sura in tree form.

tamil: பவனி தனையநு தினநினை யென அருள் ...... பகர்வாயே
புடவி வழிபட புதை பொருள் விரகொடு ...... புகல்வோனே
reading: The poet asks not to spend day and night praising women in set comparisons, hair as darkness that fights the clouds, face as the moon, eyes as arrows, breasts as lotus buds, nor to flatter them that their form is beauty, but to be told by grace to think daily of Murugan's procession on the peacock that crushes the asuras. The praise has Murugan, amid sages, tell the hidden meaning called hard to speak to Siva who burned the cities with a laugh, and has poets, scholars and ascetics declare him the six-faced one who drank from the six mothers, while devotees dance and worship at Arunai.
nuance: The fault confessed is poetic: the set similes of love poetry spent on women, against which the poet sets a new subject, the peacock procession (பவனி). புகல அரியது பொருள் இது ... புதை பொருள் விரகொடு புகல்வோனே is the teaching of Siva, though Om is not named. Two glyphs in the first lines are garbled.

reading: The poet lists the courtesans who weigh a man's capital and life, scent themselves with civet and agil, throw spear-like glances, measure the heart by the money and keep their word an instant, and says that he, deluded on their path and knowing neither the foot nor the crown, will not forget the silent word and the two great feet given with compassion at Arunai. The praise tells of Rama against Ravana's walled city, Hanuman's fire and the monkeys' causeway, names Murugan his nephew, and the vel that broke the asuras and restored the gods, and his embrace of the hunter girl.
nuance: மனது திரவியம் அளவளவு அளவியர், women who measure their heart exactly to the money, is the stock charge against courtesans. அடிமுடி அறிகிலன், 'I who know neither foot nor crown', may glance at Arunai's own story of the Lord whose foot and crown Vishnu and Brahma could not find, though the song does not tell it. The refrain repeats 371 with மவுன வசனம், the word of silence.

reading: The poet takes each charm of women and names what it truly is: the eyes not lotuses but fire-dipped arrows, the hair not a cloud but a darkness that blinds the eye of jnana, the speech not nectar but a net for life, the smile not jasmine but theft, the navel not a pool but a pit, the breasts not hills but Yama the killer, the pearls on them Yama's rope; women are not women but forms made of many deeds, and he asks when he will join with that awareness. The praise shows Valli and Devayanai at his sides, the asura armies burned, and Murugan son of compassionate Uma who fosters dharma, at Arunai where the pure sage Gautama worships.
nuance: Each line turns on அல, 'not': the poet undoes the love poet's similes (as 372 renounces them) and replaces each with a danger. மகளிர் மகளிரும் அல பல வினைகொடு சமையும் உருவு: the conclusion is metaphysical, that the woman is a body built of karma. கவுதம புநித முநி தொழ and அறம் வளர் கருணை உமை may point to a local story of Uma's penance at Arunai under the sage Gautama, which the song does not tell.

reading: The poet pictures women who walk the street like peacocks, smeared with musk, showing their breasts for sale, their hair falling and garments loose, and calls himself the fool who embraces their delusion, tasting their lips as cane and fruit; he asks for grace that scatters his base and murderous sins. The praise makes the drums sound 'Kumara Gurupara' six times over as their beat while gods, sages and Brahma worship, and names the vel that broke the asuras' horses, elephants and chariots and Murugan who embraced the hunter girl of the red hill.
nuance: விலைமுலை, breasts for sale, names the trade. குமர குருபர repeated six times is given as the drums' own rhythm (எனதாளம் குரைசெய் முரசம்), so the name of the Lord becomes the beat. ஒரு அருண கிரி குறமகள் plays on Arunagiri, the red hill, which is also the poet's name. One word (இத்ழுறல், probably இதழூறல்) is garbled.

reading: The poet pictures his death: his wife wailing 'you have undone me, husband, I am ruined', his sons crying 'father', kin and old friends weeping round the bier, drums beating, and Yama casting his thick noose; at that hour he asks Murugan to protect him and give back his life. The praise names Murugan with vel, cock and peacock dwelling in the tower of Arunai, lord of the gods, easy for poets of rare Saiva song, lover of the hunter girl on the golden hill, and the warrior who crushed Sura with mountain and sea.
nuance: The wailing is given in direct speech (கயல்விழித் தேன் எனைச் செயல் அழித்தாய், கணவ கெட்டேன், புதல்வர் அப்பா). பரிகரித்து ஆவியைத் தரவேணும் asks not for release but for the life itself to be saved at the noose. அருணையிற் கோபுரத்து உறைவோனே, the Murugan of the tower, recurs in 377 and 378.

reading: The poet speaks of women whose carp-eyes dance like Death who stirs the life, who settle the body's terms in advance, make relations in secret for coin, cause grief and sulk on the flower bed and give themselves for a high price, and says that for this painful deed he has lost his mind's sense; he asks whether he will worship the two feet that are the raft for life. The praise names Brahma who recites the Vedas, Indra with the vajra and Siva who comes with Uma, the vel that fought Sura so that the peaks and the sea dried, Murugan of the tower at Arunai sung by the wise, and the warrior who longed for the forest girl.
nuance: காசினுக்கு உறவு, relation for coin, and உயர் பொருட்கு, for a high price, name the trade. உயிர்ப் புணை இணைத் தாள், the feet as a raft for the life, is an image of crossing. The opening lines (கறுவுமிக் காவியைக் கலகும் அக் காலன் ஒத்து) and முற்பாடு கட்டளை are hard to divide, and the praise's மறைகள் புக்கார் is unclear.

reading: The poet imagines Death casting his thick noose, the life going out, the kin of passion no longer holding on, and the body left to the fire and its remains to the water; he, a dog born in this sinful birth and wasted by disease, asks whether he will hear Murugan say with love 'I have forgiven your fault, I have cut away your flaw'. The praise is obscure; it seems to name Murugan the god of the red cock banner who pierced the hill and expounded the arts, and closes as 377 does, at the tower of Arunai.
nuance: பிழை பொறுத்தாய் எனப் பழுது அறுத்தாள் என: the grace asked for is forgiveness spoken aloud. The first line repeats 376's பரியகைப் பாசம் விட்டு எறியும் காலன. The praise lines 9 to 13 (கரியமெய்க் கோலமுற்ற அரியின் ...) are hard to divide, and the last two lines are identical to 377's.

tamil: தருணமணி வானி லத்தி லருணமணி யால விட்ட
தலைமைதவி ராம னத்தி னிலைமையறி யாதெ திர்த்த
வருணமட மாதர் கற்ற வசையின்மிகை பேச முற்று
மகுடமணி வாரி சைக்கும் விகடமது லாவு சித்ர
கருணையக லாவி ழிச்சி களபமழி யாமு லைச்சி
கடுவுடைய ராநி ரைத்த சடிலமுடி மீது வைத்த
அருணமணி யால மைத்த கிரணமணி சூழும் வெற்றி
அசுரர்குலம் வேர றுத்து வடவனலை மீதெ ழுப்பி
reading: In the voice of a lovesick woman: by the moonlight that strikes her bed of fire, by the arrows of the fierce god of love who attacked without knowing her state, and by the blame the women of the town speak, her life is all but gone, and she asks Murugan to come daily on his peacock so that it does not perish. The praise names him the bridegroom of the hunter girl, the hero whose feet Siva cherished like flowers on his serpent-wreathed hair, dwelling in the tower of Arunai, who uprooted the asuras and freed the gods.
nuance: This is akam poetry in the woman's own voice (எனது ஆவி), the poet in the role of the girl in love with the god. The classical torments are here, the moon and Kama's arrows, with the town's gossip (வருண மட மாதர் கற்ற வசை). The line on Siva placing flowers on his hair (சடிலமுடி மீது வைத்த கடிய மலர் ஆதரித்த கழல்) may mean that Siva wears Murugan's feet; the division is uncertain.

tamil: முழுகிவட வாமு கத்தி னெழுகனலி லேபி றக்கு
மொழியுமட மாத ருக்கு மினியதனி வேயி சைக்கு
புழுகுதிகழ் நீப மத்தி லழகியகு ராநி ரைத்த
புணரும்வகை தானி னைத்த துணரும்வகை நீல சித்ர
எழுமகர வாவி சுற்று பொழிலருணை மாந கர்க்கு
இடைதுவள வேடு வச்சி படமசைய வேக னத்த
செழுமகுட நாக மொய்த்த ஒழுகுபுனல் வேணி வைத்த
திசைமுகன்மு ராரி மற்று மரியபல தேவ ருற்ற
reading: Again in the lovesick woman's voice: so that she does not perish from the full moon born of the submarine fire, from the blame of foolish women, from the sweet lone flute and from old King Kama, she asks Murugan to come daily on his blue peacock, so she may know how to embrace his twelve shoulders garlanded with kadamba and kura. The praise names Arunai's tower and tanks, the chest that never leaves the hunter girl, the guru who taught Siva from the first, and the deliverer of Brahma, Vishnu and the gods from prison.
nuance: The torments now include the flute (வேயிசை), a classical herald of evening longing. The moon born of the வடவாமுகம், the submarine mare-fire, explains why its light burns. சிவனை முதல் ஓதுவித்த குருநாதா: முதல் may be the first syllable, Om.

tamil: வடவையன லு஡டு புக்கு முழுகியெழு மாம திக்கு
வரைதிசைவி டாது சுற்றி யலறுதிரை வாரி திக்கு
நெடுகனக மேரு வொத்த புளகமுலை மாத ருக்கு
நினைவினொடு பீலி வெற்றி மரகத லாப சித்ர
மடலவிழு மாலை சுற்று புயமிருப தோடு பத்து
மருகபல வான வர்க்கு மரியசிவ னார்ப டிக்க
இடையரிவு லாவு முக்ர அருணகிரி மாந கர்க்கு
எழுபுவிய ளாவு வெற்பு முடலிநெடு நாக மெட்டு
reading: Told of a girl rather than by her: so that the full infatuation of the woman with breasts like Meru may end, harried by the moon that rises after plunging through the submarine fire, by the yazh sweet as speech, by the sea wailing round the eight directions, and by the formless Kama's arrows, Murugan is asked to come on his emerald peacock. The praise names Rama, who cut Ravana's twenty arms and ten crowns, as his uncle, and Murugan the guru who made Siva study the silent Veda, dwelling in the tower of fierce Arunagiri, whose vel pierced the hill and the eight serpents.
nuance: The speaker is now a third person (a mother or friend), as in 24. மவுன மறை ஓதுவித்த, taught the silent Veda, links the teaching of Siva with the silence asked for in 368 and 370. One word (வடவையன லு஡டு) has a corrupt glyph.

reading: The poet, infatuated by eyes like poison, lips, hair, smile, brow, gait and breasts, sunk in the misery of Death's trident and tightening noose, asks whether, before he dies with his old deeds unshed, Murugan will not take him into his service. The praise names him the light, Muruga, eternal, who took the hunter girl on his shoulder, Kandavel of the street of the ancient jnana-hill Sonagiri, son of the one who shares Uma, and the comrade-lord of those who sing scattering flowers of knowledge on his feet.
nuance: ஏவல் கொண்டிடாயோ, 'will you not take my service', asks to become a servant before death. பழய ஞானச் சோணகிரி calls the red hill itself a hill of ancient knowledge. பாடுமவர் தோழத் தம்பிரானே, lord who is comrade to his singers, may echo the Saiva title of Sundarar, the Lord's comrade, from the other side. The last two lines are identical to 383's.

title: திருவருணை
theme: More songs at Thiruvannamalai (திருவருணை, 2 of 6): the poet confesses to deceitful women who call wealthy men home, to eyes as deadly as the churned poison, and to a body bent by age and bound for hell; he pictures Yama coming while wife, sons and kin weep, asks for the silent seal the sects cannot know, and in three songs speaks for a girl sick with love. The praise names the Goddess in long litanies, Unnamulai of Arunai, Siva who could not be found by Vishnu and Brahma, and Murugan who hid his form to follow Valli.
structure_note: Women and their deceits (383 to 387, 391 to 393, 395), with 386 and 387 on women's eyes as poison; death and Yama (388, 389, 392); the silent seal and the sects (394); and the akam laments of a lovesick girl (390, 396, 397). 384 and 386 to 390 share closing formulas (அரியர பிரம புரந்தராதியர் தம்பிரானே; அரிவையும் ஒருபங்கு இடமுடையவர்).
source_issues: Song 394: one corrupt character in கடலு஡டுற் (line 2), clearly கடலூடுற்; also unflagged garble தொழுத்மு டூடு (line 1), probably தொழுது மூடூடு, the ்மு for மூ seen in chapter 32.
Song 383: its last two lines are identical to song 382's (see chapter 32).

reading: The poet asks that, seeing the throngs of deceitful, quarrelsome, tricky women, he not fall into the folly of delusion nor tend this divided body, but that birth, change and death leave him and he think in his mind of Murugan's sharp vel, his cock and the hunter girl of the millet slope. The praise names Kandavel of Arunai's street, the vel that went to free the gods' prisoners in the old sky, the lord who saw the world live when Sura and his foot soldiers fell, and the comrade-lord of those who sing scattering flowers of knowledge on his feet.
nuance: சாதக விகாரச் சாதல் may be birth (ஜாதகம்), change and death, the bodily cycle. The remedy is contemplation of the Lord's emblems (vel, cock, Valli) rather than his feet. The opening (பேதக விரோதத் தோதக விநோத) and the line ending தென்படாதே are hard to divide.

reading: The poet asks for grace not to fall into the maya of the sweet-tongued women who say to men of wealth 'by my oath, by your oath, my house is near, come there', foolish, quarrelsome and wicked, sauntering in the streets. The praise is a long litany of the Goddess, Kumari, Kali, Varahi, Maheswari, Gauri, Mahamayi, Abhirami, Narayani, sister of Vishnu, she who drank the poison of the sea, mother Uma who became all the Vedas, and names Murugan her son, whose vel fed the ghouls on the asuras' heads, roaming on the cloud-touched tower of Sonesar's Annamalai.
nuance: பொருளுளாரை, men of wealth, names whom the women call: the invitation 'my house is near' is the courtesan's speech of 21. The praise is chiefly of the Goddess, gathering the names of fierce and gentle forms (Kali, Varahi, Kapali, Abhirami) into the one mother Uma. Some names in the litany (மோடி, நிராபரி, சுடாரணி) are uncertain to me.

reading: The poet speaks of women who melt men like wax, comb their long hair on the street platforms, cover and loosen their breasts with their garments, play tricks and talk with deceitful hearts, and calls himself the great sinner and dunce who has fallen into their long net in the sea of strife and does not know love; he asks the sea of compassion, husband of two consorts, to give him his feet and rule him. The praise names Brahma and the gods who praise him, Vishnu with the tulasi garland as uncle, the bright vel, the one who circles the seven worlds, son of the Lady whom Hara embraces, at Arunai with its golden tower, walls and streets.
nuance: நேசமது அறியாத கசட மூடன்: the poet's fault is that he does not know love, set against the women's false love. The praise's உலகேழ் வலம் வருவோனே recalls the circling of the world in the contest for the fruit.

reading: The poet likens women's eyes to the dark poison of Siva's throat and to Murugan's own vel, Siva being described in full with hide, serpent, crescent, Ganga, fire, axe and deer, the burner of Kama; these eyes press against the earrings and swallow the lives of men like Kama, and he asks whether his dying, body and mind ruined in their embrace, will not end. The praise pictures asura heads falling like broken Meru while ghouls walk as at an offering, Kumara in Arunai's tall tower, and the one who left the six-faced form the Vedas praise to go among hunters and embrace the forest girl, lord of Hari, Hara, Brahma and Indra.
nuance: The simile is bold: the eyes that kill are compared to the poison Siva holds in his throat (கண்டகாளம்) and to the vel Murugan loves (உனது உள் உகந்த வேல்), so the deadly look is matched with the Lord's own weapons. அறுமுக வடிவை ஒழிந்து: Murugan put aside his six-faced form for Valli, a theme repeated in 387.

reading: The poet compares women's eyes to the poison that rose when the gods churned the sea with Meru as post and the serpent king as rope, a poison that spread like massed clouds, shook the elephants and mountains of the eight directions and cracked the cosmic egg; these eye-nets, guilty of the five great sins, take lovers' lives as sacrifice, and he asks whether love for such women will not end. The praise shows Taraka destroyed and the gods restored, Murugan son of Unnamulai, the ever-new goddess of Arunai, who in great infatuation hid his form and followed a hunter girl through the forest.
nuance: The churning of the sea is told in full only to explain a simile: the women's eyes are that poison. அருந்துணாமுலை (உண்ணாமுலை) is the name of the Goddess at Thiruvannamalai; the song names her as Murugan's mother. அடவியில் வடிவு கரந்து போய் ஒரு குறமகள் பிறகு திரிந்த காமுக: the god himself is called the lover (காமுக) who trailed the hunter girl, a playful answer to the poet's own desire.

reading: The poet asks that, before Yama with charred form and fiery eyes comes for his life while his wife and fine sons stand weeping and telling their griefs, Murugan look on him so that through knowledge his troubles leave and he can think of the two feet. The praise names the vel that cut the shoulders of Sura, at whose coming Vishnu, Brahma and the eight directions trembled, and Arunai of Siva, who for the Vedic priests, the gods and his devotees gave a share of himself to the Lady who practised dharma.
nuance: அறம் மேவும் அரிவையும் ஒருபங்கு இடமுடையவர்: Siva sharing his body with the Lady who practised dharma, perhaps pointing to Arunai's story that Uma there gained half of Siva; the song does not tell it. The meaning of the opening (இரவியும் மதியும் தெரிவுற எழும் அம்புவி தனில் இனம் ஒன்றிடு மாது) is uncertain.

reading: The poet pictures Yama coming by fate's way with cunning, crushing trouble and cruel disease, eyes like hot fire, raging that today is the day to take the life, while women and kin, their hearts surging, pour tears; before that tumult comes, he asks for the nature to worship the feet that remove the deeds of the line. The praise names Vishnu on the serpent and Brahma of the old Vedas, and Siva who drank the poison to end the gods' fear, rides the bull, wears the snake, moon and Ganga in his hair and fire in his hand, and shares himself with the Lady, at whose Arunai Murugan dwells.
nuance: விதி வழி வந்திடு போதில்: Death comes along fate's path. குல வினை களையும் கழல், feet that clear the deeds of the line, may mean inherited karma or the deeds that make up birth. The praise is entirely of Siva; Murugan appears only in the closing பெருமாளே.

reading: A lament for a lovesick girl, in the voice of one who watches her: should the girl, her bangles slipping in her infatuation, suffer on her lone flower bed, harried by the moon rising from the sea of sharks and makaras, by the small south breeze that comes like fire through the street where two-faced women live, and by the arrows of the bodiless god? The praise names the vel that scattered the asuras' crowns, the chest wedded to the hunter girl, the lord on the peacock at Arunai, and the master of Hari, Hara and Brahma whom the Vedas declare.
nuance: சரிவளை கழல, bangles slipping, is the classical sign of wasting in love. இருவினை மகளிர் மருவிய தெருவு, the street where women of double dealing live, seems to be the gossips of the town; the phrase could instead name courtesans.

reading: The poet asks whether, melting under women of elephant gait, by ruinous deeds that bring distress, never thinking of salvation, not knowing praise and sunk in ruinous pleasure, he must wear himself out in the world with this body of flesh and blame; he asks to enter the shade of the tree that is Murugan's feet, a raft of lotus. The praise names him the one who imprisoned Brahma, nephew of Vishnu, Murugan of Tripurai, in whom the burner of the cities delights, the vel that split the demons' hill, at Arunai, famous shrine, by the north side of its long wall.
nuance: சததள மலர்வார் புணை நின கழல் ஆர் தருநிழல்: the feet are both a raft and the shade of a tree, two images of refuge in one line (as in 377). வடசார், the north side of the wall, may place this song at a shrine within the temple.

reading: The poet asks not to droop clinging in desire to those who twist the good, not to perish crushed beneath mighty Death's foot, and not to be born into the sea of misery by cultivating friendship with the wicked, but to be given the holy feet and told the teaching of the arts. The praise names Murugan who dwells in the minds of those who think of him once and say his name twice, the victor who hid the hunter girl's honey on his chest and ran off, and the vel that fought proud Sura, at the holy tower on the red hill.
nuance: கருக்காரர் நட்பை பெருக்கு ஆசரித்து, cultivating the friendship of wicked men, adds bad company to women and death. ஒருக்கால் நினைத்திட்டு இருக்கால் மிகுத்திட்டு உரைப்பார்: devotion asks little, one thought and two utterances. ஒளித்தோடும், running away in hiding with Valli, is the eloping lover. The opening phrase அருக்கு ஆர் நலத்தைத் திரிப்பார் is hard to construe.

reading: The poet traces a life spent leaning on the breasts of carp-eyed women never parted from Kama, until strength fails, the body bends, he walks coughing, speech goes, feeling ends and the life grows faint, and asks for Murugan's two feet so that he does not enter fire-mouthed hell. The praise names the vel that ground the great hill to dust, the twelve golden shoulders that melted for the hunter girl, the one dear to Hara whom Vishnu and Brahma could not discern with their eyes, at the holy street of Arunapuri among rich fields.
nuance: The plea runs as one life, lust then decay (இருமா நடைபுக்கு, walking with a cough) then hell. திருமால் கமலப் பிரமா விழியின் தெரியா அரன், Hara whom Vishnu and lotus Brahma could not see, is the story of the column of fire that Thiruvannamalai claims as its own.

reading: The poet, crying 'come, come', worshipping, melting and losing himself in the sea of love, seeks the seal of silence that the great sinners of the noisy sects cannot know, and asks whether, without gaining the flawless true reality of jnana, he must fall into the whirlpool of the sea of birth, a mere bubble. The praise names Murugan the child of the six who drank their breasts on the bank of the old Ganga, the skilled one on the peacock at the red hill, whose vel made the fish-filled sea and the Vedas alike cry 'ko ko'.
nuance: மோன முத்திரை, the seal of silence, is set against the கோலாகலச் சமயம், the uproar of the sects, as in 369. புற்புதமாய பிறவி வாராகரச் சுழி: birth is a bubble in a whirlpool of the sea. The opening line has a garbled word (தொழுத்மு டூடு).

reading: The poet speaks of women with heavy breasts and flowered hair who hide in their garments, talk and laugh, bewitch anyone for the love of wealth, send messengers by hand and snatch a man's money, and asks for Murugan's feet of light for himself, who burns on the way to the seven hells through their tricks. The praise sounds the drums of the battle in which Sura was slain, names Murugan son of the one who dances with a raised foot, the vel that melted at the hunter girl's breasts, and the lord gracious to both the peacock of the field and the gods' true daughter at Arunai's tower.
nuance: ஆசை பொருட்டு, for the desire of wealth, and கைத் தூதுவிடுத்தே பொருளைப் பறி, sending go-betweens and snatching money, name the trade. சோதி ஒளிப் பாதம், feet of light, may glance at the hill of fire. The opening simile (ஆனை வரிக் கோடு) is unclear.

reading: In the voice of a lovesick woman alone on her flower bed: tormented by Kama's cruel arrows and the small breeze of the end, by the great moon that bears the hare and sets her body on fire, and by the sea that sends its waves to the shore, she asks whether it is fitting that her life droop, and whether her grief will not end. The praise names the vel thrown at Sura on golden Meru, the hero who came to the millet field to delight the hunter girl, dwelling in Arunai's street among screwpine-hedged fields, king of the unblinking gods.
nuance: The torments are the classical three of akam night, the wind, the moon and the sea, each given its own line ending in -ஆலே. இறுதிச் சிறுகால், the small wind of the end, makes the breeze a herald of death. The closing அவனித் திருமாதொடு சிவனுக்கு is hard to construe.

reading: A short lament for a lovesick girl, spoken for her: by the moon, the king of cold, that strikes fire, by the young north wind and the town that reproaches her, and by the arrows Kama takes up for war, the lone doe's life faints; grant her a word of grace. The praise names Kumara, Muruga, guru of the matted-haired Siva, the chest that quenches the hunter girl's desire, the giver of Amaravati back to the gods, standing in the street of Arunapuri.
nuance: இளவாடையும் ஊரும் ஒறுக்கும்: the north wind and the town punish her together, gossip set beside the weather. தனிமான், the lone doe, is the girl spoken of in third person, so the voice is a mother or friend.

title: திருவருணை
theme: Songs at Thiruvannamalai (திருவருணை, 3 of 6): the poet confesses embraces bought from courtesans whose love lasts as long as the money, the body's foulness and the ruin of old age, and asks for Murugan's feet; two songs speak for a girl sick with love; the praise centres on the tower and hill of Arunai, Murugan as Siva's guru, and stories of Siva for his devotees.
structure_note: Courtesan and lovemaking songs (398, 403, 407, 408, 410, 412), of which 403 vows not to forget the feet even in the embrace; the body as a foul vessel (402); a yogic plea (405); short prayers for grace and steadiness (399, 400, 401); love-laments in a girl's voice or about her (404, 406, 411); and 409, praise alone.
source_issues: Song 398: line 12 begins with four dots (....) instead of six; harmless.
Song 411: நாடோ ர்கள் (line 6) has a stray space inside the vowel sign; read நாடோர்கள்.
Song 412: நிறா யுற்றிட (line 25) has lost a vowel sign; probably நீறாயுற்றிட ('turned to ash').

tamil: இரத சுரதமுலை களுமார்பு குத்த நுதல்வேர் வரும்ப
அமுத நிலையில்விர லுகிரேகை தைக்க மணிபோல் விளங்க
இசலி யிசலியுப ரிதலீலை யுற்று இடைநூல் நுடங்க
இருவ ருடலுமொரு வுருவாய் நயக்க முகமே லழுந்த
அளக மவிழவளை களுமேக லிக்க நயனார விந்த
லகரி பெருகஅத ரமுமே யருத்தி முறையே யருந்த
புருவ நிமிரஇரு கணவாள் நிமைக்க வுபசார மிஞ்ச
அவச கவசமள வியலே தரிக்க அதிலே யநந்த
புதுமை விளையஅது பரமா பரிக்க இணைதோளு மொன்றி
புளக முதிரவிர கமென்வாரி தத்த வரைநாண் மழுங்க
மனமு மனமுமுரு கியெயா தரிக்க வுயிர்போ லுகந்து
பொருள தளவுமரு வுறுமாய வித்தை விலைமாதர் சிங்கி
பரவு மகரமுக ரமுமேவ லுற்ற சகரால் விளைந்த
தமர திமிரபிர பலமோக ரத்ந சலராசி கொண்ட
படியை முழுதுமொரு நொடியே மதித்து வலமாக வந்து
பழநி மிசையிலிசை யிசையே ரகத்தில் திருவா வினன்கு
டியினில் பிரமபுர மதில்வாழ் திருத்த ணிகையூடு மண்டர்
பதிய முதியகதி யதுநா யெனுக்கு முறவாகி நின்று
அரியு மயனுமம ரருமாய சிட்ட பரிபால னன்ப
ரடையு மிடரைமுடு கியெநூற துட்ட கொலைகார ரென்ற
அசுரர் படையையடை யவும்வே ரறுத்த அபிராம செந்தி
அருண கிரணகரு ணையபூர ணச்ச ரணமே லெழுந்த
இரண கரணமுர ணுறுசூர னுட்க மயிலேறு கந்த
அருணை யிறையவர்பெ ரியகோபு ரத்தில் வடபா லமர்ந்த
reading: The poet describes at length the act of love with women who sell themselves, two bodies becoming one form, hair loosened, bangles jingling, lips drunk, until mind melts into mind, and names them women of magic arts who cling only as far as the money goes; he asks for grace to be let go from them. The praise tells how Murugan circled the whole sea-girt earth in an instant and came to sit at Siva's side, names Palani, Swamimalai (ஏரகம்), Thiruvavinankudi, Brahmapuram and Thiruttani, calls him the one who became kin to the poet, a dog, and made poems, and ends at the north side of Arunai's great tower.
nuance: பொருளது அளவும் மருவுறு மாய வித்தை விலைமாதர்: the embrace lasts as far as the money does, which is why the long love scene ends in a plea for release. படியை முழுதும் ஒரு நொடியே மதித்து வலமாக வந்து சிவனிடத்து அமர் சேயே: circling the earth in a moment and sitting by Siva has the details of the contest for the fruit, though no fruit is named. நாயெனுக்கும் உறவாகி நின்று கவிதையைப் புனைவோனே may refer to the poet's own call to sing; the split of these words is unsure.

reading: The poet, who speaks the threefold Tamil of verse and song night and day, asks Murugan to give him clearly a settled firmness and his holy grace. The praise names him the great life of supreme compassion, the knower of the truth of Parasiva, and the good son born of Hara's grace, at Arunagiri.
nuance: திரம் அதனைத் தெளிவாக: what is asked is steadiness, not release or vision; the poet already sings, and wants the singing to stand firm.

reading: The poet seems to say that amid the praises of sages, Brahma, Vishnu, the gods and the devotees, his lone servant's cry goes unheard, and asks whether anyone will speak kindly for him; he wonders what the dust of Murugan's feet and his store of grace are. The praise names him the supreme guru who moves in the atom, who has the elements from wind onward for his army, who is all forms and the ancient form, who threw the vel on darkness when Vishnu and Brahma cried for refuge, and the one at Arunagiri who powders his servant's cruel disease.
nuance: அணுவில் அசைவாய், சகல வடிவாய், பழைய வடிவாகிய: Murugan as the mover within the atom and as every form is the doctrine of pervasion, unusual in so short a song. The opening (இருவர் மயலோ அமளி விதமோ) may instead describe love's confusion; how its words split is unsure.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to come quickly before him on the peacock, face blossoming and pouring grace, dancing, while the two deeds take fright, the kinds of impurity and the dark disease fade, bees hum at the kadamba and the gods shower flowers calling him the elephant-faced one's younger brother. The praise names Siva, who burned the three cities and Kama's body with a smile, rides the bull and dances in the open space of Sivam with the queen at his side, as the one whom Murugan delighted as guru, and ends with the bed of the hunter girl at Arunai.
nuance: The plea is for the sight of Murugan arriving, and the release from deeds and malas is the effect of that sight, not something earned first. சிவம் வெளி அங்கண் ... நடம் செய்து: Siva's dance is placed in the space that is Sivam.

tamil: இருவினை யூண்ப சும்பை கருவிளை கூன்கு டம்பை
இடைதிரி சோங்கு கந்த மதுவது தேங்கு கும்ப
குருவியல் பாண்ட மஞ்சு மருவிய கூண்டு நெஞ்சொ
றுலகுட னேன்று கொண்ட கருமபி ராந்தொ ழிந்து
அருணையி லோங்கு துங்க சிகரக ராம்பு யங்க
அடியவர் பாங்க பண்டு புகலகி லாண்ட முண்ட
கருணைம்ரு கேந்த்ர அன்ப ருடனுர கேந்த்ரர் கண்ட
கலபக கேந்த்ர தந்த்ர அரசநி சேந்த்ர கந்த
reading: The poet names the body a fresh bag fed by the two deeds, a bent nest grown in the womb, a ruined hollow of trouble, a pot where stench and liquor pool, a corpse that sleeps at night, a vessel shaped for pain and a hut that heart and life move out of; and asks whether, giving up the delusion he shared with the world that it will not perish, he will reach Murugan's two lotus feet. The praise names Arunai, where the gods crowd to worship, Vishnu of the Sarnga bow who swallowed the worlds as uncle, Murugan as son of the lord of dance whom the serpent king and another devotee beheld, and the lord of Indra with the vajra.
nuance: The confession is a chain of names for the body, each a container (பை, குடம்பை, பொதும்பு, கும்பம், பாண்டம், கூண்டு, குரம்பை), so the point is that what the world takes as lasting is a vessel to be left. உரகேந்த்ரர் கண்ட கடவுள் நடேந்த்ரர் probably means Nataraja as seen by Patanjali, the serpent king; the other devotee (ம்ருகேந்த்ர அன்பர்) may be Vyaghrapada, but the epithets are hard to divide.

tamil: இளகஇடை துவளவளை பூச லிட்டி ரங்க ...... எவராலும்
இதழமுது பருகியுயிர் தேக மொத்தி ருந்து ...... முனிவாறி
மொழிபதற வசமழிய ஆசை யிற்க விழ்ந்து ...... விடுபோதும்
முநிவர்சுரர் தொழுதுருகு பாத பத்ம மென்று ...... மறவேனே
உலகறிய இவனடிமை யாமெ னக்கொ ணர்ந்து ...... சபையூடே
உதறிமுறை யிடுபழைய வேத வித்தர் தந்த ...... சிறியோனே
அமரரொடு பலர்முடுகி ஆழி யைக்க டைந்து ...... அமுதாக
அருணகிரி நகரிலெழு கோபு ரத்த மர்ந்த ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet describes the act of love, hair loosened, sweat like pearls on the face, eyes rolling, garments slipping, lips drunk, until speech fails and the self is lost in desire, and says that even then he will never forget the lotus feet that sages and gods worship, melting. The praise names Murugan the child given by the old knower of the Veda who came in an old man's form to a young man's wedding, pushed in at the gate, claimed him before the assembly as his slave, and stood shaking and protesting when the youth tore the old palm-leaf deed; it also names Vishnu who churned the sea for nectar, the cock on the banner, and the tower of Arunagiri.
nuance: The plea is not to escape the embrace but to keep the feet in mind within it (விடுபோதும் ... பாதபத்மம் என்றும் மறவேனே), a different stance from the songs that ask for release from women. The story in the praise has the unmistakable details of Siva claiming Sundarar as his bondsman at his wedding, with the slave deed (ஆவணம்) torn before the assembly; that the god of the story is the giver of Murugan makes Siva himself the claimant of a servant.

reading: In a girl's own voice: the pearls on her breasts and the moon that spits fire, the flute's music that comes like the sun to take her life, the sea's waves and Kama's cruel arrows torment her, and she asks Murugan to come in time to the hill at Arunai with its gem-strewn groves so that she does not perish. The praise names him the guru of Siva who burned the three cities with a smile, the hero on the emerald peacock who powdered the asuras, the chest marked by the hunter girl's breasts, and the one who sent the vel to the seven seas.
nuance: Akam love poetry in the first person (எனது உயிர், எளியெனும்), not the poet's confession. The torments are the classical ones of evening: moon, flute and sea.

reading: The poet asks whether, instead of raising the body's fire like a forge to strike the moon so that nectar melts and flows and he reaches the supreme bliss longing for Murugan's feet, he will wander ashamed like a thief, caught in the net of infatuation with women of bow brows and pearl smiles. The praise names the vel let fly from the golden peacock to drums, the one who was death to the race of the wicked Jains, the one dwelling on the hill of Arunai in the sea-girt land, and the one who cut down the asuras, freed the gods and set up their rule.
nuance: உலையில் அனல் ஒத்து ... உடுபதியை முட்டி அமுது ஊறல் உருகி வர: the inner fire raised to the moon so that its nectar flows is the yoga of the Tirumanthiram, set here against the women. கதவு அமணர் உற்ற குலகாலா again makes Murugan the Sambandar who destroyed the Jains.

reading: A voice, perhaps the girl's mother or friend, asks whether the vanji-creeper girl of field-rich Arunai should suffer from the moon rising over the sea's waves, the evening and the talk of the gossiping women, and the south wind that scorns even the undersea fire. The praise names Murugan the hero whom Siva, who married Uma at his left, worships, the vel that split the seven hills, the lord who routed the asuras, and the master of Vishnu, Brahma and Indra.
nuance: The speaker is not named; வஞ்சி போதநலங்கலாமோ speaks of the girl in the third person. மலந்தைமார் sounds like the blaming women of akam poetry; the word is unusual.

reading: The poet paints a woman from lotus face, crescent brow and carp eyes to pearl teeth, areca neck, breasts like pots, creeper waist and peacock gait, and asks whether he should be kin to those who coax a man and snatch his wealth. The praise is a battle in drum syllables, the vel that feeds the demons on the asuras' flesh, and Murugan who went to the millet field and embraced the hunter girl in stealthy love, at Arunagiri.
nuance: குனகி பொருள் பறிபவர்: the whole catalogue of beauty ends in two words, coaxing and robbing, so the portrait is a lure. The praise closes on Murugan's own களவு with Valli, stealth in a good sense against the women's theft.
