reading: The poet describes women who talk with milk-sweet words, play at pleasure, are skilled in schemes and wind in money with their tricks, and will not call a man back unless he pays what they name, and asks that, rather than enjoying them, falling into evil and great hell and becoming a corpse, he grasp Murugan's feet and speak his praise. The praise names Vishnu who cut Ravana's ten heads as his uncle, the vel that killed Surapadman's clan, the battlefield where vultures and ghouls tear corpses, and Murugan on the peacock at Perumpatrappuliyur, where jnanis seek his anklet feet.
nuance: பலஞ் செப்பித் தர மீள அழையாதவர்: they call a man back only if he pays the sum they name. The plea sets two ends side by side: becoming a corpse in hell (நரகடைந்திட்டுச் சவமாகி) or holding the feet and speaking praise.

reading: The poet imagines the day his life departs: held captive by the buffalo-rider Death, the pleasures desired through women's eyes and the wisdom and honour he spoke of all become mere water and empty space, his body lies as food for the pyre, kin wail and carry it to the burning ground; he asks that before then Murugan grant whichever of two gains is fitting, the goal won by dying in the mind, or understanding won by living on. The praise tells of Rama, who shook the seven sal trees, killed Vali, saw Lanka burned and cut down Ravana's crowns, as Murugan's uncle, and hails Murugan as the one poet for the world, the crest-jewel of the Saiva Veda and lord of its hymns, at Perumpatrappuliyur.
nuance: மனதாலே இறந்திட்டுப் பெறவே கதியாயினும் இருந்திட்டுப் பெறவே மதியாயினும்: the poet leaves to the Lord the choice between dying to the world in mind and living on to gain understanding. ப்ரபஞ்சத்துக்கொரு பாவலனார் ... சிவ வேத சிகாமணி ப்ரபந்தத்துக்கொரு நாத: the titles fit Sambandar, the Thevaram poet, so Murugan seems identified with him.

reading: The poet describes women with swinging earrings, conch-white smiles, cloud hair, carp-arrow eyes and cuckoo voices, snatchers of gold who come with tricks, talk with betel-red mouths, name their wage and then sport on the bed, and asks Murugan to end his act of handing his goods to them. The praise names Siva who took Death's life, burned the three cities and Kama's body, felled Daksha, the sun and moon, and dances in the hall, and Murugan as that Siva's guru, the vel against Surapadman, and Valli, at Puliyur.
nuance: சம்பளம் ஈது என ஓதி: the women state their wage, love priced as hired work. தன் குருநாதா: Murugan is the guru of the very Siva whose deeds the praise lists. மூளியர் may mean women stripped of ornaments, or be abuse.

reading: The poet names women as cheats in every way, by smile, betel mouth, shamelessness, eyes, sore-ridden thighs, gait, breasts, speech, hair and song, who gather and dance through the streets, and asks that Murugan, by his own act, give the anklet of wondrous wisdom to him, a dog who wanders with them. The praise shows the vel that broke the hill and the serpent's hoods, Murugan as the teacher who lovingly taught the truth to Siva, partner of Sivakami, giving his servant the sea of the bliss of wisdom, and his secret love for Valli, at Puliyur.
nuance: எத்திகள், cheats, ends every phrase of the first half, a rhetorical list like 470's. சத்துப தேசிக்குங் குரவோனே: Murugan as Siva's teacher of the Real. உன் செயலால்: the wisdom is to come by the Lord's act, not the poet's effort.

reading: The poet says his births are more than the sands of the seven seas if counted, that now his life and body are Murugan's charge and he can no longer leave a body, that vultures, jackals, fire, earth, Yama and Brahma are all worn out with him, and that protection is Murugan's duty and this servant is his servant, so let him quickly give his feet. The praise names Uma, emerald-formed and pure, as Murugan's mother, the peacock that shakes the mountains, the vel that feeds on asura lives, and the dance at Puliyur praised by gods and sages.
nuance: கழுகொடு நரியும் எரி புவி மறலி கமலனும் மிகவும் அயர்வானார்: those who receive each body (vultures and jackals, fire and earth), the god who takes it (Yama) and the god who makes the next (Brahma) are all exhausted by his countless births, a wry turn. கடன் உனது அபயம்: refuge is the Lord's debt. இனியுடல் விடுக முடியாது may also mean he cannot bear to give up a body again.

title: சிதம்பரம்
theme: Songs at Chidambaram (புலியூர்): the poet confesses his fall to courtesans who sell themselves, the pomp of wealth that vanishes in a moment, the life that runs from the womb to Death, and the confusion of the Vedas and sects; he asks for the reality beyond form and the formless, for the lamp of knowledge rather than an ascetic's outward marks, and for the yogic ascent to the dancing Lord's hall.
structure_note: Most songs follow the two halves and end at Puliyur. The confessions are of women (495, 498, 500, 501, 503, 504, 507), of pomp (499), of the life cycle (508) and of birth (505). 496 and 506 are yogic pleas, 497 sets inner knowledge against outward austerity, and 502 is a call for Murugan to come. The praise draws on the Chidambaram dance: the serpent sage and the tiger-footed sage who watch it (501, 502).
source_issues: Song 495: one corrupt character in இணைசொல்க்஡ண (line 9); probably க்ரீவ (neck), compared with the conch.
Song 498: one corrupt character in று஡ங்கமிலார் (line 8); probably றூங்கமிலார், but the word is unclear.
Song 503: one corrupt character in வாயிதழினு஡றல் (line 7); clearly ஊறல்.
Song 504: one corrupt character in அச்சுத஡ணன (line 23); the sense (perhaps அச்சுதன் ஈன்ற, 'born of Achyuta') is unclear.
Song 506: one corrupt character in இந்துவினு஡டுற (line 3); clearly இந்துவினூடுற.
Song 499: the words விருமஞ்சித் திரமமா (line 10) do not split into clear words and may be corrupt.

reading: The poet asks to be spared the trouble of being carried off by merciless Death with his twisted rope swung at the head, and the turmoil of reciting Vedas and many shastras while the six sects quarrel one after another; he asks for the reality that has form, beyond the formless and the formed. The praise names Murugan nephew of Hari, the treasure of Parvati, Kumaresa of Puliyur where the god who wears river, moon, konrai and serpent dances, who fought the Nirudar to powder in the sea, and who never even in dreams knows anger toward those who bow at his feet.
nuance: அறுவகை சமயம் முறைமுறை சருவி, the six sects quarrelling in turn, sits beside Death's rope as a second torment: the plea is for one true object (வடிவுள பொருள்) beyond அருவுரு. The line அலைபடு தநல்முச் சினையாகும் does not split cleanly and may be corrupt.

reading: The poet describes a courtesan from lips, smile, eyes, hair and brows down to breasts, navel, waist, thighs and feet, then frankly the lovemaking on the couch with sweating faces and bird-like cries, and asks Murugan to give him another thought and rule him, since he has lost all self-control. The praise is a long battle with drums and rivers of blood, the vel thrown at the northern mountain, the gods and Vidyadharas singing and apsaras dancing, Puliyur as a golden land of groves, tanks and birds, and Murugan's union with Valli and Devayanai.
nuance: The plea is one phrase at the end of the confession: வசமெலாம் விட்டு மறவே, having let go of all control, வேறு சிந்தனையைத் தந்து ஆள்வாய், give me a different thought. The head-to-foot catalogue is the stock form of these songs, here carried to its greatest length. One word is corrupt (see source_issues).

reading: A yogic plea: the poet asks to reach the golden place that neither darkness nor the sun's ray can touch, where his two ills burn, impurity leaves, the light at the root shines and nectar flows like a stream, so that Murugan's grace becomes his whole measure and Siva rejoices; and he asks for the feet. The praise names Siva as the supreme teacher who has no teacher, with moon and coral body, and Murugan as his son, who said of the poet 'this dog is my servant' and gave him true knowledge, at Puliyur, lover of the hunter girl.
nuance: The ascent is told in the language of Tirumular's yoga: மூலக ஒளி, the light at the base, and அமுதம் welling as an அருவி. இருநோய், the two diseases, is most likely the two kinds of deed (இருவினை); that is a guess. மருவி நாயெனை அடிமையாம் என is the book's formula of being taken into service.

reading: The poet asks not to wander the whole earth wearing ochre, growing matted hair, entering forests, living on raw fruit and punishing the body, but to be given Murugan's cool lotus feet so that he may see the lamp of supreme knowledge that dawns when the self and the elements subside. The praise names the fierce hero who ruined the sinful Daruka clan, the vel whose ghouls clap and sing, and the peacock dancing, at Puliyur among groves and bending paddy.
nuance: சீவ னொடுக்கம் பூத வொடுக்கம், the stilling of the self and of the elements, is what the outward marks of the ascetic fail to bring. The song does not condemn ascetics; it says this is not the path the poet asks for.

reading: The poet describes courtesans who comb flowers into their hair, sing like cuckoos, act coy, gather asking 'will money come?', run through the streets in deceit, and join with many at once to some men's ruin, and asks whether such company is fitting. The praise names the vel that struck the Suras, Murugan who knocked the Veda-maker on the head with his kanthal hand, the son of Uma who sits beside the one who burned Kama and wears the tiger skin, and Valli as the deer whose grace kindles the yogic fire at the root and the nada, at Puliyur, the land of Siva-knowledge.
nuance: பொருள் வருமோ, 'will money come?', and விலைமாதர் mark these as courtesans. The praise gives Valli a yogic role unusual in the book: she grants grace so that the light at the root (சுடர் மூலத்தோன்) is kindled and the life joins the breath in the nadi; the syntax is not certain. One word is corrupt.

reading: The poet describes the pomp of wealth: a palanquin under champak umbrellas, servants, silk, drums, veena and conch, armies and music, and says that this false show vanishes in a moment; instead of wandering in it he asks for the feet that are hard even for the gods to reach. The praise turns the Asura host to dust with the vel amid drum syllables and roaring seas, names Murugan son of Uma, whom Hara, Hari and Brahma cannot reach, and his union with the deer's daughter, at Puliyur.
nuance: இது நொடி மறையும் பொய்ப் பவுஷு, this false pomp that vanishes in a moment, is the whole argument. The song is unusual in confessing not women but status. The words விருமஞ்சித் திரமமா do not split clearly.

reading: The poet, calling himself the lowest dog, describes a woman's neck, eyes, brows, perfumes, breasts, waist and anklets and his union with her, and asks instead to win praise by bowing at Murugan's anklets, wearing holy ash and bathing in the waters of bliss like ascetics, worshipping his feet today. The praise is a battle in drum syllables, Murugan as guru to the consort of Gauri who dances, the gods showering flowers crying 'Kanda', and his union with the gypsy girl, at Puliyur where the golden dance is held.
nuance: The plea sets one bodily practice against another: ஒண்பொடி அணிந்து, wearing the bright ash, and ஆநந்தம் புனல் படிந்து, bathing in bliss, against the perfumed body of the confession. கவுரிபங்கன் குருவெனும் makes Murugan Siva's teacher. The rhythm packs the words tightly and several splits are uncertain.

reading: The poet tells how he smelled women's perfumed hair, lay on their breasts and lived proudly in pleasure, drawn to them like a needle to a magnet, and asks whether a day will come when grace fills him and, knowing without reasoning, he wears Murugan's faultless lotus feet. The praise names Siva, whom Vishnu and Brahma could not know, dancing before the serpent sage and the tiger-footed sage, wearing the half moon in his matted hair in the golden city, and Murugan as his treasure, at Puliyur with its golden walls.
nuance: காந்தமொடு ஊசி, needle and lodestone, is the image of compulsion. பாம்புருவான முநி and புலியான பதன் are Patanjali and Vyaghrapada, the two sages for whom Siva danced at Chidambaram; the song names them by their marks, not their names.

reading: The poet calls Murugan to come with his six faces shining from the mountain of ancient knowledge, his lips speaking the Veda, his anklets ringing, mounted on the peacock with the vel, so that the poet's two deeds turn to ash and the gods sing of the wonder. The praise names Siva who swallowed the poison when the gods fled, Murugan as the guru who gave him direct experience (அநுபூதி), the embracer of the hunter girl who drives off troubles and disease, praised by the tiger-footed sage, the serpent sage and countless rishis.
nuance: அடியன் இருவினை நீறுபட, that the servant's two deeds become ash, is the only plea; the rest is a vision of Murugan's coming. குருநாதன் மிகமகிழ அநுபூதி அருள்வோனே again makes Murugan the teacher of Siva.

reading: The poet describes courtesans who talk like parrots, invite a man with 'the house is free now, come', lead him to the bed, perfume him, and make love to him frankly described; when both have drowned in infatuation they pawn his ornaments and plunder his wealth, and he asks whether such lovemaking is right. The praise is a long litany of the Goddess as Shakti, Kalyani, Abhirami, Sivakami and Uma who dances with the Supreme, and of Murugan who rode the peacock, threw the Shakti and freed the gods, Valli's husband, who dwells in the minds of those who chant his name, Subramanya at Puliyur.
nuance: ஆபரணம் வைத்து அடகு தேடு பொருள் சூறைகொளுவார்: the women pawn his jewels and loot his goods once infatuation has taken him, the courtesan's stock charge. The Goddess is called எனை ஈண மலைமாது, the mountain daughter who bore me. One word is corrupt.

reading: The poet describes saleswomen who dance like peacocks with swinging breasts and parrot voices, and asks whether he must wander, quarrelling and making love with such harlots, until he coughs, vomits and hiccups like a mangy dog while people say 'chi chi'. The praise sets the vel against the Asuras amid drum syllables, names Murugan son of Sivakami and of the Lord who kicked Death, and his union with the deer born of Achyuta, who burned the southern demons' island, at Puliyur.
nuance: The confession runs straight from the women to disease and disgust (சிச்சி சிச்சி என நால்வர் கூறிட), with no interval. The phrase about Achyuta is corrupt; the sense that Valli is Vishnu's daughter is a guess from tradition.

reading: The poet, a dog lamenting 'will birth never end?', asks that if it is his deeds that keep his mind from reaching the holy hall, Murugan come in grace as he stands crying with a dry mouth, end the anxiety of his mind, and appear before him as he comes worshipping. The praise names Uma who sits on the skin seat, Murugan as the nectar friend of those who praise him, wearer of kadamba, husband of Valli the form of knowledge, the treasure of Puliyur, who raised up the gods.
nuance: திருச்சபை is the hall of the dance at Chidambaram: the poet's goal is to reach it in mind. வாய்பாறி நிற்கும், standing with mouth dried from crying, is the posture of the plea.

tamil: நாலுசது ரத்த பஞ்சறை மூலகம லத்தி லங்கியை
நாரண புரத்தி லிந்துவி னு஡டுற இணக்கி நன்சுடர்
கோலமு முதிப்ப கண்டுள நாலினை மறித்தி தம்பெறு
கூடிய முகப்பி லிந்திர வானவமு தத்தை யுண்டொரு
ஆலமல ருற்ற சம்பவி வேரிலி குலக்கொ ழுந்திலி
ஆணவ மயக்க முங்கலி காமிய மகற்றி யென்றனை
வேலதை யெடுத்து மிந்திரர் மால்விதி பிழைக்க வஞ்சகர்
வேசது ரத்தர் தென்புலி யூருறை யொருத்தி பங்கினர்
reading: A yogic plea: the poet asks when, from the fire in the four-cornered root lotus, through the nadis and mantras, past the moon and the six junctions, with the conch-like sound of bindu and nada at the front, he will drink the gods' nectar and reach the hall of the countless dances. The praise names the Goddess who removed his delusion of anava, kali and desire and ruled him, Murugan as her son, the vel that burned the deceivers' homes and drank the eight seas, and Siva who dances at south Puliyur.
nuance: நாலுசதுரத்த ... மூலகமலம் is the four-sided base lotus (muladhara) of the yogic body, and விந்துநாதம் the bindu and nada of Tirumular's teaching; the goal is the dance hall (சபை), set inside the body. ஆணவ மயக்கம் names the root impurity. The ascent's stages are not clear to me, and one word is corrupt.

reading: The poet describes women with dark hair, pearl-adorned lips, moon foreheads and carp eyes and asks whether he must wander daily at their command; he asks for release, so that his mind may hold to Murugan's feet with true knowledge. The praise names Uma at length and Murugan as the one who told the meaning of the light to Siva with the trident and fiery body, and his union with the deer of the three Tamils, at Puliyur.
nuance: சோதிப்பொருள் கேள்விக்கிடு முருகோனே, Murugan who gave Siva the meaning of the light to hear, is the story of the teaching of Siva; Om is not named. கட்டளையாக, at their command, makes the women masters and the poet a servant.

reading: The poet traces life from a drop like dew, ten months upside down in the womb, birth, crawling and toddling, to falling into the pit of women and leaving the body unawares when cunning Death comes, and asks whether this weakening sorrow of illusion will never end. The praise names the vel that powdered the mountain of illusion and dried the sea, Murugan as the guru who knocked Brahma's four heads, and husband of the lady who enters the minds of those who think of him, the fullness of Puliyur.
nuance: The whole life is told in eight short lines, and the only adult act is falling into women (மாதர்க் குழி விழுவார்) before Death arrives. மாயத்துயர், the sorrow of illusion, names the whole cycle.

title: சிதம்பரம்
theme: The last songs at Chidambaram (புலியூர்): courtesans who take a man's wealth, the body as a pot of filth for dogs and flies, and the slide from lust to old age, death and the burning ground; against these the poet asks for teaching in the meaning of Siva's emblems, for release, for the yogic ascent through the letters of the five-syllable mantra, and he speaks to his own mind.
structure_note: 509, 512, 514 and 516 confess women; 510 and 512 dwell on the body's foulness and end; 511 is a yogic plea; 513 is addressed to the poet's mind; 515 is a litany with no plea. 516 ends at Kunruthoradal, not at Chidambaram.
source_issues: Song 509: one corrupt character in லு஡ட்டியும் (line 3); clearly ஊட்டியும்.
Song 515: one corrupt character in கருவுதனிலு஡று (line 13); clearly ஊறு.
Song 516: filed under சிதம்பரம் but ends at குன்றுதோறாடல் and names nothing of Chidambaram; the heading may be wrong.

reading: The poet asks not to be confused by courtesans who cast nets with their earrings, garlanded hair and lip-nectar, nor by their songs, their scheming life, youth and lust for gold; he asks for the day when he will be taught what Siva's emblems mean: the skull-bowl, the holy ash, the konrai in the matted hair, the axe and the deer, and the primal origin. The praise identifies Murugan with the sage who with the sword of knowledge defeated the hair-plucking Jains and sang the Veda as songs, and names the dance shown in turn to the serpent-form sage and the tiger sage of Puliyur, amid drum syllables, ghouls and Kali's host.
nuance: The plea is unusual: not for the feet but for உபதேசம், teaching on what Siva's ornaments signify (இவையிவை என). தலைபறி அமணர், the Jains who pluck their hair, and the sage who changed their community points to Sambandar, with whom the book identifies Murugan. அரிதுயில் சயன வியாளமூர்த்தன், the serpent on which Hari sleeps, is Patanjali as Adisesha. One word is corrupt.

tamil: மச்ச மெச்சு சூத்ரம் ரத்த பித்த மூத்ரம்
மட்க விட்ட சேக்கை உட்பு ழுத்த வாழ்க்கை
எய்ச்சி ளைச்ச பேய்க்கு மெய்ச்சி ளைச்ச நாய்க்கு
இக்க டத்தை நீக்கி அக்க டத்து ளாக்கி
பொய்ச்சி னத்தை மாற்றி மெய்ச்சி னத்தை யேற்றி
பொக்க ணத்து நீற்றை யிட்டொ ருத்த னார்க்கு
பச்சி லைக்கும் வாய்க்கு ளெச்சி லுக்கும் வீக்கு
பத்தி சித்தி காட்டி அத்தர் சித்த மீட்ட
reading: The poet calls his body a vessel of flesh, blood, bile and urine bound together, a rotting bed of pleasures, a worm-eaten life that becomes food for the tired ghoul, the dog and the fly, and asks Murugan to remove this pot and place him in that other one, granting release. The praise names Murugan at Puliyur who turns false anger to true anger and places devotees at his golden feet, and the son of Hara who took into service the hunter of the field, who offered green leaves and water from his mouth.
nuance: இக்கடத்தை நீக்கி அக்கடத்துள் ஆக்கி, remove this pot and make me within that pot, plays on கடம், pot or body: the second pot is the state of release. The leaves and the water carried in the mouth (பச்சிலை, வாய்க்குள் எச்சில்) are the marks of the hunter Kannappar's worship, which Hara accepted. Who the பொக்கணத்து நீற்றை இட்டு ... புனவேடன் is, Kannappar or Murugan as hunter, is not clear to me.

reading: A yogic plea: setting out the elements, the letters na, ma, si, va and ya at their places in the body, the cosmic sphere where the rays are stilled, the breath in its two channels, the purified senses, the sun and moon circles, the yantra, bindu and nada, the poet asks when he will reach that union. The praise is a battle in drum syllables with Vidyadharas, Tumburu and Narada singing and the Suras' bones and crowns scattered, and names the town that the serpent and the tiger saw.
nuance: நகர, மகர, சிகர, வகர, யகர are the five letters of நமசிவாய, set beside the elements (மண், கங்கை, மாருதம், ககனம்) as Tirumular sets them. The sequence is dense and I cannot follow every stage. உரகு உனும் புலி கண்ட ஊர் is Chidambaram as the place where Patanjali and Vyaghrapada saw the dance.

reading: The poet describes courtesans from hair to feet, who sell their breasts in the street, cheat and take a man's goods, and make love to him; caught in that infatuation he ruins his body, turns grey like a crane, loses sight and hearing, leaks filth, totters on a stick while people say 'chi chi', until Death takes his life, the corpse is dressed and named, drums are beaten, kin cry and beat their faces, and it is fed to the fire in the burning ground; he asks whether he must take up such sorrow daily. The praise names Siva who came as guru at the ford to take the horses and set his foot on the ascetic's head, the gods crying 'Kumara guru para', Vishnu's deeds as Narasimha, Vamana and Rama, and Murugan's embrace of the gypsy girl, at Puliyur.
nuance: The longest confession in these chapters, it runs without pause from the courtesans' trade (முலைவிலை உரைசெய்து, பொருள் பற்றி) to old age and the funeral, so that lust is shown leading straight to the burning ground. குருவின் உருவென ... குதிரை கொளவரு ... தவசி தலை பொற்பதம் வைத்து recalls the story of Manikkavasagar, for whom Siva came as guru and brought horses; the text gives its details, not the name.

reading: The poet speaks to his mind: 'Mind, come near and keep my word; I tell you what is good for you: worship the god of the peacock, king of his devotees, who gives the gods Siva's world and cuts the root of impurity, the supreme Brahman, our treasure and refuge.' The praise names Murugan as guru of Siva who sits with Kalyani, who took the Suras' heads while the ancients showered flowers, and who melts for the peacock-like Valli, at Tamil Puliyur.
nuance: The whole plea is addressed to மனமே, the mind as a separate party, as the lover speaks to his heart in love poetry; here the mind is urged toward worship rather than a beloved. மலநிலை வேர் அறுக்கவல, able to cut the root of the state of impurity, is Siddhanta language.

reading: The poet speaks of courtesans with parrot voices and pearl-hung breasts who seize a man's wealth and call in others, and asks that he, a dog caught in the net of deceitful women, be given knowledge and attainment on the seat of light, his whole mind gathered to Murugan's six, and be told the meaning with love. The praise names the vel that killed the Daityas of the seven islands, Murugan as son of Uma who is half of the dancing Lord, his embrace of the gypsy girl, and the husband of Indrani's daughter, at Puliyur.
nuance: பொருள் பற்றி வேறு அழைத்திடுவார், they take the wealth and call another, is the courtesan's trade. உனது ஆறினம் வைத்து may mean the six faces or the six-syllable mantra; the sense is uncertain.

reading: A litany with no plea, each line ending 'see, the Lord': the supreme guru who gives the state of teaching, the one exalted in the space of light without day or night, who rules the worlds, seen as Sivaya in earth, sky and elements, Uma's husband who rides the bull, the experience that has no end of ages, who ends the deeds and illusion that enter in the womb, the god of world-light who dances without ceasing in the golden hall.
nuance: Every epithet here belongs to Siva (உமைதன் மணவாளன், the dancer of கனகசபை), so the song either praises Siva or makes Murugan one with him; it does not say which. The refrain பெருமாள் காண் is unusual in the book. One word is corrupt.

tamil: வஞ்சமே கோடி கோடிகள் நெஞ்சமே சேர மேவிய
வம்பிலே வாது கூறிகள் கொஞ்சியே காம லீலைகள்
பஞ்சமா பாவ மேதரு கொங்கைமேல் நேச மாய்வெகு
பந்தியாய் வானு ளோர்தொழ நின்றசீ ரேகு லாவிய
அஞ்சவே சூர னானவ னுய்ஞ்சுபோ காம லேயயில்
அன்பினோ டேம னோரத மிஞ்சமே லான வாழ்வருள்
கொஞ்சவே காலின் மேவுச தங்கைதா னாட ஆடிய
கொந்துசேர் சோலை மேவிய குன்றுசூழ் வாக வேவரு
reading: The poet speaks of courtesans with crores of deceit in their hearts, cooing and quarrelling, who bring desire, and asks not to waste away daily talking of love to breasts that bring the five great sins, but to be given the lotus feet the gods worship. The praise names the vel thrown at Sura to free the gods, Murugan as son of the konrai-wearer who danced with tinkling anklets, the supreme first, who dances on every hill.
nuance: பஞ்சமா பாவம் ஏதரு கொங்கை, breasts that bring the five great sins, puts lust among the gravest faults. The song ends at குன்றுதோறாடல், not at Chidambaram (see source_issues).

title: கயிலைமலை
theme: Songs at Kailasa (கயிலைமலை): two yogic pleas for the self to become Siva's form in light, nada and bliss, three confessions of courtesans who take a man's wealth, a life from the womb, and a short prayer for the gift of song that Sambandar had; the praise dwells on Siva's dance, his swallowing of the poison and the demon who lifted Kailasa.
structure_note: 517 and 518 are yogic; 519 and 522 confess courtesans; 520 runs from the womb to a ruined life; 521 is an eight-line song asking for poetry.
source_issues: Song 518: line 2 is corrupt (பழ஧த்தசிவ ...... ம ளுறத்), with a bad glyph ஧ and a broken word; the sense of the opening image cannot be completed.

tamil: திருநில மருவிக் காலி னிருவழி யடைபட் டோ டி
சிவசுட ரதனைப் பாவை மணமென மருவிக் கோல
இருவினை பொரியக் கோல திருவரு ளுருவத் தேகி
இருவரு முருகிக் காய நிலையென மருவித் தேவ
பரிபுர கழலெட் டாசை செவிடுகள் படமுத் தேவர்
பரிவொடு சுழலச் சேடன் முடிநெறு நெறெனக் கோவு
அரஹர வுருகிச் சேசெ யெனதிரு நடனக் கோல
அலரணி குழல்பொற் பாவை திருமக ளமளிப் போரொ
reading: A yogic plea: the poet asks that, with the breath's two paths closed, he go by the path of Siva to the one beyond, join Siva's light as in a marriage, his two deeds roasted, and enter the golden land beyond darkness and sun, where the body is made steady and both melt into one. The praise is Siva's dance, with anklets deafening the eight directions, the three gods and the Vedas bowing, trident, axe and deer whirling, Adisesha's crowns crackling and devotees crying 'Hara Hara', and Murugan as Uma's son, at Kailasa of the devotees.
nuance: காலின் இருவழி அடைபட்டு, the two ways of the breath closed, and சிவசுடர் ... மணமென மருவி, joining Siva's light as in marriage, are the stages of the ascent. The second half of the plea does not split cleanly, and what is asked at its end (இளையவன் என வித்தாரம்) is not clear to me.

reading: The poet asks that his bound deeds be powdered, his self become Siva's form, the 'I' and the flesh fall away, and that in the light of nada and Brahman knowledge well up so that he rejoices daily in bliss and attainment; he asks for the feet. The praise names Siva, our father, whose hand took the ocean's poison so that the sky, the poet, Brahma and Vishnu might live, Murugan with the bee-hummed kadamba garland, and Kailasa, where Valli delights.
nuance: சீவன் சிவச்சொருபம் என தேறி and நானென்பது அற்று, the self found to be Siva's form and the 'I' gone, are the language of union. The opening likens the hoped-for grace to honey, the three fruits, milk, cane and tender coconut, but its last words are corrupt.

reading: The poet speaks of women who laugh, stare, threaten, act and polish their faces to stir infatuation, and gather the wealth that comes, and asks whether he must fall into the net of these thieving women. The praise names Murugan who cut off the demons' heads, rode the dark peacock and embraced the girl of the millet field, the Lord of the white mountain, who keeps a woman in his spread matted hair and holds the deer.
nuance: திருட்டு முலைப்பெண் மருட்டு வலை, the deluding net of thieving women, names deceit and theft together. The closing marks, Ganga in the matted hair and the deer in the hand, are Siva's, here given to Murugan.

reading: The poet traces his life from a drop like dew in the womb, growing small as a seed and then as large as palm and coconut fruit, slipping head down to earth as a doll of nine gates moved by the rope of breath, crawling and crying at his mother's breast, and then, through past wrongs, forgetting virtue until his mind was ruined and his body stank; he asks now for the anklets. The praise is a battle in drum syllables in which the vel is thrown with a smile, and names Siva, Ganapati and Murugan rejoicing at Kailasa, and his union with the kurinji girl.
nuance: ஒன்பது வாசல் சேர் உருவம் ... வளிகயிறினுடன் ஆடி, a figure of nine gates dancing on the rope of breath, makes the body a puppet. இனி, now, is the turn from the life told to the plea.

reading: A short song: the poet asks to be given, as Murugan's servant, the gift of singing garlands of immortal poems like the wise one of Pugali, lord on earth. The praise names the lone vel thrown against the Asuras and Murugan as the meaning of Namasivaya, Lord of the silver mountain.
nuance: புகலியில் வித்தகர் is Sambandar of Sirkazhi (Pugali), the model of the poet-saint; the plea is to be a poet as he was. நமசிவயப் பொருளானே makes Murugan the meaning of Siva's five syllables.

tamil: முகத்தைப் பிலுக்கி மெத்த மினுக்கித் தொடைத்து ரத்ந
முழுக்கக் கழப்பி யெத்தி மழுப்பிப் பொருட்ப றித்து
நகைத்திட் டழுத்தி முத்த மளித்துக் களித்து மெத்த
நடுக்குற் றவர்க்கு மெத்த மனத்தைப் பெருக்க வைத்து
செகக்கச் செகக்க செக்க தரிக்கத் தரிக்க தக்க
செகத்துக் கொருத்தர் புத்ர நினைத்துத் துதித்த பத்த
மிசைத்துத் திடத்தொ டுற்று அசைத்துப் பொறுத்த ரக்கன்
மிசைக்குற் றடுத்து மற்ற பொருப்பைப் பொடித்தி டித்து
reading: The poet speaks of courtesans who polish their faces, loosen their breast-bands, deceive and snatch a man's goods, invite him to bed, laugh, kiss and grip his neck, and asks whether he must perish daily trembling for them. The praise names Murugan as son of the one who dances for the world in drum syllables, who gives attainment to devotees who think of him, and the Lord at Kailasa, which the demon heaved up, who powdered and trampled the other mountain.
nuance: பொருட்பறித்து, snatching wealth, marks the courtesan. The end tells of the demon (Ravana, by his deed) who lifted Kailasa; whether மற்ற பொருப்பைப் பொடித்து, powdering the other mountain, means Krauncha is my guess.

title: ஸ்ரீ சைலம் திருமலை
theme: The one song at Srisailam (திருமலை): the poet asks to know the constituents of the self, reach the feet within, and see the six-faced Lord, rather than wander the streets in idle talk.

reading: The poet asks that, knowing the ten, twenty, sixty and six, he seek the two feet within, melt, and shine with the light of the full moon and fire in inner space, and that he not wander in the streets talking with everyone like a block of wood, but be granted the sight of the six-faced Lord. The praise names Ganapati of the great belly, who eats fruit, gram, pulses and sweets and wrote the ancient tale, as Murugan's elder brother, and Tirumalai where elephants and deer roam.
nuance: ஒருபது இருபது அறுபது உடன் அறு adds to ninety-six, the number of tattvas in the Tamil Siddha count; that reading is mine, and the song does not name them. தெருவினில் மரமென, like a tree in the street, sets idle talk against inward seeing. பழமொழி எழுதிய கணபதி is Ganapati as scribe of the Bharata.

title: திருவேங்கடம்
theme: Songs at Tiruvenkatam (வடமலை): the body's old age, the women's net, the fire of desire and the sea of sects, and Death taking the soul alone, against which the poet asks to serve the Lord's servants before the body ripens, to chant the six-syllable name and to escape hell; the praise, at Vishnu's hill, dwells on Murugan as nephew of Rama and Krishna.
structure_note: Every song names Vishnu's deeds in its praise, fitting the shrine: Rama at Lanka (524, 529), Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer (527, 529), Kaliya and Narasimha (526). 527 and 528 share their last two lines.
source_issues: Song 527: வேங்யு மானும் (line 13) has a broken word, perhaps வேங்கையு or another animal name.

reading: The poet describes old age: black hair whitened, eyes sunken, cheeks dried, ears turned to skin, neck and back bent, teeth fallen, drool, a cough that shakes the bones at night, a cracked voice and a stick for a leg; before his body ripens so, he asks whether he will eagerly serve those who are Murugan's servants. The praise tells of Vishnu who brought back the Vedas from the sea, bridged the ocean, took Hanuman to his side and cut Ravana's ten heads with his bow, and names Murugan, with the vel in his lotus hand, his nephew, at the northern mountain.
nuance: உடம்பு பழுத்திடு முன், before the body ripens, puts the plea before old age, not at death. The service asked is to the Lord's servants (உனக்கடிமை படுமவர் தொண்டு), a step below serving the Lord himself.

reading: The poet asks that, chanting 'Saravanabhava, treasure, six-faced one, supreme guru' and melting in Tamil like the devotees, his birth and death end, he reach Sivam, his disease end and his life be well, and that one day he be given the shade of Murugan's feet so that the sufferings of creatures on the sea-girt earth may cease. The praise names Murugan as Ganapati's younger brother, who gives life to poets, who walks at Tanigai, Sivagiri and the northern mountain, who dispels the darkness of impurity from devotees' minds like the sun, nephew of Vishnu and Narasimha, son of Uma, on the peacock that shakes the nether worlds.
nuance: The opening repeats the formula சரவணபவ நிதி அறுமுக குருபர three times, so the song enacts the chanting it describes. The plea widens beyond the poet to all creatures (கடலுலகினில் வரும் உயிர்படும் அவதிகள்).

reading: The poet describes a woman's hair dense with flowers, bees and incense smoke and her forehead with its mark like Kama's or Indra's bow, and asks for grace for one who, drawn by these, gave up the true worship that says there is no refuge but Murugan's flower feet. The praise names Vishnu who danced on the serpent's hood, holds conch, discus and lotus and tore the night-demon, Murugan as his nephew with twelve shoulders, who fought the dark demon clans, at the northern mountain.
nuance: The plea turns on மெய் வழிபடல் ஒழிவனை, one who left off true worship, and its object, the feet as the only support (துணைப் பதமலர் அலது இலை). The rhythm compresses the words heavily and the split of the plea is uncertain.

reading: The poet speaks of desiring women's breasts, spear eyes, dark hair, bangled hands and mango-leaf bodies, unable to leave their union and wandering in great wrong, and asks not to die that way and fall into hell. The praise names Murugan who became a sage and a vengai tree to win the hunter girl, nephew of the one who drove the Pandavas' chariot, who told the Pandya king to wear holy ash, Lord of Venkatam where tigers, elephants and deer live, who gives his devotees whatever they ask.
nuance: நரகில் வீழ்ந்து அலையாமல், not to fall and toss in hell, is a rarer fear than Death in the book. பாண்டியன் நீறணிய மொழிவோனே again identifies Murugan with Sambandar, who brought the Pandya king to wear the ash.

reading: The poet tells how he could not swim the sea of quarrelling sects or quench the fire of desire, trusted worldly people as his help, and melted over women until his understanding failed, and asks whether it is right that he go alone into the power of Death, who takes the life as one wails. The praise names Valli of the forest, Murugan as Visakha and Saravana, Lord of the gods and of the Veda, husband of Devayanai, Guha and Senthan, at the Venkatam hill, who gives his devotees whatever they ask.
nuance: யான் தனி போய்விடுவது இயல்போதான், is it right that I go alone, is the plea: at death the friends trusted (உலகர் தாம் துணையாவர்) do not come. சமய விரோத சாங்கலை வாரி, the ocean of hostile sects, stands beside desire as the second thing the poet cannot cross.

reading: The poet asks to be spared drinking lip-nectar on the bed under women's fish-like eyes and dark hair, caught in their net and the illusion of their faces, and to be given the two feet so that 'mine' and 'theirs' fall away and the harsh frenzy of impurity and delusion ends. The praise names Krishna as the charioteer of the Pandavas against Duryodhana, the discus-bearer, and Rama who pierced Vali and the seven sal trees and shattered Ravana's ten heads, and Murugan as Guha, their nephew, at Tiruvenkatam.
nuance: எனதாம் தனதானவை போய் அற, that what is mine and what is theirs go, names attachment as the root beneath lust; மலமாம் கடு மோக விகாரம் makes the delusion itself an impurity.

title: வள்ளிமலை
theme: Songs at Vallimalai (வள்ளிமலை), the hill where Murugan wooed Valli: the poet confesses the lure of women, the body as a bag of filth, sectarian wrangling and a household life that ends on the pyre, and asks for the feet before Death comes; the praise keeps returning to the hill itself, the valli creeper and the god who bowed at the hunter girl's feet.
structure_note: Every song but 538 ends on a punning refrain built from வள்ளி (the creeper, the hill, the girl): வள்ளிபடர் சாரல் வள்ளிமலை, வள்ளிக்குழாம் அடர்ந்த வள்ளிக்கல், வள்ளிக்கு வாய்த்த. 534 and 536 share the formula கள்வைத்த தோற்பை for the body. 537 is spoken for a lovesick girl, not by the poet. 538 and 539 both make Murugan the one who praises or worships Valli's feet.
source_issues: Song 532: the first half (கையொத்து வாழு மிந்த ... உள்ளப்பெ றாக நின்று) is hard to split and may be corrupt.
Song 534: several bag-words (ஞெள்ளற்பை, துராற்பை, வெள்ளிட்ட சாப்பி சிதமீரல்) are unclear and may be corrupt.

reading: The poet tells of women whose lily eyes and jasmine smiles raise a sea of desire, and of the day when home and young kin slowly turn strangers and Yama on his strong buffalo mocks him and plunders his life; he asks for Murugan's golden anklets on that day so that he may be saved. The praise names the guru who teaches the Lord whom the ancient Vedas sought and could not find, the one who dwells in the forest that shamed the leaping spotted deer, and whose vel killed the asuras so that the gods might live, Valli's bridegroom at Vallimalai.
nuance: இல்லும் இளையோரும் மெல்ல அயலாக, home and the young ones slowly becoming strangers, is the dying man's isolation before Death's arrival (வல்லெருமை மாயச் சமனாரும் எள்ளி). தொல்லைமறை தேடி இல்லையெனு நாதர் is Siva, whom the Vedas sought and could not find, and Murugan is his teacher. The spotted deer shamed (புள்ளியுழை நாண) may allude to Valli's birth from a doe; that is my guess. The line அள்ளவினி தாகி நள்ளிரவு போலும் உள்ளவினை யாரத் தனமாரும் is hard to construe.

reading: The poet lists what holds him: phlegm and disease, infatuation, the five senses of desire, the mire of many books of stratagem he cannot cross, a heart that leaps and dies in them, the false wish for household life, a body that never turns to the yoga by which the soul is saved; he, who talks petty knowledge and suffers, asks to be joined to the two good feet. The praise names the one whose twelve red shoulders embrace the woman of the true grove, who fought Sura as the mango in the sea so that the kin of the rider of the white elephant might live, the lord of the peacock and of the three Tamils, Valli's bridegroom at Vallimalai.
nuance: உபாயப் பலநூலின் அள்ளல், the swamp of many books of means, sets bookish learning beside phlegm and lust as one more bondage; புல்லறிவு பேசி, 'speaking petty knowledge', is the poet's verdict on himself. The remedy named is yoga (ஆவி உய்யும்வகை யோகம்) and then the feet. வெள்ளமுது மாவை, Sura as the mango tree in the sea, is the usual battle myth; வெள்ளையிபம் ஏறு வள்ளல் is Indra on Airavata.

tamil: கையொத்து வாழு மிந்த மெய்யொத்த வாழ்வி கந்து
கல்லுக்கு நேரும் வஞ்ச வுள்ளத்தர் மேல்வி ழுந்து
உய்யப்ப டாமல் நின்று கையர்க்கு பாய மொன்று
உள்ளப்பெ றாக நின்று தொய்யப்ப டாம லென்று
ஐயப்ப டாத ஐந்து பொய்யற்ற சோலை தங்கு
அல்லைப்பொ றாமு ழங்கு சொல்லுக்ர சேவ லொன்று
வையத்தை யோடி யைந்து கையற்கு வீசு தந்தை
வள்ளிக்கு ழாம டர்ந்த வள்ளிக்கல் மீது சென்று
reading: The poet confesses that he left the true life for a false one, became infatuated, fell on women with hearts like stone and thieving breasts, and grew weary serving the tricks of the low and the liars; he asks Murugan to tell him the one thing by which the mind dies within and never droops again. The praise names Devayanai of the five trees of heaven, the fierce cock on his banner that crows against the night, the one who ran round the world while the father gave to the five-handed one, and the lord who climbed Valli's hill thick with creepers in longing for Valli.
nuance: உள்ளத்தின் மாய்வது ஒன்றை மொழியாயோ asks for a teaching that makes the mind itself die, not only for rescue; how the poet means it is my inference. வையத்தை ஓடி ஐந்து கையற்கு வீசு தந்தை points to the story of the fruit: Murugan circled the world while Siva gave the prize to Ganapati; the following words (மெய்யொத்த நீதி கண்ட) and much of the first half are hard to split.

tamil: முல்லைக்கு மார னங்கை வில்லுக்கு மாதர் தங்கள்
முள்ளுற்ற கால்ம டிந்து கொள்ளிக்குள் மூழ்கி வெந்து
எல்லைக்கு மார ணங்கள் சொல்லித்தொ ழாவ ணங்கு
எள்ளற்கு மால யர்ந்து வுள்ளத்தி லாவ என்று
அல்லைக்க வானை தந்த வல்லிக்கு மார்பி லங்க
அள்ளற்ப டாத கங்கை வெள்ளத்து வாவி தங்கி
வல்லைக்கு மார கந்த தில்லைப்பு ராரி மைந்த
வள்ளிக்கு ழாம டர்ந்த வள்ளிக்கல் மீது சென்று
reading: The poet, wilting before jasmine, Kama's bow and women's teeth and striving for pleasure, sees the end ahead, the body folding, burned in the firebrands and dropped into the pit, and asks whether he will leave the company of those who never think of Murugan's name of grace. The praise names the one who wears a garland for the creeper-like woman given by the elephant, the lord born among lotuses in the pool fed by the Ganga, the son of the destroyer of the cities at Thillai with twelve wrestling shoulders, who went up the creeper-thick hill in longing for Valli.
nuance: கொள்ளிக்குள் மூழ்கி வெந்து பள்ளத்தில் வீழ்வது, sinking into the pyre's brands, burning and falling into the pit, gives the end of the pleasure-seeker in one line. The middle (ஞான எல்லைக்கு மாரணங்கள் ... இணங்கை ஒழிவேனோ) is very hard to split and my reading of it is a guess. அல்லைக்கவானை தந்த வல்லி is probably Devayanai, raised by the elephant Airavata.

reading: The poet names his body as a string of bags: a heap-bag of deceit, a holed bag of flesh, a skin bag holding the toddy of anger, a leaking bag of wind, a bag of rubbish, a bag of the mire of soul and bond, of delusion, of pus, and a carcass for dogs to drag and tear, a body no one would take; he asks whether he will be rid of it. The praise names Murugan as nephew of Vishnu on the flood, as the one who came by the forest path loud with crickets, and as the lord destined for Valli who guarded her creeper-thick hill.
nuance: Every unit of the first half ends in பை, bag: குவாற்பை, புலாற்பை, தோற்பை, காற்பை, அள்ளற்பை, சீப்பை. பசுபாச அள்ளற்பை makes the body the swamp in which the soul's bond is held. Several of the bag-words (ஞெள்ளற்பை, துராற்பை) and most of the praise (வெள்ளுத்தி மால், சிள்ளிட்ட காட்டில் உள்ளக் கிரார்) are obscure to me.

reading: The poet, struck by Kama with his jasmine arrows, caught in a house of false talk and care, asks whether he must be tossed among the learned quarrels of the stubborn logicians of the six sects and their many paths of meaning. The praise names the younger brother whose cock crows away the night, the god of boundless compassion, the lord who grants grace and is welcomed at Vallai, Thillai and by Valli, the one destined for Valli who guarded her hill.
nuance: சமயமாறின் பல்லத்த மார்க்க வல்லர்க்கர் மூர்க்கர் கல்விக் கலாத்து அலையலாமோ, 'must I wander in the learned wrangling of the stubborn logicians of the six sects', is the clearest line; the rest of the song is dense rhythm and its splitting is mostly my guess.

reading: The poet asks not to carry the body, a thieving worm-house of flesh made of sky, wind, fire, water and earth, a skin bag holding the toddy of anger and pride; he asks to be given the inner eye that sees the one thing that remains at the end of the ages, the shining formless form the end of the Vedas speaks of. The praise names Murugan as the treasure of Siva, whom Brahma, lord of the white lady in the lotus, could not see, who bears the poison and took the many-mouthed flood on his matted hair, and as husband of the emerald Valli of the hunters' clan on the hill.
nuance: The plea moves from the five elements of the body (ககனம், அநிலம், அனல், புனல், நிலம்) to the one thing beyond the end of the ages (யுக இறுதிகளின் இறுதியில் ஒரு பொருள்) seen with the inner eye. அருவுரு, formless form, and மறை இறுதி, the Veda's end, are Vedantic terms. வெள்ளைப் பிராட்டி இறை is Brahma as Saraswati's lord.

reading: A song for a lovesick girl: bodiless Kama shoots his lily arrows, the young moon scatters fire, the south wind stirs her doubt on the bed, and the speaker asks that Murugan, without being angry at the lotus-like girl standing alone or calling it her old karma, give her his kadamba garland where the striped bees drink honey. The praise names him the poet who reached the shore of all learning, who taught the one word when Siva wearing honeyed konrai worshipped him, and the peacock hero who married Valli on Vallimalai.
nuance: The girl (அரவிந்த வல்லி) is spoken of, not speaking, so the voice is a mother's or friend's, and the cure asked is the god's garland, the lover's token. கொன்றை வள்ளல்தொழ அன்று கல்லறைவு ஒன்றை அருள்வோனே seems to mean teaching Siva the one word to learn, the Om story without the word Om; the split is uncertain.

reading: The poet confesses that he took household life, mother, wife, children, women with cuckoo voices, good family and wealth as all he needed and did not grasp the guru's word; he asks whether, before cruel Yama ends his days and he is carried off in grief and burned at the cremation ground, he will come to know Murugan's two feet. The praise names the Kumara on the spotted peacock who guards the silver mountain in the north, the good bridegroom who praised beautiful Valli's feet and guarded Vallimalai, who removes the faults of earlier days, and who is good to devotees who crown his feet with lilies.
nuance: The household, not the courtesan, is the snare here: குடிவாழ்க்கை அன்னை மனையாட்டி பிள்ளை, all taken as a gain (வாய்த்தது) while the குருவார்த்தை went unheard. வள்ளி அடிபோற்றி, praising Valli's feet, reverses the usual direction of worship, and 539 does the same.

reading: The poet describes the body as an illusion held together of head, limbs, eyes, ears, a deceitful heart, blood and bone, which has a few sorrows and joys and then burns in red fire, while the soul, crying that Death has come quickly to fight, wanders and perishes; before that he asks for a love free of karma that seeks Murugan's feet. The praise names Vishnu who sleeps on the serpent, the vel that split Sura's chest when the gods fled, and the lord who, on the hill where deer, elephants, bees and monkeys play, stood and worshipped the lotus feet of the hunter girl.
nuance: திண்பொருந்திடு மாயம, an illusion firmly joined, is the body; அந்தகன் பொரவந்தது, 'Death has come to fight', is the soul's cry at the end. The closing line (குறமங்கை பங்கயம் வரநின்று கும்பிடும்) has the god worship the girl's feet, the same reversal as 538.

reading: The poet describes lovemaking with false women, from delighting in their kohl eyes and stroking their feet to the cries of birds, falling into the pool of the navel, melting like wax in fire, biting lips, nail marks, the scattered hair and the bed, and asks whether he will ever forget that pleasure, which wipes out awareness, and think of Murugan. The praise names Rama, who crossed the sea with the monkeys, entered Lanka and cut off the demon's heads, as his uncle, and Murugan as the vel who at Madurai scattered the Jains and spread the white ash crying 'Hara Hara Sankara', son of Aram Valar Sundari, who came gladly to the woman's hill.
nuance: வரைவில் பொய் மங்கையர், 'false women without bounds', comes close to the classical word for courtesans (வரைவின் மகளிர்), but no money is named. மதுரையில் வெண்பொடியும் மரந்திட அரகர சங்கர என்று வென்றருள் is Sambandar's victory over the Jains, given to Murugan. அறம்வளர் சுந்தரி is the goddess Dharmasamvardhini; அரிவை விலங்கல், 'the woman's hill', is Vallimalai.

title: திருக்கழுக்குன்றம்
theme: Songs at Thirukkazhukundram (திருக்கழுக்குன்றம்), the Vedagiri worshipped by eagles: the poet confesses a life spent on women, children and gold until grey age and Yama's rope, and the sea of birth sunk in passion; the praise centres on Murugan as Sambandar and as the teacher of the pranava who bowed at the hunter girl's feet.
structure_note: 541 and 543 follow the two halves; 542 is praise only, a portrait of Murugan as Sambandar; 544 is a short song whose plea is only for the wisdom to love him. 543 is built throughout on doubled sound-words (தனா தனா, பளீர் பளீர், குகா குகா).
source_issues: Song 542: முலையினு஡றி has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ (முலையினூறி).
Song 543: வி஡ணர் வி஡ணரென is corrupt (probably விரீர் விரீரென, with ஡ண for ரீ); the line நிணங்கள்ழு ழுவென has lost a syllable.

reading: The poet tells how, struck by Kama's arrows that waste a life, he sank in the sea of lies of laughing kohl-eyed women and fell into sorrow, then took this world as real, clung to children and gold, and grew weak, breathless, bilious and grey; he asks that before he is caught in Yama's rope Murugan grant him grace to be like the good devotees whose minds never leave devotion to his flower feet. The praise names Siva who burned Kama and the three cities with a laugh and a smoking eye, Vishnu the discus-bearer who set enmity among men so that sons and grandsons perished in war, and Murugan who hid his kadamba-garlanded shoulders in a strange disguise to embrace the girl of the millet field, at Thirukkazhukundram, equal to the city of the gods.
nuance: The life moves in stages: Kama's arrows and the women, then இகத்தை மெய்க்கொண்டு, taking this world as true, with children (பாலர்) and gold, then old age, then எமக்கயிறு, Yama's rope. The goal is not release but equality with the devotees (நற்றொண்டர்க்கு இணையாக). The discus-bearer who set kin against kin so that all their sons died (புத்திரர் சேயர் அசனைத்தும் செற்றிட) points to Krishna and the Bharata war; the text does not name it.

reading: A song of praise only: Murugan is the one whose mouth is fragrant with the nectar that welled from the breast of the first Goddess, whom Vishnu, Brahma and Rudra call their Lady; the pure one of wisdom among the Kauniyas of Kazhi, the hero-poet and guru who made the palm leaf of Tamil swim against the stream and sent the Jains to the stake; the son of Siva who plays with axe, deer, skull, drum, trident and bell; the one who imprisoned Brahma; and the lord of the banana grove at Vedagiri, where eagles worship and the Vedas and Tamil are recited like the sea's roar.
nuance: Every detail of the second quatrain is Sambandar's: the Goddess's milk, the Kauniya clan of Kazhi (Sirkazhi), the leaf floated upstream and the impaled Jains. Here they are Murugan's own deeds. கழுகுதொழு வேதகிரி names the eagles of Thirukkazhukundram, and மறைதமிழ்கள் ஓது sets the Vedas and Tamil side by side. One glyph is corrupt (முலையினு஡றி for முலையினூறி).

tamil: வோசை பெற்ற சிலம்பு கலீர் கலீரென ...... விரகலீலை
ரோம குச்சு நிறைந்து சிலீர் சிலீரென ...... அமுதமாரன்
ஆர முத்த மணிந்து அளா வளாவென ...... மருவுமாதர்
ஆறெ ழுத்தை நினைந்து குகா குகாவென ...... வகைவராதோ
வாகை பெற்ற புயங்கள் கறேல் கறேலென ...... எதிர்கொள்சூரன்
வாய்பு தைத்து விழுந்து ஐயோ ஐயோவென ...... உதிரமாறாய்
மேன்மை பெற்ற ஜனங்கள் ஐயா ஐயாவென ...... விசைகள்கூற
வேத வெற்பி லமர்ந்த க்ருபா கராசிவ ...... குமரவேளே.
reading: The poet describes lovemaking in a run of doubled sound-words, bees humming, hands clapping on the head, anklets tinkling, birds crying in the throat, sweat running, hair bristling, and asks whether, sunk in the sea of birth and unable to rise, his heart will ever come to think of the six syllables and cry 'Guha, Guha'. The praise, in the same doubled words, shows Sura's garlanded heads red, his teeth white and arms black, his chest crushed, ghouls leaping, the sea dried up and the people crying out, as Murugan took up the vel; it ends at the Tamil Veda hill, Vedagiri, with the son of Siva who married the hunter girl.
nuance: The sound-doubling (சலா சலா, சிலீர் சிலீர்) runs through both halves, so that the cure, குகா குகா, comes in the same form as the passion. ஆறெழுத்து, the six syllables, is Murugan's mantra. பவசாகரம், the sea of birth, is where the scene ends. Two corrupt words (வி஡ணர் வி஡ணரென, probably விரீர் விரீரென) and a gap in நிணங்கள்ழு ழுவென leave the doubled words of two lines uncertain.

tamil: வேத வெற்பி லேபு னத்தில் மேவி நிற்கு ...... மபிராம
வேடு வச்சி பாத பத்ம மீது செச்சை ...... முடிதோய
ஆத ரித்து வேளை புக்க ஆறி ரட்டி ...... புயநேய
ஆத ரத்தோ டாத ரிக்க ஆன புத்தி ...... புகல்வாயே
காது முக்ர வீர பத்ர காளி வெட்க ...... மகுடாமா
காச முட்ட வீசி விட்ட காலர் பத்தி ...... யிமையோரை
ஓது வித்த நாதர் கற்க வோது வித்த ...... முநிநாண
ஓரெ ழுத்தி லாறெ ழுத்தை யோது வித்த ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: A short song: the poet asks the twelve-shouldered god, who at the right moment bowed his vetchi-crowned head to the lotus feet of the lovely hunter girl in the millet field on Vedagiri, to tell him the wisdom by which he may love him with love. The praise names him as the one who, to the shame of the sage, taught the six syllables within the one syllable to the lord who had taught the gods, so that he too learned.
nuance: ஓரெழுத்தில் ஆறெழுத்தை ஓதுவித்த, teaching the six syllables within the one, joins Om to Murugan's six-syllable mantra. The taught one (இமையோரை ஓதுவித்த நாதர்) is Siva, and the shamed sage (முநி நாண) is probably Brahma. The line காதுமுக்ர வீரபத்ர காளி வெட்க is unclear to me.

title: பேறைநகர்
theme: A single song at Peraiyur (பேறைநகர்): the poet asks whether he must wander, blind with infatuation, among women's hair, faces, eyes and breasts; the praise makes Murugan nephew of Vishnu as the Boar and the Man-Lion.
source_issues: Chapter 49 is a single song under the heading பேறைநகர்.

tamil: நீலமயில் சேரு மந்தி மாலை நிக ராகி யந்த
நீடுமதி ரேக இன்ப மாகியச லாப சந்த்ர
ஆலினிக ரான வுந்தி யாலுமட வார்கள் தங்கள்
ஆடியக டாமி சைந்த வார்முலைக ளாலு மந்த
கோலவுரு வாயெ ழுந்து பாரதனை யேயி டந்து
கூடமுறை நீடு செம்பொன் மாமதலை யூடெ ழுந்த
பீலிமயில் மீது றைந்து சூரர்தமை யேசெ யங்கொள்
பேடைமட ஓதி மங்கள் கூடிவிளை யாடு கின்ற
reading: The poet lists women's hair dark as an evening sky, faces like the full moon, navels like the banyan leaf, carp eyes that cast the net of desire and swaying breasts, and asks whether he must wander, blind and infatuated, among them. The praise names Vishnu, who rose as the Boar and lifted the earth and who sprang in anger as the Man-Lion from the golden pillar, as Murugan's uncle, and Murugan as the one of the peacock and the great vel who won against the Suras, come to dwell in Peraiyur, where young swans play.
nuance: The confession is a plain catalogue of the woman's body, part by part, each with its stock comparison, and the poet's state is அந்தனாகி மயல், blinded by infatuation. The two avatars are named by their details: the boar lifting the earth (பார்தனையே இடந்து) and the lion from the golden pillar (செம்பொன் மாமதலை ஊடெழுந்த கோபவரி நாரசிங்கன்).

title: மயிலம்
theme: A single song at Mayilam (மயிலம்): the poet, melting like wax before women's eyes, asks Murugan to come when Yama's messengers take his life; the praise turns on Murugan himself infatuated with the hunter girl and falling at her feet.
source_issues: Song 546: னு஡டே and கானு஡ டே have the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ (னூடே, கானூடே).
Chapter 50 is a single song under the heading மயிலம்.

reading: The poet asks whether women's eyes are arrow or sword, poisoned spear or carp, fish or deer, and whether, overcome by their cuckoo speech, thread-thin waists and mountainous breasts, melting like wax in the forge and drowning in the sea of passion, he must perish by the disease of the body's five great sins; he asks that on the day Yama's messengers come shouting with club and noose to take his life, Murugan grant him his feet. The praise names the vel that dried the roaring sea and turned Sura's array to ash, the one who took another form, went into the hunters' forest, fell in love with the hunter girl and fell at her feet, the lord whose feet Sambhu worships, at the cool hill of Mayilam.
nuance: The opening is a riddle of comparisons (கோலோ வாளோ ... மீனோ மானோ), the familiar question of what the woman's eye is. The same word, மயல், describes Murugan's love for Valli (மயல்கொண்டு உலாய் அவள் தாள்மீதே வீழ்): the god's infatuation is praised in the song that confesses the poet's. உறுதண்ட பாசமொடு ஆரா வாரா is Death's men coming with club and noose, shouting.

title: திருசிராப்பள்ளி
theme: Songs at Thiruchirappalli (திருசிராப்பள்ளி, Trisira hill), the first fifteen: most confess bondage to courtesans who sell their arts and refuse a man without gold, one torments the poet with the tortures of Yama's servants, and a few turn inward to the mind, the guru's secret and the Reality beyond speech and yoga; the praise names Murugan as Sambandar, as the guru who took the poet publicly, and as the son of the Lord of the rock, often with Vayalur beside it.
structure_note: Courtesan songs: 547, 549, 550, 552, 553, 554, 555, 559, 560. 548 is addressed to the poet's own mind; 551 asks for love that scorns union; 556 is a litany of namo namas; 557 is an eight-line song asking for the guru's secret; 558 is a catalogue of Yama's tortures; 561 describes the Reality that reading, worship and speech cannot reach. Vayalur (வயலூர்), near Trichy, is named in many of the songs.
source_issues: Song 547: the line அங் மாய்ப்பரி சுத்தத் has lost a letter (probably அங்கமாய்); வயலு஡ரா has ஡ for ஊ.
Song 551: திநட்முழ்குங் is corrupt and is not flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS.
Song 553: வயலு஡ரா has ஡ for ஊ.
Song 554: ஓ஡ணர் பா஡ணர் வா஡ணர் சோணர் is corrupt; with ஡ண for ரீ it reads ஓரீர் பாரீர் வாரீர், and சோணர் may be சேரீர்.
Song 555: மதனு஡லின் has ஡ for ஊ.
Song 557: சகசிரகிப் has probably lost a syllable (சகசிரகிரிப்).
Song 558: அனலு஡டே has ஡ for ஊ.
Song 559: க்஡ணடா is corrupt (probably க்ரீடா, with ஡ண for ரீ).
Song 561: வயலு஡ரத்தில் has ஡ for ஊ.

reading: The poet describes courtesans who beckon with an outstretched hand, show and hide their breasts, act out a false love and deal with a man as far as his coins go, recite the deceitful science of pleasure, cry like cuckoo and anril, rake him with nails and strike him to rouse his lust, having studied day and night how to confuse lustful men; he asks to leave his delusion over these whores and worship the lotus feet praised by Siva. The praise names Murugan as the one present everywhere, lacking nothing, the conscious form, the bliss the pure attain, distinct from the end of the thirty-six tattvas, the guardian of heaven whom Indra praised, the hero of Vayalur whose vel beat Sura while ghouls ate and danced, the lord of the gods on the hill of south Sirappalli with its golden towers.
nuance: காசளவு உறவாடி, 'relating to the measure of the coins', and சூளைகள, whores, make the trade explicit. The women's arts are a learned discipline (இன்ப சாஸ்த்ரம், பண்டு இராப்பகல் கற்று). The praise borrows Saiva Siddhanta: முப்பத்தாறினின் முடிவு வேறாய், beyond the end of the thirty-six tattvas. The line அங் மாய்ப்பரி சுத்தத் has lost a letter (probably அங்கமாய்).

reading: The poet speaks to his own mind: alas, do not trust this body, a contraption of strings, a lock Brahma made; from now on, without fear, let us belong to the vel-bearer who turned the mountain to cotton; this is our refuge, here is the peacock-rider's deed of possession, 'we come to rule you', and the holy ash he has bound on us; do not forget the cry 'Son, Kumara'. The praise names the drums and Vedas of the battle where Murugan played ball with the vel among the slain on his peacock, the child of grace of 'my father Sadasiva' who wears the moon, the serpent, the Ganga and the skeleton, and the lord who married the doe-eyed one and looks into the minds of those who say 'Sirappalli'.
nuance: The song is a speech to the mind (அந்தோ மனமே), not to the god. மயில்வாகனர் சீட்டு இது, 'this is the peacock-rider's deed', with வந்தாளுவம் நாம், 'we come to rule you', reads like a deed of possession, the claim of a master on his servant; that it alludes to a particular story is my guess. என்தாதை சதாசிவ, 'my father Sadasiva', makes the poet Siva's son as well. Many splits in the middle lines are uncertain.

reading: The poet describes lovemaking with women whose hearts melt, falling on their breasts, bathing in agil and sandal paste, nail marks like crescents, hair falling, bird cries, drooping carp eyes and sweat on the face, drinking their lips night and day, and asks whether Murugan should abandon him, a lecher, to be mocked. The praise names Vishnu of Srirangam, who grants grace to those who reach the supreme state through charya and kriya, as his uncle, and Murugan as the guru who came on the peacock with the vel that broke the mountain and took the poet as his own so that the world knew it, the one who appeared as a forehead mark to the Lord of the hill at Sirappalli.
nuance: மயிலினில் வந்தெனை ஆட்கொளல் சகமறியும்படி காட்டிய குருநாதா, 'the guru who showed the world that he came on the peacock and took me', is the poet's own claim to a public grace. The praise of Vishnu uses the Saiva terms சரியை and க்ரியை for the way to his heaven (பரமபதம்). உருவளர் குன்றுடையார்க்கு ஒரு திலதம் makes Murugan the ornament of Siva of the rock.

tamil: அழுதழு தாசார நேசமு முடையவர் போலேபொய் சூழ்வுறும்
அவருடன் வாய்பேசி டாமையு முனிதலு மாறாத தோஷிகள்
விழிகளி னால்மாட வீதியில் முலைகளை யோராம லாரொடும்
விரகிகள் வேதாள மோவென முறையிடு கோமாள மூளிகள்
வழியினில் வாழ்ஞான போதக பரமசு வாமீவ ரோதய
மதுரையின் மீதால வாயினில் எதிரம ணாரோ ரெணாயிரர்
செழியனு மாளாக வாதுசெய் கவிமத சீகாழி மாமுனி
திருவுடை யாய்தீதி லாதவர் உமையொரு பாலான மேனியர்
reading: The poet describes whores who weep and weep as if loving, entrap fools, will not speak to the lustful on a day they give no gold, are always angry, whose greed for coin has no end, whose eyes are steeped in poison, who price their breasts to anyone in the mansion streets, and asks whether his life can be saved from their works. The praise names Murugan as the supreme guide to wisdom, the vel of Vayalur who is everywhere, and as the poet-sage of Sirkazhi who at Madurai made the eight thousand Jains mount the stakes, spread the ash, made the Pandiya his servant and sang 'Siva Siva Mahadeva', the lord of the gods at Sira hill.
nuance: பொன்கொடா நாள் அவருடன் வாய்பேசிடாமை, not speaking on a day no gold is given, and அறுதியில் காசாசை, an endless greed for coin, put money at the centre. The Sambandar story is told in full detail (ஆலவாய், எண்ணாயிரர், கழு, செழியன், சீகாழி மாமுனி) and given to Murugan (வந்துபாடும் திருவுடையாய்).

reading: The poet speaks of creeper-like women whose small waists are a trap for young men's hearts, and of bowing at their feet and drinking their lips, and asks for the love that scorns such union and worships Murugan's shining golden anklets. The praise names him as the son, in Siva's love, of the Lord who dances to the drum in the hall that is the heart of unfailing devotees while the four Vedas sing in rhythm, the garlanded one of the Trisira hill.
nuance: கலவியை நிந்தித்து, 'scorning union', is unusually explicit: the plea is for a love that condemns the pleasure, not only escapes it. அன்பர்க்கு உளமெனும் மன்றில், 'in the hall that is the devotees' heart', moves Siva's dance from Chidambaram into the heart. The word திநட்முழ்குங் is corrupt.

reading: The poet speaks of the greed for money that the kin of women with mountainous breasts present as affection, demanding gems bright as the sun, coral and pearls, and calls himself a rogue glad at heart, mocked and deluded, futile, base, witless and without patience, and asks when Murugan will end his wandering after getting and eating. The praise names the twelve-armed one whose chest is embraced by the daughter of the lord of heaven and the daughter of the hunters, at Vayalur and at Sira hill where drums sound.
nuance: The demand comes from the woman's family (சுற்றம் பரிவென வைக்கும் பணவாசை): their greed wears the face of affection. The self-abuse is a list (துட்டன், அவத்தன், குணவீனன், அறிவிலி, பொறையிலி).

reading: The poet describes women who play with one man with their eyes, another with their breasts and a third with their hands, give their thoughts to one, their scorn to another and both their words to a third, and asks Murugan to end his delusion that such women have great love for him and to grant the feet that bees circle as if they were lotuses. The praise names the peacock that makes the serpent tremble, the hero of Vayalur whom the gods, devotees and sages worship, and the lord of Trisira hill, where Siva with the Goddess at his side, whom Brahma delights in, dances.
nuance: The six lines of ஒருவரொடு carry the charge: the deceit is a division of the body and mind among many men. The delusion confessed is the belief (மனநினையும் இந்த மருள்) that the love is real. வயலு஡ரா has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

reading: The poet describes women with lily mouths and nectar speech whose earring-touching eyes are arrow, spear and carp, who stand saying 'learn, look, come, join our desire for your shoulders', and money before a man so much as touches their cloth, and asks whether he must keep falling on their breasts and wander without rising. The praise strings epithets: the giver and great knower praised by the gods, rider of the peacock, lord of Vayalur, the deathless, ageless young one, the hero whose vel fought the demons of darkness, Uma's son, the god and king of the gods on the Trisira hill.
nuance: உடைதொடாப் பணம், money before the garment is touched, names the price. The women's invitation is corrupt in the source (ஓ஡ணர் பா஡ணர் வா஡ணர் சோணர்); with ஡ண read as ரீ it is ஓரீர் பாரீர் வாரீர், and சோணர் may stand for சேரீர். The praise is a chant of short epithets ending in ஏ (தேவே கோவே வேளே).

reading: The poet describes lovemaking with kohl-eyed women at length, drinking their lips, bird cries, the coral lips, embraces and blows done by the book of Kama, and asks whether he will stop sinking in the sea of passion. The praise is a litany of the Goddess, attended by Saraswati, Lakshmi, Rati, Sachi, the Krittikas and Rambha: Durga, the terrible one, Lady of the worlds, cause of all, Shakti, Parvati of the Himalaya, Rudri, the stainless, Lady of the religions, the partless, Kundali, Sivai, Gauri, Ambika, Tripura, Yamalai, who bore Murugan in love; and it ends at the Trisira hill of towered halls, where the Father of the hill worshipped him.
nuance: மதனூலின் படியிலே செய்து, 'doing it by the book of Kama', makes the lovemaking a learned art, as in 547. The second half is nearly all the mother's names, Shakta and Saiva titles together (குண்டலி, சமய நாயகி, நிஷ்களி). Whether திரிசிராமலை அப்பர் is Siva of the hill or the saint Appar is not certain; I read the former. மதனு஡லின் has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

tamil: சத்தி பாணீ நமோநம முத்தி ஞானீ நமோநம
சத்து ரூபா நமோநம ரத்ந தீபா நமோநம
பத்தி பூணா மலேயுல கத்தின் மானார் சவாதகில்
பட்டி மாடான நானுனை விட்டிரா மேயு லோகித
அத்ர தேவா யுதாசுர ருக்ர சேனா பதீசுசி
அர்ச்ச னாவாக னாவய லிக்குள் வாழ்நாய காபுய
சித்ர கோலா கலாவிர லஷ்மி சாதா ரதாபல
சிட்ட நாதா சிராமலை யப்பர் ஸ்வாமீ மகாவ்ருத
reading: The poet confesses that he never took up the devotion that sings 'Hail, hail' to Murugan as bearer of the spear, knower of release, teacher of the tattvas, the true form of bindu and nada, the jewelled lamp, but fell like a stray bull on breasts smeared with civet, agil and camphor; he asks Murugan to come now and give his red lotus feet so that he does not leave him. The praise, mostly in Sanskrit epithets, names the fierce commander of the gods, the one of the tradition of offerings and soma sacrifice, the lord of Vayalur who holds the rosary, the teacher of the Saiva Agamas and tantras, the swami of the Father of the Sira hill, the lord of Vedic brahmins who keep great vows with darbha grass.
nuance: The opening namo-namas are quoted as the song the poet failed to sing (என்றுபாடும் பத்தி பூணாமலே), so the litany is both praise and confession. பட்டிமாடு, the stray bull that grazes anywhere, is his image for himself. The praise ties Murugan to Vedic and Agamic ritual (சோமாசி, சிவாகம தந்த்ர போதா, தெர்ப்பை).

reading: A short song: the poet asks Murugan to tell him the secret of the knowledge that makes clear that the Lord is the guru, so that he does not waver day and night, and to grant him the settled state of experience. The praise names him lord of this world and the next, of the three Tamils of verse and music, Saravanabhava, the god of the hill.
nuance: பதி குருவெனத் தெளி போத ரகசியம், the secret by which one knows that the Lord is the guru, is the doctrine that God comes as the teacher; அநுபூதி is direct experience. The shrine word சகசிரகிப் has probably lost a syllable (சக சிரகிரிப் பதி?).

reading: The poet traces a life from the womb through birth, pleasure and pain to death, and then the torments of Yama's servants: they bind the subtle body tight, beat and terrify it, roll it, pour sand and drop it in fire, grind it in an oil press, knock out the teeth, make it embrace a red-hot copper figure, tie it on thorns, poke the eyes, cut and feed its flesh, break and crush it and bind it in chains; he asks Murugan to end the suffering of Yama's blows. The praise names him the supreme guru at Seyppathi, praised by those who still the breath, shed the mind's cares and the senses' desires and walk charya, kriya and yoga, and the son of Siva, Rudra of three eyes and the axe who burned the three cities, quality and beyond quality, at Trisira hill.
nuance: The tortures follow the hell lists of Saiva and Puranic texts: செக்கிலரைத்து, ground in the press, எரிசெப்புருவைத் தழுவ, embracing the burning copper image. புரியட்டகம் is the eightfold subtle body that the messengers bind. Nothing is confessed here; the fear itself is the plea. அனலு஡டே has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

reading: The poet heaps names on courtesans: lustful for wealth, seats of play, shameless among men, women of illusion who throw their cloth over their breasts, goddesses of misfortune who make men poor, who couple even with outcastes, with crores of tricks, who fall on many, read only the books of union, who drink the demon's water, sinners without compassion, and asks whether pleasure with them is pleasure. The praise names Murugan as the teacher of the Vedas and Agamas by the guru's glance, the vel that killed the hunters crying 'ko ko', the lord of the peacock, born in the reed pond, with twelve shoulders, at the Trisira hill with its towers.
nuance: பொருளின் மேல் ப்ரிய காமாகாரிகள், 'women whose desire is for wealth', and மிடியர் ஆக்கு மூதேவிகள், 'misfortune-goddesses who make men poor', name money. பேய்நீர் ஊணிகள் probably means they drink liquor. க்஡ணடா பீடிகள் is corrupt; with ஡ண read as ரீ it is க்ரீடா பீடிகள், seats of sport.

reading: The poet speaks of women whose minds are set on seizing wealth, their musk-scented breasts, slipping cloth and loosened hair, and asks whether he will stop wandering in passion and, with a melting heart, praise Murugan's two feet. The praise names the bearer of the vel who went lovingly to the hill and married the peacock-like girl who guarded the millet, who came to Vayalur, and the little one given by the great Lord who appeared on the first day at the Trisira hill.
nuance: பொருள்கவர் சிந்தை அரிவையர், women with minds bent on seizing wealth, is the whole charge; the rest is the stock catalogue. முதனாளில் தெரிய இருந்த பெரியவர் may refer to a shrine legend of Siva's first appearance on the rock; I cannot identify it.

tamil: வாசித்துக் காணொ ணாதது பூசித்துக் கூடொ ணாதது
மாசர்க்குத் தோணொ ணாதது நேசர்க்குப் பேரொ ணாதது
ஓசைக்குத் தூர மானது மாகத்துக் கீற தானது
யோகத்தைச் சேரு மாறுமெய்ஞ் ஞானத்தைப் போதி யாயினி
ஆசைப்பட் டேனல் காவல்செய் வேடிச்சிக் காக மாமய
ஆலித்துச் சேல்கள் பாய்வய லு஡ரத்திற் காள மோடட
நாசிக்குட் ப்ராண வாயுவை ரேசித்தெட் டாத யோகிகள்
நாகத்துச் சாகை போயுயர் மேகத்தைச் சேர்சி ராமலை
reading: The poet describes the Reality that cannot be seen by reading, reached by worship or spoken aloud, that cannot appear to the impure or be named even by those who love it, that maya cannot surround, far beyond the sound of bindu and nada, beyond the sky, the origin of the world; having seen it, he asks Murugan to teach him the true knowledge by which he may join yoga, and asks whether he must stay bewildered without casting off the flesh. The praise names the Kanda who, longing for the girl who guarded the millet, worshipped her golden feet, the peacock hero of Vayalur wearing the serpent, the Lord whom yogis who expel the breath through the nose say cannot be found, the swami of the Lord of Sira hill.
nuance: The first half is a negative description (வாசித்துக் காணொணாதது, பூசித்துக் கூடொணாதது, வாய்விட்டுப் பேசொணாதது) of the kind Saiva mystics use for the Lord. The tension within the song is worth noticing: the poet asks for yoga (யோகத்தைச் சேருமாறு) while the praise says breath-controlling yogis cannot find the Lord (நாசிக்குட் ப்ராண வாயுவை ரேசித்து ... காணொணாது); the second may mean only yoga without grace. வயலு஡ரத்தில் has the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ.

title: திருசிராப்பள்ளி
theme: The last song at Thiruchirappalli (திருசிராப்பள்ளி): the poet confesses delusion by poisonous, deceitful women who look on a man with contempt once his money is gone, and yet vows never to forget, in dream or waking, the fragrant feet that gave release; the praise centres on the vel that saved Indra and the hunters' submission.
source_issues: Chapter 52 holds only song 562, the sixteenth song under திருசிராப்பள்ளி, split from chapter 51 by the fifteen-song limit.

reading: The poet describes poisonous women who frighten and ensnare, loosen their clothes, deceive, are eager in a moment and look with contempt on a man who has no money left, dancers and lechers with musky breasts who beguile everyone with words, eyes, hair, waist and gait; he says that, though he has been deluded in vain and toiled to make money, he will not forget in dream or waking the long-anklet feet fragrant with many flowers that gave release. The praise names the twelve-handed Guha who protected the thousand-eyed Indra and ended his poverty, the guru of Pasupati, whose vel powdered the thieving demons while the hunters paid tribute and pleaded, Saravanabhava at Thiruchirappalli hill, round which the sun and moon circle.
nuance: விரவிய திரவியம் இலரானால் வெறுத்து நோக்கிகள், women who look with disgust once the money is gone, is the courtesan's mark. Unlike most songs, the turn is a vow rather than a plea: கனவிலும் நனவிலும் மறவேனே, 'I will not forget, in dream or waking'. மோக்ஷமது அருளிய ... கழல் makes the feet the giver of release. செருக்கு வேட்டுவர் திறையிட முறையிட, the proud hunters paying tribute and pleading, is from the Valli story. The words க்ருஷிபணு தடத்து are hard to split.

title: திருக்கற்குடி
theme: Songs at Thirukkarkudi (திருக்கற்குடி): the poet confesses the sea of union with women whose breasts overpower even ascetics, and the wealth poured out on them, and fears Yama's messengers who will open his account and torture him by its total; he asks for the feet and for Murugan to come on the peacock, and praises him as the god who was himself caught by the hunter girl's eye.

reading: The poet describes women's breasts as conquerors that shatter the pot, chase off the elephant, defeat the mountain peak, crush the flocks of birds and swell so proudly that ascetics of the great principle faint, and asks for Murugan's feet so that he may be free of weariness in the sea of union. The praise names the god who, deeply desiring the hunter girl in the forest millet field, was caught at the corner of her kohl-dark eye, who was born in the pond and revived the heavenly world with his matchless vel, the lord of Thirukkarkudi, famed for Tamil and for poetry.
nuance: The breasts are described with the verbs of a conqueror (தகர்த்து, துரத்தி, செறுத்து, குமைத்து), each beating one of the stock comparisons: pot, elephant's temple, hill, the chakravaka birds. குருத் தத்துவத்துத் தவர் சோர, even the ascetics fainting, is the measure of their power. In the praise Murugan is the one caught (மைக்கட் கடைப்பட்டு நிற்கைக்கு உரியோனே).

reading: The poet confesses that he poured out wealth on mountainous breasts and was caught in their pleasure for many days, and fell into the stupor of deep sleep; he asks that when Yama's messengers seize, bind, kick, drag, trample, open his bundle of accounts and, according to the total, twist, turn, burn, push him into filth and abuse him, he not be left to wander so tormented, but that Murugan, pleased with his Tamil, come in anger on the peacock with the vel's command in hand and stand at his side. The praise asks Murugan to give him the thought fit to praise him in words, the lord of the devotees at Karkudi, the place of attainment.
nuance: கணக்குக் கட்டு விரித்துத் தொகைக்குட் பட்ட இலக்கப்படிக்குத் தக்கபடியே, opening the bundle of accounts and punishing 'according to the figure in the total', makes Yama a clerk with a ledger; the torture is measured by the sum. சுழுத்தி is the state of deep sleep, here the soul's stupor. The poet's claim on Murugan is his Tamil (தமிழ்க்குச் சரித்து). Splits in the first lines (கொடத்துக் கத்தை யவத்தைக் கடுக்கை) are uncertain.

title: இரத்னகிரி
theme: Songs at Ratnagiri (இரத்னகிரி): the poet confesses he has lost goodness and sense to women's eyes, hair and breasts and to the five senses that cheat him toward death, and in a short song asks to sing the Thiruppugazh with devotion until he is freed; the praise names the vel against Sura and the jewel hill.
structure_note: Two songs of plea against women and the body (565, 566), the second with a long battle passage in drum syllables, and a short song of pure devotion (567).

reading: The poet says that through the kohl-dark eyes like carp that rival the doe, the dark hair like a fragrant swarming cloud and the breasts like golden pots, hills and caskets, he has lost goodness, knowledge and feeling, and asks how he will ever gain the good path. The praise names Murugan who struck down the mango-tree form in the dark sea and ended the gods' grief, the source of the three Tamils and of the meaning of japa, the true Kumara shining on Ratnagiri.
