nuance: நலமற்று அறிவற்று உணர்வற்றனன்: the confession is a triple loss, goodness, knowledge and feeling, in one breath. கடலில் புகு கொக்கு: கொக்கு is the mango tree, and the line points to Sura hiding in the sea in that form, though the splitting of the line is not certain.

reading: The poet describes himself caught in a sorrowful household like a fish in a net, like straw fallen into gruel, his body like wax in a fire, a basket of impurity driven by the senses, while the five cheats of sound, touch, smell, form and taste play their falsehood as heedless Death draws near; he asks whether, seeking women's houses, he must stumble to his end in a body that stinks, and asks for the state that does not end. The praise is a battle dance in drum syllables in which Hari, Brahma, Siva and the goddess dance, Yama, foxes and ghouls feast as the vel is thrown, and names Murugan, lover of the doe-girl guarding the millet, at Ratnagiri.
nuance: சூதர் ஐவர் சத்த பரிசான மண ரூப ரசம்: the five senses are named as five gamblers or cheats, the five sense-objects listed in order. The similes for the trapped self (மீன் in the net, செத்தை in the gruel, மெழுகு in the fire) are piled one on another. சீசி இது நாற is the poet's own disgust at his body.

reading: A short song: the poet asks that, holding to Murugan with devotion and singing his great Thiruppugazh again and again, he become one freed and reach liberation. The praise names Murugan the best one, friend of the good who give, dweller on the peerless gem hill, the wise one who is the descent of the power of knowledge, the lord of the victorious vel.
nuance: The song names the book's own title (மா திருப்புகழ் பாடி) and makes singing it the way to mukti. ஞானசத்தி நிபாதா: சத்திநிபாதம், the descent of grace on a ripe soul, is a term of Saiva Siddhanta, here made a name of Murugan.

title: விராலிமலை
theme: First songs at Viralimalai (விராலிமலை, 1 of 2): the poet confesses bondage to courtesans who sell their bodies, to his own flattery of misers and his poems on women, and to the malas, and asks for the feet, for samadhi and for the teaching of jnana beyond the tattvas; the praise names Vayalur, where Murugan commanded the poet to sing, and identifies him with Tamil saints.
structure_note: Courtesan and body songs (569, 574, 576, 578, 580, 582), the long head-to-foot song 572; songs of yoga and knowledge (570, 573, 575, 581); begging from patrons (571, 579); a song of meditation on Murugan's form (568); and 577, a string of Siva's names.
source_issues: Song 568: one corrupt character in லு஡டாடி (line 17), probably லூடாடி.
Song 571: unflagged garble செர்ருபமி (line 6), probably ஸ்வரூப; the same garble appears as செர்ருப in 580 and 584.
Song 573: one corrupt character in னு஡றில் (line 12), probably ஊறில்.
Song 574: one corrupt character in லு஡த்தை (line 5), probably ஊத்தை; the last two lines of the song nearly repeat lines 13 and 14.
Song 575: two corrupt characters, புண்ட஡ணகன் (line 5, புண்டரீகன்) and வயலு஡ரா (line 18, வயலூரா).
Song 576: unflagged garble லுற்முழ்கி (line 9).
Song 580: three corrupt characters, வா஡ண ரி஡ணர் (line 6, வாரீர் வாரீர்) and வயலு஡ரா (line 21); also the unflagged செர்ருப (line 1).
Song 581: one corrupt character in வயலு஡ரா (line 12); also the unflagged ச்முக (line 13), probably ஷண்முக.

reading: The poet asks that, lowly as he is, he may every day hold in thought Murugan's flower faces crowned with gem garlands, his twelve arms, his two fragrant feet, Valli and Indra's daughter on either side, the vel, the peacock and his beautiful form of true knowledge. The praise tells how at Madurai, when the forty-nine poets disputed the meaning of a work, Murugan came as a mute merchant's child at Alavai and settled it, and names him nephew of Krishna who hid the sun with his discus, at Viralimalai by the Kaveri.
nuance: The plea is a meditation list (தியானம்), the god's form part by part, rather than a confession. ஏழேழு பேர்கள் கூற வரு பொருள் அதிகாரம் ... ஊமர் போல வணிகரில் ஊடாடி: the Madurai story of the mute child who judged the commentaries on Iraiyanar's Akapporul, here told of Murugan, so he is identified with a figure of the Tamil Sangam. பாநு மறைவுசெய் is Krishna covering the sun in the Bharata war.

reading: The poet calls himself the one who sang poems of every kind, from feet to hair, on women who put a price on breasts like Meru and stir desire with words of milk, syrup and honey; a goblin-witted, ungenerous, untrue sinner without penance, a fool busy with bondage, he asks to become the dust of Murugan's feet and not fall into hell. The praise shows Death and his messengers afraid, Brahma and Vishnu fleeing, Vedic priests chanting Sivaya nama as Sura dies, and the groves of Viralimalai where bees hum ragas.
nuance: பாதாதி கேசமாக வகைவகை கவிபாடும்: the poet confesses not only desire but misuse of his art, poems describing women from foot to head, a recognised genre. பசுபாச வ்யாபார மூடன் uses the Siddhanta terms for the bound soul and its bond. முலையினை விலைகூறி names the sale.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to think of him so that ascetics who speak no idle word may say of him day and night that he has no passion, no diversion, no greed and no infatuation, and so that he gains the experience of samadhi in which the mind dissolves into the transcendent that pervades all moving and unmoving worlds. The praise names Siva who wears the moon and the river and crushed Ravana's arms, and Murugan the bridegroom of the hunters' daughter, at Siramalai, Piranmalai and Viralimalai.
nuance: மநோலய சமாதி அநுபூதி: samadhi as the dissolution of mind, a yogic term. The long run of Sanskrit epithets (சதாசிவ மயேசுர சகலலோக சராசர வியாபக பராபர) may describe the state sought or the god addressed, and உமாபுருஷன் என may compare the poet to Siva or be divided otherwise.

reading: The poet asks whether, not fixing his mind on the stainless, ancient, transcendent one whom Siva, Vishnu and Brahma praise and who is the form of heaven, earth and all beings, he will go with longing for gifts to faithless, indifferent men of empty fame. The praise plays on Ravana's name in telling of Rama, names Murugan the younger brother of the elephant-faced lord of arts, and ends at Viralimalai.
nuance: The second line of the plea (துரால்புகழ் பராதின கராவுள பராமுக துரோகரை தராசையுற்று அடைவேனோ) seems to name patrons, men of chaff-like fame who turn their faces away, as in 579 and 589. The song is a dense chain of Sanskrit compounds and its division is doubtful throughout.

reading: In a long rhythm the poet describes a woman from her bathed and scented hair to her anklets, and asks whether a day will come when, no longer melting in such women's wiles, the delusion ends, grace comes into his hands, and he sees the high way of devotion and the path to supreme liberation. The praise is a long battle in drum syllables, with sun and moon restored and the gods regaining their rule, and recalls that at Vayalur Murugan appeared before the poet and told him to sing the rare great Thiruppugazh so that his delusion and impurity might end; it ends at Viralimalai with Murugan on the peacock.
nuance: வயலியில் ... மயலொடு மலமற அரிய பெரிய திருப்புகழ் விளம்பு என் முன் அற்புதம் எழுந்தருள் குக: an autobiographical line, the poet's own call at Vayalur to sing the book, set inside the praise. The woman's description is a full head-to-foot catalogue of the kind 569 confesses to having composed.

tamil: உருவேற வேஜெ பித்து வொருகோடி யோம சித்தி
உணர்வாசை யாரி டத்து மருவாது வோரெ ழுத்தை
தரியாத போத கத்தர் குருவாவ ரோரொ ருத்தர்
தழலாடி வீதி வட்ட மொளிபோத ஞான சித்தி
குருநாடி ராச ரிக்கர் துரியோத னாதி வர்க்க
குலையாமல் நீதி கட்டி யெழுபாரை யாள விட்ட
மருகா புராரி சித்தன் மகனே விராலி சித்ர
மதுரா புரேசர் மெய்க்க அரசாளு மாறன் வெப்பு
reading: The poet asks whether the knowledge handed on by gurus, one after another, who teach japa until the mantra takes form, a crore of fire-offerings, devotion to the Agamas, holding the one syllable and restraining the breath, can be a refuge; if Siva the fire-dancer himself gave the light and the attainment of knowledge, that would be it, and he has not found it. The praise tells of the Kauravas destroyed and Kunti's sons ruling by justice, Vishnu the dwarf who grew tall, and names Murugan Siva's son with the vel at Viralimalai, the master who cured the Pandya king's fever and straightened his hump at Madurai.
nuance: The plea weighs ritual and yogic discipline taught by human gurus (ஜெபித்து, ஓம சித்தி, ஆகமத்து, ஊதை) against knowledge given by Siva and asks whether the first is a refuge (தஞ்சமாமோ). மாறன் வெப்பு வளைகூனையே நிமிர்த்த: Sambandar's cure of the Pandya, so Murugan is again Sambandar. The split of தரியாத போதகத்தர் is uncertain, and so whether these gurus are praised or doubted.

tamil: எதிரெதிர்கண் டோ டி யாட்கள் களவதறிந் தாசை பூட்டி
இறைவைகொளுங் கூவல் மூத்த கறையொழுகுந் தாரை பார்க்கி
அதிவிகடம் பீழ லாற்ற அழுகிவிழும் பீற லு஡த்தை
அருவிசலம் பாயு மோட்டை அடைவுகெடுந் தூரை பாழ்த்த
விதுரனெடுந் த்ரோண மேற்று எதிர்பொருமம் பாதி யேற்றி
விரவுஜெயன் காளி காட்டில் வருதருமன் தூத னீற்ற
மதியணையுஞ் சோலை யார்த்து மதிவளசந் தான கோட்டின்
மலைமருவும் பாதி யேற்றி கடிகமழ்சந் தான கோட்டில்
reading: The poet describes women who bind men with desire and show them a pit to stumble into, and in deliberately foul images, a well drawn by bucket, a channel of old stains, a rotting hole stopped with cloth where streams flow, calls their sex a ruined mire, and asks Murugan to take him as his own so that he does not sink in it. The praise tells of the Bharata war, Vidura, Drona, Jayadratha and Arjuna, Krishna as Dharma's envoy and Arjuna's charioteer as Murugan's uncle, at Viralimalai with Uma at Siva's half.
nuance: அளறில் அழுந்தாமல்: அளறு is mire and also hell, the word the Kural uses for the courtesan. The method is that of the Naladiyar's body chapters, desire countered by naming the body's filth. The images are crude and partly obscure (இறைவைகொளுங் கூவல், சீலை தீற்று), and the last two lines of the praise nearly repeat each other.

reading: The poet defines Sivayoga as the abiding of everything, the five elements, six religions, mantras, Vedas, Puranas and arts, the fifty-one letters, all beings, Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, sun and moon, the ajapa, bindu and nada, as one form, its own nature, and asks whether, with the malas of anava, maya and karma gone, he will gain that path in the line of the teaching guru. The praise shows the demons routed, the gods back in Indra's world, the goddess crying 'Hara Hara Sankara' as the vel pierces Meru, and ash-smeared sages in samadhi in the caves of Viralimalai where peacocks dance.
nuance: ஏக வடிவம் அதன் சொரூபமதாக உறைவது சிவயோகம்: Sivayoga as seeing all things abiding as one form, which is pervasion turned into a practice. The three malas are named exactly (ஆணவ மாயை கருமம்), and the path is to be had in a guru's tradition (உபதேச குருபர சம்ப்ரதாயமொடு).

reading: The poet describes lovemaking in detail and asks whether, before his youth turns to age, he will come to know and gain Murugan's feet. The praise tells of Rama's army of bears and monkeys, Lanka shaken and Ravana's ten heads falling like palm fruit, Krishna who kicked down the marudu trees, and asks Murugan at Viralimalai to take the poet, the son who worships him gladly as Kanda, into hereditary loving service.
nuance: இளமை கிழம்படு முன்: the urgency is time, to reach the feet before youth becomes age. வழிவழி அன்புசெய் தொண்டு: servitude by succession, the வழியடிமை of other songs.

tamil: கரிபு ராரி காமாரி திரிபு ராரி தீயாடி
கரவு தாச னாசாரி பரசு பாணி பானாளி
பரம யோகி மாயோகி பரிய ராஜ டாசூடி
பரத மாடி கானாடி பரவ யோதி காதீத
சுருதி யாடி தாதாவி வெருவி யோட மூதேவி
சுழல வேலை தநமுள அழுத ளாவி வாய்பாறி
திகிரி மாதி ராவார திகிரி சாய வேதாள
செருவி னாடு வானீப கருணை மேரு வேபார
reading: The first half is a chain of Siva's names, the elephant's foe, Tripura's foe, Kama's foe, the dancer in fire, lord of Kailasa, skull-bearer, great yogi, wearer of matted hair, the knower beyond words, rider of the bull, dancer in the forest, ending with a plea for grace and the city of supreme knowledge. The praise shows Brahma fleeing, Meru whirling, Sura dying, the world-rim hill tilting and vultures and ghouls dancing on the battlefield, and names Murugan the Meru of compassion at Viraliyur.
nuance: The plea is almost wholly epithets of Siva (கரிபுராரி காமாரி திரிபுராரி தீயாடி ... பசுவேறி), as if Murugan were addressed as Siva himself, or Siva first praised and then asked. Which is meant, and what பரம ஞான வூர்பூத asks for, is unclear.

reading: The poet describes women's eyes as Kama's weapons that carry off young men's lives, running to the earrings, sharp as sword and spear at the corners, Yama's messengers, rivals of the blue lily, and says that because Murugan once appeared and saved his servant from the delusion that wears endless blame, he will never forget his power. The praise names the goddess in her many forms and the six Krittika mothers who reared Kumara, and Murugan who taught the true meaning of the Upanishads and Vedas to Siva of Kailasa, at Viralimalai where Siva worship and giving never fail.
nuance: Unusually the song gives thanks rather than asking: நீ தோற்றி முன் நாளும் அடிமையை ஈடேற்றுதலால் உன் வலிமையை மறவேனே, a past rescue remembered, perhaps the same as the Vayalur call in 572. வேலின் முனை கடை யமதூதர்: the eye is Death's servant, a classical figure. The teaching of Siva is of Upanishad and Veda meaning, not explicitly Om.

tamil: கொடாதவனை யேபு கழ்ந்து குபேரனென வேமொ ழிந்து
எடாதசுமை யேசு மந்து எணாதகலி யால்மெ லிந்து
சுடாததன மான கொங்கை களாலிதய மேம யங்கி
கெடாததவ மேம றைந்து கிலேசமது வேமி குந்து
தொடாய்மறலி யேநி யென்ற சொலாகியது னாவ ருங்கொல்
நடாதசுழி மூல விந்து நளாவிவிளை ஞான நம்ப
படாதகுளிர் சோலை யண்ட மளாவியுயர் வாய்வ ளர்ந்து
விடாதுமழை மாரி சிந்த அநேகமலர் வாவி பொங்கு
reading: The poet confesses praising the man who never gives as if he were Kubera, fawning and wandering in vain, bearing burdens, wasted by poverty, without seeking Murugan's grace to end it, and his heart deluded by women's breasts; he asks whether, before his worthless body and life ache and die, Murugan's tongue will say 'Death, do not touch him'. The praise names Murugan son of the mother who bore the seven worlds, the lord of knowledge born where the bindu meets the root whorl, at Viralimalai of rain-fed groves and flowering pools.
nuance: கொடாதவனையே புகழ்ந்து குபேரனெனவே மொழிந்து: the poet's begging songs to misers, a confession of the court poet's trade. தொடாய் மறலியே நீ: the plea at death is for a single spoken word from Murugan to Death. நடாதசுழி மூல விந்து names the kundalini centre in the praise.

reading: The poet lists the courtesans' arts in a string of names: wholly of maya, endless schemers, eyes that saw through lives, who melt even sages with laughter, who cry 'come, come', rouse desire, quarrel when not paid, drink themselves wild, and steal without counting sin, and asks whether a bond with these women of low conduct who sell their breasts is fitting. The praise tells of the child Krishna drinking the cowherd women's milk, curd and ghee, tied to the mortar and beaten by Yasoda until he cried, whose flute calls back the herds, as uncle of Murugan of Vayalur, at Viralimalai.
nuance: ஈயாத போதில் அறப் பிணக்கிகள் and விலைத் தனத்தியர்: money is named twice. The list form (each name ending -கள், -கிகள்) is a set piece of abuse. The Krishna story is told with unusual tenderness, his ears held as he weeps.

reading: The poet says that though he is a great sinner walking maya's twisted way, with infatuation, desire and anger unceasing, Murugan is now his mother and father; he has not studied the four Vedas or the Agamas, so that his days not pass in vain he asks for the teaching of knowledge beyond the thirty-six. The praise names the child adorned with fragrant sandal, Murugan of Vayalur and Viralimalai, the six-faced son of the lord of ghouls and goblins, foe of Sura, lord of the gods.
nuance: ஆறாறு மீதில் ஞானோபதேசம்: teaching beyond the six times six, the thirty-six tattvas of Saiva doctrine. The poet's lack of learning (நான் ஓதினேனும் இலை) is made the ground of the plea, not a bar to it.

tamil: மேக மெனுங்குழல் சாய்த்திரு கோக னகங்கொடு கோத்தணை
மேகலை யுந்தனி போய்த்தனி யேகர ணங்களு மாய்க்கயல்
கோகில மென்றெழ போய்க்கனி வாயமு துண்டுரு காக்களி
மோகர துந்துமி யார்ப்ப விராலி விலங்கலின் வீட்டதில்
மூதிசை முன்பொரு காற்றட மேருவை யம்பினில் வீழ்த்திய
ஆக மடிந்திட வேற்கொடு சூரனை வென்றடல் போய்த்தணி
ஆதி யிளந்தலை காத்தர சாள அவன்சிறை மீட்டவ
reading: The poet describes lovemaking, hair loosened, girdle slipping, eyes closing, cries like peacock, quail and cuckoo, and says that even if he sleeps exhausted on the breasts after union he will not forget Murugan's lotus feet. The praise names Murugan dwelling on the hill of Viralimalai with drums sounding, worshipped by the three worlds and praised by the goddess who once felled Meru with an arrow, who killed Sura with the vel, freed the gods from prison and resettled the worlds.
nuance: துயில் கூரினும் அம்புயதாள் துணை மறவேனே: the song does not ask to leave the embrace but vows remembrance of the feet within it. It may be read as hyperbole of devotion or as a different stance from songs that ask to be freed from women.

title: விராலிமலை
theme: The last song at Viralimalai (விராலிமலை, 2 of 2): drowned in the maya of women who deceive the body, the poet asks when Murugan will come running as guard before Yama's messengers bind his legs with their rope; the praise centres on Uma, one with Brahma, Vishnu and Siva, who gave Murugan.
source_issues: Chapter 56 is a single song, the remainder of the run under விராலிமலை.

reading: The poet says that, sinking in the maya of women whose breasts sway like Meru and who deceive the body, he has a fool's understanding, and asks on what day Murugan will come running as his guard to see his servant, so that Yama's messengers do not come and drag him with a rope bound tight on his legs. The praise names Uma, in whom Brahma, Vishnu and Siva the dancer of the burning ground are one, the trident-bearing virgin, great mother and Gauri, who gave Murugan, and ends at the grove-filled town of Viralimalai where the peacock roams.
nuance: காலில் இறுக ... இழாதே: Death's men bind the legs, not the neck, and drag. காவல் என விரைய ஓடி: Murugan is asked to run, the urgency of the plea at the hour of death. ஆதி மறையவனும் மாலும் ... அரனும் இவர் ஒன்றதான ஆயி: the praise makes Uma the one in whom the three gods are united.

title: விநாயகமலை - பிள்ளையார்பட்டி
theme: A song at Vinayakamalai, Pillaiyarpatti (விநாயகமலை - பிள்ளையார்பட்டி): a litany of salutations to Murugan by his names, born in Saravana, son of Uma, root of this world and the next, asking only for grace, with praise of the vel that shook the worlds and of Vishnu and Brahma worshipping his feet.
source_issues: Song 584: unflagged garble செர்ருபா (line 5), probably ஸ்வரூபா.
The heading joins two names, விநாயகமலை and பிள்ளையார்பட்டி; the song itself names only விநாயக மலை.

tamil: சரவண ஜாதா நமோநம கருணைய தீதா நமோநம
தருணக தீரா நமோநம நிருபமர் வீரா நமோநம
பரம செர்ருபா நமோநம சுரர்பதி பூபா நமோநம
பகவதி பாலா நமோநம இகபர மூலா நமோநம
இரவியு மாகாச பூமியும் விரவிய தூளேற வானவ
றிடர்பட மாமேரு பூதர மிடிபட வேதா னிசாசர
மரகத ஆகார ஆயனு மிரணிய ஆகார வேதனும்
மயிலுறை வாழ்வே விநாயக மலையுறை வோலா மகீதர
reading: A song of salutations: the poet bows again and again (நமோநம) to Murugan as born in Saravana, lotus-footed, young and valiant, lord of the world, supreme form, king of the gods, wearer of fragrant kadamba, child of Uma, Kali and Bhagavati, root of this world and the next, and asks for grace. The praise shows the vel thrown so that dust rose to the sun, the seven seas cried out, Meru was shattered and the demons fell, and Vishnu, Brahma and Isa worshipping his feet, the lord on the peacock dwelling on Vinayakamalai, support of the forest people.
nuance: The plea is a litany in the form of a mantra of praise (நமோநம repeated twelve times), with no confession. இகபர மூலா: root of this world and the next. சமதளவூரா and வசுவெனும் ஆகார ஈசன் are not clear to me.

title: திருச்செங்கோடு
theme: First songs at Tiruchengodu (திருச்செங்கோடு, 1 of 2), also called Nagagiri: the poet confesses his infatuation with courtesans and their arts, his begging songs to hard-hearted patrons, and a life of births bound by malam, and asks for the feet, for union with the devotees and for the wisdom of Agastya; the praise names Murugan the teacher of Siva and gives the Ramayana in brief.
structure_note: Short courtesan songs in the same metre (585 to 587), longer courtesan songs (590 to 594, 597), birth and malam (593, 595, 596), begging from patrons (589), union with devotees (588), and two short songs on Nagagiri (598, 599), the last in long syllables only.
source_issues: Song 590: one corrupt character in வயலு஡ரா (line 14), probably வயலூரா; also பாவிகளள் (line 3) with a doubled letter.
Song 594: one corrupt character in வயலு஡ரா (line 12).
Song 597: unflagged garble பல்ருடே (line 6).
Songs 597 to 599 name the shrine நாகமலை / நாககிரி, another name for Tiruchengodu, not the heading's name.

reading: The poet asks whether, instead of coming with love to bow at Murugan's feet, he will keep thinking of women whose eyes are poison-filled lotuses and whose hair is full of bees, and wander deluded and fighting without end. The praise names Murugan son of the dancer of the hall, wearer of kadamba, whose vel ends the births of those who come and bow, and asks him to come with his red cock wherever the poet goes calling 'Kanda', at Tiruchengodu of red paddy and lotus.
nuance: சென்றே இடங்கள் கந்தா எனும்பொ(து) ... வரவேணும்: a plea for the god's company in daily wandering, not only at death. ஐம்பூதம் ஒன்ற நினையாமல் is unclear: perhaps 'not thinking of the five elements becoming one'.

reading: The poet asks that he not wither away, his life bursting with crowded desire, over women whose palms ache from playing ball, whose garlanded hair and lotus faces draw singing bees and whose breasts do harm, but that Murugan give his grace. The praise names Kanda, son of Hara and nephew of Mukunda, the one who split the hill, bridegroom of the celestial maiden, wearing a kadamba garland on his strong shoulders, at Tiruchengodu.
nuance: The song is short and conventional; the women are pictured at play (பந்தாடி அங்கை நொந்தார்), an image from love poetry. கன்றா விலங்கல் ஒன்றாறு கண்ட and the eight elephants sleeping at Tiruchengodu are hard to divide.

reading: The poet asks for grace so that he does not decline, forgetting Murugan's flower-decked feet, among women whose spear-like eyes defeat Kama's arrows and bewilder all who see them. The praise names Murugan nephew of Vishnu of the discus and conch, Kumaresa who stands as part of the devotees who melt in song and true friendship, joy of Siva who dances in the hall, at Tiruchengodu of red paddy.
nuance: நண்போதும் அன்பர் பங்காகி நின்ற குமரேசா: Murugan stands as a share of his devotees, close to them rather than above them.

reading: The poet, whose mind is confused and deluded in the way of union with women with carp eyes and sweet words, asks when he will be one with the devotees who think to lay their speech, knowledge, life and feeling on Murugan's lotus feet as a garland. The praise shows the hill split, the gods resettled and Indra's city flourishing, the demon armies of elephants, chariots, horses and foot ruined and the sea crying out, at Tiruchengodu of rich fields.
nuance: உரையையும் அறிவையும் உயிரையும் உணர்வையும் ... உரவாடு புனைதர: the whole self, speech, mind, life and feeling, is offered as a garland at the feet, and the goal is the company of devotees (அடியரொடு ஒன்றாக).

reading: The poet confesses going from place to place, begging and accepting, sinking in the fire of hunger, singing paltry poems shaped to the rules of Tamil grammar to iron-hearted men who show no pity, faltering, trembling and cringing in praise, and asks whether such a one can gain love for Murugan. The praise, in heavy wordplay, names Murugan who gave his arms to the hunter girl, the vel at Tiruchengodu, who grants joy to those who reach, feel, melt, bow and know him.
nuance: இயல் தண் தமிழ் நூலின் உடம்பாட்டுடன் பாட்டு இயம்பா: the poet's skill in correct Tamil is spent on patrons who do not pity. The rhyme runs in clusters (இறுங்கார்க் கிரும்பார்க் குநெஞ்சார்க் கிரங்கார்க்கு), which makes the splitting of the words partly uncertain.

reading: The poet asks not to perish in the sidelong glances of sinful women who melt thought and sight with words sweet as strained cane juice; he says he longs to receive the teaching that turns him away, and asks Murugan to say 'do not fear' so that he gives up the evil his mind plans by its deeds. The praise names the vel that cuts down the demon armies and the teacher through whom liberation bears fruit at once for those few who know how to call on his feet, at the towered Tiruchengodu.
nuance: விலக்கும் போதகம்: the teaching asked for is one that turns him back from women. அஞ்சேல் என: the plea is for the assuring word of the Lord, a common gesture (the hand of fearlessness) put into speech.

reading: The poet asks not to wander in the lewd, sorrowful trade of women who show rolling eyes and their breasts to many, deceive, and give the cane-sweet juice of their lips, and asks whether Murugan, whom Brahma, Vishnu and Siva the slayer of Death could not see, will protect him, let him hear the sweet words of the meaning, and look on him with grace. The praise names Murugan who drove out Sura hiding in deceit, who stands in the company of devotees in the kura groves, who wooed the hunter girl in the millet field, at Tiruchengodu in the Kongu country.
nuance: தொழில் பண்டாட்டம்: the courtesan's life is called a trade, a bargaining. பொருள் கொண்டாட்டத்து இன்ப வாக்யம்: perhaps the teaching sentence (vakya) of the true meaning, asked as a gift to the ear; the phrase is not certain.

reading: After a long head-to-foot portrait of courtesans who sell themselves, the poet says that, leaping into union with them, he has caught diseases and sunk in birth, and asks for the knowledge by which his deeds flee, so that coming the great way of bowing to the kadamba-garlanded feet his burning ends, he drinks the sea of nectar, approaches the coral-red form and chants 'radiant Muruga' with love. The praise names the goddess in many forms, Murugan the teacher and destroyer of Sura, Vishnu's deeds against Hiranya, Vali, Kumbhakarna and Ravana and his sport with the cowherd girls, Valli's beauty, and Tiruchengodu.
nuance: கோல விலை மாதர் and கலியநோய்கள் கொண்டே: the courtesans are named by their price and the poet names disease caught from them, a rare literal consequence in these songs. அமுத வாரி here is the nectar of grace, not Tirumular's yogic fluid.

reading: The poet says he never once thought to cut the rope of false birth, and, wounded, doubting and troubled, became a vessel of desire for cruel lotus-eyed women; he asks for good nature and the anklet-bearing red lotus feet, so that he may serve and prostrate at Tiruchengodu. The praise tells of Siva flaying the elephant to delight Uma, and of Murugan who explained the sense of the word 'thou' (தொம்பதம்) to Sambhu, the beautiful lord on the red peak.
nuance: சம்புவுக்குத் தொம்பதத்துப் பண்பு உரைத்து: தொம்பதம் is the 'tvam' of the Vedantic sentence tat tvam asi, so the familiar story of Murugan teaching Siva is here told in Vedantic terms rather than as the meaning of Om. The opening lines (பொங்கி முக்கிச் சங்கை பற்றிச் சிங்கி ஒத்த) are uncertain in sense.

tamil: மந்தக் கடைக்கண் காட்டுவர் கந்தக் குழற்பின் காட்டுவர்
வஞ்சத் திரக்கங் காட்டுவர் நெஞ்சிற் பொருத்தங் காட்டுவர்
சந்தப் பொருப்புங் காட்டுவர் உந்திச் சுழிப்புங் காட்டுவர்
சண்டைப் பிணக்குங் காட்டுவர் பண்டிட் டொடுக்கங் காட்டுவர்
பந்தித் தெருக்கந் தோட்டினை யிந்துச் சடைக்கண் சூட்டுமை
பைம்பொற் பதக்கம் பூட்டிய அன்பற் கெதிர்க்குங் கூட்டலர்
கொந்திற் புனத்தின் பாட்டிய லந்தக் குறப்பெண் டாட்டொடு
குன்றிற் கடப்பந் தோட்டலர் மன்றற் ப்ரசித்தங் கோட்டிய
reading: In a refrain of 'they show' (காட்டுவர்), the poet lists the courtesans' displays, the slow sidelong look, the back of the scented hair, turmeric-gold skin, false pity, agreement of heart, firm attachment, breasts, navel, conch-like neck, quarrels and pretended modesty, and asks whether he will stop showing longing for them. The praise names Murugan the guru whom his father worships, who drove off the enemies of a devotee who had adorned him with a golden pendant, who embraced the hunter girl, at Tiruchengodu in Kongu.
nuance: The refrain makes the whole courtship a show (காட்டுவர்), so that the poet's own feeling (இரங்கம் காட்டுவது) is the last display in the list. The devotee with the golden pendant (பைம்பொன் பதக்கம் பூட்டிய அன்பன்) is an allusion I cannot identify.

reading: In packed, clipped syllables the poet seems to say that, leaving true support for false, he cannot climb out of the sea of births of constant sorrow, maddened for honey-sweet women, while those who cherished Murugan's golden anklets came later and gained the good portion. The praise names Murugan of Tiruchengodu, lord of the millet-hill girl Valli, wearer of vetchi flowers, the pure one, the pearl, the lord of liberation.
nuance: மெய்ச்சார்வு அற்றே பொய்ச்சார்வு உற்றே: losing the support of truth for the support of the false is the clearest phrase. The song is a feat of doubled consonants (செச்சா லிச்சா லத்தே றிச்சே) and most of it can be divided several ways.

tamil: வருத்தங் காண நாடிய குணத்தன் பான மாதரு
மலக்கங் கூடி யேயின வுயிர்க்குஞ் சேத மாகிய
பெருத்தும் பாவ நீடிய மலத்தின் தீமை கூடிய
பெறத்தந் தாள வேயுயர் சுவர்க்கஞ் சேர வேயருள்
இரத்தம் பாய மேனிக ளுரத்துஞ் சாடி வேல்கொடு
இசைக்குந் தாள மேளமெ தனத்தந் தான தானன்
திருத்தன் பாக வேயொரு மயிற்கொண் டாடி யேபுகழ்
திரட்சங் கோடை வாவிகள் மிகுத்துங் காவி சூழ்தரு
reading: The poet asks not to bind himself to women whose nature seeks to cause pain and to men who die harming others, and that, with birth full of sin and the evil of malam ended, Murugan give his two feet, rule him and tell him the sharp strength of grace so he reaches the high heaven. The praise shows the vel slaying the demons with bodies bathed in blood, the ghost hosts beating time with drums, and Murugan rejoicing on the peacock at Tiruchengodu of pools and lilies.
nuance: சுவர்க்கம் சேர: heaven is named as the goal, less common than release in these songs. The first lines (மலக்கங் கூடியே இன உயிர்க்கும் சேதமாகிய மரிக்கும் பேர்கள்) are uncertain.

reading: The poet lists courtesans who are venomous as cobras, whose eyes cut like swords, who call to anyone at all, dance along the streets, rouse hopes, loosen hair and sari and glitter with scent, and drown men in maya, and asks whether, caught in lust, he must wander in births of malam without the life of serving Murugan. The praise tells the Ramayana in order, Dasaratha's son guarding the sage's sacrifice, the stone made woman by his foot, the bow broken at Mithila, the exile, Vali and Ravana slain, and names Murugan the teacher of knowledge on the great Naga hill.
nuance: மலச் சனனம்: births are named as the work of malam. The Ramayana sequence in the praise is unusually complete. நெருவைப்பதி is a place name I cannot identify.

reading: A short song: the poet asks not to draw near Death and not to be born again on earth, and to be given the honey-nectar of the wisdom of the virtuous Agastya. The praise names Murugan hard for Vishnu and Brahma to reach, never parted from the great ascetics, the meaning of the four Vedas, the lord of Nagagiri.
nuance: சீல அகத்திய ஞான: probably the knowledge of Agastya, whom Murugan taught (see 28); it could also be read as 'the knowledge within' (அகத்து இய). The song asks for knowledge as the escape from death and birth.

reading: A song made almost wholly of long syllables: through strings of vocatives the poet seems to ask the lord of the earth to protect his life in danger, lest he, a sinner, fall into the burning ground. The praise is a chain of names, Kama-like in beauty, the playful child, wearer of kadamba, the son, the Vel, the flower, the king, the god, lord of the gods.
nuance: யாபத்து எனது ஆவி ... காவாய் ... ஈமத்து உகலாமோ: 'protect my life in danger; should I fall into the pyre?' is the only clear plea. The song is a metrical feat (தாமா தாமா லாபா லோகா) in which nearly every word can be split another way.

title: திருச்செங்கோடு
theme: Last songs at Thiruchengode (திருச்செங்கோடு, 2 of 2), the serpent hill: the poet asks not to fall with his impure body into hell, to be freed from the tangle of wealth-lust and women, and from the illusion that a bubble-like life with wife, sons and house will last for aeons; he gives thanks for the grace that set him to sing the Thiruppugazh, and asks Murugan to come on the peacock to the battle in which his servant defeats Death.
structure_note: Six songs. 600 and 604 are in dense, clipped rhythms whose word divisions are often unsure. 602 is a thanksgiving for the book, 603 a meditation on impermanence, 605 a death-hour plea that names Arunai although it stands under Thiruchengode. The shrine is named as சர்ப்பகிரி, பணிசயிலம், the serpent hill.
source_issues: Song 605 names Arunai (அருணையில் ஒருவிசை வரவேணும்) though it is grouped under Thiruchengode; the praise's பணி சயில, serpent hill, fits Thiruchengode.

reading: The poet asks whether he, a servant, should drive this impure body about and fall into the fiery hell; the opening lines, which seem to describe a mountain, a great tree heavy with flowers and fruit and a place he should not speak of, are too broken by the rhythm for a sure reading. The praise names the leaping deer and the sage of the Upanishads (Valli's birth), Murugan's twelve shoulders that embraced the hunters' parrot-like girl sweet as honey and nectar, and the emerald and gold peacock that carried him against the demon clans.
nuance: மலவுடல் நடத்தி எரிகொள் நிரயத்தின் இடை அடிமை விழலாமோ is the one clear plea: the body is called impure (மல) and the fear is of hell, not of rebirth. The praise's தத்து கவன வரிணத்து உபநிட விதத்து முநி seems to allude to Valli's birth from a deer to a sage. The first eight lines run syllables together (அத்து கிரினலது ரத்து அலனவள கத்து ...) and I cannot divide them with confidence.

reading: The poet confesses that, gripped by desire for wealth and looking on, he became kin to parrot-like women and was distracted in a loveless company, his mind running to clasp their shoulders; he asks whether he will call his mind back, cut the tangle of a false life, gain firm and beautiful speech, praise Murugan and adorn him with vetchi flowers. The praise names Murugan king over kings, holder of the cock and the vel at the serpent hill, and the true word of the right path of reasoning that establishes the tattvas, forty-eight and forty-eight.
nuance: அத்த வேட்கை, desire for wealth (அத்தம்), stands first, before the women. தத்வ நாற்பத்தெட்டு நாற்பத்தெட்டு makes ninety-six, the larger Saiva count of the tattvas; Murugan is the true teaching (சத்ய வாக்யம்) of the logic-shastra that sets them out. கொத்து நூற்றுப் பத்து நாட்ட is unclear to me.

reading: The poet says he will never forget the grace by which Murugan appeared to him and set even him, a small servant, to sing the Thiruppugazh, rich in the sound of beautiful poetry, which devotees in the east, west, south and north recite as a wonder, so that it spread through the world. The praise names the hunter girl who guarded the millet slinging stones at the screaming parrots and whom Murugan embraced, and Murugan as the one who taught the whole of the Vedas' truth and the Supreme to his father, who keeps Shakti on his left side, at the serpent hill.
nuance: This is the book naming itself again: திருப்புகழைச் சிறிது அடியேனும் செப்பென வைத்து, the grace of being set to sing it, and தெரிசித்த, that Murugan showed himself. Here it is already sung in the four directions. மறைநூலின் தத்துவ தற்பரம் முற்றும் உணர்த்திய is the teaching of Siva without naming Om.

reading: The poet says that he lives in the illusion that this life, impermanent as a bubble, in a false hut of a body, with wife, sons, house and friends, is an unshaken greatness that will stand for a crore of aeons, and asks Murugan to think of a way for the love he has set daily on his feet to stay. The praise names Murugan lord of the serpent hill, delight of the three Tamils, nephew of the one with discus and mace, the Brahmin of Kazhi who impaled the dumb arguing Jains, and lord of the hunters' daughter whose chastity never failed.
nuance: புற்புதம், the bubble, and ஒரு கோடி கற்பம், a crore of aeons, set the real span of life against the imagined one; நிட்டை, a steady state, is used ironically of the illusion. தர்க்க சமண் மூகர் மிக்க கழு ஏற வைத்த ஒரு காழி மறையோன் is Sambandar's story told of Murugan.

reading: In a clipped, hammering rhythm the poet describes women whose breasts are bound in green silk bodices worked with gold and likened to lotus buds, praised by young men, and asks not to wander in their stony-hearted, false madness, loving them and being struck; he asks Murugan to teach him with love the word by which he may learn and attain, and to give his victorious anklets. The praise hears the cock crow (குக்குக்குக்), names Murugan the bearer of the cock banner and the life of Kochai, and ends at the high serpent hill.
nuance: பொய்ப் பித்தம், false madness, is the poet's word for the infatuation. கொச்சைப் பதி is a name of Sirkazhi, Sambandar's town, so the praise may again make Murugan Sambandar. The song is built almost entirely of doubled consonants (கற்சித்தச் சுத்தப் பொய்ப்பித்தத்திற் புக்கு), and many divisions, especially in the closing lines on Daksha (தக்ஷப் பற்றுக்கு), are guesses.

reading: The poet asks that, on the day when cruel Death and his army fall as Murugan's stammering servant, who worships his two feet, fights with his grace, Murugan come once to Arunai to see that battle, mounted on the emerald horse with his six faces, many eyes, his shoulders that embraced the hunter girl and his sun-bright banner, while old devotees and the gods praise him on both sides with Tamil and the Vedas. The praise lists Siva's emblems, matted hair, poison, serpents, axe, moon, fire, drum, deer, and the many-mouthed river, names Murugan his son, and ends with the battle against the night-roaming demons.
nuance: The plea reverses the usual fear: the servant himself fights Death (கொடிய மறலியும் அவனது கடகமும் மடிய) with the Lord's grace, and asks Murugan only to come and watch (அமர் காண). அருணையில் ஒருவிசை வரவேணும் names Thiruvannamalai inside a Thiruchengode song; பணி சயில, the serpent hill, is the local name in the praise.

title: கொல்லிமலை
theme: Songs at the Kolli hills (கொல்லிமலை): the poet laments the jasmine-smiling women who took his gold and then said there was none, and asks for the bliss that stands beneath the whole ladder of being, from the one and the two to the Vedas, senses, tattvas, souls and bonds.
structure_note: Two songs: a courtesan song with a play on வல்லி (Valli, creeper) in the praise, and a song built on a counting ladder from one to six.
source_issues: Song 607: one corrupt character in குழலு஡துங் (line 10), read as குழலூதும், 'who plays the flute'.

tamil: கட்ட மன்னு மள்ளல் கொட்டி பண்ணு மைவர்
கற்ற விஞ்ஞை சொல்லி யுற்ற வெண்மை யுள்ளு
இட்ட மெங்ங னல்ல கொட்டி யங்ங னல்கி
எத்து பொய்ம்மை யுள்ள லுற்று மின்மை யுள்ளி
முட்ட வுண்மை சொல்லு செட்டி திண்மை கொள்ள
முத்து வண்ண வல்லி சித்ர வண்ண வல்லி
பட்ட மன்ன வல்லி மட்ட மன்ன வல்லி
பச்சை வன்னி யல்லி செச்சை சென்னி யுள்ள
reading: The poet says that, tending this house of the body where the five senses dwell, he poured out whatever jasmine-smiling women wanted and gave them gold, and they said there was nothing and went; thinking of their deceit and of his own poverty, he asks whether it is right that he should waste away like this. The praise names Murugan as the merchant who came speaking the whole truth, the bridegroom of Valli of pearl colour, of painted colour, of release and heaven, the lord of the Kolli hills, wearing green vanni, lilies and vetchi, rider of the green peacock.
nuance: பொன்னை இல்லை என ஏகி: the gold is given and the women deny it and leave; the poet then dwells on his own lack (இன்மை உள்ளி). ஐவர்கட்கு மன்னும் இல்லம், the house where the five live, is the body. செட்டி, the merchant, is a disguise of Murugan in the Valli story; the wordplay on வல்லி runs through the praise. The opening lines (கட்ட மன்னும் அள்ளல் கொட்டி பண்ணும்) and கற்ற விஞ்ஞை சொல்லி are hard to divide.

reading: The poet asks for the state that stands as the shoreless ocean of one's own nature and bliss, which is the ancient first, itself one, then the two, the three gunas, the pure four Vedas, the fierce five senses, the six limbs of the Veda, the many sounds, the bonds of soul and pasa, abundant Tamil become music, and all the many lives. The praise names Krishna whose flute melts stones and calls the cattle in distress, Siva who worshipped Murugan as he told the true knowledge, and Murugan who went to Valli's millet field, plundered by Kama's flower arrows, carrying leaf garments, at the Kolli hills.
nuance: The plea is a counting ladder (ஒன்று, இரு பேதங்கள், குண மூ, சதுர் வேதங்கள், புலன் ஓர் ஐந்து, ஆறு அங்கம்) whose end is சொருபாநந்த பெளவம், the sea of the bliss of one's own form, which is all of them and beyond them. பசு பாசங்கள் names two of the three Siddhanta categories. In the praise கைதொழ மெய்ஞ்ஞானஞ்சொல் is the Siva-teaching story; கையன் மிசை யேறும்பன் is unclear to me.

title: ராஜகெம்பீரவளநாட்டு மலை
theme: A song at the hill of Rajagembira Valanadu (ராஜகெம்பீரவளநாட்டு மலை): the poet, wasting with women whose every limb outdoes a thing of beauty and who seek coins, asks for his impurity to be removed and for the vision of the supreme truth in which the soul becomes one; the praise tells the wrecking of Daksha's sacrifice.
source_issues: Song 608: one corrupt character in சென்று஡துகுயில் (line 5), read as சென்றூது குயில், 'the cuckoo that calls in the grove'.

reading: The poet catalogues women whose hair beats the cloud, brow Indra's bow, eyes the arrow, lips fruit, voice the cuckoo, breasts the mountain, waist the drum, hips the serpent's hood and thighs the plantain, who dance in public and come seeking coins, and says he wastes away with them, called a rogue; he asks Murugan to remove his impurity and give the vision of the supreme truth, light-giving, in which the soul becomes one. The praise tells how, when Uma spoke in haste, a hero came to end the great sacrifice: the moon's body was worn away, the sun's teeth knocked out, Agni's hand cut off, Brahma's head fell, Saraswati's nose slipped and Mayan was defeated, while ghouls danced; then the sages called Murugan son and asked for the vision.
nuance: Every line of the confession is built on தோற்ற, 'defeated': each limb outdoes its standard comparison, and the list ends in காசு தேடுகின்றார், women seeking coin. The plea's சீவன் ஒன்றான பரமார்த்த தெரிசனை is union, the soul become one. The sacrifice story (மாமகம், உமை, the punished gods) is Daksha's, with Veerabhadra as the hero (வீரன்); its last lines (முநிவரர் வந்து சேயென்று ஈசநண்பான புருஷார்த்த தெரிசனை தா) are hard to construe.

title: ஞானமலை
theme: Songs at Gnanamalai (ஞானமலை): the poet rejects the diseased, bargaining women of the street who stand beside gamblers and killers, and, mocked by wife, town and kin, asks at death for the feet he was once given, the feet that melted him and gave the experience of yoga.
structure_note: Two songs: 609 a courtesan catalogue, 610 a song of public shame that recalls an earlier gift of the feet at this shrine.

reading: The poet lists gamblers and killers and women greedy for money, filthy, pallid and blue-faced, aching with colic and rheumatism, sinful and slanderous, who boast in the street, call 'come', name their price by the measure and the pot and jut their chins in pride, and asks whether relationship with them can be right. The praise names the vel that dried the seven seas to mire while Vedic sages, children, women and Brahmins cried out, the son of Sivakami and Abhirami, and Murugan at Gnanamalai with the daughter of Narayana.
nuance: சூது கொலைகாரர் ஆசைபண மாதர் sets gamblers, killers and money-loving women in one list, and the women's diseases (சோகை, சூலை, வாதம்) are named as warning. நாழி தாழி விலை கூறி: they price themselves like grain or a pot of goods. நாரண சுவாமி ஈனும் மகள் is the tradition that Murugan's consorts are Vishnu's daughters.

tamil: மனையவள் நகைக்க வூரி னனைவரு நகைக்க லோக
மனமது சலிப்ப நாய னுளமது சலிப்ப யாரும்
அனைவரு மிழிப்ப நாடு மனவிருள் மிகுத்து நாடி
றடியனு நினைத்து நாளு முடலுயிர் விடுத்த போது
தனதன தனத்த தான எனமுர சொலிப்ப வீணை
தடிநிக ரயிற்க டாவி யசுரர்க ளிறக்கு மாறு
எனைமன முருக்கி யோக அநுபுதி யளித்த பாத
இமையவர் துதிப்ப ஞான மலையுறை குறத்தி பாக
reading: The poet describes how his wife, the town and the world's women laugh at him, his father and kin are troubled, and everyone babbles abuse, and how his mind's darkness grows until he asks 'is this the welfare I gained by taking a body?'; he asks that when his life leaves the body Murugan come near and give the feet he gave before. The praise names the vel that blazed in battle against the demons with drums, veena and Vedas sounding, the feet that melted his mind and gave the experience of yoga, Uma's son, and Murugan at Gnanamalai with the hunter girl and Indra's daughter.
nuance: The shame is told as an ever-widening circle: wife, town, women, father, kin, everyone (அனைவரும் இழிப்ப). முன் அளித்த பாதம் and எனை மனம் உருக்கி யோக அநுபுதி அளித்த பாத point back to a gift of the feet already received, which tradition places at Gnanamalai. நாயன் உளமது சலிப்ப, 'the lord's heart troubled', is unclear: the lord may be the poet's master or the Lord himself.

title: ஊதிமலை
theme: Songs at Oothimalai (ஊதிமலை): the poet, ignorant of the Siva Agamas and given to the desire for women, asks for mercy, firm knowledge and instruction; the praise makes Murugan the teacher who spoke the Vedic mantra into Siva's ear and the light that is the life of the letter Om.

tamil: ஆதிமக மாயி யம்பை தேவிசிவ னார்ம கிழ்ந்த
ஆதரவ தாய்வ ருந்தி யாதியரு ணேச ரென்று
பூதமது வான வைந்து பேதமிட வேய லைந்து
பூணுமுலை மாதர் தங்கள் ஆசைவகை யேநி னைந்து
நீதயவ தாயி ரங்கி நேசவரு ளேபு ரிந்து
நேர்மைசிவ னார்தி கழ்ந்த காதிலுரை வேத மந்த்ர
ஓதுமறை யாக மஞ்சொல் யோகமது வேபு ரிந்து
ஊனுமுயி ராய்வ ளர்ந்து ஓசையுடன் வாழ்வு தந்த
reading: The poet asks to be able to worship Murugan, the son given by the primal Mahamayi Ambai who delighted Siva, as the Lord of grace; he confesses that he has wandered through the five elements without knowing the full Siva Agamas, thinking only of the desires of women and wanting pleasure, and asks Murugan to pity him so that the path of right may shine. The praise names Murugan as the one who spoke the Vedic mantra into Siva's ear and came on the blue peacock, and who, to end the karma of those who practise the yoga taught by Veda and Agama, grew as their flesh and life and gave them life with sound, at Oothimalai.
nuance: The fault named is ignorance of the Agamas (பூரண சிவாகமங்கள் அறியாதே) as much as lust. சிவனார் திகழ்ந்த காதில் உரை வேத மந்த்ர is the Siva-teaching story as a whisper in the ear. ஊனும் உயிராய் வளர்ந்து ஓசையுடன் வாழ்வு தந்த may play on the shrine's name (ஊதி, 'blowing'): the Lord as the body, life and sound of the yogi; the sense is uncertain.

reading: The poet asks not to think in his heart of the petty pleasure of women with combed, heavy hair buns, deceitful and charming, but for Murugan to destroy his weak mind, give firm knowledge and stand gracious where he tells Murugan's deeds. The praise names Murugan nephew of Vishnu, the father of four-faced Brahma; the guru son of the Lord; the dancer to drum syllables who gives mercy to the soul that leaves the inert body; and the bright light who is the restraint of the recited letters, the mercy to devotees and the breath of the letter Om, at Oothi hill.
nuance: கோழை மனத்தைக் கெடுத்து வன்புல ஞான குணத்தைக் கொடுத்து: a weak mind exchanged for a firm knowledge. ஓம் எனும் எழுத்துக்கு உயிர்ப்பும் என் சுடர் ஒளியோனே makes Murugan the breath of Om, and நாத நிலைக்குள் the state of nada. The lines on the trouble at the sacrifice (நாடு மகத்து எற்கு இடுக்கண்) and on the soul leaving the body (சடத்தில் நின்று உயிரான துறத்தற்கு) are hard to construe.

title: குருடிமலை
theme: A song at Kurudimalai (குருடிமலை): the poet says he cannot understand the ways of poets who flatter men of the world as Vishnu and patch together stolen verses for the ignorant; the praise is of the flooding river at the hill.

reading: The poet describes poets who cry out praising worldly men as the dark cloud riding on Garuda or a lotus jewel, slip their names into their verses, hunt through old sayings, steal and knead a measure of them, and sing poems that enter only the ears of the ignorant, and says he does not know how to grasp even a little of what such poets say. The praise pictures the river called Madhuram flooding both banks and toppling agil and marutham trees where wild goats graze, and names Murugan of Kurudimalai who rides the peacock to grind the northern peak to chaff, Kumara the guru, the sun to darkness.
nuance: The target is the patron-poet's trade: praising a man as Vishnu (கருடன் மிசைவரு கரிய புயல்), inserting his name (அவர்பெயர் செருகி), and stealing from older poems (திருடி ஒருபடி நெருடி). Whether 'I do not know their ways' is irony or confession is not said; the song has no explicit plea, which is unusual.

title: தென்சேரிகிரி
theme: Songs at Thenserigiri (தென்சேரிகிரி): the poet asks to be freed from courtesans who give their lips and take a man's wealth and life, and from the infatuation of dancing women, and asks for the meaning once told to Siva; the praise dwells on Krishna's flute, the gopis' clothes and Kamsa.
source_issues: Song 615: one corrupt character in வயலு஡ரா (line 15), read as வயலூரா, 'lord of Vayalur'.

reading: The poet gives the women's own words, offered to whoever comes, 'here, the one who cannot bear your passion', 'here, take my sweet lips', with eyes dancing and desire melting, and says they take every possession and life without hesitation; he asks for the cool grace that frees him from the sea they call the good of music and lovemaking. The praise names Krishna who took conch and discus, followed the cattle playing the bamboo flute and climbed the tree with the clothes of the women, Brahma bewildered, the gods freed from prison and the demons beaten, at Thenserigiri.
nuance: As in 21, the courtesans' speech is quoted (இங்கே வருக, இந்தா), and the charge is that they strip a man of wealth and life alike (பொருள் உயிர்கள் ... பறிகொளும்). சங்கீத கலவி நலம் என்று ஓதும் உததி: the ocean they call the delight of song and love.

reading: The poet lists women's cajoling speech, eyes, hair heavy with flowers, breasts like Meru, the posture of their display and slender waists, as they dance with many, like peacocks, and asks Murugan, to free him from the delusion of desire for them, to grant the meaning he told Siva of old, from the ancient Veda, ending all arguments. The praise names the lord of Vayalur's fields, nephew of the cloud-dark one who kicked Kamsa, the six-faced god holding the red cock, at Thenseri hill with its golden walls touched by the moon.
nuance: மருள், delusion, is what the meaning cures, and the meaning is the one Murugan told உமை பங்காளர், Siva, the Siva-teaching story. தர்க்கங்கள் அற: the knowledge ends disputation. மன்றாடிக்கு அன்பு தரு may mean the one dear to the dancer in the hall, Siva, and is unsure.

title: கொங்கணகிரி
theme: A song at Konganagiri (கொங்கணகிரி): a litany of requests, for control of the senses, love in Tamil praise, knowledge from austerity and the way to release, a mind turned from women to Murugan, and worldly honour besides.

reading: The song is a string of prayers, each ending 'grant': a mind like Ganapati's that has driven off the five senses and a thought beyond night and day; a mind to praise Murugan with love in the Tamil that grows on earth; the knowledge of austerity, so that as a servant he gains release and a way to the moon-space; a grand palanquin and splendour esteemed in the eight directions; a mind that turns from the pleasure of women to think of Murugan; and the meaning that a father gained by grace on the southern bank in Kongu. It ends with Murugan, younger brother of the elephant-faced one, at Konganagiri.
nuance: A rare song with no confession and no myth, only petitions (அருள்வாயே eight times). It asks for both release (அடிமை முத்திபெற, சந்திர வெளிக்கு வழி, the moon-space of the yogi) and a palanquin with worldly honour (தண்டிகை கனப் பவுசு), without seeing a conflict. கொங்கில் உயிர் பெற்று வளர் தென்கரையில் அப்பர் அருள் may allude to a Kongu miracle of restoring life; I cannot identify it, and the மண்டலிகர் line is also unclear.

title: தீர்த்தமலை
theme: A song at Theerthamalai (தீர்த்தமலை): the poet rebukes his own mind, which neither melts at song nor fears the coming of Death, and urges it to cling to Murugan; the praise tells Siva's deeds and Sambandar's ordeals by water and fire.

reading: Addressing his own mind, the poet says it does not melt at song, does not melt on hearing, does not melt watching the road by which Death comes, does not desire the release that is the Lord's grace, cannot praise with the tip of the tongue, and will not leave the cage of the body that refuses the good path or see the course of fate written on the leaf; then he says, 'Hear one word: will you not cling to Murugan, who is easy for devotees and removes the two karmas of those who praise him?' The praise names Siva who bent the northern mountain with the serpent for a string, burned the three cities, kicked Death, burned Kama to ash, ruined the sacrifice and set a goat's head on its lord, and Murugan as the guru who sent the palm leaf against the river, showed it unburnt in fire and impaled the angry Jains, at Theerthamalai.
nuance: The refrain of negatives (உருகிலை, அறிகிலை, விழைகிலை, விடுகிலை) is spoken to the mind as a separate party, the நெஞ்சு of love poetry turned to devotion. ஏட்டின் விதி, fate written on the leaf, is set beside Death's road. The praise names Sambandar's ordeals at Madurai: சீட்டை எழுதி வை யாற்றில் எதிருற ஓட்டி, அழல் பசை காட்டி, the leaf that swam upstream and did not burn.

title: கநகமலை
theme: A song at Kanagamalai (கநகமலை): the poet asks to give up the bewildering pleasure of women and to see Murugan's faces, shining like sun and moon, so that all sorrow leaves him and he bows at his feet.

reading: The poet asks whether he will give up the one thing he longs for on the wrong path, the world's pleasure that follows women and bewilders him until his mind aches as a fool's, and asks that, seeing Murugan's exalted faces shining as if sun and moon stood full together, all his inner sorrows go and he praise with love and bow at the pair of feet. The praise names the Shakti vel that made the demons fade, the clan mountains shake and the seas tremble, Murugan coming with jingling ornaments while Gauri fondles him, the kadamba-chested younger brother of the elephant-faced god, at Kanagagiri.
nuance: The cure asked for is a sight: பரிதி மதி நிறைய நின்றஃதென ஒளிரும் உனது படிவ முகம், the faces bright as sun and moon together. கருணை பொழி கிருபை முந்தப் பரிவினொடு கவுரி கொஞ்ச: the praise includes a tender scene of the mother fondling the child.

title: புகழிமலை
theme: A song at Pugazhimalai (புகழிமலை): the poet fears drowning in the sea of women, possessions, wife and children, and asks Murugan to come on the peacock with the life of the lotus feet.

reading: The poet asks whether, through women's fragrant hair, lined eyes, faces and young breasts, through the possessions he thinks of, and through wife and children, he will sink and wander in the waves of the sea; he asks Murugan to come before him on the peacock with compassion and give the life of the lotus feet. The praise names Murugan worshipped by Brahma, Vishnu, gods and sages, lord of the Bhoga land with its rivers and groves, who threw the vel that pierced Sura's mountain and dried the sea, at Pugazhimalai, praised by the Tamil sage.
nuance: The list moves from women to wealth (கருது பொருள்) to wife and children (மனைவி மகவு) as one sea, so that household life and courtesans are the same entanglement. தமிழ் முநிவர், the Tamil sage, is probably Agastya.

title: பூம்பறை
theme: A song at Poomparai (பூம்பறை): the poet asks whether a relationship with price-women who speak of kinship and seek out rich houses can be right; the praise names Krishna dancing on the serpent.

reading: The poet describes women with bodies soft as mango shoots who talk of kinship, look for houses where men live well, make friends, smear sandal on their breasts and play until their waists ache, and asks whether a shameless relationship with such price-women can be right. The praise names Krishna who danced to rhythm on the serpent's heads and helped the Pandavas, Murugan his nephew, and the groves of vengai, palasa and plantain and the flowering tanks of Poomparai.
nuance: விலைமாதர், price-women, is the plainest name; முறை பேசி, talking of kinship, is their false familiarity, and வாழ்ந்த மனை தேடி, seeking out prosperous houses, their motive. பாந்தள் முடிமீது ... நடமாடு is Krishna's dance on Kaliya.

title: கொடுங்குன்றம்
theme: Songs at Kodunkundram (கொடுங்குன்றம்): the poet asks Murugan to look on his crippled service, bent by women, and promises never to forget the dancing feet even as the body perishes in the sea of lust; one song's praise is a long drum-syllable battle.
structure_note: 621 is a short song; 622 is one of the longest in the book, with its confession built on the image of breasts as war elephants and its praise almost wholly drum syllables.

reading: The poet says that through eyes where Kama's five arrows dwell, through breasts like golden hills and pots, and through women who grow angry and exact payment in public, his service is crippled, and asks whether Murugan will not see it and be glad today. The praise hears the bees humming in the dense groves and names the Lord who dwells on the rich, steep hill of Kodunkundram.
nuance: முடங்கும் என்றன் தொண்டு: service is not abandoned but bent and crippled, and the plea is only that the Lord look at it. மன்றம் கண்டும் தண்டும் பெண்கள் may mean women who take a man to the public hall and exact money; the reading is unsure.

reading: The poet describes breasts as rutting war elephants that burst their bodices, run with musk, break the pearl chains that bind them, crush their keepers, shake even Kama and three-eyed Siva and swallow young men's lives; then the women who set a price in public, their embraces, poisonous carp eyes and kisses, and the net of lovemaking in which he sinks into a dark sea of senses. He vows that even when this hut of the body, a shirt for the senses, perishes, he will not forget Murugan's dancing feet at Kodunkiri. The praise is almost all drum syllables and a battlefield of vultures, Bhairavas bathing in blood and demons beheaded.
nuance: கொங்கை யானை, breast-elephant, is sustained for many lines, with chains (நிகளம்), goad (அங்குசம்) and keepers (பாகர்). பொதுவில் விலையிடு மகளிர் are women who set their price publicly. இந்திரிய சட்டைக் குரம்பை, the body as a hut that is the senses' shirt, is the image of what perishes; the plea is not to escape but not to forget (மறந்திடேனே).

title: குன்றக்குடி
theme: Songs at Kundrakudi (குன்றக்குடி), also named Mayuragiri, the peacock hill: the poet asks to leave the sorrow of women, the net of lovemaking that wastes his knowing mind, and the love-sickness of moon, cuckoo and Kama's arrows; the praise names Murugan as teacher of Siva and Agastya, Rama's and Krishna's nephew, and the vel at which Death's servants tremble.
structure_note: Seven songs. 623, 625, 627 are courtesan confessions with a single plea; 624 is a vast song of breasts and battle drums; 626 an abusive catalogue of courtesans; 628 and 629 use the love-sickness motifs (moon, cuckoo, flute, gossip). Vayalur is named with Kundrakudi in 624 and 625.
source_issues: Song 629: corrupt characters in தாமோக முடனு஡று and உரலு஡டு (line 13), read as ஊறு and உரலூடு; also துய்ருடே (line 8), probably துயரூடே.

tamil: அழகெ றிந்த சந்த்ர முகவ டங்க லந்த
அடிது வண்ட தண்டை கலிலெ னுஞ்சி லம்பொ
சுழியெ றிந்து நெஞ்சு சுழல நஞ்ச ணைந்து
துணைநெ ருங்கு கொங்கை மருவு கின்ற பெண்கள்
எழுது கும்ப கன்பி னிளைய தம்பி நம்பி
இதம கிழ்ந்தி லங்கை யசுர ரந்த தங்க
மழுவு கந்த செங்கை அரனு கந்தி றைஞ்ச
வளமி குந்த குன்ற நகர்பு ரந்து துங்க
reading: The poet asks when he will leave the sorrow of women whose moon faces, nectar speech, gait with anklets and bells, and two poison eyes that whirl the heart, draw him. The praise names Rama, the cloud-dark one who rejoiced when Kumbhakarna's younger brother came and bowed, and won Lanka's golden city, Murugan as the guru who stood and spoke the mantra while Siva, axe in hand, bowed to him, at the rich town of Kundram.
nuance: மழு உகந்த செங்கை அரன் உகந்து இறைஞ்ச மநு இயம்பி நின்ற குருநாதா: the Siva-teaching story with Siva bowing and the teaching called மநு, the mantra. எழுது கும்பகன் பின் இளைய தம்பி is Vibhishana coming over to Rama.

reading: At great length the poet describes women's breasts with elephant tusks, golden pots and pearl-bearing rivers, their dark fragrant hair, their voices of peacock and cuckoo, their eyes like Death's fortress, nail marks, slipping bangles and bitten lips, and says that in the net of lovemaking his knowing mind was wasted; he asks whether Murugan of Vayalur and lord of Kundrakudi will not grant that he think of his feet so that birth ends. The praise is a long run of drum syllables and a battlefield of vultures, ghouls and jackals, where Murugan broke the demons' armies and gave the gods protection.
nuance: வருமறலி அரணமொடு முடுகு சமர் விழியிணைகள: the eyes are Death's fortress pressing into battle, a link the poet often draws between lust and Death. என தறிவுடைய கலைபடுதல் is the waste of knowledge in lust; the cure is உந்திப் பிறப்பற நினைந்திட உன் அடி. The image-chains in the first half are hard to divide in places.

tamil: கடினதட கும்ப நேரென வளருமிரு கொங்கை மேல்விழு
கனவளக பந்தி யாகிய நிழல்தனிலி ருந்து தேனுமிழ்
துடியிடைநு டங்க வாள்விழி குழைபொரநி ரம்ப மூடிய
தொனியெழவி ழைந்து கூரிய கொடுநகமி சைந்து தோள்மிசை
இடிமுரச றைந்து பூசல்செய் அசுரர்கள்மு றிந்து தூளெழ
எமபடரு மென்செய் வோமென நடுநடுந டுங்க வேல்விடு
வடிவுடைய அம்பி காபதி கணபதிசி றந்து வாழ்தட
வகைவகைபு கழ்ந்து வாசவன் அரிபிரமர் சந்த்ர சூரியர்
reading: The poet asks whether he will give up the pleasure of women whose breasts are like great pots, their lips, their dark hair, their sounds like bees, cuckoos, peacocks and quails, the nail marks and the swoon of union on the shoulder. The praise names Murugan whose vel made the demons break, the seven seas cry out and Yama's servants tremble asking 'what shall we do?', who rides the storm-wind peacock, dwells at Vayalur and Kundram where Ambikapati and Ganapati live, and is worshipped by Indra, Hari, Brahma, sun and moon.
nuance: எமபடரும் என் செய்வோம் என நடுநடுநடுங்க: Death's servants, whom the confessions fear, are themselves made to tremble by the vel, the answer to the death-hour plea told as praise.

reading: The poet pours out abuse of courtesans: frauds of pretended love and display, foul-mouthed, keeping company with base men for their money, swearing without shame 'you are me and I am you', liars who stand and show off, who torment whoever they cling to, painted beauties who flash their skin and cry 'oho, come, come', and asks whether a relationship with them is fit even if they come near. The praise names Krishna who silently drank Putana's life and defeated the demons Kamsa sent, Murugan who destroyed Sura's host, and Mayura hill, Kundrakudi, ringed by the river Thenaru.
nuance: The confession is a torrent of epithets ending in -கள் (மட்டைகள், படத்திகள், பிலுக்கிகள், மினுக்கிகள், பகட்டிகள், வம்பிகள்). நீயே நானே என்றொரு சத்தியம் வாய் கூசாது ஓதும்: the oath of oneness spoken without shame is the centre of the charge. பேயானாள் is Putana.

reading: The poet asks whether, struck by Kama's bow through young women of sweet flattering speech, he should go the great false way that multiplies the tangle of birth, take on such a nature, shrink, let his greatness bend and his actions fail, and suffer disgraces through desire for the carp eyes of petty women. The praise names Murugan who fought Sura with all his kin until their crowns were scattered, the guru who once spoke the mantra so that the short sage gained the meaning of bliss, at Kundrakudi.
nuance: சிறுமை பொருந்திப் பெருமை முடங்கி: lust is told in the Kural's terms, smallness gained and greatness bent. குறுமுநி இன்பப் பொருள் பெற ... மநு உஞ்சொல் குருநாதா is Murugan as Agastya's teacher.

reading: A short song: the speaker asks whether he must be so bewildered, thinking ceaselessly, by the fire of the white moon, the arrows of playful Kama and the cuckoo's calling. The praise names the beautiful chest on which lie the breasts of the coral-lipped young deer of the hunters, at the peacock hill.
nuance: The love-sickness is told with the stock trio of moon, Kama and cuckoo (cf. 14). Nothing marks the speaker's sex or names women as the cause, and the praise ends on Valli on Murugan's chest, so this may be a lovesick girl's lament for Murugan rather than the poet's confession; the text does not settle it.

reading: The poet says that through the cuckoo, Kama's spear, the moon that burns daily like sunlight, the gossip of women and the flute's music, he has been deceived in the net of desire and is maddened all day, and asks not to go into the sorrow of women with arrow eyes but to be given grace to join Murugan in the high, undying state. The praise names Krishna, who climbed the mortar to steal milk and play while Yasoda did not see, Damodara and Murari, Murugan's shoulders that delight the great lady, the forest lady and the lady of the cloudy hill, at Mayuragiri ringed by the Thenaru.
nuance: The love-poetry machinery (குயில், மதி, வேயூது இசை, மாதர் வசை) is the poet's own state here, unlike 628: he names விழிமாதர் and asks for அழியாத மேலான பதம், release. தாமோதரன், 'rope-bellied', is the child Krishna tied to the mortar. The three ladies in the praise are not all identifiable.

title: பொதியமலை
theme: Songs at Pothiyamalai (பொதியமலை), Agastya's mountain: the poet asks not to be debased by the beds of wicked women, nor to wither, diseased and laughed at by kin, but to be called near, given a place among the great ascetics and given the vel and peacock; the praise names Murugan as the one who told the word Om when Siva danced.
source_issues: Song 630: two corrupt characters, in மார்பினு஡டு (line 3) and வானினு஡டு (line 13), both read as -ஊடு, 'through'.

tamil: மைக்க ணிக்கன் வாளி போல வுட்க ளத்தை மாறி நாடி
மத்த கத்தி னீடு கோடு வைத்த தொத்தின் மார்பி னு஡டு
இக்கு வைக்கு மாடை வீழ வெட்கி யக்க மான பேரை
எட்டு துட்ட மாதர் பாய லிச்சை யுற்றெ னாக மாவி
துர்க்கை பக்க சூல காளி செக்கை புக்க தாள வோசை
சுற்றி வெற்றி யோடு தாள்கள் சுத்த நிர்த்த மாடு மாதி
திக்கு மிக்க வானி னு஡டு புக்க விக்க மூடு சூரர்
செச்சை பிச்சி மாலை மார்ப விச்சை கொச்சை மாதி னோடு
reading: The poet describes women whose kohled eyes, like Kama's arrows, change the heart, who wear honeyed garlands, whose breasts move under their bands, who cheat bashful men, kiss and speak sweetly, and asks whether, with desire for the bed of these wicked women, body and life wearing out daily, he should become debased. The praise names the dance of the First One, with Durga beside him and Kali with trident beating time, and Murugan who told the sacred syllable so that it stood by the word, the vel that struck Sura's host, and the son at the mountain with vetchi and jasmine garlands and the hunter girl of rustic speech.
nuance: தாரம் is a name of the syllable Om; சொற்கு நிற்குமாறு தாரம் மொழிவோனே seems to make Murugan teach it to the dancing Siva, though the line's syntax is unsure. விச்சை கொச்சை மாது: Valli, whose speech is rustic. செப்பு வெற்பு, if it names the shrine, is Pothigai.

reading: The poet describes women who loosen their hair, stare, shake their girdles and breasts, flash their ear-leaves and bangles, smile and frighten with sidelong eyes, call anyone, give their mouth's water to drink and make a man cringe like a dog; then disease comes, he is half-dead, and mother, kin and clan laugh as his body wastes. He asks Murugan to mark him, call him near, set him among the great ascetics, give him the vel and peacock and make his mind know that the Veda speaks of one. The praise names the battle in which Murugan burned the sea and broke Sura's mountain, freed the gods from prison and made Indra rejoice, esteemed by his father and uncle, at Agastya's mountain.
nuance: மாதவர் கணத்தின் மேவென: the plea is for a place among the company of great ascetics, not only for the feet. வேதமும் ஒருத்தன் ஆமென சிந்தை கூராய்: the Vedas speak of one. நாயென முடக்கு, crouching like a dog, is the poet's harshest picture of himself under women.

title: கழுகுமலை
theme: Songs at Kazhugumalai (கழுகுமலை): the poet confesses the bitter infatuation with women who sell their breasts and seize men's wealth, refuses any longer to plead his poverty before base men, and asks to swim the wave of births to the pure feet; the praise names Rama, Murugan's vel given by Siva, and Murugan become a vengai tree for Valli.

reading: The poet says that the infatuation with women of lisping speech who take wealth and sell their breasts has been bitter beyond bitter, and that he, bewildered as a child, can no longer, in his youth, plead his poverty before many base and cruel men. The praise names the cloud-dark nephew of Vishnu who threw the vel so that Sura, who opposed Rama's bow, fell, and Murugan at the great town of Kazhugumalai, rich in virtue, among plantain and areca and fields where bees hum.
nuance: The two humiliations are set side by side: money lost to women (நிதிக் கொள்வார், முலையை விலை செய்வார்) and then poverty pleaded to the wicked (பதகர் ... இடத்திலே மிக வறுமை புகல்வதே). இனி முடியாதே, 'no longer can I', is the plea. The praise line on Sura and the bow is hard to construe.

reading: The poet describes whores who hide and bare their breasts, loosen their clothes and lie down, kiss again and again on beds of flowers, embrace until a man is shaken, destroy men's strength of mind and snatch their wealth from their hands while their passion is great, and asks whether a relationship with them can be right. The praise names Rama who bent the bow so that Ravana's ten crowns flew and his body was pierced, Murugan nephew of that archer, the victorious vel given by Siva who bears the moon and Ganga, at Kazhugumalai.
nuance: வேசைகள் is the bluntest name; the sequence runs from seduction (முத்திக் கொடுப்பர்) to the destruction of the man's will (மனவலியைத் தட்டழிப்பர்) to the theft (பொருளைக் கைப் பறிப்பர்). மால் பெரிது: they take it while the man's infatuation is at its height.

tamil: கோங்க முநகுயு மெலிய வீங்கு புளக களப
கூர்ந்து குழையை அமளி தோய்ந்து குலவு மினிய
வாங்கு பகழி விழியை மோந்து பகலு மிரவும்
வாஞ்சை யுடைய அடிமை நீண்ட பிறவி யலையை
ஓங்க லனைய பெரிய சோங்கு தகர மகர
ஓய்ந்து பிரமன் வெருவ வாய்ந்த குருகு மலையில்
வேங்கை யடவி மறவர் ஏங்க வனிதை யுருக
வேண்டு மடியர் புலவர் வேண்ட அரிய பொருளை
reading: The poet, a servant with an unending longing for women whose eyes are bent arrows and whose lovemaking is sweet as nectar, sleepless day and night, asks whether he will swim the long wave of birth and reach the pure feet. The praise names Murugan's vel against Sura hiding in the sea of ships and sharks, Brahma afraid, the lone vel-bearer riding the peacock on the heron hill, the Kumara who took the form of a vengai tree to the hunters' grief so that the girl melted, and the Lord who gives devotees and poets the rare thing they ask, as much as they ask.
nuance: பிறவி அலையை நீந்தி அமல அடி வந்து அடைவேனோ recalls the Kural's sea of births crossed by the feet. வேங்கை வடிவு மருவும் குமரேசா: in the Valli story Murugan hid as a vengai tree when her kin came; the text names it. குருகு மலை, heron hill, stands for the shrine's own name, the vulture hill.

title: வள்ளியூர்
theme: A short song at Valliyur (வள்ளியூர்): the body is an illusion like lightning at night, and the poet asks whether he must suffer along every stony road; the praise names the vel that ruined the Suras' town and Murugan between his two consorts.

reading: The poet calls the body an illusion, like the lightning at night and not even that, and asks whether he and his hand must suffer along every stony road. The praise names the vel that wore down the old Suras and ruined their town, and Murugan dwelling at Valliyur with his two consorts on either side.
nuance: அல்லில் நேரும் மின் அதுதானும் அல்லதாகிய உடல் மாயை: the body is less lasting than a flash of lightning at night. The second quatrain (கல்லின் நேர அவ்வழி தோறும் கையும் நானும் உலையலாமோ) may speak of wandering on hard roads or of begging with the hand; I cannot settle it.

title: கதிர்காமம்
theme: Songs at Kathirkamam (கதிர்காமம்) in Ilam, the Lord of the hill among waterfalls, fruit trees and monkeys: the poet confesses courting women and flattering patrons, the household that eats up a life, and the hour of Death's torturers, and asks for bhakti, the feet and the stainless state of sayujya; two songs lament a lovesick girl, and two are praise alone.
structure_note: Pure praise (636, with the refrain பெருமாள்காண், and 642, addressed to Murugan and then to Siva); patrons and women (637, 641, 644, 649); the householder (638); bhakti, jnana and the end of the paths (639, 643, 646); akam laments in another's voice (645, 647); Death's men (648); 640 is largely obscure. Murugan is twice identified with Sambandar (639, 641), and 643 names the Thiruppugazh as the gift he gave the poet.
source_issues: Song 637: நீழ்வாடை (line 30) is probably நீள்வாடை.
Song 643: unflagged garble சுகசெர்ரு பத்தை (line 136), probably சுகசொரூபத்தை.
Song 649: it closes on அருக்கொணாமலை rather than Kathirkamam; it may belong under Thirukkonamalai (chapter 77), whose song 650 names திருக்கொணாமலை.

reading: A song of praise only, each line closing 'behold the Lord' (பெருமாள்காண்): Murugan is the nephew of Murari with Lakshmi on his chest, the Kumara whose songs fill earth and sky, the emerald-peacock lord who plays in the minds of devotees, the lord of Kathirkamam where waterfalls fling gems and pearls, the hero who ground mountains to dust as the demons died, and the guru of the pure Siva with serpent, crescent and Ganga in his hair. It ends with the lord of the gods and the lover of the hunter girl.
nuance: The refrain காண் ('see!') makes the song a pointing-out, as if the poet showed the god to the listener line by line. மருவும் அடியார்கள் மனதில் விளையாடு: the devotees' minds are named as one of his playgrounds, beside the hill and the field. இருவினை இலாத ... இமையவர் are the gods free of the two deeds.

tamil: அலகின் மாறு மாறாத கலதி பூத வேதாளி
அழிவு கோளி நாணாது புழுகு பூசி வாழ்மாதர்
பலக லாக ராமேரு மலைக ராச லாவீசு
பரிவு றாத மாபாதர் வரிசை பாடி யோயாத
இலகு வேலை நீழ்வாடை யெரிகொள் வேலை மாசூரி
இமய மாது பாகீர திநதி பால காசார
கலக வாரி போல்மோதி வடவை யாறு சூழ்சீத
கனக நாடு வீடாய கடவுள் யானை வாழ்வான
reading: The poet heaps abuse on the shameless, civet-scented women without grace who deluded him, and confesses that he sang the praises of great sinners who show no kindness, calling them masters of the arts, Meru, the rain cloud and the wish-tree, tirelessly seeking gifts; he asks Murugan to look on him so that he does not die so. The praise names the vel thrown into the sea at Sura, Murugan as son of the Himalaya's daughter and of the Ganga and the lake, husband of the hunters' daughter and Devayanai, the young one of the old town Kathirkamam.
nuance: The patron's praises are given in his own flattering terms (மேரு, பருவமேகம், தரு), the stock comparisons of court poetry, so the confession is also a poet's shame at his craft misused. The opening string of abuse (கலதி, பூத வேதாளி, ஞாளி, கோமாளி) is hard to divide; நீழ்வாடை in the praise is probably நீள்வாடை.

reading: The poet counts what a householder needs: cloth to wear, rich food for hunger, water and clothes, remedies for the body's sickness, a young woman within and a house to sleep in; getting all this, he bathes in the sea of delusion as protector of a long line of kin and his life goes in vain, and he asks for the day when Murugan calls him, gives him a mind of grace and the awareness of jnana, and rules him as he whirls in the mountain of births. The praise tells at length how the monkeys were sent searching west, north and east, and Maruti, crossing south, found the lady in the grove and gave Rama's golden ring.
nuance: The plea is built of a repeated வேணும் ('one needs'), so the household appears as a list of wants that never ends; the verdict is உயிர் அவமே போம, the life simply wasted. The Ramayana in the praise follows Hanuman rather than Rama, and how it connects to Murugan at Kathirkamam is not clear from the text; the line குறிப்பிற் குறிபோன போதிலும் வரலாமோ is obscure.

reading: A short song: the poet asks for matchless bhakti, the thought of the sweet feet morning and evening, and for Murugan to dwell close in the ocean of his heart and shine within him. The praise names the dweller on Kathirkamam hill with arms like golden Meru, whose anklets carry sweet speech, and the Lord who straightened the hump of the Pandya.
nuance: வழுதி கூன் நிமிர்த்த: straightening the Pandya king's hump is Sambandar's miracle at Madurai, so Murugan is identified with Sambandar, as in 641, 653 and 666.

reading: Much of this song is hard to divide. It seems to praise the hero of Kathirkamam hill, who rides the peacock dancing until the northern peak is powdered, and to confess that the poet does not worship as one of the hereditary kin; it then names Murugan who went to the millet field as the servant of the new maiden of the forest and wearied there, the life of those who make room for the poor, seated on an emerald peacock, and ends: whether one speaks kind words or proud words, the Lord pities the poor.
nuance: The close is the clearest line: இதமொழி பகரினும் மதமொழி பகரினும் ஏழைக்கு இரங்கும், grace that does not wait on the right words. அபிநவ குமரி அடிமையாய் புனம் சென்று reverses the usual servitude: the god becomes Valli's servant. The opening lines (கனகத நககுலி புணரித ...) resist division.

reading: The poet describes women who stroll the streets like peacocks with eyes like spears, who bring under their bodies' power even those on the paths of chariyai, kiriyai and yoga, deceitful women whom he calls the great snare of death and maya, and asks that Murugan's grace come to him, sunk on their shining bed. The praise names Murugan son of Uma, the Gayatri and Parasakti, who wrote a madal and served by the watch-platform for the hunter girl, the king of poets who freed the gods, and the sun of the Kauniya clan who wept and saved the world, at Kathirkamam.
nuance: The women undo even those on the ordered Saiva paths (சரியை க்ரியை யோகத்தின் வழிவருக்கு), so the danger is set above ascetic discipline. அழுது உலகை வாழ்வித்த கவுணிய குலாதித்த is Sambandar, of the Kauniya gotra, who wept as a child and was fed by Uma: Murugan is identified with him. மடலெழுதி: Murugan himself in the lover's extremity, as in 656 and 664. The phrase மகாதத்தை in the plea is uncertain.

reading: A song of praise in two parts: first Murugan, born in the reeds, who leapt at Sura, followed him as far as he fled, split his body in two, heaped his heads and chests and won the cock as his banner, with a plea for the lotus feet; then Siva, who laughed and burned the cities when their lords came to fight, flayed and wore the elephant's hide, and burned Madana to charcoal with the look of his brow. It ends with Murugan the pearl of Kathirkamam.
