The praise names Murugan son of the goddess who wears the crescent and is the form of Vedic mantra, the one who dwells in the five mayas, five elements and five nadas and all that moves and stays, who embraced the hunter girl when the elephant frightened her, at Meru Mangai.
nuance: தூல பங்க காயம்: the 'gross' body, a technical word that implies the subtle body beside it. The elephant that frightens Valli into Murugan's arms is Ganesha helping his brother.

reading: The poet confesses that he fell in love with long-haired women and lost his way, ran over the earth seeking wealth until his heart withered, never thought justly of the life in Siva, and, a deceiving sinner, made a crore of songs giving names to what only feeds ruin; he asks how he will live, and whether Murugan will not look on him with the gaze he has for his devotees. The praise names Uttaramerur, where Vishnu, Brahma, those who know the Agamas, Ganesha, jnanis and the twelve hundred Vedic priests dwell, and Murugan who came there on the peacock, whose vel burned Sura to ash, the lord of the deer's daughter.
nuance: பாழினுக்கு இரையாய நாமம் வைத்து ஒருகோடி பாடல்: I read this as the poet's regret at having sung praise of perishable men or things, a confession about his own art; the line could be divided otherwise. ஆயிரத்திருநூறு மறையோர் is a local detail of the shrine.

reading: The poet tells how, infatuated by women's breasts and pearl strings, fragrant hair, carp-like eyes, feet, waist and crescent foreheads, he is ruined and wanders daily in the sea of desire, and asks the twelve-shouldered master of a thousand arts to grant grace to him who wanders as a man of the middle sort. The praise names Murugan the treasure of Siva, who came with a deed into the assembly, called a madman and asked for his answer, and by that just stratagem claimed faultless Sundarar for his own, and the lord of Meru Mangai, home of priests of true Tamil, with its Vedas and sacrifices.
nuance: சாதனங்கொடு ... பித்தா ... சுந்தரனைத் தான் ஒற்றிகொள்: the story of Siva appearing with a bond to claim Sundarar as his hereditary slave, in which Sundarar called him பித்தா. It is the book's model of service by claim (thondu). மத்திபன் may mean a middling or mediocre man, and the lines on the priests who establish Vedas and sacrifices are hard to divide.

title: மதுராந்தகம்
theme: Songs at Madurantakam (மதுராந்தகம்), at its northern Chirrambalam: the poet asks to cling to the feet as a raft instead of the leaking body, asks to be taught the instruction Murugan once gave Siva, and asks to leave house, kin and wealth for the vastness of silence.
source_issues: Song 719: corrupt character in கம்பரி¨ன் (line 2), probably கம்பரின்.

reading: The poet asks that he not tire and whirl taking as everything this hut of the senses, skin and holes from which blood spurts and drains, packed with deeds, a vessel of filth, but that he be given the thought to hold the raft of the twin lotus feet with golden bells and anklets. The praise names Murugan nephew of the cloud-dark one who bears mace, Sarnga bow, sword, conch and discus, bridegroom of the cane-sweet girl of the millet field, born in the lotus as the son of the destroyer of Kama, lord of the northern Chirrambalam at Madurantakam.
nuance: உபய அம்புயப் புணை: the feet as a raft across the sea of births, an image the Kural also uses (kural:10). குணபாண்டம் is perhaps 'corpse-vessel' (குணபம், corpse). The line உதித அம்பரத்தை உயிர் கெட is obscure to me.

reading: The poet asks whether Murugan's guruship would be diminished in the least if he spoke to him, small as he is, the instruction he gave Siva, who gave the mountain-daughter his left side and keeps the Ganga in his hair, so that Siva's speech ended, his action died, his mind loosened and he attained the eternal. The praise names the vel that split the mango in the sea so the gods might live, the blue peacock that circled the whole universe in an instant, and the one who broke the ancient golden hill, at Madurantakam.
nuance: The teaching of Siva is described by its effect, not named as Om: உரைமாள, செயல் மாண்டு, சித்தம் அவிழ, நித்தத்துவம் பெற. The plea is witty: சற்றும் குருத்துவம் குறையுமோ, would it cost the guru anything to teach the poet too? கொக்கு is the mango tree that Sura became.

reading: The poet seems to ask when, leaving house, sons, kin, horses, grain, wealth and town and the delusion of 'I and mine', he will be taken into the vast silence and given Murugan's feet. The praise, much of it in drum syllables, names Siva who dances in space, whose child Murugan is, the elephant-faced brother with the mouse, the six-faced lord of Madurantakam honoured by the gods.
nuance: யானெனதென்று: the plea names the 'I and mine' that binds, and மோன தடம்பர the expanse of silence that replaces it. The song is set to a dense rhythm, and most compounds in both halves (வணவாம்பிர மாத குணங்குறி, இடவார்ந்தன சானு) can be split several ways, so this reading is only the outline.

title: சேயூர்
theme: A single song under the heading Seyur (சேயூர்): the poet asks whether he must perish in the beds of women who bewitch all with their eyes, and praises the vel that turned his two deeds to dust.
source_issues: Song 721 is filed under சேயூர் but names its shrine வளவாபுரி; whether these are the same place should be checked.

reading: The poet describes the women with cloud-dark hair, bow brows, carp eyes, pearl smiles, breasts like towers, thread waists and peacock grace, who bewitch everyone with whirling glances, and asks whether he must perish in their beds. The praise names the vel thrown so that the gods' city cried out and the dark demons' army, the seven seas and the mountains were crushed, the son of the gracious Lady of the lotus and of the Lord the gods worship, Valli's bridegroom in a land of magizh, malati, rose-apple and jackfruit groves, and the lord of Valavapuri who threw the vel to turn his servant's two deeds to dust.
nuance: அடியேன் இருவினை தூள்பட அயில் ஏவிய: the vel that destroyed the demons is also said to have shattered the poet's own deeds, so the battle becomes his release. The song names the shrine வளவாபுரி, not Seyur.

title: திருவக்கரை
theme: Songs at Tiruvakkarai (திருவக்கரை): the poet asks to stop babbling scriptures without speaking of Murugan, to escape the hell the womb leads to and the round of births, and to be counted among his servants; and asks to be freed from courtesans who paint their faces and grasp at money while the world says 'shame'.

reading: The poet asks that he stop babbling some scriptures noisily without saying even a little about Murugan, not fall again and again into the cruel hell the path of the womb leads to, and stop wandering through many births in the world, and that he, a dog of a servant, be taken into the throng of Murugan's servants and given the two flower feet. The praise names the peacock hero who fought the night-roamer until the great mountains cracked and the sea dried, the hunter girl's lover, the lord of Tiruvakkarai where conches crawl in the waves and give up pearls, who grants devotees whatever they wish.
nuance: கலைகள் பிதற்றுவது: learning recited without the Lord is the first thing the poet wants to give up, before hell and rebirth. உனதடிமைத் திரள் அதனினும் உட்பட: the plea is to belong to the company of servants, not only to reach the feet alone.

reading: The poet describes the women who rub green herbs on their faces to make them shine, cunning in crafty arts, who think only of seizing the money in a man's hand, who bewitch with pearl smiles and glances, give the spittle of their lips as if fruit and sugar, flatter on the cushioned bed and draw him into their embrace; he asks for the good feet so that he may give up this trade and this habit, which leave him wretched every day while the world says 'chi, chi'. The praise names Vishnu who sleeps on the serpent, Lakshmi's lord with the conch and tulasi, who set the mountain in the sea and churned out nectar, as uncle, Murugan dear to the hunter girl of rustic speech, and the lord of Tiruvakkarai of lotus fields and moat.
nuance: உலகத்தவர் சிச்சியெனத் திரி: public contempt is part of the poet's suffering. இத்தொழில் இக்குணம்: he calls his own habit a trade, as if visiting courtesans were his occupation.

title: சிறுவை
theme: Songs at Siruvai (சிறுவை, சிறுவாபுரி): a plea that Murugan come dancing with his peacock in sight of all the gods, a litany of salutations, a plea to escape birth through the feet that opened the way of silence, and a confession about courtesans with a long string of the goddess's names; the town is praised as the place where two boys fought Rama.
source_issues: Song 724: corrupt character in செற§ருப (line 14), perhaps செறிரூப.
Song 725: corrupt characters in ப்¡£தா (line 3), clearly ப்ரீதா ('beloved'), confirming ¡£ for ரீ.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to come dancing with his peacock so that Indra is resettled in his city, the demons are changed, the gods rejoice, Siva who dances with the goddess, Ganesha and Uma are glad, and the world, the sages, all in the eight directions, Brahma and Vishnu with Lakshmi see him before them. The praise names the lotus-eyed bridegroom of the gods' daughter, full of wisdom, whose vel split the sea and the mountain, with a pearl-hung chest, dear to cool Tamil, at Siruvai where he dwells in his devotees' hearts.
nuance: The plea asks for nothing for the poet: it asks for an epiphany, Murugan coming in sight of everyone (எதிர்காண). தண்டமிழின் மிகுநேய, the lover of cool Tamil, and அடியார்கள் சிந்தையது குடியான, who lives in his devotees' minds, frame the shrine.

reading: A litany of salutations (நமோ நம) to Murugan: to the cool lotus feet, to the one who delights in Narada's songs, to the lover of the cock and peacock, the crest the Vedas seek, the essence of the Agamas, the commander of the gods' army, the axe that cuts sins so that souls reach their goal, the terror of the asura king, the child of Parvati, ending in a plea for grace. The praise names the brother of the elephant-faced one, the one dear to Siva, the nephew of Lakshmi's lord, the six faces like full moons, praised by Vishnu and Brahma, and Siruvapuri, richer than the gods' city and Alaka.
nuance: The whole first half is salutation, not plea, until the closing அருள்தாராய். பாதக நீவு குடாரா, the axe that cuts away sin so the soul reaches its goal (கதி தோய), is the one line about the poet's need.

tamil: பிறவி யான சடமி றங்கி வழியி லாத துறைசெ றிந்து
பெருகு தீய வினையி னொந்து கதிக டோறு மலைபொ ருந்தி
நறைவி ழாத மலர்மு கந்த வரிய மோன வழிதி றந்த
நரர்சு ராதி பரும்வ ணங்கு மினிய சேவை தனைவி ரும்பி
பொறிவ ழாத முநிவர் தங்கள் நெறிவ ழாத பிலனு ழன்று
பொருவி லாம லருள்பு ரிந்து மயிலி னேறி நொடியில் வந்து
சிறுவ ராகி யிருவ ரந்த கரிப தாதி கொடுபொ ருஞ்சொல்
செயம தான நகர மர்ந்த அளகை போல வளமி குந்த
reading: The poet asks that he not perish trusting in birth, which has no hold: coming down into the inert body, crowding into pathless places, wandering in sickness and sorrow, grieving under growing evil deeds and roaming through every state; that the lotus feet which opened the rare way of silence never leave his mind; and whether, desiring the sweet service that men and gods offer, he will be counted Murugan's servant. The praise seems to tell how Murugan, mindful of a demon in a cave who troubled the sages, came in an instant on the peacock and, delighted, accepted Tamil, and names Siruvai, rich as Alaka, the town where two boys fought Rama with his elephants and foot soldiers and won.
nuance: மோன வழி திறந்த நளின பாதம்: the feet themselves open the way of silence. The cave (பிலன்), the demon, the sudden coming on the peacock and the Tamil (தமிழ் புனைந்த) may point to Nakkirar freed from a demon's cave by his Murugan poem, but the text does not name him. The boys who fought Rama are the shrine's own legend, presumably Lava and Kusa.

reading: The poet speaks of women with spear eyes who sell love for money, who abuse a man without regard for the hour and are called whores, and of himself, a small man wandering in desire for them, and asks that he never forget the feet worshipped by Vishnu, Brahma, Siva, the gods, the sages and Indra, that he worship desiring the good path to Siva's bliss, and that his troubles be removed. The praise names Murugan as the child given by the goddess under a string of names (Nila Sundari, Komali, Yamali, Narani who dances, Purani, Sulini, Malini, Uma, Kali, Sivakama Sundari), the teacher by Siva's grace, nephew of Vishnu who lies on the banyan leaf to keep the world steady, at Siruvapuri with its golden towers.
nuance: வேசி என்பவர், காதலின் பொருள் மேவின பாதகர்: here the women are named outright as harlots who trade love for money. The praise is mostly a list of the goddess's names, so it centres on Shakti more than on Murugan. சிவபோக நல் நூல் நெறி, the good path to Siva's bliss, is set against the women's போகம்.

title: திருவாமாத்தூர்
theme: Songs at Tiruvamathur (திருவாமாத்தூர், மாதை): four confessions of bondage to women, seen as deceivers of the young, as Death in a woman's form, as common women singing to the measure of the coin, and as the snare that keeps the poet sunk in caste and clan; he asks for the feet and to stop swinging like a balance beam between devotion and desire.

tamil: அடல்வடி வேல்கள் வாளிக ளவைவிட வோடல் நேர்படு
தளவிய கோடு போல்வினை யளவள வான கூர்முலை
துடியிடை யாலும் வாலர்கள் துயர்வுற மாய மாயொரு
தொழுதவர் பாத மோதியுன் வழிவழி யானெ னாவுயர்
அடவியி னூடு வேடர்க ளரிவையொ டாசை பேசியு
அழகிய தோளி ராறுடை அறுமுக வேளெ னாவுனை
விடையெறு மீசர் நேசமு மிகநினை வார்கள் தீவினை
விரைசெறி தோகை மாதர்கள் விரகுட னாடு மாதையில்
reading: The poet speaks of women whose eyes strike like spears and arrows, whose breasts are like the tusks of a rutting elephant, whose drum-like waists torment young men, and who deceive them boldly, and asks whether, having worshipped and said 'I am your hereditary servant', he must still have his life swing up and down like the beam of a balance in their company. The praise names Murugan who spoke longingly with the hunter girl in the forest and bowed at her feet, the treasure of the ascetics who chant him knowingly as the six-faced lord, at Mathai, the ancient town of those who think of Siva on the bull, where evil deeds run far away.
nuance: துலையலை மாறு போல் உயிர் சுழல்வேனோ: the image of a balance beam tipping between his vow of service (வழிவழியான் எனா) and the women is the song's own. அடிதொழுது ஆடும் ஆண்மை: Murugan's bowing at Valli's feet is called manliness.

tamil: கண்க யற்பிணை மானொடுற வுண்டெ னக்கழை தோளானது
கஞ்ச மொத்தெழு கூர்மாமுலை குஞ்ச ரத்திரு கோடோடுற
பெண்ட னக்குள கோலாகல மின்றெ டுத்திளை யோராவிகள்
பின்பொ ழித்திடு மாமாயையி லன்பு வைத்தழி யாதேயுறு
விண்ட னக்குற வானோனுடல் கண்ப டைத்தவன் வேதாவொடு
வெந்த னத்துமை யாள்மேவிய சந்த னப்புய மாதீசுரர்
தண்பு டைப்பொழில் சூழ்மாதையில் நண்பு வைத்தருள் தாராதல
தண்டரக் கர்கள் கோகோவென விண்டி டத்தட மாமீமிசை
reading: The poet describes women with carp and doe eyes, bamboo shoulders, breasts like lotus buds and elephant tusks and hair darker than collyrium, as if Death had put on a woman's form to seize young men's lives, and asks that he not perish setting his love on the great maya they lay, but be given grace to cherish Murugan's feet even a little. The praise names Murugan the treasure of Siva on the bull, at whose feet Indra, Brahma and Vishnu fall, with Uma on his side and the elephant hide as his cloak, the lord who loves Mathai and whose vel made the demons cry out.
nuance: உயர் காலன் பெண் தனக்கு உள கோலாகலம் இன்று எடுத்து: the women are Death himself in a woman's festive dress, come for young men's lives. The plea asks only for கிஞ்சில் அத்தனை, the least amount, of love for the feet. விண்டனக்கு உறவானோன் உடல் கண்படைத்தவன் seems to be Indra, whose body was covered with eyes.

tamil: கருமுகில் போல்மட் டாகிய அளகிகள் தேனிற் பாகொடு
கலவிகள் நேரொப் பாகிகள் மதனிகள் காமக் க்ரோதிகள்
பொருகயல் வாளைத் தாவிய விழியினர் சூறைக் காரிகள்
பொதுவிகள் போகப் பாவிகள் வசமழி வேனுக் கோரருள்
தருவடு தீரச் சூரர்கள் அவர்கிளை மாளத் தூளெழ
தனதன தானத் தானன எனஇசை பாடிப் பேய்பல
அரிதிரு மால்சக் ராயுத னவனிளை யாள் முத் தார்நகை
அரவொடு பூளைத் தார்மதி அறுகொடு வேணிச் சூடிய
reading: The poet speaks of women with dark cloud hair and speech like honey, syrup and fruit, lustful and quick to anger, heavy-breasted, with carp-like eyes, plunderers who sing their love to the measure of the money, common to all, sinners of pleasure, and asks when Murugan will grant grace to him who perishes in their power. The praise is a battle, with drum syllables and ghouls feeding on flesh, and names Murugan son of Uma, the younger sister of Vishnu who bears the discus, and of the lord who wears the serpent, poolai flowers, the moon and arugu grass, at southern Mathai.
nuance: பொருள் அளவு ஆசைப்பாடிகள், பொதுவிகள்: love sung to the measure of the coin, and women belonging to all, are the Kural's two charges against the courtesan. Uma as Vishnu's younger sister explains why Vishnu is always Murugan's uncle.

reading: The poet speaks of women whose eyes are the arrows of the bodiless Kama, who quarrel and whose minds are set on the coin, frauds with lying speech, in whose flower beds he perishes, and asks to be given the end of the lowness of being sunk in caste and clan, the attainment of the feet high in open space, and much thought of austerity. The praise tells of Krishna, who sleeps on the serpent, plays the flute to the herds, stole butter and curd from the hanging pots and was beaten with the rope, and of Rama who felled the seven trees and Vali and with one arrow the ten heads and twenty arms of Ravana, as uncle, and the six-faced lord of fragrant Mathai.
nuance: சாதி குலம் உறு படியினில் முழுகிய தாழ்வு அற: the poet names caste and clan as something he is sunk in and wants freed from, an unusual plea set beside the courtesans. காசின் அளவு ஒருதலை அணு மனதினர் repeats the charge of love measured by the coin. The Krishna scenes (butter, rope) are told unusually fully.

title: தச்சூர்
theme: A single song at Tachur (தச்சூர்): the courtesan's flattering speech, which ranks the client above Murugan himself, and the poet's question whether he will go mad with desire for such women; the praise recalls Murugan teaching the poet 'the eighth letter'.

tamil: ளைப்போல் விழிக்கூர்மை நோக்கிக் குழைந்து ...... உ றவாடி
reading: The poet gives the courtesan's wheedling: she shows her breasts, aims her arrow-eyes, calls him 'cousin', says he made her long and then held back, that he stayed away that time and has no love for her, and that if one looks for his equal, even Kadamban falls short; with such talk she calls him her sugar, brings him home and lies with him on a grass mat, and the poet asks whether he will wander mad with desire for such women. The praise names the pearl who told 'the eighth letter' to the poor poet, the vel that cut down Sura's ranks, the adept who split him and made him peacock and cock, who fell at the hunter girl's feet and married her, and the lord of Tachur.
nuance: உனக்கு ஈடு பார்க்கில் கடம்பன் மட்டோ: the courtesan's flattery makes the client the equal of Murugan, an irony aimed at the poet who sings Murugan's praise. எட்டாம் எழுத்து ஏழையேற்குப் பகர்ந்த may refer to the poet's own initiation; which letter is meant (perhaps அ, which is also the Tamil numeral for eight) is not said. The opening of the praise (எச்சாய் மருட்பாடு ... பிச்சாசருக்கு) and the geography of the last lines are obscure to me.

title: திருக்கோவலூர்
theme: A single song at Tirukkovalur (திருக்கோவலூர், கோவை மாநகர்): the poet asks whether he will cease to be caught by women's breasts, eyes, hair, lips and smiles, and praises the supreme lord whom the Vedas and the gods cannot see, in a town loud with Vedic chant and festival.

tamil: பாவ நாரிகள் மாமட மாதர் வீணிக ளாணவ
பார்வை யாமிகு கூரயி லாலு மாமணி யார்குழை
சாவ தார விதாரமு தார்த ராவித ழாலித
சார்வ தாவடி யேனிடர் வீற மாலறி வேமிகு
ஆவ ஆர்வன நான்மறை யாதி மூல பராவரி
ஆதி யாரருள் மாமுரு கேச மால்மரு கேசுர
கோவ தாமறை யோர்மறை யோது மோதம் விழாவொலி
கோவை மாநகர் மேவிய வீர வேலயி லாயுத
reading: The poet speaks of sinful, foolish women puffed with pride, their breasts like tender coconuts, eyes sharper than a spear, hair weighed with jewels, lips sweet as nectar and moon faces, and asks whether, so that his trouble ends, he will give up being drawn into that essence of infatuation. The praise names the supreme lord whom the four Vedas, Vishnu and Brahma cannot see, Murugan by the grace of the First, whose feet the gods all worship, the hero of the vel at Kovai, where the Vedas are chanted and festival and Agamic sounds roar, dwelling with the maid reared by the elephant.
nuance: The plea is short and set inside a long catalogue of the women's parts. கோதை யானையினோடு is Devayanai, named by her elephant nurture. கோவை is the shrine's name shortened.

title: தேவனூர்
theme: Songs at Devanur (தேவனூர்), all three without a confession about women: the poet asks to pass beyond the counted tattvas and the scriptures into the silence where craving ends, asks to stand praising Murugan's names, and declares Murugan the one reality beyond form, speech, Veda, bindu and nada, turiya and beyond.
structure_note: 734 and 736 are doctrinal; 735 is a plea to praise. 734 and 735 share their closing line.
source_issues: Song 735: corrupt characters in நம்ப ¡£சனாரி (line 13), probably ரீ, but the word (நம்பரீசனார், or நம்பர் ஈசனார்) is unclear.

tamil: ஆறு மாறு மஞ்சு மஞ்சும் ஆறு மாறு மஞ்சு மஞ்சும்
ஆறு மாய சஞ்ச லங்கள் வேற தாவி ளங்கு கின்ற
ஈறு கூற ரும்பெ ருஞ்சு வாமி யாயி ருந்த நன்றி
யாவு மாய்ம னங்க டந்த மோன வீட டைந்தொ ருங்கி
மாறு கூறி வந்தெ திர்ந்த சூரர் சேனை மங்க வங்க
வாகை வேல கொன்றை தும்பை மாலை கூவி ளங்கொ ழுந்து
சீறு மாசு ணங்க ரந்தை ஆறு வேணி கொண்ட நம்பர்
தேவர் யாவ ருந்தி ரண்டு பாரின் மீது வந்தி றைஞ்சு
reading: The poet counts off sixes and fives and fours, the constituents of the world, and asks when, beyond these restless things and beyond the art of the Vedas and Agamas, in the great lord whose end cannot be told, without anything else to say, alone and yet all things, he will reach the house of silence beyond the mind, gathered in, with his craving stilled. The praise names the vel that drove back Sura's army over the sea, and Murugan teacher of the lord with matted hair who wears konrai, thumbai, vilva shoots, the young moon, the hissing serpent, karanthai and the river, and the lord who came to shine at Devanur, where all the gods gather.
nuance: ஆறும் ஆறும் அஞ்சும் அஞ்சும் ... அறுநாலும்: the counting points to the tattvas, but how the numbers add up is not said and I don't reconstruct it. மனங்கடந்த மோன வீடு and யான் அவா அடங்க: release is a house of silence beyond the mind, reached when the 'I' and its craving are stilled. தேசிகா: Murugan is again Siva's teacher.

tamil: தார காசு ரன்ச ரிந்து வீழ வேரு டன்ப றிந்து
சாக ரோதை யங்கு ழம்பி நீடு தீகொ ளுந்த அன்று
ஆர வார வும்பர் கும்ப வார ணாச லம்பொ ருந்து
ஆசை கூரு நண்ப என்று மாம யூர கந்த என்றும்
பார மார்த ழும்பர் செம்பொன் மேனி யாளர் கங்கை வெண்க
பார மாசு ணங்கள் சிந்து வார வார மென்ப டம்பு
சேர வேம ணந்த நம்ப ¡£ச னாரி டஞ்சி றந்த
தேவர் யாவ ருந்தி ரண்டு பாரின் மீது வந்தி றைஞ்சு
reading: The poet asks whether he will stand praising Murugan as the friend whom the gods' elephant-reared maid and the hunter girl of the hill desire, as Kanda of the great peacock, until his longing is satisfied. The praise names the vel that uprooted Tarakasura, shook the mountains and set the sea on fire, and Murugan the treasure of the cool lotus-like Lady on the left of the lord with the scars, golden body, Ganga, white skull garland, konrai, thumbai, serpents and arugu, at Devanur.
nuance: The plea asks for nothing but the chance to praise: ஆவல் தீர என்று நின்று புகழ்வேனோ. Taraka, Sura's brother, is named here rather than Sura. தழும்பர் is Siva marked with scars, possibly those of Uma's embrace; the text does not say.

reading: A song of praise with no plea: the one that cannot be seen, both form and formless, that cannot be spoken yet gives speech, the fullness at the end of the four Vedas, dwelling in the bond of the five-element body, unknown to the illusory body, coming before the embodied and speaking as them, the light in space, unknown to Vishnu and Brahma, growing as the world in difference and non-difference, as bindu and nada, as the knowledge of the kalas, as turiya and beyond it, the fruit of the poet's austerity and the fullness of grace: that one is Murugan. The praise names the vel that crushed the demons and gave their lives to Yama, the child who drank Uma's milk, who struck Brahma on the tuft of his head, the thief who sought the girl on the millet platform, and the lord of Devanur who dwells in the hearts of true jnana-yogis.
nuance: The first half is a definition of the Absolute in negatives and pairs (காணொணாதது உருவோடு அருவது, பேசொணாதது உரையே தரவது, பேதாபேதமொடு உலகாய் வளர்வது), ending ஒன்று நீயே, 'the one is you'. Striking Brahma's tuft (குடுமியிலே கரமொடு மோதின) is the punishment for not knowing Om, though Om is not named. காயமானவர் எதிரே அவரென வந்து பேசி may mean the Lord appearing as a human guru.

title: திருவதிகை
theme: Songs at Tiruvathigai (திருவதிகை) on the Kedilam river, where Siva burned the three cities: two confessions about common women and their bed, one asking to be rid of the mind's whirling, the other to escape the sea of births and the two deeds by naming Murugan's twelve arms; one praise calls Murugan the poet who received his songs at the wish of the Lady of Kailasa.

reading: The poet describes common women whose eyes close like carp, whose voices falter like cuckoos and parrots, who give the nectar of coral lips, whose breasts sway, whose hair slips and waists sag as their garments fall in lovemaking on the flower bed, and asks Murugan to remove the anxiety of his mind, whirling in that sweet union, before he melts away. The praise names the nephew of Achyuta, whose arrow cut the ten heads of the dark asura, the poet of honour who received his poems in full as the Lady on the left of the lord of Kailasa wished, and the lord of Tiruvathigai, where the Kedilam floods past areca and plantain and the drums beat.
nuance: கயிலைமலைக் கிழவன் இடக் குமரி விருப்பொடு கருதக் கவி நிறையப் பெறும் வரிசைப் புலவோனே: Murugan as the poet favoured by Uma may point to Sambandar, whom she fed with milk and who then sang, and whom the book often makes Murugan; the text does not name him. பொதுமாதர் are women common to all, but money is not mentioned.

reading: The poet speaks of women with eyes of poison and spears, nectar words and artful breasts, poisonous ones who cast the deeds and the lives of even manly and handsome men into their double net, and asks that he not join them or suffer, but in the company of those who think of Murugan never be lost in the sea of seven births nor sink in the baseness of the two deeds, and be given to say each day, 'Lord, your twelve arms', which freed the gods, sages and Indra from their trouble. The praise names Rama who brought down Ravana's twenty arms and ten crowned heads with one arrow and shot fire into the sea, Vishnu asleep on the serpent in the milk sea, as uncle, the peacock hero of the battle, and the lord of Devayanai at Adhigai, where the cruel demons' three cities were burned.
nuance: உனை நினைபவர் துணைகொள: the company of devotees is the remedy, as in 722. இருவலை, the double net, catches both deeds and life. The shrine's own myth, the burning of the three cities (திரிபுரம் எரிசெய்த அதிகை), closes the song.

title: திருவர்முர்
theme: A short song at Thiruvamur (headed திருவர்முர்): a voice sick with love says the burning of the cool moon, Kama's bow and the beating sea leave the night as long as an aeon, and turns to Kumaresa on the peacock, life of his loving devotees, who makes Death turn his back.
source_issues: Heading and song 739 line 5: திருவர்முர் is probably a corruption of திருவாமூர் (Thiruvamur).
Song 739 line 4: படியொதான் is probably படியோதான்.

reading: A short love song: the speaker asks whether the night as long as an aeon must be spent this way, burned by the fire of the cool moon, by the bow Kama bends in anger and by the sea whose waves beat on. The song names Murugan as Kumaresa on the peacock at Thiruvamur, the great life of his loving devotees, who makes Death show his back.
nuance: The four torments (moon, Kama's bow, the sea, the endless night) are the stock signs of a woman's love-sickness in akam poetry; the song has no confession of sin, so the speaker is the lover longing for Murugan, though the text does not name her. காலன் முதுகை விரிக்கும், making Death turn his back in flight, sets the Lord against Death even in a love song. படியொதான் is probably படியோதான். மாது புகழை வளர்க்கும் may allude to a woman of the shrine's story, which I cannot identify.

title: வடுகூர்
theme: A song at Vadugur (வடுகூர்): the poet praises Siva in his acts, the laugh that burned the cities, Ganga in his hair, the eye that felled Kama, and asks grace to worship Murugan's feet calling him the Kumara who gladdens Siva's heart.

reading: The first half praises Siva: the lord whom Hari and Brahma could not find, who burned the cities with a smile, who bears a woman on his matted hair and holds fire and axe, who has the mountain's daughter as his half and felled Kama's body with his eye; the poet asks for grace to worship Murugan's two flower feet, calling him the Kumara who gladdens that lord's heart. The praise names Murugan who circled the earth on a peacock and split the mountain, who threw the vel at the asuras' heads, and who went into the millet forest to embrace the hunter girl, at Vadugur of the sages.
nuance: The plea is a single line of worship (இருதாள் மலரடி தொழுமாறு அருள்வாயே), framed by Siva's deeds: Murugan is approached as the joy of Siva's mind. அவனியை வலமாய் வருவோனே, who goes round the earth on the peacock, points to the story of the contest for the fruit, though the fruit is not named.

title: திருத்துறையூர்
theme: Songs at Thiruthuraiyur (திருத்துறையூர்): the poet asks whether company with ornamented singing women befits him, and fears fate, Death's rope, the pyre and hell; he asks for the flower feet, and praises Murugan as the guru who taught and as lord of the shrine where gods and sages receive grace.
structure_note: Two songs: 741 on women and Murugan as guru, 742 a long confession of fate, death and the pyre.

reading: The poet describes women who hold a yaazh and sing while their cloth and hair slip, scented with rosewater and civet, with earrings swaying, eyes like spears and carp, lips like sugar and kovai fruit, voices like cuckoos and waists like thread, and asks whether he should keep company with these maddening women of fickle anger. The praise names Sivakami, the goddess the devotees worship, and Murugan as the guru who taught one joined to Bhadrakali, as the hero whose vel struck Sura's mountain and sea, and as the lord of the shining hunter girl at Thuraiyur.
nuance: பித்தர்கள் உறவாமோ closes the description with a question rather than a plea. The line பூமிக்கடல் மூவர்க்கு முன்னாள் பத்திரகாளிப் புணர் போகர்க்கு உபதேசித்தருள் குருநாதா makes Murugan a teacher, but whom he taught is unclear: போகர் may be Siva as Bhadrakali's consort or the siddha Bhogar, and the first words do not split with certainty.

reading: The poet says that through many forms and births, in a womb-pit made of deeds, he has learned the elders' word that fate cannot be turned aside; he fears the hour when he is seized and bound with rope, the body becomes a heap of worms, is melted like wax and burned with rising smoke, becomes food for hell, while his kin stand at the door weeping, and asks to be freed from these and given the flower feet of grace to bow to. The praise names Murugan of the vel on the galloping peacock, who gives grace at Thuraiyur to sages, siddhas, Maheswaras, Hari and Brahma.
nuance: விதியாரும் விலக்கவொணாது எனும் முதியோர் சொல்: the poet cites, and accepts, the proverb that no one can avert fate, and the plea is to escape it by grace. உபாதிகள், afflictions, is the word for the whole chain from rope to pyre. Several lines (சாதக விதம், மகாகட சலதாரை, சதிகாரர் விடக்கு) are hard to split, so the order of events is a reading.

title: திருநாவலூர்
theme: A love song at Thirunavalur (திருநாவலூர்): a speaker wasting with longing in the evening, under Kama's arrows, the cuckoo and the poisonous moon, asks Murugan to come daily to embrace; the praise names the vel and the shrine where he freed the gods.

reading: The speaker says that by the evening, the arrows of cruel Kama, the loud cuckoo in the grove and the moon that pours fire like poison, life itself grows faint, and asks Murugan to come every day with longing to embrace. The praise names him as nephew of Narayana, whom four-faced Brahma also praises, the peacock hero who took up the vel so poets honour him and destroyed the mountain, the lover of the hunter girl, at Naval where he freed the gods from prison.
nuance: The torments of evening, cuckoo and moon are the stock signs of a heroine's longing; the plea to be embraced (ஆசைகொடு அணைக்க வரவேணும்) makes the speaker a woman in love with Murugan, though the voice is not named. நாகம் may be the mountain (Krauncha) or a serpent; I take it as the mountain.

title: திருவெண்ணெய்நல்லூர்
theme: A yogic song at Thiruvennainallur (திருவெண்ணெய்நல்லூர்): the poet asks to burn the tattvas, still the breath and enter the space of Siva and the dance in the golden hall; the praise names Murugan as the poet who impaled the Jains and the old man who came to Valli.

reading: The poet describes a yogic ascent: burning the many tattvas, the darkness consumed by fire, stopping the breath and closing the one path so that it runs by the sun's path into the sky until all is Siva, then melting in the golden hall where the dance is done to ringing anklets and sinking in the full sea, ever with Gauri and Hara; he asks for grace that this may come. The praise names Murugan as the young one who won fame as the poet who set the base Jains on stakes in rows, who came to the hunter girl as an old man by the spring and embraced her when the elephant came, and as son of the pure goddess, at Thiruvennainallur by the Pennai where he dances on the peacock.
nuance: பவனம் ஒழித்து, stopping the breath, and பருதி வழி, the sun's path, are terms of breath yoga, and சிவமயம் names its end; the song then moves to the dance in கனக சபை, Chidambaram's golden hall. அமணர் உடல்களை நிரையில் கழுக்களில் உறவிடு சித்திர புலவன் identifies Murugan with Sambandar. The goddess lines (குமரி தகப்பனை மழுகொடு வெட்டிய) seem to recall Daksha's punishment, and the last line of the plea (கழிய நலக்கினி நிறமென விற்றுடல்) does not split with certainty.

title: திருப்பாதிரிப்புலியூர்
theme: A song at Pathiripuliyur (திருப்பாதிரிப்புலியூர்): the poet describes the body as a diseased nine-holed hut of flesh and bone, confesses he has no austerity, japa or love, and asks Murugan to come on the peacock and make clear the Upanishads; the praise names Rama's arrow and the vel.

tamil: உ யர்விலி யெனினுமெ னெஞ்சு தானினை ...... வழியாமுன்
reading: The poet describes the body as fat, blood, nerves, flesh, gut, bone and skin packed row on row, an old frame struck by disease and impurities, a hut with nine holes, and confesses that while living in it he has done no austerity and has no awareness, no japa, no restraint, no order, no love; yet before his heart's thought perishes he asks Murugan to come on the emerald peacock with his six faces shining and make clear to him the Upanishad of the four Vedas. The praise names Vishnu who as Rama bent his bow so the ten crowned heads of Lanka's king rolled on the earth, the vel that shook Kailas, crumbled the seven mountains and churned the sea, and Murugan as the teacher at Patalai, where the goddess did penance.
nuance: நவதொளை உடைய குரம்பை, the hut with nine holes, is the old image of the body's nine openings. The list of lacks (உணர்விலி, செபமுதல் ஒன்றுதானிலி, அன்புதானிலி) is the poet's self-indictment, and the plea is for teaching, not rescue: நான்மறை உபநிடம் அதனை விளங்க. தேசிக, teacher, names Murugan as guru. அமலை முன் அரிய தவஞ்செய் பாடல வளநகர is the Pathiripuliyur story of the goddess's penance.

title: திருமாணிகுழி
theme: A song at Thirumanikuzhi (திருமாணிகுழி): the poet, calling himself a dog, confesses he has drowned in women's breasts and lips and has not sought Murugan's anklets, shoulders, weapons and peacock; the praise is a battle scene and the shrine's groves and ponds.
source_issues: Song 746 line 3: corrupt character in கொங்¨க்முழ்கி; probably கொங்கைமூழ்கி.
Song 746 line 15: corrupt character in த¨முள; probably தழலுள (in fire).
Song 746 line 22: corrupt character in லு¡றிய; probably லூறிய.

reading: The poet describes women with faces like the moon, eyes like carp, fragrant long hair and breasts in which he drowns, who fall upon men daily while he sips the honey of their lips, and calls himself a dog; he asks whether it is right to languish in ruin without seeking Murugan's anklet-ringed feet, his twelve shoulders and earrings, the peacock, the vel, the cock, the trident and the bow. The praise names the vel that crushed the Sura armies, chariots and elephants and burned their city while ghouls and Kali danced on the corpses, and the shrine at Manikuzhi where monkeys leap in areca and plantain groves and honey flows in the ponds, worshipped by the gods.
nuance: The plea is a catalogue of what the poet has failed to seek: the feet first, then the twelve shoulders, the weapons and emblems one by one, as if to contemplate them were the cure (நாடாது பாழில் மயங்கலாமோ). பண்டநாயேன், I the dog, is the self-abuse of the book.

title: திருவேட்களம்
theme: Songs at Thiruvetkalam (திருவேட்களம்): in one the poet vows never to forget the vision of Murugan's feet, faces and gracious look that ended his impurity; in the other he confesses chasing gold for women and praising fools as gods, and asks whether he must wander so.
structure_note: 747 is a song of remembrance with no confession; 748 confesses wasted life and begging.

reading: The poet vows he will not forget what Murugan showed him: the experience of Siva's grace, the anklet feet that dried up his anava impurity, the twelve shoulders and six faces, the form on the peacock that showed the sea of compassion, and the look that gently brought him among the devotees of three Tamils so that he might reach the supreme state. The praise names the vel that scattered the mountains and the Suras' crowns, the goddess who is the power of the foot that struck Death, and Vishnu who set Vidura against Duryodhana and drove Arjuna's chariot, at Thiruvetkalam.
nuance: Each line ends in a thing seen (பாதம், கோலம், பார்வை) and the whole song hangs on மறவேனே, 'I will not forget': it is thanksgiving, not plea. ஆணவ மலம் அற்றிட is Saiva Siddhanta language for the root impurity. சிவபத்தினி கூற்றினை மோதிய பதசத்தினி makes the goddess the power in the foot that kicked Death, the left foot being hers. The opening lines (சதுரத்தரை நோக்கிய பூவொடு கதிரொத்திட ஆக்கிய கோளகை) are obscure.

reading: The poet confesses that, not reckoning that life may slip in a moment, he took this life as lasting, and for the desires roused by women who receive any man, he went seeking gold, praising fools in the world as if each were Vishnu of the milk sea, and asks whether he must wander so. The praise names Murugan as the lord of the state reached by those who leave the six systems and still the mind, the son of the dancer to the beat, the bridegroom of the hunters' peacock girl, at Thiruvetkalam where the Vedas sound.
nuance: பார்க்களம் மீதினில் மூர்க்கரையே கவி பாற்கடலான் என: the poet's fault is flattering patrons as gods for gold; the gold is wanted for women (பாற்படு ஆடகம்). சாத்திரம் ஆறையும் நீத்த மனோலய சாத்தியர் sets the goal beyond all six philosophical systems.

title: திருநெல்வாயில்
theme: A song at Thirunelvayil (திருநெல்வாயில்): the poet confesses he sang fine Tamil to fools, misers and cheats and now lies in the fire of poverty like a writhing worm, and asks for pity; the praise sets the joy of the heavenly women against the grief of the demons' widows and names the vel that split the mango in the sea.
source_issues: Song 749 line 1: corrupt characters in அறிவி லாதவ ¡£னர்; probably அறிவிலாத ஈனர்.
Song 749 line 19: corrupt character in லு¡டு; probably லூடு.

reading: The poet lists the men he has praised: the witless and base, the double-tongued, misers, sinners, fools who adorn women, men who perish melting for women, who do not know the fruit of the books of justice, who take wealth by gambling, and fools fallen into the world's delusion; to them he sang fine Tamil until his thought was ruined and his eyes failed, and now, lying in the fire of poverty like a long worm writhing, he asks Murugan to pity him. The praise sets the heavenly dancers who rejoice and sing embracing their lovers against the wives of the slain demons who weep for their husbands, and names the vel that cut in two the tree that hid in the sea and spread a crore of branches, at Nelvayil with its fields and moon-touched mansions.
nuance: சிறந்த தமிழ் கூறி: the confession is not of lust but of misusing Tamil on unworthy patrons, and the list of patrons runs to a dozen kinds. The praise is a diptych of joy and grief, the gods' women and the demons' widows (மணாளர் தோள் பிரிந்து). The tree in the sea (கவடு கோடியின் மேலுமாய்ப் பரந்து வளரும் மா) is Sura's last form, split in two by the vel.

title: விருத்தாசலம்
theme: Songs at Viruthachalam (விருத்தாசலம், முதுகிரி): the poet rejects courtesans who sell themselves and strip men of wealth, asks for grace among the loveless, and describes old age with staff and failing eyes as a birth to be freed from; the praise names Murugan who taught Siva and impaled the Jains.
structure_note: 750 on courtesans, 751 mostly praise with a short plea, 752 on old age.

reading: The poet describes women with breasts like lotus pots, moon brows, hair like cloud, carp eyes, voices like the yaazh, parrot and cuckoo, and the gait of peacocks, who mock the many lustful men, smile like lightning and strip of wealth those who kiss them, women who sell themselves, and asks whether their friendship befits him. The praise names Rama who bridged the sea and destroyed Ravana's clan as uncle, Siva who cut Brahma's head and burned the cities, Uma in Siva's half, the vel that uprooted the poisonous asuras and freed the gods, Murugan the beautiful one of the hunter girl, at Viruthachalam where 'my mother' dwells.
nuance: விலைமாதர், women with a price, and பொருள் பறிப்பார், who snatch wealth, make the charge explicit. என தாய் உறை விருத்தாசலம names the shrine's goddess as the poet's own mother.

reading: Mostly praise: Murugan, born in the pond, once gave Siva the holy word as Siva served at his side; at Madurai he sent the Jains to the stake; he came to Arunai in an instant so the whole world praised him; he became a tree before the hunter girl's eyes; he is Hari's nephew and the first one who speaks in compassion. In the middle the poet, suffering among those who have no love for Murugan's grace, asks whether he will be given grace, at Mudhukiri, the old hill.
nuance: அரன் உனது உழி பணி செய முன் அருளிய: Siva serves at Murugan's side to receive the word, the teaching of Om in the book's usual story, here without naming Om. அருணையில் ஒருநொடி தனில் வரு மயில்வீரா refers to an appearance at Tiruvannamalai, which tradition ties to the poet's own life; the text says only that he came in a moment. The last line (முடிபவர் வடிவறு சுசிகர முறைதமிழ்) is obscure.

reading: The poet describes old age: the body dried and sapless as deeds ripen, the gait tottering, the hands scratching, the teeth bare, eyes blinded by cataract, skin wrinkled like fruit, hair white as a crane, bile and wind rising, weak, gripping a staff and left standing outside; he asks whether there will be a day when Murugan frees him from this birth of suffering and sets grace on him. The praise names the gods led by Indra who covered the earth with flowers after Murugan's victory over the asuras, Krishna as his uncle, and the Siva devotees who sang sweet words and won grace at Viruddhagiri.
nuance: The portrait of age is built of small physical signs, and its last image, வெளிநிற்கும் விதம், standing outside the house, adds the social exclusion of the old. The plea is not against age itself but against the birth (ஜனனம்) that leads to it. The Siva devotees who won grace with sweet words may be the Tevaram poets; the text does not name them.

title: வேப்பூர்
theme: A song at Veppur (வேப்பூர்): the poet asks Murugan to speak to him with his own word the form of the experience that shines to those who, with both kinds of deeds gone, sleep in awareness; the praise names the burning of the sea and the demons' widows entering the fire.

reading: The poet asks that, rather than tending the hut that carries life and dances in this sea-girt world and the dark-eyed people with their quarrels, he be told by Murugan's own holy word the form of the experience (அநுபூதி) that shines only to those who, both kinds of deeds ended, sleep in awareness. The praise names an episode of the Kuru clan, the wives of the night-roaming demons leaping into fire while Indra's city prospers, the vel that set the sea ablaze to its depths, and Veppur, whose fertile fields end want in the seven worlds.
nuance: இருவினையற உணர்வொடு தூங்குவார்க்கே விளங்கும் அநுபூதி: the state is open only to those in whom good and bad deeds have ceased and who sleep yet are aware, a known description of the knower's waking sleep. The plea is for teaching by word (வாக்கால் மொழிந்தருள). குருகுல வேந்து தேர்ப்பாகன் மைந்தன் probably alludes to Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer, but how the phrase splits and whose son is meant is unclear.

title: நிம்பபுரம்
theme: A song at Nimbapuram (நிம்பபுரம்): the poet asks for the one release beyond elements, organs, day and night, beginning and end, and for delight in Tamil to sing the feet that went into the forest for the hunter girl.

reading: The poet asks to gain that one release which knows neither the five elements, the four inner faculties, night nor day, and has no end, middle or beginning, and for the delight of fine Tamil to sing the lotus feet that came into the forest seeking the hunter maiden of the misty slopes. The praise names Murugan's chest that embraces Devayanai's kumkum and sandal breasts, the vel thrown so Sura's heart split and the mountain shook, and the lord of Nimbapuram with its walls, the king of heaven and earth.
nuance: The release is defined by negation: அஞ்சுவித பூதமும் கரண நாலும் are tattvas, and அந்தி பகல் யாதும் அறியாத is the state beyond waking and sleep. The way to it is song: the feet to be sung are those that walked to Valli, so the love story becomes the subject of the release-giving Tamil. குஞ்சர கலாப வஞ்சி is Devayanai, raised by Indra's elephant.

title: வேப்பஞ்சந்தி
theme: A short song at Veppanchandhi (வேப்பஞ்சந்தி): the poet asks that his gaze not sink into women's breasts and praises the giver of lotus feet to devotees, the warrior vel, and Ganapati's younger brother.

reading: A short song: the poet asks that his gaze not settle and sink on the hills of women's breasts, and names Murugan as the one who gives his lotus feet to the devotees who hold firm. The praise names the battle in which he scattered the hosts who came against the gods, the vel that shines with the mind of Death, and Murugan as younger brother of the pot-bellied elephant god, at Veppanchandhi.
nuance: The song is in clipped beats, and the plea is one line: நாட்டம் தங்கிக் கொங்கைக் குவடில் படியாதே, the eye is the point of danger. கூற்றன் பந்திச் சிந்தைக் குணமொத்து ஒளிர்வேலா, a vel like Death in temper, is my reading of a hard split.

title: திருக்கூடலையாற்றூர்
theme: A song at Koodalaiyatrur (திருக்கூடலையாற்றூர்): the poet confesses that deeds, the three desires and women's charms brought disease, and asks that when Death's summons comes Kalan not approach; the praise names Siva at Madurai bearing sand, the goddess who burned Death, and Murugan who lives in the poet's heart.

reading: The poet says that his deeds surrounded him, desire and the three desires lit a fire like an axe heated in the forge, and that, adorned with flowers, sandal, civet and rosewater, he sported with women of painted eyes until caught in their net, then disease, pain and wind came on him, and he had no love for Murugan; he asks that when Yama's men drive him and the summons marked by Brahma arrives, cruel Kalan not come near, and that Murugan give him his grace and love. The praise names Murugan who freed the gods with the vel and loved the hunter girl, Siva who came to Madurai in another form and bore sand on the Vaigai's bank, burned the cities and rides the bull, the goddess who burned Death, and Murugan who leapt so that Death fell and who lives in the poet's body, at the meeting of the Vellar and Manimuthar.
nuance: மூவாசை are the three desires, for land, gold and women by tradition. சீட்டு is Death's written summons, which Brahma has marked (வேதன் அடையாளம்). The praise turns the same motif round: கூற்றுவனைக் காய்ந்த அபிராமி and கூற்று விழத் தாண்டி name the goddess and Murugan as conquerors of Death. மதுராபுரியில் ஆடி வைகை ஆற்றின் மணல் தாங்கு is Siva's carrying earth at Madurai, and எனது ஆகமதில் வாழ் places Murugan within the poet.

title: கடம்பூர்
theme: A song at Kadambur (கடம்பூர்): the poet describes dancing women who invite a man in, demand money and leave in spite when it is not enough, and asks not to go where they are; the praise names Vishnu as uncle and Siva's dance sung by Narada and Tumburu.
source_issues: Song 757 line 2: corrupt character in னியலு¡டே; probably னியலூடே.

reading: The poet describes dancing women who say 'come here, this is the house', tell their maids to spread the mat, speak like courteous hosts and take a man to bed, then before joining him say the cash and the cloth are not enough and go off in spite; he asks not to go where they are and to be given Murugan's cool feet. The praise names Narayana, Rama, Kesava with the discus as his uncle, Siva who dances while Narada and Tumburu sing as his father, and the vel that sent Sura's sea to ruin so the sun's chariot could run, at Kadambur where the Kaveri and Seeraru meet.
nuance: The women's own speech is quoted (வாரும் இங்கே வீடிதோ, வாடி பெண்காள் பாயைப் போடும்), as in Kural and Naladiyar warnings; ஆசார வாசகம் போல், like words of courtesy, names the pretence. காசு ஆடை போதாமை is the turn: love lasts until the price falls short. Some words of the opening (பணம் பாஷாணம், மால் கடந்தே போம் மேனி) are hard to construe.

title: திருவரத்துறை
theme: A song at Thiruvarathurai (திருவரத்துறை): the poet asks whether he should fall to young women who flirt, steal hearts and wealth and exhaust a man on the bed; the praise makes Murugan the four-Veda child of Sirkazhi to whom the Lord of the shrine gave the pearl palanquin.

reading: The poet describes women who, angry or kind, put on kohl, call sweetly, recite poems, laugh and sport, melt the heart with arts of stealth, cruelly snatch away what a man had saved, embrace his neck and leave him faint on the bed, and asks whether he should be caught by them. The praise names Murugan as the one who stills birth, the partless Brahman in whose sea of conscious bliss sages bathe, and as the four-Veda child of Kochai to whom the Lord gave the pearl umbrella and palanquin, at Thiruvarathurai.
nuance: களவு வித்தை and முன் கருதி வைத்த வைப்பவை சேர தறுகணில் பறித்து: theft is named twice, of the heart and of the hoard. கொச்சை is Sirkazhi, and the pearl palanquin at Arathurai belongs to Sambandar's story; the song addresses that child as Murugan (சதுர்வேதச் சிறுவ), the book's identification of Murugan with Sambandar.

title: யாழ்ப்பாணாயன்பட்டினம்
theme: A song at Yazhppanayanpattinam (யாழ்ப்பாணாயன்பட்டினம், Jaffna): the poet asks to be rid of desire for women whose eyes are Kama's arrows and Death's messengers and who bind the rich with illusion, and to gain knowledge by Murugan's word; the praise is a litany of the goddess and Murugan as guru and giver of Tamil.
source_issues: Heading: யாழ்ப்பாணாயன்பட்டினம் is Jaffna (யாழ்ப்பாணம்); the song's last line has the same form.

reading: The poet describes flower-haired women whose glance is spear and sword, Kama's war arrows and Death's own messenger, who daily bind those with money in hand in delusion, skilled in illusion, with nectar lips and lying words, thread waists and perfumed, jewelled breasts, and asks Murugan to destroy his desire for their bodies and grant that by his true word he gain knowledge and worship him. The praise is a litany of the mother: Vishnu's sister, the maiden Uma, Sivai who dances in bliss, Tripurai, Bhairavi among ghouls, lady of the worlds who makes, holds and destroys and dwells at Siva's side in play; her son is the guru of the renouncers' knowledge and the giver of the Tamil prosodists weigh, at Yazhppanayanpattinam with its golden walls.
nuance: நமன் விடு தூது: the women's eyes are Death's messengers, joining the book's two themes in one image. கைப்பொருள் உடையவர் marks them as women who want money. The goddess litany (திரிபுரை, பயிரவி, புவநேசை) uses Sakta names. யாழ்ப்பாணாயன் பட்டினம் is Jaffna, one of the book's shrines in Lanka.

title: ஸ்ரீமுஷ்டம்
theme: Songs at Srimushnam (ஸ்ரீமுஷ்டம், திருமுட்டம்): one asks Murugan to appear wearing every kind of pearl garland on the peacock with his consort and devotees; the other rejects courtesans who snatch money and ruin families; the praise names the goddess, Devayanai, and the daughter of Adi Varaha.
structure_note: 760 is a vision prayer with no confession; 761 is a courtesan song.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to come before him on the green peacock with his consort and the throng of his servants, wearing on his chest garlands of pearls from bamboo, cloud, elephant, mountain, conch, sea, serpent and fire. The praise names the mother who bore us, bright as rain-cloud and lisping like cuckoo and parrot, the dark-throated Siva with datura, Murugan their son, the bridegroom of Devayanai and of the lady of release, who cut the bonds of the gods Sura had imprisoned, at Thirumuttam.
nuance: The pearl list follows the traditional sources of pearls (bamboo, cloud, elephant tusk, conch, sea, cobra), each as a separate garland; the plea is simply to see. அடிமைக் குழாமொடு: Murugan is asked to come with the company of his servants, not alone. திருமுத்தி மாதின் மணவாளா, bridegroom of the lady of release, is either a name of Valli or a figure.

tamil: விருதிட் டுக்குடி கேடிகள் சேடிகள் ...... உ றவாமோ
reading: The poet describes women with arrow-eyes and bow brows who stir deep infatuation and dance to the beat, and calls them greedy prostitutes who snatch money, deceivers, sinners, worn by excess, quarrel-makers, ruiners of families, and asks whether their friendship befits him. The praise names Siva who burned Kama with laughter, the goddess at his side who bore the three worlds, Rama who churned the sea with Vasuki and gave the first nectar, and Murugan who sported with the daughter of Adi Varaha at Thirumuttam.
nuance: The second half of the confession is a run of abusive nouns in -கள் (பறிகாரிகள், மாறிகள், கேடிகள்) set to the rhythm; பணம் எத்தப் பறிகாரிகள் and குடிகேடிகள் carry the charge. ஆதிவராகர் தம் மகள் makes Valli the daughter of Vishnu as the Boar, whose temple is at Srimushnam.

title: திருநல்லூர்
theme: A yogic song at Thirunallur (திருநல்லூர்): the poet describes the ascent from the root centre through the three mandalas and bindu and nada, up the central pillar on the rope of knowledge, and asks whether he will meet the light of a hundred crore moons; the praise names the goddess and the saint who imposed the ash on the Jains.
source_issues: Song 762 line 24: corrupt character in லு¡ர; probably லூர (Nallur).

reading: The poet describes an inner ascent: the root centre and the mantra of experience, the supreme lights of the three mandalas, the six centres, the boundless light of a thousand rays, bindu and nada, the sound of 'Olam' kept to many rhythms, the nectar drunk, the course of moon, sun and fire stilled, and the climb up the middle pillar on the rope of knowledge, and asks whether he will not meet the light of a hundred crore moons. The praise names the goddess by many names, Murugan as destroyer of Sura and helper of Indra, who dances to the sound of the Veda, the lotus-handed one who put sacred ash on so that the Jains who refused it died on the stake, the lover of Devayanai and the doe, at Nallur where Siva as Thiyagar dwells.
nuance: The plea is a single question (சத கோடி சந்த்ர ஒளி சந்தியாதோ) at the top of a ladder of yogic terms: மூலம், மண்டலம் மூணு, விந்து நாதம், நடு தூண் (the central channel), ஞான வண் கயிறு. சீல வெண்பொடி இடாத வெஞ்சமணர் மாள ... நீறிடும் is the Sambandar story again. Many compounds in the first half split uncertainly.

title: திருமயேந்திரம்
theme: A song at Thirumayendram (திருமயேந்திரம்): the poet describes women who rejoice at gold and, when it is gone, hand a man the begging bowl and staff and poison him, and asks whether he must wander as a dog; the praise names the vel that ground the asuras while Death swung his noose.

reading: The poet describes women with bee-haunted hair, arrow eyes, pearl teeth, cuckoo voices and creeper waists who rejoice and chatter when they see gold, gossip, flatter and dance making eyes whirl, cheats who, when the gold is gone, hand a man the begging bowl and staff and say 'go', and even give poison, and asks whether he, a dog, must wander and perish for them. The praise tells how, when the gods and sages and Brahma cried out, Murugan came saying 'fear not' and threw the vel that crushed the asuras, turned mountains to dust while Death swung his noose, names him son of Siva with the ash and serpent and moon in his hair, and lover of the moon-faced girl who has entered the poet's heart, at Mayendram.
nuance: பொன் கண்டவுடன் களிகூர்ந்து and கஞ்சுளியும் தடியும் ஈந்து போ என: the women's welcome begins at gold and ends by sending the man away as a beggar. அந்தகனும் கயிறு ஆங்கை வீசிட turns Death's noose against the asuras. என்றன் உளம் புகு பாங்கி மானொடு is uncertain: the doe may be Valli, and பாங்கி may be her companion.

title: சீகாழி
theme: Songs at Sirkazhi (சீகாழி, also called Pugali, Sanbai, Kochchai, Kazhumalam and Brahmapuram): the poet confesses to courtesans who take money, to the decaying body and to delusion, and two songs voice a lovesick girl; the praise again and again makes Murugan the child-saint of Sirkazhi who sang Tamil at Madurai, cured the Pandya with holy ash and sent the Jains to the stakes.
structure_note: Courtesan songs (767, 770, 776) and the poet's infatuation (765, 769); the body (766) and royal comfort ending in ash (774); the patron-singer's shame (768, 773); praise and vows of remembrance (771, 775); akam songs in a lovesick girl's own voice (764) and another's (772), and one that folds love-sickness into the hour of death (777). The Sambandar identification runs through 766 to 769, 774 and appears in 764 (the Kaundinya son).
source_issues: Song 765: two corrupt characters in வ ¡£ரா (line 13), probably வீரா; மூடர் is written முடர் throughout lines 9 to 12, an unflagged loss of the long vowel.
Song 768: one corrupt character in சுற்று¡ மர் (line 9), probably சுற்றும் அமணர் or சுற்று அமணர்.
Song 773: one corrupt character in தெற்கிலு¡தை (line 2), probably தெற்கில் ஊதை, 'the south wind'.
Song 775: two corrupt characters in ஆலவ ¡£தரு (line 14), probably அருளால் அவர் ஈதரு.

reading: In the voice of a lovesick girl, the singer says the sea, Kama's bow, the evening wind, the blame of women, the swinging bull-bells, the anril and the cuckoo come at her like fire; she melts like wax, sweats, finds musk and agil like poison, her ornaments burn to ash and her breasts pour heat, and she asks whether, his anger ended, he will not give her his honeyed, vel-adorned garland of lotus and end her longing. The praise names Uma as Bhairavi and Tripura, riding the lion and dancing with Siva among ghosts and drums, Valli who served at his feet, and Murugan the Kaundinya son of Kazhi.
nuance: அரிவையர் வசை, the blame of women, is the gossip (அலர்) of classical akam, set beside the anril, the cuckoo and the bull's bell. என் மாலை is probably மால், her infatuation, playing on the garland (தார்) she asks for. கவுணியர் மைந்த, son of the Kaundinyas, is Sambandar's clan name given to Murugan. The lines on Valli serving his feet among peacocks, cuckoos and parrots are hard to divide.

tamil: இரத மான தேனூற லதர மான மாமாத
இனது போடு மேகாச உ டையி னாலு மாலால
விரக மாகி யேபாய லிடைவி டாமல் நாடோறு
விளையு மோக மாமாயை கழலு மாறு நாயேனும்
அரக ராஎ னர்முடர் திருவெ ணீறி டர்முடர்
அறிவு நூல்க லர்முடர் நெறியி லேநி லர்முடர்
புயலு லாவு சேணாடு பரவி நாளு மீடேறு
reading: The poet confesses that, maddened by the honeyed lips, breasts, slipping silk and poisonous eyes of women, he lay day after day in passion, sunk in the shade of their musk-scented hair, and asks that, worthless as he is, the great delusion this breeds come loose and grace be given. The praise speaks of the fools who do not say Hara, do not wear the holy ash, do not anoint the Lord's feet, do not learn the books of knowledge, keep to no path and weigh no dharma, rolling in the seven hells, and calls Murugan the light and full form who lives at Pugali.
nuance: The repeated மூடர் (written முடர் here) marks a list of the irreligious: those who do not cry அரகரா, wear திருவெணீறு or learn அறிவு நூல். கரையேற, 'to reach the shore', sits in the list in a way that leaves unclear whether these fools are the ones Murugan lifts out or the ones who fall; the reading takes the seven hells as their end. விழலன், a useless reed, is the poet's name for himself.

tamil: ஊனத்தசை தோல்கள் சுமந்த காயப்பொதி மாய மிகுந்த
ஓதப்படு நாலு முகன்ற னாலுற்றிடு கோல மெழுந்து
கூனித்தடி யோடு நடந்து ஈனப்படு கோழை மிகுந்த
கூசப்பிர மாண ப்ரபஞ்ச மாயக்கொடு நோய்க ளகன்று
சேனக்குரு கூடலி லன்று ஞானத்தமிழ் நூல்கள் பகர்ந்து
தீரத்திரு நீறு புரிந்து மீனக்கொடி யோனுடல் துன்று
கானச்சிறு மானை நினைந்து ஏனற்புன மீது நடந்து
காணக்கணி யாக வளர்ந்து ஞானக்குற மானை மணந்து
reading: The poet calls the body a bundle of flesh and skin, a stinking, pus-hot hut shaped by the four-faced Brahma who recites the Vedas, which runs, stumbles, tires, walks bent on a stick and fills with phlegm, and says he has loved this rubbish-body; he asks that the cruel diseases of the illusory world leave him and that today he be given the beautiful feet. The praise makes Murugan the teacher who at Kudal spoke Tamil books of wisdom, sent the Jain host up the stakes and with holy ash cured the fish-bannered king's fever, and who wooed Valli in the millet field and lives at Kazhi.
nuance: ப்ரபஞ்ச மாயக் கொடுநோய்கள்: the diseases are of the world as maya, not of the body only. The second half tells Sambandar's Madurai story in detail (ஞானத்தமிழ் நூல்கள் பகர்ந்து, சமணோர் கழுவின்கண் மிசையேற, திருநீறு, மீனக்கொடியோன்) and calls its hero குருநாதா, so the saint is Murugan himself.

reading: The poet describes women graceful as a bow, scented, jewelled and finely clothed, praised as matchless by ring-handed men, who tend their bodies, run many trades and will not give a man a moment without money, deceivers who do not worship the Lord's feet; fallen among them, a sinner, he asks how he can reach the shore and begs for one gift by a wonder. The praise shows the vel that turned the dark hill to dust and ruined Sura's city, the peacock, Devayanai and Valli, heralds blowing 'divine supreme guru', and the hand that gave ash and sent the Jains to the stakes at Brahmapuram, Kazhi.
nuance: பணமே ஒரு காசு and சற்பனைகாரர் (deceivers) mark the women as courtesans. பாதகன், sinner, and எப்படி ஓர் கரை சேர்வது set the plea as a crossing. நீறிடு கையா ... கழுவேறிட again gives Sambandar's deeds to Murugan; பிரமாபுரம் is one of Sirkazhi's twelve names. The opening lines are hard to divide.

reading: In tight, clipped rhythm the poet says he sang verses for men blind with drink, lust and anger, in rambling, padded words, and wore himself out for a bent and wretched gain, and asks Murugan to remove this evil. The praise tells how he sang away the fever of the Pandya Maran, against the shameless mat-wrapped Jains, and came to Kazhi, chased Valli through the thorny forest, and calls him pearl, the three fires, father, pure one, ancient one, lord of release.
nuance: The confession is of the patron-poet's trade, singing praise to the unworthy (கவிபாடிக் கச்சா பிச்சா), as in 245 and 773. மாறன் வெப்பு ஆறப் பாடி is Sambandar curing the Pandya's fever; பாய் சுற்று அமணர் are the Jains wrapped in mats. The compressed syllables make most of the plea uncertain.

reading: The poet says he was drawn by women's hair, poisoned eyes, breasts, waists, gait, words, lips and smiles, a doubter without tradition and a wretch, yet the Lord gave him by grace the sight of the two anklet-bearing feet that ended his wasted days, and this he will not forget in dream or waking. The praise shows the sea crying out and the demons' crowns broken by the vel, Murugan of Sanbai who thinks of the gods' troubles, and ends with a long abuse of the Jains as sinners without dharma and the eight thousand sent to the stakes.
nuance: Unusually the plea is a thanksgiving: grace has already been given (விழி அருள் தந்த பேரருள்), and the vow is கனவிலும் நனவிலும் மறவேனே. The abuse of the Jains (பறிதலை, அறநெறி பயனிலர், கழுமிசை) takes up the whole close; எணாயிரர், the eight thousand, is the number the Sambandar story gives.

reading: The poet describes sandal-anointed, bangled women of swan gait and deceitful minds who come close to those who give wealth, steal it with charm and spells, flare up if no gold is given now and quarrel that a month has passed without a gift, and asks for grace so that this poison and cruel poverty leave him. The praise names Murugan the nephew of the cloud-hued one who held the mountain as an umbrella for the herds in the rain, the Saravanabhava of Ambika, brother of the elephant-faced god and husband of Valli, at Sanbai where bees hum the rhythm in champaka groves.
nuance: நிதிதர, பொருள்கவர், செம்பொன் இங்கு இனி இலையெனில் and the month without a gift (திங்கள் ஒன்றினில் ... பொருள் உதவிலன்) make the money plain. தந்த்ர மந்த்ரிகள் accuses the women of spells. The poverty asked to be removed (கொடு மிடிமை) is the result of the courtesans. மந்தரம் குடையென is the story of Krishna lifting the hill, with the hill named Mandara.

reading: The poet vows never to forget, and to speak with love, Murugan's glories: the Tamil that confounded the Jains and those who said there is no faith, his grace, victory and renown, Saravana, the vel, the peacock, the feet the gods melt to worship, his gifts, and his stroking of Valli's feet and marrying her. The praise is long on Vishnu, who burnt Lanka, saved the elephant in the pool, broke the cart and the marutha trees, became the dwarf and shot at the sea, as Murugan's uncle, and ends at Brahmapuram, where Indra did penance and Guha dwells in hearts.
nuance: There is no confession: the plea is the vow மறவேனே, so the song is a list of what to remember. சமயமும் ஒன்றிலை என்றவரும் பறிதலையரும் sets those who deny any faith beside the Jains, both silenced by Tamil. The Vishnu catalogue gathers Rama and Krishna stories (சகடு, மருது, குறள்) into one uncle.

reading: In a short song in another's voice, the singer says that the moon rising from the sea like fire, the fragrant south wind and the night coming at evening have made the simple girl in love faint and stand alone, and asks Murugan to shine so that the conch-filled sea grows dim. He is the one who fights with the poison-bright vel, sweet to the words of rhythmic poets, at Sanbai.
nuance: The voice is a mother's or companion's (அன்புற்றெழு பேதை மயங்கித் தனியானாள்), and the classical torments of evening are the moon, the south wind and the dark. சந்தக்கவி நூலினர் may glance at the poet's own rhythmic verse.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to see how he stands ashamed, having wilted in mind and sung rich verses to rubbish men, calling them elephants, mountains of gold, wish-trees of giving, suns of the three worlds and treasuries of the learned; the opening tormentors, the crescent in the red sky, Kama of the cane bow, the southern wind, the vina and the gossip of mothers, are a lover's, and how they bear on the plea is unclear. The praise makes Murugan the one who taught the principle of the Veda beyond Vishnu and Brahma, split the hill and struck Sura hiding in the mango, the Muttamizh lord of Kochchai.
nuance: செத்தை யோகத்தினர், men of rubbish worth, and the flattering titles (கற்பதாரு, செகத்த்ரய பாநு) show the patron-poet's shame again, as in 768. The teaching of the தத்வ வேதம் to those Vishnu and Brahma could not reach is the guru-myth without Om named. The first four lines may describe the poet as a lover, or a girl's torments; the split is uncertain.

tamil: தினமணி சார்ங்க பாணி யெனமதிள் நீண்டு சால
செழுமணி சேர்ந்த பீடி கையிலிசை வாய்ந்த பாடல்
இனவளை பூண்கை யார்க வரியிட வேய்ந்து மாலை
இனிதிரு மாந்து வாழு மிருவினை நீண்ட காய
வனசர ரேங்க வான முகடுற வோங்கி ஆசை
மயிலொடு மான்கள் சூழ வளவரி வேங்கை யாகி
கனசமண் மூங்கர் கோடி கழுமிசை தூங்க நீறு
கவிதரு காந்த பால கழுமல பூந்த ராய
reading: The poet pictures a life of royal comfort: walls and mansions reaching the sun, a jewelled seat, singers on both sides, bangled women waving chowries, garlands, musk, agil and sandal paste, ruling as a king, and asks whether this body of two deeds, living in pride, should simply become a handful of ash. The praise shows Murugan taking the magic form of a vengai tree on the hill among the hunters with Valli and her friends, sending the Jains to the stakes and giving the Pandya land the ash in grace, the Kaundinya king at Kazhumalam.
nuance: ஒருபிடி சாம்பல், a handful of ash, is the whole of the rhetorical question; the splendour is described only to be weighed against it. வேங்கையாகி மலைமிசை தோன்றும் மாய வடிவோனே: Murugan's disguise as a tree in the Valli story. கனசமண் ... கழுமிசை தூங்க நீறு கருணைகொள் பாண்டி நாடு is Sambandar's story again.

reading: The praise tells how Vishnu with Lakshmi on his breast, four-faced Brahma, Indra and the sages, not having searched the Vedas, fled in fear from the warring asuras and praised Siva with garlands of song, Siva of the ash, konrai, Ganga, moon and serpent, and how by his grace the war-vel and Murugan on the blue peacock came, crossing the earth and six worlds in a moment as general of the gods. The plea asks Murugan to protect the deceiver who wanders without praising him with love as moon-faced, Kama-lovely and kadamba-garlanded.
nuance: The song is nearly all praise, built as a narrative of Murugan's birth for the war with the asuras; the confession is only வஞ்சனேனை, the poet's failure to praise. The lines naming the adornments of Siva's matted hair (மாதுளை, கூவிளை) and the line with corrupt characters (ஆலவ ... தரு) are hard to divide.

tamil: மதனச்சொற் காரக் காரிகள் பவளக்கொப் பாடச் சீறிகள்
மவுனச்சுட் டாடிச் சோலிகள் இசலிப்பித் தாசைக் காரிகள்
குதலைச்சொற் சாரப் பேசிகள் நரகச்சிற் சாடிப் பீடிகள்
கொளுவிக்கட் டாசைப் பாசனை பவதுக்கக் காரச் சூதனை
கதறக்கற் சூரைக் கார்கட லெரியத்திக் கூறிற் பாழ்பட
கதிர்சுற்றிட் டாசைப் பால்கிரி யுறைபச்சைப் பாசக் கோகில
திதலைப்பொற் பாணிக் கார்குயி லழகிற்பொற் றோகைப் பாவையை
திலதப்பொட் டாசைச் சேர்முக மயிலுற்றிட் டேறிக் காழியில்
reading: The poet heaps up names for the women who sell themselves: women of love-words and coral earrings, scolders in silk, women of silent hints and quarrels, lisping talkers, pits of hell, and asks that he, bound by desire, the trickster caught in birth's sorrow, be given service at Murugan's golden lotus feet. The praise shows the vel that made the sea roar and burn and fed the sky's kites, Gauri's son, Valli embraced daily, and Murugan who rides the peacock at Kazhi and spoke into Siva's ear what Siva praised.
nuance: விலைமாதர், women for a price, names the trade, and the long string of -காரிகள், -சோலிகள் forms an insult catalogue in the rhythm. சிவன் மெச்சக் காதுக்கு ஓதிய: the teaching in Siva's ear, with Om not named. சேவையில் அருள்வாயே asks for service (சேவை) at the feet, not only for refuge.

reading: The poet says the moonlight burns like poison and the undersea fire and spreads like the sun, Kama's flower arrows wound, and on the last day, when fire boils in every direction and Death comes near to strike, he asks Murugan to come with grace and embrace him in that helpless, bewildered state. The praise shows the peacock-like Valli given by the hill people and Devayanai of the elephant, Murugan as younger brother of the elephant-faced god, son given by the mountain's daughter, Vishnu's nephew and the lord of Kazhumalam.
nuance: The torments of a lover (the moon, Kama's arrows) run straight into the day of death (கடைநாளில் அணுகி நமன் எற்ற), so that the lover's longing and the dying man's need meet in one request: அவசமொடு அணைத்து அருள வரவேணும். It is unclear whether the first half is the poet's own or a borrowed lover's voice.

title: கரியவனகர்
theme: The single song at Kariyavanagar (கரியவனகர்): a confession to courtesans who take money and turn away the penniless, a plea to be shown the feet, and praise of the battle and of Murugan who listens to songs in Tamil.
source_issues: Song 778: one corrupt character in மிசையிற் று¡சு (line 7), probably மிசையில் தூசு, with the long ஊ lost.

reading: The poet lists what the women do: show their bee-circled hair, kindle the fire of union with their eyes, spend the time in bed, give themselves to young men and ask for coins, show a peacock's grace, parade the streets, brush dust from their breasts, put face to face to rouse desire, send far away those without wealth and measure up anyone to embrace, and asks that love for them be removed, his trouble ended, and grace given by showing the feet. The praise shows the battlefield of blood, ghosts and vultures and the vel that killed the night-roamers, Murugan on the peacock with a golden garland, son of Parvati, worshipped by Valli, who in grace hears songs in Tamil at Kariyavanagar.
nuance: காசு கேட்கவும் and இருநிதி இலரைத் தூர நீக்கவும் (sending away those without wealth) make these courtesans. The confession is built as a string of infinitives (-வும்), each a habit of the women. கருணைய தமிழிற் பாடல் கேட்டருள் may point to the poet's own songs.

title: வைத்தீசுரன் கோயில்
theme: Songs at Vaitheeswaran Koyil (வைத்தீசுரன் கோயில், the Velur of the physician Lord): the poet confesses the darkness of mala, countless births in delusion and the lure of courtesans, and asks for the feet of wisdom, the company of devotees and the yogic ascent to nectar; the praise names Murugan as lord of the healer's shrine.
structure_note: Short plea against mala (779); births and maya (780, 782); courtesans (781, 784); and a full kundalini song (783) that sets the body's yoga against the courtesan's bed of the next.
source_issues: Songs 780, 783, 784: one corrupt character each in §வ்ளுர் (lines 15, 17 and 24), for வேளூர், the shrine's name.
Song 783: முலாதாரமொ (line 1) is probably மூலாதாரமொ, an unflagged loss of the long vowel.
The chapter heading names Vaitheeswaran Koyil; the songs call it வேளூர் (Pullirukkuvelur).

reading: The poet says he cannot speak even a little of Murugan, the unique wisdom of the heart, and asks whether, like a block of wood, he should perish covered in the darkness of mala. The praise names Murugan the life of those of high virtue, who grants life at his feet, son of the just giver of boons, Vaidyanatha the lord.
nuance: மரத்துறை போல், like a thing of wood, is the image of the unaware soul, and மலத்திருள் the darkness of impurity of Siddhanta. வயித்திய நாதப் பெருமாளே: the shrine's name for Siva, the physician, is given to Murugan.

tamil: எத்தனை கோடி கோடி விட்டுட லோடி யாடி
இப்படி மோக போக மிப்படி யாகி யாகி
சித்திடில் சீசி சீசி குத்திர மாய மாயை
சித்தினி லாட லோடு முத்தமிழ் வாண ரோது
நித்தமு மோது வார்கள் சித்தமெ வீட தாக
நிட்கள ரூபர் பாதி பச்சுரு வான மூணு
பைத்தலை நீடு மாயி ரத்தலை மீது பீறு
reading: The poet asks how many crores of bodies he has left after running and dancing in them, how many have gone, how often he has fallen into such pleasure and what will come hereafter; caught in the tangle of mean maya, which on thought is only 'chi, chi', he asks for the wondrous feet of wisdom sung by the masters of the three Tamils. The praise shows Murugan dancing in the hearts of those who chant him daily as his house, son of the formless Siva who is half green and bears the trident, on the peacock that tears the thousand-headed serpent, at Velur of the areca and the leaping fish.
nuance: எத்தனை கோடி கோடி விட்டுடல்: the count of bodies left behind opens the song, as in 493. சீசீ, the cry of disgust, is set inside the plea. நிட்கள ரூபர் பாதி பச்சுரு: Siva the partless with the green half that is Uma.

reading: The poet describes women with anklets and silk, like painted dolls, breasts like tower peaks and speech like cane and sugar, who walk the streets with bees around their hair singing like flocks of birds, flatter and trick, saying 'bring money first, then what you like', and set up a ladder for a man to climb, and asks whether this is to be his lot. The praise shows the demons destroyed, hills and seas dried by the vel, gods raining flowers, sages as heralds and Lakshmi praising, Murugan singing to Valli in the millet field, and the child who comes dancing to give kisses at the praise of Siva of the hill of wisdom and his consort.
nuance: வாரும் முற்பணம் தாரும் இட்டமென, 'come, give the money first, then as you please', is the courtesans' own speech. ஏணி வைத்து வந்து ஏற விட்டிடுவர் may mean they lift a man up only to drop him; the image is not clear. நாதர் மெச்ச வந்து ஆடு முத்தம் அருள்: Murugan as the child giving kisses to his parents.

tamil: மாலி னாலெ டுத்த கந்தல் சோறி னால்வ ளர்த்த பொந்தி
மாயை யாலெ டுத்து மங்கி னேனை யாஎ னக்கி ரங்கி
வேலி னால்வி னைக்க ணங்கள் தூள தாஎ ரித்து உ ன்றன்
மேவி யானு னைப்பொல் சிந்தை யாக வேக ளித்து கந்த
காலி னாலெ னப்ப ரந்த சூரர் மாள வெற்றி கொண்ட
காம பாண மட்ட நந்த கோடி மாத ரைப்பு ணர்ந்த
சேலை நேர்வி ழிக்கு றம்பெ ணாசை தோளு றப்பு ணர்ந்து
தேவர் மாதர் சித்தர் தொண்டர் ஏக வேளு ருக்கு கந்த
reading: The poet calls himself a belly raised on rags and rice, a mind that takes changing forms, wasted by unjust maya, and asks Murugan to pity him so that he is not born and does not die again: to burn the hosts of deeds to dust with the vel, set him among the devotees who keep his house of release, make his mind like Murugan's own, and let him say 'Kanda Vel is mine'. The praise names the vel that killed the Suras spread like wind, Siva of the bull as father, Valli embraced, and Murugan who dwells in the love of devotees, worshipped by gods, siddhas and servants at Velur with the cock banner.
nuance: The plea climbs from release from birth to burning deeds (வினைக்கணங்கள் தூளதா எரித்து), to the company of devotees (அன்பர்கண் மேவி), to likeness of mind (உனைப்போல் சிந்தையாக). The line on Siva who burnt Kama's arrows and 'embraced endless crores of women' (காம பாணம் அட்ட நந்த கோடி மாதரைப் புணர்ந்த) is obscure.

reading: The poet describes the yogic ascent: raising the fire from the root centre through the six supports, driving the breath up the middle channel, hearing the music of nada, the milk-white light and the self held fast, then mounting the seat of mantra in the city of wisdom where mother and father sit, and asks Murugan to show him the three lights in that house, feed him the honeyed nectar of the moon and rule him. The praise names Uma who bears the trident and guards day and night, Siva who cured disease and deed at Velur, and Murugan's vel that dried the seven seas, the peacock and his pity for Vishnu's daughter.
