nuance: The plea is technical yoga: மூலாதாரம், ஆறாதாரம், சுழிமுனை, நாதம், and the moon's nectar (சந்திர ... தேனமுது). வீடே மூணொளி காட்டி: in the house of release, show the three lights (perhaps sun, moon and fire). சூடோடு ஈர்வினை வாட்டி ... வாழ்வினை தீர்த்த சங்கரர்: the healing at Vaitheeswaran is named in passing. Several syllable runs in the first half are hard to divide.

tamil: மேனி வாசனைகள் வீச அல்குல் மோதிபரி ...... மளமேற
reading: The poet describes women with swaying hair, breasts, earrings and eyes, scent rising from them, gait like a peacock, anklets ringing and voices like cuckoos, who gather in the streets, call passers-by 'come', melt with play, take them home and embrace them, and asks whether, having sunk in their breasts and sweated on the bed, he must wander in a sea of colic and many diseases. The praise gathers the serpent world, moon and sun worlds, Brahma's world, the gods, ganas, Siva, Brahmins and sages, Narayana, Puranas and Vedic song around the vel thrown at the hill, Valli embraced, and Murugan at Velur on the Kaveri.
nuance: வீதிவருவோரை வாருமெனவே, calling passers-by in the street, and மனையே கொடு அணைவார்கள், taking them home, mark the courtesans. The end of the confession is disease (சூலை பல நோய்கள் கடலாடி), the cost of the bed. The song ends with Velur, but the Kaveri lies some way off.

title: திருக்கடவூர்
theme: Songs at Thirukkadavur (திருக்கடவூர்), where Siva kicked Death: the poet pictures the fated body as food for vultures and asks Murugan to come on the peacock at the hour it falls, and asks for release through yoga; both songs name Siva's defeat of Death.
structure_note: A death song (785) and a yoga song (786); both praises name the kicking of Death that the shrine is known for.
source_issues: Song 786: one corrupt character in அழலு¡டெ (line 3), probably அழலூடே, 'through the fire'.

reading: The poet says that, as written in fate's leaf, the soul is shut in the cruel house of the body, whipped by three lashes and driven like a boat on the sea, gripped by desire for wealth and for women, not knowing where it truly dwells, tending the body and adorning it as if it were Kama; on the day this cave of filth falls to the ground as a packed meal that vultures and crows hail as their food, he asks Murugan to come on the peacock with his anklet-bound feet. The praise retells the Mahabharata, the house set on fire, the dice, the forest and the war, with Krishna as uncle, the vel bright as the sun, and Uma whom Siva joined when he kicked Death, at Kadavur.
nuance: ஏட்டின் விதிப்படி, by the writing on the leaf, puts fate at the start; கசை மூணு, three whips, may be the three humours or the three desires. பொதி சோறு, a packed meal for the road, makes the corpse provisions for the birds. கூற்று மரித்திடவே உதை is the Kadavur story of Siva kicking Death.

tamil: சூலமென வோடு சர்ப்ப வாயுவைவி டாத டக்கி
சூழுமிருள் பாவ கத்தை வீழ அழ லு¡டெ ரித்து
மேலைவெளி யாயி ரத்து நாலிருப ராப ரத்தின்
வேலுமயில் வாக னப்ர காசமதி லேத ரித்து
ஓலசுர ராழி யெட்டு வாளகிரி மாய வெற்பு
ஓதுகுற மான்வ னத்தில் மேவியவள் கால்பி டித்து
காலனொடு மேதி மட்க வூழிபுவி மேல்கி டத்து
காலமுதல் வாழ்பு விக்க தாரநகர் கோபு ரத்துள்
reading: The poet asks to hold the serpent-like breath without letting it go, see the pure light, burn the surrounding darkness of sin in fire, enter the matam where a jewelled seat of light is set, plunge into the space above, the thousand, and the light of Arunachala, and there see the vel and the peacock shining, and be given release. The praise shows the vel that pierced the eight hills and the magic mountain, Murugan who held Valli's feet in the forest and embraced her with the teaching of Om, son of the Shakti on the left of Siva who crushed Death and his buffalo, at the tower of Kadavur.
nuance: சர்ப்ப வாயுவை விடாது அடக்கி: the breath held like a coiled serpent, then the light, the fire and the space above (மேலைவெளி, ஆயிரம்), a compressed yoga ladder. ஓமெனும் உபதேச வித்தொடு அணைவோனே gives the teaching of Om to Valli, not to Siva. காலனிடம் மேவு சத்தி: Uma on the left side, the side with which Siva kicked Death at Kadavur.

title: திருப்படிக்கரை
theme: The single song at Thiruppadikkarai (திருப்படிக்கரை): the poet asks to turn from courtesans who strip a man's wealth to praising the shrine and singing Murugan's Thiruppugazh; the praise is Rama's war and the father who praises Murugan's Tamil.

reading: The poet describes women who come close, smile softly, line their eyes, call, say sweet things, loosen the silk bought by selling a half-panam, embrace, give their lips and melt a man with love until they have taken his wealth without limit, and asks whether, without delusion for them in his heart, he will praise the shrine of Seyppathi and sing Murugan's Thiruppugazh. The praise tells of Rama with the army of monkeys, the dammed sea and the arrow that shattered the demons, as uncle, and names Murugan the one in the three Tamils whom his father praises, at Thiruppadikkarai.
nuance: மட்டறப் பொருட் பறிப்பவர், those who pluck wealth without measure, names the courtesans. உனைத் திருப்புகழ்ப் பகர்வேனோ: the poet names his own work as the alternative to the women, as in 263. செய்ப்பதித் தலம் is probably the shrine itself, or Vayalur, whose name is the same; the reading leaves it open.

title: மாயூரம்
theme: The single song at Mayuram (மாயூரம், the peacock town, Sikandiyur): a confession of infatuation with women whose lips feed lust, and a praise that names Murugan as the one who cleared the poet's mala, bade him sing and praised his verse.

reading: The poet describes women whose lips are nectar, pressed mango, milk and sugar, who serve them like hosts lovingly feeding the hungry in summer heat, with pearl-hung breasts that sway as they fall on a man, and calls himself the sinner ruined in their spell; he asks to hold the sounding feet, praise them and live. The praise tells of Ravana, who took Sita of spotless chastity, and of Rama who destroyed his line with the monkeys as uncle, of Murugan who removed 'our mala' and bade 'sing', then praised the verse sung and gave the high reward, at Sikandiyur south of the Ponni.
nuance: எமது மலத்தைக் களைந்து பாடென அருள அதற்குப் புகழ்ந்து பாடிய இயல்கவி மெச்சிட்டு: an autobiographical line, the poet's call to sing told as Murugan's grace, the removal of mala coming before the command. The women's lips given like food to the hungry (வருபசியர்க்கு ... அருள்பவர் ஒத்து) is an ironic image of hospitality.

title: பாகை
theme: Songs at Pagai (பாகை): the poet asks to be spared Kama's arrows, women, the begging of patrons, the body's diseases and the burning ground, and asks for Sivayoga and the silent bliss; the praise names Murugan as the Tamil hero who straightened the Pandya's hunch, and describes the town's ponds, groves and towers.
structure_note: A plea against desire and patron-seeking (789), against disease and death (790), and against women for the ocean of silent bliss (791).

tamil: ஆடல் மாமத ராஜன் பூசல் வாளியி லேநொந்
ஆர வாணகை யார்செஞ் சேலி னேவலி லேசென்
சேடன் மாமுடி மேவும் பாரு ளோர்களுள் நீடுந்
தேடி நான்மறை நாடுங் காடு மோடிய தாளுந்
பாடு நான்மறை யோனுந் தாதை யாகிய மாலும்
பாக நாண்மலர் சூடுஞ் சேக ராமதில் சூழ்தென்
கூட லான்முது கூனன் றோட வாதுயர் வேதங்
கோடி தானவர் தோளுந் தாளும் வீழவு லாவுங்
reading: The poet asks not to faint, sweating and infatuated, under the arrows of Kama, not to go at the bidding of women's fish-like eyes and wither, and not to wander asking who on this serpent-borne earth gives generously, and asks whether he will reach today the feet that ran into the forest the four Vedas seek. The praise names Brahma, Vishnu and Siva who daily wear flowers, Murugan the ruler of walled southern Pagai, the Tamil hero whose tongue spoke the Veda in debate so that the old hunch of the king of Kudal ran away, riding the peacock.
nuance: த்யாகம் ஈபவர் யாரென்று அலையாதே: the poet's wandering in search of patrons is set beside desire. நான்மறை நாடும் காடும் ஓடிய தாள் are Murugan's feet that ran in the forest after Valli, which the Vedas search for. கூடலான் முதுகூன் அன்று ஓட is the Pandya Koon (the hunchback) straightened by Sambandar, again Murugan.

reading: The poet asks not to waste away with phlegm, fever, chills and wind, not to lose his life in the little nest of the body and go to the burning ground, and not to sink in the fire with brain, bones, nerves and sinews falling apart, and asks Murugan to speak to him so that he may live in the state of Sivayoga called the root. The praise describes Pagai, where fish leap and tear nets in the ponds, ketaki flowers are crushed, areca groves are beaten by the sea and backwaters, and Murugan who loves the peacock.
nuance: மூலம் எனும் சிவயோக பதம்: the alternative to the burning body is a state, Sivayoga, not escape. The diseases (ஈளை, சுரம், குளிர், வாதம்) are named first, then the cremation fire that takes the parts of the body. The praise is all landscape.

reading: The poet confesses that, drawn to women whose spear-like eyes rush at their earrings and to their musk-scented breasts, he grew infatuated day by day and melted in play, and asks whether his life, whirling amid the waves of the sea, will not sink into the ocean of silent supreme bliss. The praise names Murugan the one who came after the elephant-faced Ganapati with cheeks and trunk, bearer of the bright vel, at Pagai whose towers of coral, emerald, gold and diamond are brushed by the horses of the sun's chariot.
nuance: மவுன பரம சுக ... உததி: the ocean of silent supreme joy is set against the sea of waves in which the life whirls, two seas in one plea. The word between (சுகோம கோததி) is hard to divide.

title: திருவிடைக்கழி
theme: Songs at Thiruvidaikkazhi (திருவிடைக்கழி), the shrine of the kura tree: the poet confesses useless learning, the body's hut, courtesans who take money and kick a man out, and the ocean of birth, and asks for the feet as a raft, the company of devotees and the gift of song; one song is a lovesick girl's plea for the kadamba garland, and the praise names Murugan teaching Siva and Brahma's prison.
structure_note: Learning and the body (792, 795, 796); patron-poets and the sea of birth (793); a list of boons (794); courtesans (797, 799); and an akam song (798) that takes its last lines from 797.
source_issues: Song 796: unflagged garbles பிதற் றிடுலொக ...... மு முடர் (line 4, probably பிதற்றிடும் உலக மூடர், 'the babbling fools of the world') and திருப் புழோத (line 8, probably திருப்புகழ் ஓத).
Song 795: the praise lines தடவிகட மத்தகத் தடவரைய ரத்தரத் தடலனுச (lines 13 to 14) are hard to divide and may be garbled.

reading: The poet asks whether, not cherishing the hut of blood with fire and three gunas, and not learning sorrowful, anxious, useless arts without knowing their meaning, he must still be crushed in the corners of the eyes of cruel women who cajole and melt and join in union. The praise names Valli of the millet field, Murugan who told Siva with coral matted hair the one word to make him clear, the bright vel that split the golden-peaked hill, at Idaikkazhi where fish leap in the backwater.
nuance: சவலைக் கலை கற்று அதனிற் பொருள் சற்று அறியாதே: learning without knowing its meaning is joined to the body and to women as one wasted life. சிவனுக்கு ஒருசொல் பகர்வோனே is the guru-myth with Om not named. கடவேனோ, 'must I?', frames the whole first half as a question.

reading: The poet tells of the vanity of those who say 'I give generously to those who beg, even in dreams; which poet matches me in verse and music?', tie on turbans and rings and keep betel bags in lordly style, and of women who hide in their clothes faces, hair and brows likened to moon and cloud; to cross the ocean of birth that is mired in this hoof-print puddle, he asks for the raft of the golden feet. The praise shows the battle, the hills and seas dried, the gods returned to their city and Brahma imprisoned, Murugan at Idaikkazhi, and Valli in the millet field of pearls from tusks and bamboo, whom he took by the hand to the hunters' shame.
nuance: குளப்படியிற் சளப்படும் இப்பவக் கடல்: the ocean of birth is mocked as a hoof-print puddle, and yet the feet are needed as a raft (கழற் புணை) to cross it. The boasting in the first lines may be the poet's own or that of patrons; the reading leaves it open.

reading: The poet asks for a list of gifts: the meaning of the three Tamils, the fruit of true austerity, many kinds of life, the ancient state of release, the life of the wish-tree, a faultless mind, kingship and a wondrous great life, and with the senses gone, the strength of praise. The praise names Murugan of the Saravana pool, who embraced the hunter girl in the lone forest and split the peaked hill, at Idaikkazhi of the kura groves.
nuance: The plea is all asking, with no confession; worldly gifts (அரசு, கற்பகத்தரு வாழ்வு) sit beside release (முத்தியிற் பதம்) and end in புகழ் பலம், the power of praise, the poet's own gift. புலன் அகற்றிட: the senses removed.

tamil: உ டலது பொ றுத்தறக் கடைபெறுபி றப்பினுக்
reading: The poet describes the body of earth, water, fire, wind and space, the false embryo, the states, the three gunas, diseases, marrow, semen, blood, bone and fat, a hungry hut, and confesses that, bearing it in a birth low in virtue without an aware mind, he wanders; he asks for the pair of feet and a place among Murugan's own people. The praise names the cock banner, Valli's arms, Murugan the son of the true father, poet of the three Tamils, at Idaikkazhi which grants release.
nuance: The catalogue mixes the elements, the states of consciousness (அவத்தை) and the three gunas with the body's fluids, a doctrinal and a physical body in one list. உனது தமர் ஒக்க வைத்து: be set among your people. The praise lines on the battle and the elephant (தடவிகட மத்தகத் தடவரை) are hard to divide.

reading: The poet confesses that, carrying the blamed hut of the body, he fell into the pit of illusion women offer and gropes for the way out, that the world's fools babble of old things, and that he sought many useless arts without grasping the one meaning; before he dies he asks to seek the lotus feet, melt with nectar welling in his heart and sing Murugan's holy praise. The praise is a battle in drum syllables, the sea churning, Meru shaking and the gods crying victory, the kadamba-wearing Saravana on the peacock, lord of Arunai, Tiruttani, Nagamalai, Palani, Kodai and Idaikkazhi.
nuance: ஒருபயனைத் தெளியாது: learning without the one aim is the fault, as in 792. உனது திருப்புகழ் ஓத (written திருப்புழோத) asks for the poet's book by name. The list of shrines at the close makes Idaikkazhi one of Murugan's many seats.

reading: The poet describes women who laugh and say 'come' when a wealthy man arrives, take his finger to the bed, play thigh to thigh, babble and talk sweetly until the agreed money reaches their place, and lull him to sleep on their breasts; when his wealth ends they twist round, kick and abuse him, and he asks that the work of these traitors end and he be driven to worship the two flower feet. The praise shows the vel that killed the asuras from the peacock's back, Murugan the son of Siva, who plucked Brahma's head with a nail, smiled at the triple city and gives grace in his devotees' thought, embracing the hunter girl on a fragrant bed, under the kura tree praised by sages, Indra and Brahma.
nuance: பொருள் தீரின் முறுக்கியே உதை கொடு வசை உரைதரு: the expulsion when the money runs out is shown as a physical kick, the courtesan story told at its harshest. திருக்குராவடி நிழல், the shade of the holy kura tree, is the sthala tree of Idaikkazhi, named again in 798.

reading: In another's voice, the singer asks that the fragrant flower bed not burn the girl, that the mother who raised her and her kin not speak blame, and that the neighbours not slander her, and asks Murugan to send his kadamba garland now. The praise names the husband of the creeper-waisted girl, the hero on the emerald peacock, who dwells in the shade of the holy kura tree, with the beautiful vel in hand.
nuance: The three dangers are the bed (கொதியாதே), the family's blame (வசை) and the neighbours' gossip (அயலவர் பழி), so the garland is asked to stop talk as well as longing. The eight lines take their praise words from 797 (மருக்குலாவிய மலரணை, திருக்குராவடி நிழல், திருக்கை வேல் வடிவழகிய).

tamil: முலைகு லுக்கிகள் கபடிகள் வடிபு ழுக்கைக ளசடிகள்
மொழிப சப்பிகள் விகடிகள் அழும னத்திகள் தகுநகை
கலவி யிற்றரும் வசவிகள் விழிம யக்கினில் வசமழி
அலைநெ ருப்பெழ வடவரை பொடிப டச்சம ணர்கள்குலம்
அரன ரிப்பிர மர்கள்முதல் வழிப டப்பிரி யமும்வர
சிலைமொ ளுக்கென முறிபட மிதிலை யிற்சந கமனருள்
திரள்வ ருக்கைகள் கமுகுகள் சொரிம துக்கத லிகள்வளர்
reading: The poet heaps names on the women: breast-shakers, deceivers, dull ones, thieves, coaxers, mockers, fakers who weep, women who loosen their clothes and take young men's wealth, give half a betel roll in union and then abuse; he asks for grace so that the worry of losing himself in their bewitching eyes may end. The praise shows the hill turned to dust and the Jains impaled by the peacock hero, Murugan who told Siva, Vishnu and Brahma each a meaning, nephew of Rama who broke the bow at Mithila and won Sita, at Idaikkazhi of jackfruit, areca and plantain.
nuance: இளைஞர்கள் பொருள் பறித்த and ஒருபாதி வெற்றிலைச் சுருள் (half a betel roll) mark these as courtesans who take much and give little. அவரவர்க்கு ஒரு பொருள் புகல் பெரியோனே widens the guru-myth to all three gods. சமணர்கள் குலம் அணி கழுப்பெற gives the impaling of the Jains to the peacock hero.

title: தான் தோன்றி
theme: A single song at Thanthondri (தான் தோன்றி): the poet asks to understand that this body, a hut propped up by deeds, rots and ends as fine ash, and to be ruled so that, past burning and past deeds, he worships the feet; the praise plays on the shrine's name, the Lord who stands self-arisen.

reading: The poet speaks of this hut of a body, a pillar rooted in sorrowful deeds, which tires, wears out, decays and becomes fine ash in the fire, and of not grasping that flaw; like those who dig through learning seeking great wealth and come with outstretched hands, he has gone astray, and asks to be taken as a servant so that, with burning and deeds gone, he worships the good feet in the way that bears fruit. The praise shows ascetics and gods tending his feet, Murugan on the sky-high peacock with arms embraced by his golden-bangled consorts, the vel that fought the Suras of the sunken hill, and the son of the Father of Thanthondri, able to stand self-arisen (தான்தோன்றி).
nuance: The song is built of long-vowel clusters ending in -ந்த, -ன்ற (சூழ்ந்தேன்ற, வீழ்ந்தீண்டி, வாழ்ந்தான்ற), so word division is often a guess. The last line puns on the shrine: தான்தோன்றி is both the place and the Lord who appears of himself. வேம் பாங்கும் அற்று வினையாம் பாங்கும் அற்று may mean freedom from burning (birth and death) and from deeds; the simile of the learned beggars is unclear.

title: கந்தன்குடி
theme: A single song at Kandankudi (கந்தன்குடி): the poet asks Murugan to come one day on the peacock like a light filling the worlds and give his feet, so that the bonds of his trembling body and the births of a deceitful heart end; the praise shows the child playing as Siva worships and Murugan coming to save a devotee who calls him guru.

reading: The poet asks that one day Murugan come on the peacock, blazing like a light that fills the heavens, the cosmos, the earth and every direction, and give his red-gold feet that bring joy, so that the ties of his trembling, defective body and his sorrow end; he asks whether the births of this lonely rogue, whose heart houses deceit and always gathers faults, will not cease. The praise shows the little bells of the child's necklace sounding as he plays daily while Siva, the Sambhu, worships, and Murugan coming that day with love so that the devotee who praises him as 'Kandan, Guha, my guru' might see and be saved, at Kandankudi of pools sweet with spilled fruit.
nuance: The song chimes on nasal clusters (எந்தன், பங்கம், தொந்தங்களை, வஞ்சம்), and the shrine's name is echoed in the devotee's own formula கந்தன் குகன் என்றன் குரு. நெஞ்சன் துகள் என்றும் கொளும் வண்டன் தமியன்: the self-abuse is of a heart that keeps choosing fault. The devotee saved by Murugan's coming is not named.

title: திலதைப்பதி
theme: Three songs at Thilathaippathi (திலதைப்பதி): a short plea not to be tossed by impurity and maya, a confession of wandering in waves of pleasure addressed to the Lord who knows it, and a plea to stop singing the praise of men and sing his; the praise includes the rescue of the elephant Gajendra.
structure_note: 802 is a four-line song on malam and maya; 803 confesses lovemaking without an explicit plea; 804 sets Kama's arrows against the poet's praise and turns from praise of the world.

reading: In a short song the poet asks whether he must be tossed about by impurity and maya, too great to tell, through a life that is a mere moment and even that a time of eating from a leaf. The praise names the vel that ended the imprisonment of the gods kept in the great jail, at Thilathaippathi.
nuance: இறை அத்தனையோ ... இலையிட்டு உணல் ஏய்தரு காலம்: the life span may be called 'only a moment' and taken up with eating; the opening lines are compressed and the sense is a guess. அறையில் பெரிதாம் மலமாயை names impurity and maya together, a Siddhanta pairing.

tamil: பனகப் படமி சைந்த முழையிற் றரள நின்று
பரிவற் றெரியு நெஞ்சில் முகிலிற் களிய கொண்டை
அனமொத் திடுசி றந்த நடையிற் கிளியி னின்சொல்
மளவிப் புளக கொங்கை குழையத் தழுவி யின்ப
தனனத் தனன தந்த தனனத் தனன தந்த
தகிடத் தகிட தந்த திமிதத் திமித வென்று
செநெனற் கழனி பொங்கி திமிலக் கமல மண்டி
திருநற் சிகரி துங்க வரையைப் பெருவு கின்ற
reading: The poet describes the women whose breasts, like a serpent's hood, bear pearl strings and gold, with cloud-dark hair full of flowers, swan's gait and a parrot's sweet speech, and says that, his heart burning without pity, his mind deluded, he embraces them and wanders in the waves of pleasure; he says this to the Lord 'who knows it always' and makes no further plea. The praise has Murugan come to the sound of the drum, given in the metre's own syllables (தனனத் தனன தந்த, தகிடத் தகிட), at Thilathaippathi of red paddy, lotus, sugarcane and a tall peak.
nuance: The plea is replaced by a statement: திரிவன் என்று அறிவோனே, 'you who know that I wander so'. Lines 9 and 10 set out the song's metrical pattern (தனனத் தனன தந்த ... தனதானா) as the drum's sound, and the next line continues it as the beat of the drum.

tamil: மகரக் குழைக்கு ளுந்து நயனக் கடைக்கி லங்கு
வடவெற் பதைத்து ரந்து களபக் குடத்தை வென்று
உ கமெய்ப் பதைத்து நெஞ்சும் விரகக் கடற்பொ திந்த
உ லகப் புகழ்ப்பு லம்பு கலியற் றுணர்ச்சி கொண்டு
புகர்கைக் கரிப்பொ திந்த முளரிக் குளத்தி ழிந்த
பொருமித் திகைத்து நின்று வரதற் கடைக்க லங்கள்
திகிரிப் படைத்து ரந்த வரதற் குடற்பி றந்த
சிவபத் தர்முத்த ரும்பர் தவசித் தர்சித்த மொன்று
reading: The poet asks whether, freed from the eyes that dart toward the makara earrings with enchanting arrows, from breasts that outdo Meru and the sandal pot, and from Kama's flower arrows that torment a trembling body and a heart in the furnace of longing, and rid of the babble of praising the world, he will wander speaking the praise that is rightfully Murugan's. The praise tells how the elephant entered the lotus pool, was seized by the crocodile and stood struggling and bewildered, and how Vishnu, the boon-giver, came at once as its refuge and threw the discus; Murugan is the son of Siva's consort, born of the same body as that Vishnu, at Thilathaippathi where Siva's devotees, the freed, gods, ascetics and siddhas gather with one mind.
nuance: உலகப் புகழ் புலம்பு கலி அற்று ... உன் உரிமைப் புகழ் பகர்ந்து: the poet sets the praise of worldly men against the praise that belongs to Murugan, a turn his songs at the court shrines make often. The praise tells the story of Gajendra in its unmistakable details (the pool, the crocodile, the discus). Uma is called Vishnu's sister (வரதற்கு உடற்பிறந்த சிவை).

title: திருவம்பர்
theme: A single song at Thiruvambar (திருவம்பர்) in the Chola land: the poet, who did not seek the light, mantra and inner space, but gambled, raced horses and danced for pleasure until the senses failed, asks when the trouble of the burning ground will end; the praise sets the peacock leaping across the cosmic circles.

reading: The poet says that, without taking hold of the light, the mantra, the teaching and the open space where the golden flower blooms, he talked of gambling and wagers, of five breeds of horses leaping in the street circuits, dressed up and danced for pleasure until his eyes grew dim and his five senses shrank, and that when the term written on the leaf by Brahma is reached, men run to the burning ground, fall and are burnt; he asks when this trouble will end. The praise has the peacock leap over the circles of sun, moon and sea and search the cosmos, the dust of the deceivers' realm fly to the sky while Murugan smiles, and Murugan infatuated with the forest girl, lord of Ambar in the Chola land where Indra and the gods worship.
nuance: சோதி மந்திரம் போதகம் ... வெளி தோடு அலர்ந்த பொன் பூ இருந்த இடம்: the first lines seem to name the yogic goals, the inner light, the mantra, the open space and the golden lotus, which the poet failed to reach. The second half is built on மண்டலம் (circles of sun and moon, of the sea, of the cosmos), perhaps also the yogic circles. The lines on gambling and horses (அஞ்சுவகை சாதி, சிந்துபரி) are hard to divide.

title: திருமாகாளம்
theme: A single song at Thirumakalam (திருமாகாளம்): after a detailed scene of lovemaking, the poet asks that, without 'who am I, who are you', he hold to the feet that took his life and chant Murugan's names daily; the praise names Murugan as the guru who gave joy and understanding to Siva.

reading: The poet describes lovemaking on the bed: earrings swinging, eyes wheeling like swords, ornaments slipping, hair and flowers loosened, legs entwined, anklets and garments, the nectar of the lips and a cuckoo's voice in the throat, and calls himself infatuated with such women; he asks for grace so that, without asking 'who am I, who are you', he may think anxiously on the feet that seized his life and chant daily 'Lord, Kumara, Muruga'. The praise names the vel that sent Sesha's thousand hoods, Meru, the seven seas and the Suras' bodies to dust so the earth could live, Vishnu on the serpent in the milk sea who routed Ravana's host and was friend of the five Pandavas as uncle, and Murugan the guru who gave the joy of understanding to Siva the dancer on the bull with Uma at his side, at Thirumakalam where Vishnu and devotees worship.
nuance: நான் ஆரு நீ எவன் எனாமல்: perhaps a plea to hold the feet without the questioning that keeps self and Lord apart, or simply without hesitation; the phrase is open. எனது ஆவி கவர் சீர்பாதம்: the feet are said to have already taken the poet's life, so the turn is to what has claimed him. Siva is called மாடேறி ஆடும் ஒரு நாதன், and Murugan the guru who gave him போதம்.

title: இஞ்சிகுடி
theme: A single song at Inchikudi (இஞ்சிகுடி): the courtesans who take a day's worth of coins and goods with false love, and the plea to sing Murugan and reach release instead; the praise is of Rama's march to Lanka with Hanuman, Sugriva and the monkey host.
source_issues: Song 807: two corrupt characters in தசக் ¡£வ (line 13) and சுக் ¡£வ (line 15), clearly ரீ: தசக்ரீவன் (Ravana) and சுக்ரீவன்.

reading: The poet describes the women with breasts perfumed with kumkum, camphor, musk and sandal under a breast-cloth, combed hair, poison-like eyes that fight the ears, who with cruel deceitful eyes and deceitful hearts speak desire, play the lover with everyone, and take the coins and goods the day is worth; he asks whether, instead of falling into the net of their false love, one day he will sing Murugan and enter release. The praise tells of Hanuman, son of the wind, who went to the ten-necked Ravana with a message, Sugriva and the seventy vellam of monkeys, the sea dammed with hills and the night-roamers' clan scattered by Rama, Murugan's uncle; it names Murugan the six-faced Guha and 'my Swaminatha', the vel of Vayalur, and the lord at Inchikudi blessed by Siva Parvatheesar.
nuance: அன்றளவுக்கான காசு பொருள் கவர்: the courtesans take exactly what the day yields, the money-measured love of 33. அன்புடை மெய்க் கோலராக: they put on a 'loving true form' for everyone. The Rama story is told with Hanuman and Sugriva named. Murugan is also called the vel of Vayalur, a shrine dear to the poet.

title: திருநள்ளாறு
theme: A single song at Thirunallaru (திருநள்ளாறு) that turns the catalogue of a woman's body to the Goddess: the poet asks whether he will melt calling Murugan the son of Parvati, who with two measures of paddy gives charity to every house in the world; the praise names the six faces, the vel against Sura's kin and Vishnu as uncle.

reading: The poet lists the beauties of Parvati, breasts like green mountains, fish-like eyes, pearl teeth, coral lips, a bow-like brow, a banyan-leaf belly and a waist thin as a thread, calls her Abhirami, Mohini and the parrot, the beauty of inner experience, and the one who, settling every clan, hut and world in her house, shares out charity at all times with two measures of paddy; he asks whether he will melt calling Murugan 'Kumara' as her son. The praise names his belt and sword, twelve arms, twelve eyes and six faces, the vel that cut out the root of Sura's kin so the kalpaka heaven could live while siddhas and vidyadharas cried 'well done', Vishnu on the white serpent with Garuda, bow, conch and discus as uncle, and Murugan coming with Valli of the millet field and the elephant's daughter to Nallaru.
nuance: The opening uses the form the poet usually gives to courtesans, the catalogue of breasts, eyes, lips and waist, but the woman is the Goddess, and it ends in devotion, not confession. இரு நாழி நெல்லால் அறம் எப்பொதும் பகிர்வாள: the Goddess who keeps the charities with two measures of paddy, as at Kanchi. அநுபூதியின் அழகாள் may mean 'she whose beauty is inner experience'.

title: வழுவூர்
theme: Two songs at Vazhuvur (வழுவூர்): a plea to be kept from women and Death and given true knowledge and the shade of the feet, and a song of thanksgiving recalling, stage by stage, the poet's initiation: teaching, Tamil, light, nada and the peacock's coming.
structure_note: 809 is a plea in the usual two halves; 810 replaces the plea with remembrance (மறவேனே), listing what the Lord has already done.

reading: The poet asks not to sink in the sea of unending infatuation with cuckoo-voiced deceitful women, nor to have Death, fiery-eyed, with noose and trident, cloud-black on his buffalo, come near; and that, with the sins of this impure body since the womb, its sorrow, desire and deceit, and his poverty ended, true knowledge, ripened awareness and love of Siva come, and the shade of the anklet-bearing feet be given. The praise shows Murugan on the new peacock with Indra's daughter on one side and the hunters' deer on the other, the twelve-armed hero with civet and rosewater garlands and the sacred thread, son of Siva the Mahadeva and Sadasiva, at the old town of Vazhuvur of cool tanks, groves and paddy, known for its great penance.
nuance: The plea moves from two dangers to avoid (women, Death) to a list of gifts: போதம், மெய்ஞானம், சிவநேசம். கருவூறிய நாளும் ... மல தேகம்: the body is impure from conception. மிடி (poverty) is named among the ills to end, beside sin and desire.

reading: The poet recalls what the Lord did: on the first day made him praise the feet with love, fed him the meaning of the teaching, bathed him in the sea of mantra, penance and knowledge, joined him to his company, fed him the three Tamils the gods do not know, showed the Veda's path, showed the light of the kala circling the mandala, raised him to the nada beyond the light, set him at the doorstep of the fragrant whorl, leapt over fate, brought him to Kamalalaya and the open space, and then came lovingly mounted on the radiant peacock; he will not forget it. The praise names the vel that felled the hill and the demons' heads, Murugan who fed Siva, Sivakami's rogue lover with serpent garlands, the meaning of Siva-knowledge, Valli's husband, and the lord of Vazhuvur where the gods praise his dance.
nuance: A rare autobiographical song: the plea is replaced by remembrance (செயல் மறவேனே), and the stages read as an inner ascent: teaching (உபதேசப் பொருள்), Tamil (முத்தமிழ்), the light of kala (கலை சோதிக் கதிர்), nada (நாதப் பரம்), the whorl (சுழி), the space (வெளி). கமலாலைப் பதி may be Tiruvarur, whose tank is Kamalalayam, or the lotus within; I cannot settle it. சிவகாமிக்கு ஒரு தூர்த்தர் is a playful epithet of Siva.

title: கன்னபுரம்
theme: A single song at Kannapuram (கன்னபுரம்) on the Kaveri, against the sects: the poet asks to be rid of the pettiness of 'this is mine', of learning the books of yoga and other paths, and to be given a life that cannot be called 'this'; the praise shows Murugan waiting outside Valli's cave at night like a thief.

reading: The poet speaks of thinking that this flesh body made of food, under the reckoning of Brahma born on the lotus, will not die, of entering others' paths and learning the many books of the delusion called yoga, and of the pettiness of sect that says 'this is for me'; he asks whether Murugan will not destroy that pettiness, free him from trouble and give a life that cannot be named 'this'. The praise shows Murugan, for the girl with cane-sweet speech, braided hair and swan's gait, standing sweating late at night at the mouth of a cave in the hill like a burglar, unable to enter; it names the Lord of Kannapuram on the Ponni with the serpent bracelet and Murugan lord of the kings of the golden world.
nuance: The song alliterates on அன்ன/இன்ன/கன்ன throughout, so word division is uncertain. இன்னது எனக்கு என்னும் மதப் புன்மை: the fault named is sectarian pride; முச்சடங்க யோகம் may refer to a threefold practice. இன்னது எனப்படா வாழ்க்கை: the life asked for cannot be named or defined. கன்னமிட in the praise compares Murugan at Valli's cave to a housebreaker, a striking image.

title: திருவாஞ்சியம்
theme: A single song at Thiruvanchiyam (திருவாஞ்சியம்) on kings: lords of elephant armies and conquered directions, perfumed and jewelled, end as a handful of ash when the life slips away, yet they do not think to worship Murugan's feet; the praise names Vishnu of Venkatam and Murugan as Kama's kin.

reading: The poet describes kings: lords of elephants and the wheel of rule, commanding armies, honoured, conquering the directions, swelling with pride on round cushions, with victory garlands, silks, perfumes and jewels, whose body, when the life slips away among the kin, is lit with fire and becomes a handful of ash; they do not know it, and with longing do not think to worship Murugan's feet. The praise names Vishnu, boon-giver to the Pandavas of the Kuru line, Hrishikesa, Uma's brother, dweller on northern Venkatam with bow and discus, as uncle, and Murugan as son of the destroyer of the triple city and kin of Kama, Subrahmanya of the six faces, at Thiruvanchiyam where the king grants release.
nuance: The confession is not the poet's own but a portrait of rulers, an argument from impermanence: ஒரு பிடி சாம்பல் பட்டது அறிகிலர். உன் அவாஞ்சை மிக்கு அடிதொழ நினையாரே may pun on the shrine's name (வாஞ்சியம், வாஞ்சை 'longing'). Murugan is called மைத்துனன் of Kama, both being in the poet's scheme Vishnu's kin.

title: திருச்செங்காட்டங்குடி
theme: A single song at Thiruchengattangudi (திருச்செங்காட்டங்குடி): against courtesans who are gamblers, killers of families and lovers of money, the poet asks for the teaching in his ear, with the nada sounding, the darkness of maya burnt and the root fire rising; the praise is a chain of 'namo nama' and names the shrine where Siva drank the curry of love.

reading: The poet describes women with jewelled chests, garlanded hair, earrings bright as rays, bow-like brows and spear-like eyes, who speak like parrots and invite all comers with 'come, be close', and calls them cheats, gamblers, killers, ruiners of families, lovers of money, outcasts and wretches; he asks that, rather than wander in their net of maya, the dense darkness of maya burn away with the conch-like nada sounding and the root fire rising, and that the teaching be spoken into his cool ear so he reaches the two flower feet. The praise is a chain of 'namo nama' to the peacock rider, Kumara, the teacher of Siva, Parvati's son and the bright vel, names the vel that turned Sura, the sea and the hill to dust, Brahma struck down, Murugan gone to the forest for love of Valli, and Chengadu, where the eight-armed Siva with love drank the curry of love.
nuance: சங்கோதை நாதமொடு கூடி ... மூல அழல் வீச உபதேசமது தண் காதில் ஓதி: the remedy is yogic and given by a guru, the inner sound (nada) and the root fire (மூலாதார) rising, with the teaching whispered in the ear. எண்டோளர் காதல் கொடு காதல் கறியே பருகு செங்காடு names the shrine's story, Siva eating the curry offered by Siruthondar; the text names only the curry and the place. The courtesans' abuse list (சூது, கொலைகாரர், குடிகேடர், பண ஆசையுளர்) is harsher than usual.

title: திருவிற்குடி
theme: A single song at Thiruvirkudi (திருவிற்குடி): women who measure every mind and stand in the golden street like a rutting elephant, and the poet who fears fading in their net like an elephant in a pit; the praise is a battle in drum syllables and Brahma imprisoned.

reading: The poet describes women with breasts lovelier than in a painting, waists thin as a hair, who measure every mind as one would count the sea's sand, with musky hair, fish-like eyes and bright laughter, speaking spells of infatuation and standing in the golden street like a green-gem peacock or a rutting elephant, and asks whether, caught in their net, he will fade like an elephant that has fallen into a pit. The praise is a battle in drum syllables, conch and drums sounding, the sea, the mountains of the directions and the serpent's hoods shaken as the wicked Suras die; Murugan gave Indra back his place and married the parrot-like Devayanai, and seized Brahma, beat his head and imprisoned him to his shame; he is lord at Virkudi praised by the freed.
nuance: சித்தம் அத்தனையும் முற்று அளப்ப கடல் மொய்த்த சிற்றுமணலுக்கும் எட்டியது: the women can measure a whole mind as if counting the sea's grains, so their skill is knowledge of men. The poet becomes the elephant trapped in a pit (குழி உற்ற அத்தி), after the women were compared to a rutting elephant (அத்தி ஒத்த மதம்). Brahma's imprisonment is given without its usual cause.

title: விஜயபுரம்
theme: A single song at Vijayapuram (விஜயபுரம்) on the body: a hut of gut, fat and bone with nine gates of filth, quicker to vanish than a water bubble, which the poet desired and tried to keep with medicines and yogas; he asks to reach the anklet-bearing feet; the praise names Siva burning the triple city and Murugan born of his eye.

tamil: குடல்நிண மென்புபு லால்கமழ் குருதிந ரம்பிவை தோலிடை
குதிகொளு மொன்பது வாசலை யுடையகு ரம்பையை நீரெழு
அடலையு டம்பைய வாவியெ அநவர தஞ்சில சாரமி
றலமரு சிந்தையி னாகுல மலமல மென்றினி யானுநி
இடமற மண்டு நிசாசர ரடைய மடிந்தெழு பூதர
இமையவ ருஞ்சிறை போயவர் பதியு ளிலங்க விடாதர
விடதர கஞ்சுகி மேருவில் வளைவதன் முன்புர நீறெழ
விழியினில் வந்து பகீரதி மிசைவள ருஞ்சிறு வாவட
reading: The poet describes the body as gut, fat, bone, flesh, blood and nerves, wrapped in skin so the filth sloshes within, a hut with nine gates of impurity, perishing faster than a bubble on water; desiring this ashen body, he kept trying worthless medicines and many yogas until his anguished mind cried 'enough, enough', and he asks whether he will now reach the beautiful flower feet with anklets. The praise names the night-roamers dead, the mountain crushed, the great sea dried and the gods freed from prison, Siva who bent Meru with the thousand-hooded serpent and burned the triple city with a smile and glared at Kama, and Murugan who came from his eye and grew on the Ganga, at Vijayapuram.
nuance: குடல் நிணம் என்பு புலால் ... ஒன்பது வாசலை உடைய குரம்பை: the body is the familiar hut with nine openings. The plea rejects the means of preserving it: சாரமில் அவுடதமும் பல யோகமும் முயலா நின்று அலமரு சிந்தையின் ஆகுலம் அலமலம், medicines and yogas tried on the body are a source of anguish, not rescue.

title: திருவாரூர்
theme: Seven songs at Tiruvarur (திருவாரூர்): three in long syllables with a shared refrain (one on a wasted life, one in a lovesick girl's voice, one on a lullaby's endearments), a short plea for the feet of knowledge, two courtesan songs, one of which tells the story of Manu's justice, and a song that turns the questions of desire into questions about the inner light.
structure_note: 816 to 818 share the closing line சேயே வேளே பூவே கோவே தேவே தேவப் பெருமாளே and are made of long syllables; 819 is four lines; 820 and 821 confess infatuation; 822 recasts the lover's questions as questions about the light within.
source_issues: Song 816: corrupt characters in வானோ ¡£சா (line 9) and தீனா ¡£சா (line 13), probably ரீசா or ஈசா ('lord').
Song 817: corrupt characters in றா¡¢ற் (line 8), probably றாரிற்.
Song 818: corrupt characters in பே¡£யா (line 7); the word is unclear.
Song 819: corrupt character in ந¨டுழிக் (line 1), probably நீடூழி ('for long ages'); also the unflagged garble எருரிற் (line 4), probably ஆரூரிற்.
Songs 820 to 822: unflagged garble ர்ருர் for ஆரூர் in மர்ருர (820, line 16), அருளர்ருர் (821, line 21) and சீ ரர்ருர் (822, line 24).
Song 821: corrupt characters in மடலு¡டே (line 9), clearly மடலூடே, and யெழு¦பொருள் (line 13), unclear.

reading: The poet asks whether it is right that his days go in vain, a dog's life, without his singing the vel, putting the koothalam garland Murugan loves on his shoulders, speaking his name and falling at the feet beyond the Veda, the mind turning nowhere else. The praise calls Murugan friend, lord of the gods, the kadamba-wearer who went to the millet field for the deer-like Valli, lord of the land of kalpaka trees, lord of the lowly, the great life of glorious Arur, child, Vel, flower, king and god of gods.
nuance: The song is made almost entirely of long syllables in two-syllable words ending in -ஆதே (கூசாதே, பாடாதே, பேசாதே, வீழாதே), a list of what the poet has failed to do. The first line (கூசாதே பார் ஏசாதே மால் கூறா நூல் கற்று) is hard to divide; it may describe learning, unashamed, books that tell no delusion.

reading: In the voice of a girl in love, the singer calls to the sharp-beaked crane: the one who left has not come back, her life has withered to a husk, her mother has turned against her, the town's slander is heard, and the young north wind cuts like a saw and burns like fire; she asks whether she must be ruined like those who sing the names of misers and never prosper. The praise names the unbeaten vel that let no Sura live and gave grace to the gods, the light of Arur with Uma in his half, and Murugan as son of Siva who burned the enemies' towns.
nuance: This is akam poetry: the crane as messenger (கூர்வாய் நாராய்), the mother's anger and the north wind (இளவாடை) are classical, and the poet's own confession is absent. ஈயா வாழ்வோர் பேரே பாடா ஈடேறாரின் கெடலாமோ: the girl compares her fate to poets who sing for misers, the poet's own recurring complaint (827, 828). Word division in the long syllables is uncertain.

reading: The first half strings the endearments of a lullaby, 'are you milk, honey, syrup, the nectar of the gods' sea, the glory of the world, the sun, the pearl of the sky', and asks whether it is fit to be reproached without having sung that lullaby, talo talelo, with a mother's love. The praise shows Murugan, hearing Valli's bird-scaring cry, going in love to the millet field and falling at her feet, and names him the great life of Arur with its fish-filled tanks.
nuance: பாலோ தேனோ பாகோ ... தாலோ தாலேலோ: the opening is a lullaby's string of questions, the form of pillaitamil, and 822 opens with the same words for a woman's speech. Who is reproached and what is asked in lines 5 to 8 is unclear; the line with பே¡£யாதே is damaged. ஆயாள் தாள்மேல் வீழா: Murugan falling at Valli's feet is a recurring image of his humility in love.

reading: In four lines the poet asks Murugan to be gracious for long ages in every way and to give him, as a great gift and treasure, the feet of great knowledge. The praise names him Brahma's kin, the hero of true virtue, the light in the adharas, lord at Arur.
nuance: மாஞானக் கழல்: the feet are named as knowledge itself. ஆதாரத்து ஒளியானே: the Lord as the light in the yogic centres. வேதா மைத்துன: Brahma, as Vishnu's son, is Murugan's cousin in the poet's scheme.

reading: The poet describes women whose long eyes, like arrows, are nets that end men's lifetimes, and whose speech, musk and sandal on their breasts draw his mind, and asks whether that mind will not think of Murugan's anklet-bearing lotus feet. The praise names the Nirutas' host dead and the hills crushed, Rama who made the lord of rivers cry out with a single arrow as Narayana, Murugan's uncle, and Arur, where in every grove of the Siva shrine the bees hum in order.
nuance: மனிதர் வாணாள் அடங்க வருவார்: the women are said to come to end men's lives, the courtesan as a form of Death. நதிபதி கதற ஒரு கணை: Rama threatening the ocean with one arrow before the bridge.

reading: The poet, who wanders infatuated with women whose hands are lotuses, faces moons and breasts hills, asks whether a day will come when, with night and day, enmity, impurity and infatuation gone, tears flowing and heart melted, he gains the sweetness of the word 'the young one who sank into the breasts of the hunter girl, too beautiful to draw on the madal' and reaches the two feet. The praise tells how a cow, whose calf had been killed, rang the bell of Manu's justice; the king heard of the wrong, melted crying 'Hara Siva', and ordered the chariot driven over his own guilty son, splitting his body, while the cow wept; Murugan is the six-faced son of Siva, Ganapati's younger brother, lord at that Arur of grace, whose vel made the sea cry out.
nuance: குறமகள் ... மடலூடே எழுத அரியவள்: Valli is the girl too lovely to draw on the madal, the banner of the lover's palmyra horse, so the love theme is carried into the praise. The praise tells, unusually at length, the Tiruvarur story of the Chola king of Manu's justice, who executed his own son for a calf; the king is not named beyond மனுவின் நெறி.

reading: The poet, delighting in a woman and asking whether her speech is milk, honey, jackfruit, the gods' nectar, cane syrup or the milk of knowledge given to the child who melted, whether her eyes are vel or arrow and her face sun or moon, asks for grace to melt instead asking: what is the light of the six faces, is the light growing within me I or you, is the place that shines like crystal a land or release, tell me the middle word, Lord of the golden hall. The praise has the gods rain flowers, sages hail 'Hara Siva', the demons and the roaring sea cry out and the hill split, and names Murugan the son born to the maiden who is Uma, Lakshmi and Saraswati, at Arur, where the pure say 'this is the bliss of Siva's state, let us stay here'.
nuance: The song uses one form for two loves: the lover's questions (மொழி பாலோ தேனோ, விழி வேலோ கோலோ) are matched by the seeker's (நானோ நீயோ, நாடோ வீடோ). ஊனோடு உருகிய மகன் உண அருள் ஞானப் பால் refers to the milk of knowledge given to the child Sambandar. எனது அகம் வளர் ஒளி நானோ நீயோ: whether the inner light is self or Lord is put as a question, not answered.

title: பெரியமடம்
theme: A single song at Periyamadam (பெரியமடம்), a monastery: the poet confesses learning the arts of love from courtesans and wasting the body and its days, and asks for initiation to stand on the path; the praise is a litany of 'potri' that names Murugan the lord of the tower at Arunai and 'the father called Arunagirinathar'.
source_issues: Song 823: corrupt characters in தீ¨க்ஷ (line 12), clearly தீக்ஷை ('initiation'), and தக்ஷ¢ணா (line 22), clearly தக்ஷிணா (Dakshinamurthy).

reading: The poet confesses that in the hands of quarrel-eyed women he learned the false, thieving books of love, bathed and perfumed himself with civet, musk and tulasi for desire of their breasts, made a bed known to the whole land, waited at the window, thought all wealth and rule had come true, ran melting and stammered in embrace, and so wasted this illusory body and precious days; he asks that Murugan give initiation to one without sense, so he may stand on the path. The praise is a chain of 'hail': to the master exalted by boundless Tamil, to the one fond of the tower of Arunai, to the rider of the peacock, the six-faced lord called the father, the dancer who runs through all shrines, the father called Arunagirinathar, the vel against the Asuras, the guru of Siva who holds the skull, Valli's embrace, and the lord of the joy of Periyamadam, gained by the penance of a Dakshinamurthy unknown to Brahma, a lion to other sects.
nuance: நெறி நிற்க நீ தீக்ஷை தரவேணும்: the plea is for formal initiation (தீக்ஷை), fitting a monastery shrine. அருணை நகர் கோபுர விருப்பனே and அருணகிரி நாத எனும் அப்பனே: Murugan is called by the name of the Lord of Arunai, which is also the poet's own name, and placed at Tiruvannamalai's tower. Whether the Dakshinamurthy of the last lines is Siva as the silent teacher or the ascetic who founded the madam, a 'lion to other sects' (பரசமய கோளரி), the text does not settle.

title: சோமநாதன்மடம்
theme: A single song at Somanathan Madam (சோமநாதன்மடம்): the poet asks for the sword of teaching in the silent word, which strikes down Yama's servants, so that body, life and wandering heart melt; the praise honours Somanathan, the ascetic who worships the Lord of Arunai and founded the monastery, and Murugan who never grows angry with his devotees' many wants.

tamil: ஒருவழிப டாது மாயை யிருவினைவி டாது நாளு
உ டலுமுயிர் தானு மாயு னுணர்விலொரு காலி ராத
கிரவுபகல் போன ஞான பரமசிவ யோக தீர
எமபடரை மோது மோன வுரையிலுப தேச வாளை
அரிவையொரு பாக மான அருணகிரி நாதர் பூசை
அமணர்குல கால னாகும் அரியதவ ராஜ ராஜன்
முருகபொரு சூரர் சேனை முறியவட மேரு வீழ
மொழியுமடி யார்கள் கோடி குறைகருதி னாலும் வேறு
reading: The poet speaks of the passion, infatuation and enjoyment that wander daily and never go one way, with maya and the two deeds never leaving him, and asks that, so his body, life and a heart that never stays a moment in awareness of the Lord may melt, Murugan give him the sword of teaching in the silent word, called the steadfast yoga of Siva-knowledge where night and day are gone, which strikes Yama's servants who fling the noose in anger, and so end his enemies. The praise names the monastery of Somanathan, praised on earth, a wise man who never fails in the worship of the Lord of Arunai who is half woman, death to the Jains' clan, a king among ascetics; Murugan who broke the Sura army and Meru; and the god who never knows anger though countless devotees state their wants.
nuance: மோன உரையில் உபதேச வாள்: the teaching given in silence is a sword against Death's servants, joining the two common pleas (the guru's word, rescue at death). The praise honours a human founder, சோமநாதன், as அமணர் குல காலன், the same title the poet gives Sambandar. The last line, முனிய அறியாத தேவர், praises the Lord's patience with petitioners.

title: த்ரியம்பகபுரம்
theme: A single song at Thiriyambakapuram (த்ரியம்பகபுரம்): courtesans who befriend men to seize their wealth, and the plea to be freed from that base work; the praise is a battle of drum syllables and ghosts drinking blood, and the gods bowing at the feet saying 'Kanda, given by Gauri'.

reading: The poet describes the women who see that men struck speechless are easy prey, befriend one and seize all his wealth, skilled in every art, the price-women whose breasts thrill and who make love in every way on the flower bed; they take what a man has earned and think others' wealth their own, and he asks to be freed from the base work of standing in their anger. The praise has Murugan mount the peacock to end the Asuras' age and free the world from fear, the drums sounding in syllables, ghosts drinking blood from a shoreless sea of it, the hunter girl embraced, and the gods bowing at Thiriyambakapuram saying 'Kanda, six-faced, given by Gauri'.
nuance: விலைமகள் is named outright. அயல் தனங்களும் தனது என நினைபவர்: the courtesans think others' wealth their own. வெகுளியின்கண் நின்று இழிதொழில் is obscure; it may mean the base life of serving their tempers.

title: சிக்கல்
theme: Two songs at Sikkal (சிக்கல்): the courtesans who say 'put down whatever is in your hand', and a confession of singing false praise to misers to end poverty, with the plea to be looked on by Murugan instead; the praise names Singaravelan of Sikkal and its fragrant groves.
structure_note: 826 is a courtesan song; 827 opens with the flattering verse a poor poet sings to a patron, which is the confession.
source_issues: Song 827: corrupt character in ரக்ஷ¢க் (line 1), clearly ரக்ஷிக் ('protecting').

reading: The poet describes courtesans with cane-sweet speech who melt hard hearts, startled glances, who spread their hands saying 'put down everything in your hand', pull a man's hands to their breasts and say 'untie my braided hair where I put the flowers', and asks not to wander in desire for such petty women but to be given the grace of the lord who spoke the word to Siva, delighted by the freed who praised him as the merciful one who pours out the three Tamils. The praise names Vishnu who cut the demons' crowns as uncle, the sharp vel that took Sura's head as he came spreading like a serpent's poison, Valli's breast, and the lord of Sikkal, where great ascetics of upright heart dwell.
nuance: கையில் உற்ற பொருட்கள் யாவையும் வை என கை விரிக்கும்: the courtesans' demand for everything in the hand is given as speech. பிஞ்ஞகர்க்கு உரை செப்பு நாயக: the teaching given to Siva, here without Om named; முத்தமிழில் தயாபர is how the freed praise him.

reading: The poet confesses singing to misers drunk on their wealth: 'kalpaka tree that protects poets, mountain of sweet virtue, whose arms press women's breasts, whose fame has gone to the eight directions, is there anyone in the world equal to you in friendship and truth, who is as generous to priceless Tamil words?', telling them his plight to end his poverty; a fool in great hardship, he now clings to Murugan's lotus feet as refuge and asks to be looked on with grace and given unfailing life. The praise names Murugan with the vetchi garland, the child of Himalaya's daughter, lord of the young forest girl and of the one Indra gave, Vishnu's nephew, and Singaravelan of lovely Sikkal, whose groves' scent carries thirty-eight kathams, who cut down the Asuras in battle.
nuance: The first half quotes the poet's own flattery, so the confession is in the genre of patron praise (செம்பாகமாகிய கவி), not of desire. வெறிகொள் உலுத்தர்க்கு என் பாடு கூறிடும் மிடி: it is poverty that drives the poet to beg from misers. சிங்கார வேலவ names Sikkal's god.

title: நாகப்பட்டினம்
theme: Three songs at Nagapattinam (நாகப்பட்டினம்): the poet repents of praising dull men as famous and the base as lords; he will not forget the feet even while he wanders in desire; and he asks for an unfailing boon against a life wasted in materialism and infatuation.
structure_note: 828 repents of patron praise; 829 is a catalogue of women's bodies ending in a vow not to forget the feet; 830 names Lokayata.
source_issues: Song 828: corrupt character in று¡ம ரை (line 3), clearly ஊமரை ('the dumb').
Song 829: unflagged garble தந்த்முல (line 21), perhaps தந்த முல; the next lines on Valli are uncertain.

tamil: ஓல மிட்டி ரைத்தெ ழுந்த வேலை வட்ட மிட்ட இந்த
று¡ம ரைப்ர சித்த ரென்று மூட ரைச்ச மர்த்த ரென்றும்
கோல முத்த மிழ்ப்ர பந்த மால ருக்க ரைத்த நந்த
கோப மற்று மற்று மந்த மோக மற்று னைப்ப ணிந்து
வாலை துர்க்கை சக்தி யம்பி லோக கத்தர் பித்தர் பங்கில்
வாரி பொட்டெ ழக்ர வுஞ்சம் வீழ நெட்ட யிற்று ரந்த
ஞால வட்ட முற்ற வுண்டு நாக மெத்தை யிற்று யின்ற
நாலு திக்கும் வெற்றி கொண்ட சூர பத்ம னைக்க ளைந்த
reading: The poet confesses that, asking who in this sea-girt world equals the clouds and the kalpaka trees, he called the dumb famous, fools capable and base men lords, composed fine Tamil prabandhas for them, spoke countless wants and wandered in vain like a dog; he asks when, with anger and delusion gone, Murugan will give him liberation, to worship him and join him. The praise names the Mother, Durga, Shakti, Ambika, who is in the half of the mad Lord and bore him, the vel thrown at Krauncha, Narayana who swallowed the world and sleeps on the serpent as uncle, and the slayer of Surapadma at Nagapattinam.
nuance: ஊமரைப் பிரசித்தர் என்றும் மூடரைச் சமர்த்தர் என்றும் ஊனரைப் பிரபுக்கள் என்றும்: the inversions of patron poetry are listed plainly. முகில் தருக்கள் ஒன்றும் அவர் ஆர்: the patron is flattered as cloud and kalpaka tree, the same flattery quoted in 827.

reading: The poet lists, part by part, the bodies of dancing young women: breasts like hills with necklaces and garlands, sword-like eyes, swinging earrings and heavy hair, moon faces and lotus lips, conch throats, turmeric arms, nails like parrots' beaks, a thin waist, the 'vessel of pleasure', banana thighs, anklets and bells, and says that even if he wanders thirsting for union with them he will not forget the feet where the anklets ring. The praise has drums and conches sound as Sura's pride is ended and the many-hooded serpent's peak struck while the vel dances, names Vishnu who as Narasimha made Hiranya tremble and with the bow ended Ravana's clan, the hunter girl, the nectar-formed maiden of knowledge, 'my one mother', and the lord at Nagai praised by devotees.
nuance: The plea is concessive: கலவி தாகம் உண்டு உழல்கினும் கழல் உறும் கழல் மறந்திடேனே, even while wandering in desire, the poet will not forget the feet. Valli is called என்றன் ஒரு தாய், 'my one mother'. Line 21 ends in a garble (தந்த்முல), which leaves the lines on Valli uncertain.

reading: The poet asks that, rather than let his days pass in waste, not thinking the body will fall, doing only what binds deeds, with Lokayata in the ascendant and weeping and ruined by infatuation with women, he be given an undying boon: to praise Murugan and be joined as kin to his flower feet. The praise names the god who uproots the deeds of those who worship and gives the stainless supreme, king of the gods, abode of compassion, life of devotees, the end of the unwritten Veda, the Lord who rules the poet, and asks him to give whatever is to be given, even himself, at Nagai.
nuance: உலகாயதம் மேலிடவே: the poet names Lokayata, the materialist school that denies anything beyond the body, as part of his wasted life. எழுதா மறை, 'the unwritten Veda', is the oral scripture. இறைவா எது தாவது அது தா தனையே is open; it may ask the Lord to give himself.

title: எட்டிகுடி
theme: Four songs at Ettikudi (எட்டிகுடி), one of which names Kanjirangudi: the poet confesses abandoning penance for women's breasts, being ruined and made poor by desire, and wandering in shameless lust, and asks for the teaching of Om and for the Lord's mark on him; the praise names Murugan the master of three Tamils and lists his shrines.
structure_note: 831, 833 and 834 are confessions of desire; 832 is a short plea for the teaching of Om; 834 ends with a list of shrines.
source_issues: Song 832 names Kanjirangudi (காஞ்சிரங்குடி) in its last line, not Ettikudi, the heading it stands under.
Song 832: ஓம்பை றும் (line 2) looks damaged.

Song 834: corrupt characters in விராலு¡ர் சேலு¡ர் (line 19), clearly விராலூர் சேலூர், §வ்ளுர் (line 21), probably யூர் (Vidaikkazhiyur), and வயலு¡ரா (line 21), clearly வயலூரா; also unflagged வர்ருர் (line 20) and தர்ருர் (line 21), the ர்ருர் garble for ஆரூர் seen in chapter 149, so the shrine names here are partly uncertain.

reading: The poet describes women with breasts like twin caskets, round, soft and thrilling, burdening the waist, smeared with sandal, and asks whether, abandoning penance, he will wander, quarrelling and embracing them again and again. The praise names Murugan the dear kinsman of Kama, son of Vishnu, who raised the cock banner and fought the Asura army, who in grace speaks the three Tamils to those who love him, and the lord at Ettikudi where pearls shine in the fields.
nuance: சருவிச் சருவித் தழுவித் தழுவித் தவம் அற்க விடுத்து: the doubled verbs enact the repetition of desire, and penance is what it gives up. அரி புத்திர சித்தச: Kama as Vishnu's son and Murugan's cousin.

reading: In a short song the poet, who grieves while thinking of pleasure as his five senses run, asks Murugan to rule him by speaking Om and what follows from it. The praise names Kumaresa, whose drawn arrows struck the Suras' clan, husband of the elephant's daughter and the hunter girl, life of devotees with minds free of attachment, the six-faced lord at Kanjirangudi.
nuance: ப்ரணவாதி உரைத்து எந்தனை ஆள்வாய்: the teaching of Om is asked for directly. ஓம்பை றும் before it looks damaged. The song names Kanjirangudi (காஞ்சிரங்குடி), not Ettikudi, the heading it stands under.

reading: The poet describes women with eyes like the sea, poison, arrows, does, fish and flowers, and breasts like lotus buds, caskets and hills that pierce him, and says that, unable to leave them and craving their union, he lost his wealth, fell into poverty and ruin and sank in mind; he asks Murugan to come to him, alone and weak, and give his lotus feet in friendship. The praise names Rama, whose unstoppable arrow took the life of the wicked ten-headed king and freed the lotus-born Sita from prison, as uncle, Murugan as the eye-like son of Siva who danced in the golden hall, and Ettikudi where shells spit pearls in the fields.
nuance: மிடலுற்ற கலவிக்குள் உளம் நச்சி வளமற்று மிடிபட்டு மடிபட்டு: here desire leads to poverty by itself, without the courtesans' theft. கனகப் பொதுவில் நட்புடன் அடித்த சிவன்: the dance in the golden hall is that of Chidambaram.

reading: The poet asks of women: is the dark hair sapphire or cloud, are the eyes fish or vel, is their speech milk, syrup or honey, the face the moon, the breasts tender coconuts or Meru, the waist a thread; and as a dog who wanders crying 'chee chee' while craving their limbs and uniting shamelessly, he asks not to suffer and wander, but to have Murugan set his mark on him, look on him with grace and come on the peacock. The praise names the child whom the three-eyed Siva praised, Kama's kinsman, Vishnu's nephew, master of the three Tamils, the lamp and incomparable form, Muruga who gives liberation to devotees, lord of Viralur, Selur, Palani, Arur, Vidaikkazhi and Vayalur, the mother within every scripture, the vel of Ettikudi.
nuance: The catalogue is put as questions (நீலோ மாலோ, சேலோ வேலோ), as in 822. தற்பொறி வைத்து அருள்: the Lord's mark set on the poet, like the brand on a servant. எச்சுருதிக்குளும் நீயே தாயே calls Murugan the mother in all scripture. Several shrine names in lines 19 to 21 are damaged.

title: எண்கண்
theme: A single song at Enkan (எண்கண்): the poet asks Murugan to come on the peacock to the sound of drums and anklets, enter his mind and tell him to praise, know and bow to the red feet; the praise names Rama's war with Lanka, Kumbhakarna shaken, and Indra's place restored.
