அம்ப கும்ப னுங்க லங்க வெஞ்சி னம்பு ரிந்து நின்று
இந்து வுங்க ரந்தை தும்பை கொன்றை யுஞ்ச லம்பு னைந்தி
இந்தி ரன்ப தம்பெ றண்டர் தம்ப யங்க டிந்த பின்பு
reading: The poet asks Murugan, his shoulders smeared with sandal and kumkum and wreathed with kadamba and champak, his anklets and bells ringing, to mount the peacock and come dancing to the drum's syllables, rejoicing and gracious, enter his mind and tell him: 'praise always, understand, and bow to the red feet'. The praise names Rama, whose monkey burned Lanka, who shattered the proud one's body to dust, shook Kumbhakarna and won with arrows, as uncle, Siva who wears the moon, karanthai, thumbai, konrai and the Ganga as father, and Murugan who settled at Enkan after freeing the gods from fear so Indra could regain his place.
nuance: The plea asks not for rescue but for an instruction: செம்பதம் பணிந்திர் என்று மொழிவாயே, that Murugan himself tell the poet to praise and bow. The song chimes on nasal clusters (சந்தனம், திமிர்ந்து, அணிந்து), set to the drum's திந்திமி தந்தன.

title: திருக்குடவாயில்
theme: Two songs at Thirukkudavayil (திருக்குடவாயில்): a plea to be freed from the price-women and from mala, maya and the gunas, and a song of wonder at Murugan as everything, the guru who made the poet speak of him, praised as the child of Uma who came as the Kauniya brahmin and sent the disputants to the stake.
structure_note: 836 is the usual plea and praise; 837 has no confession at all: its first half lists what Murugan is, and its second tells the Sambandar story.

reading: The poet speaks of the price-women with spear-like kohl eyes whom strangers court, deceivers even as they lie on the bed, and asks that his wandering infatuation end, that mala, maya and the gunas change, and that by the Veda he gain grace and the wondrous feet sweet as a honey garland. The praise names Murugan who gave the meaning as a command to the lord of Kailasa, who threw the bright vel at old Sura hiding in the sea, the clever lover of the Kurava girl, at Kudavayil among groves where cuckoos sing.
nuance: கயிலாயப்பதி உடையாருக்கு ஒரு பொருளே கட்டளை இடுவோனே: Murugan does not merely explain the meaning to Siva but lays it down as a command, the guru over the father. மறையால் மிக்கருள் பெறவே, grace through the Veda, is an unusual route for this poet, who more often asks grace through song or devotees; the phrase may also be read otherwise.

reading: The poet marvels that Murugan, who is the Veda, grammar and the many languages, beginning and middle, renunciation, dharma and the path, the joy of the wise, cloud and rain, sun, moon and stars, space and light, beyond day and night, the supreme maya none can know, became his guru and made him speak of it, and wonders whether this is the fruit of some first day. The praise tells how Murugan came as the Kauniya brahmin child who drank Uma's milk, a poet beyond all singers, sent the disputants to the stake, spread holy ash, straightened the cruel Maran's hunch and made Madurai flourish, and dwells at Kudasai.
nuance: The second half is the story of Sambandar told as Murugan's own: கவுணியர் குல வேதியன், the child who drank உமை's milk, the வாதிகள் impaled, the Pandya கூன் straightened, ash applied (நீறிட), all unmistakable details. நீ குருவாய் இது பகருமாறு செய்தாய் suggests the poet's own song is the guru's gift, a thanksgiving rather than a plea. The long list of what Murugan becomes is the pervasion the Tirumanthiram calls வியாபகம்.

title: வலிவலம்
theme: One song at Valivalam (வலிவலம்): the poet confesses to common women who leave one man for another with more wealth, and to delighting in house, wife, kin and wealth as if they were permanent, and asks to be set among devotees who worship with flowers.

reading: The poet speaks of common women who, though the young man who joined them from the first day is still there, go to another if they find more wealth with him, and of his own failure, caught in their snare and in deeds Brahma wrote, to wear ash and say 'Hara Hara'; he calls himself a poor fool who rejoices that house, wife, kin and wealth are permanent, and asks to be placed with the devotees offering flowers, to reach the higher state and worship the red-jewelled anklets of the feet on the peacock. The praise names Rama, who cut Ravana's crowns with one arrow, Siva of erukku, konrai, Ganga, crescent and bone garland, the vel that crushed Nirudan who stood as a mango tree, and the kadamba garland wet from Valli's breasts, at Valivalam.
nuance: அடுத்த பேர் மனை துணைவியர் தமர் பொருள் பெருத்த வாழ்விது சதமென மகிழ்வுறும் அசட்டன்: the confession turns from the women to household attachment, taking house, wife, kin and wealth for permanent (சதம்). The opening lines on the woman and the young man (தொடுத்த நாள் முதல் மருவிய இளைஞனும் இருக்க) are hard to divide, and the reading of them is tentative.

title: வேதாரணியம்
theme: Three songs at Vedaranyam (வேதாரணியம், Vedavanam): pleas against the bond of deeds, disease and lust, and against the women whose eyes conquer the land, with praise that dwells on Rama's story as the deeds of Murugan's uncle.
structure_note: 840 and 841 share their closing lines, naming Tiruttani, Senthil, Palani and Vedavanam; both praise Rama at length. 839 is a short song.
source_issues: Song 840: corrupt character in அள§முசத் (line 3); the word is unclear.
Song 841: corrupt character in வ¨ல்முழ்கிச் (line 5), probably a word for flood or sea with மூழ்கி.

reading: The poet asks whether he, a poor man who has not thought of the Lord as a companion in his karmic bond, his sorrow, long disease and wasting lust, must wander daily in griefs, and asks Murugan to remove his faults and give him thought of the red feet. The praise names the dark-cloud uncle who bridged the sea and conquered Lanka, the younger brother of the elephant-faced one, and the son given by Sankara of Vedavanam.
nuance: சோரம் இதற்குச் சிந்தை நினைந்துறு துணையாதே: the failure confessed is not to have taken the Lord as companion (துணை) in distress. The line on Rama's seven days at Lanka is hard to read.

tamil: சேலை யுடுத்துந டந்து மாலை யவிழ்த்துமு டிந்து
தேனி லினிக்கமொ ழிந்து காமு கரைச்சிறை கொண்டு
மாலை மயக்கில்வி ழுந்து காம கலைக்குளு ளைந்து
வால ரவிக்கிர ணங்க ளாமென வுற்றப தங்கள்
பாலை வனத்தில்ந டந்து நீல அரக்கியை வென்று
பார மரத்திரள் மங்க வாலி யுரத்தையி டந்து
வேலை யடைத்துவ ரங்கள் சாடி யரக்கரி லங்கை
மேவு திருத்தணி செந்தில் நீள்பழ நிக்குளு கந்து
reading: The poet describes women who walk in fine sarees, loosen and tie their garlands, comb their hair, speak sweeter than honey, imprison lustful men and conquer every land with their eyes, and asks whether he must fall into their evening bewilderment, sink into the arts of love and wander in pain; he asks for the grace of feet like the young sun's rays that end maya. The praise tells Rama's story: the walk through the wilderness, the dark rakshasi defeated, seven trees pierced with one arrow, Vali's chest torn, the sea bridged at Varuna's word, Lanka destroyed and grace given to Vibhishana, Murugan's uncle, and names Tiruttani, Senthil, Palani and Vedavanam.
nuance: மாலை மயக்கு can mean the bewilderment of the garland or of evening; both suit a street scene at dusk. The feet are likened to the rays of the young sun (வால ரவிக் கிரணங்கள்) that dispel maya, light against darkness.

tamil: நூலினை யொத்த மருங்குல் தேரினை யொத்த நிதம்பம்
நூறிசை பெற்ற பதங்கொள் மேருவை யொத்த தனங்கள்
சேலினை யொத்திடு கண்க ளாலும ழைத்திடு பெண்கள்
சீலம னைத்து மொழிந்து காமவி தத்தி லழுந்தி
வாலஇ ளப்பிறை தும்பை யாறுக டுக்கை கரந்தை
மாவலி யைச்சிறை மண்ட ஓரடி யொட்டிய ளந்து
மேல்முடி பத்தும ரிந்து தோளிரு பத்தும ரிந்து
மேவுதி ருத்தணி செந்தில் நீள்பழ நிக்குளு கந்து
reading: The poet lists the women who lure with thread-thin waists, anklets, Meru-like breasts and fish eyes, and asks whether, plunging into the sea of pleasure on their honey lips, giving up all virtue and sunk in lust, he must wander having lost the tapas that brings clarity. The praise names Murugan the son of Siva who wears the crescent, thumbai, the river, konrai, karanthai and Vasuki, and the nephew of Mukunda, who measured Mahabali's world with a step and cut the ten heads and twenty arms of Lanka's king.
nuance: சீலம் அனைத்தும் ஒழிந்து ... தேறு தவத்தை இழந்து: the loss named is of conduct and of tapas, not only of wealth or health. The closing two lines repeat 840's word for word.

title: கோடி - குழகர் கோயில்
theme: One song at Kodi, the Kuzhagar temple (கோடி - குழகர் கோயில்): a plea against women, land-greed and wealth-greed, before the body falls into Death's mouth like a frog in a snake's, asking to say 'Murugavel' once among the devotees.

reading: The poet asks that he not wander daily in love of women with cloud-dark hair, nor strive like a fish in the waves out of greed for land and wealth, and that before his body falls into Death's tongue like a frog into a snake's mouth he be granted to join those who chant with love and say once 'Muruga Vel'. The praise tells how Murugan sported with the peacock-like Kurava girl guarding millet from her platform and drove the bright vel into the hunters who came searching for a thief, names him son of Uma who plays with the ash-smeared Lord and younger brother of the elephant-faced one, at Kodi of Kuzhagar.
nuance: காலனது நா அரவ வாயில் இடு தேரையென: Death's tongue is a snake's mouth and the body a frog already in it, an image of death as already begun. புவியாசை பொருளாசை, the greed for land and for wealth, is named beside the women.

title: திருப்பெருந்துறை
theme: Three songs at Tirupperunthurai (திருப்பெருந்துறை): the body as a house of blood and bone that sickens, bends and becomes a corpse; the embrace of women and the great sea of birth; the memory of a night's lovemaking that the poet asks to have erased. Murugan is praised as guru to his father, beside Siva seated as guru under the kurunda tree.
structure_note: 843 is a body-and-ageing song, 844 and 845 courtesan and lovemaking songs; 843 and 844 both name Murugan or Siva as guru at this shrine.
source_issues: Song 844: corrupt character in கடலு¡டே (line 12), clearly கடலூடே.

reading: The poet pictures the body as a house of earth and water built of blood, fat, marrow, bone, flesh, guts and nerves, which the soul enters and lives in, flown off with deceit and the greed for wealth like a bird, then struck by fever, bile and winds, its strength shrinking until it goes on a stick, bent like the monkey clan, and asks whether, afraid when it finally slips, he will simply become a corpse. The praise, in drum syllables, shows the vel that scattered Sura and the hill, the gods bowing until their head-garlands scent the golden feet, and names Murugan the guru who gave the discourse of wisdom to his father, guru of the world, at Tirupperunthurai.
nuance: மண்சல வீடு, a house of earth and water, makes the body a hut built of the elements; பொருளாசை எனும் புள் makes greed a bird that carries the soul off. சடமாமோ, 'shall I become a corpse?', ends the plea as a question rather than a prayer. செகத்தினின் குருவாகிய தந்தைக்கு அளித்திடும் குரு ஞானப் ப்ரசங்க: Murugan as guru to Siva, the world's guru.

reading: The poet speaks of women with kumkum-painted breasts whose bangled arms embrace and whose fish eyes roll in delight until understanding is lost, and asks whether Murugan will now be willing to give his holy feet so that he may cross the great sea of birth. The praise names the vel that burned the hill and the demons' city, Vishnu who held Mandara in the sea, and the four-faced Brahma who worship the feet, and Sankara who sits as guru under the holy kurunda tree, with whom Murugan dwells at Tirupperunthurai.
nuance: திருக்குருந்தடி அமர் குருத்வ சங்கரர்: Siva seated as guru under the kurunda tree at Perunthurai, the scene of Siva's teaching of Manikkavasagar there, though the song does not name the saint. Here the guru is Siva and Murugan dwells with him, a reversal of the songs where Murugan teaches Siva.

reading: The poet describes a night of lovemaking in detail, dark hair, poisoned eyes, sweating brow, coral lips, conch bangles crying out, breasts pressed until no space is left between them and life joins life, and asks for grace now so that the memory of that moment and the longing to see those faces leave his heart. The praise tells of Rama, before whom the sea came trembling to worship, who killed the twenty-armed hero and broke Lanka, names Murugan the young one who circles the earth on his peacock faster than thought, at Perunthurai among pearl-bright fields and kurundam shade.
nuance: The plea asks not for escape from the women but for the end of the memory (நினைவு நெஞ்சினின்று அற) and of the longing to see their faces (முகமது தெரிசனம் செயும் பரிவற): the trouble is what the mind keeps. உயிர் உயிருடன் உற, life with life, is the poet's own phrase for the union.

title: திருத்துருத்தி
theme: One song at Tirutturutti (திருத்துருத்தி): the poet confesses to courtesans who are never satisfied with any sum and to the disease that follows, and recalls that Murugan called him, gave him the experience of release and told him to recite the Thiruppugazh.

reading: The poet describes the courtesans, heavy-breasted and thread-waisted, who loosen their garments and bewitch with spear eyes, then turn their glance against the men who trusted them, say that even thousands upon thousands of gold coins poured on their breasts are not enough, and cast men off; he calls himself a vain man whom a great disease has crippled and shamed and asks for the lightning-bright feet. The praise names Murugan who called him, a dog, as one taking refuge, gave him the experience of release and bade him recite the Thiruppugazh, the child who gave a poem in triple Tamil to the teacher who burned the three cities, and Valli's lover at Tirutturutti.
nuance: அழைத்து முத்தியதாம் அநுபூதி என் அருள் திருப்புகழ் ஓதுக வேல் மயில் அருள்வோனே: the poet's own call, in which Murugan names the Thiruppugazh, appears here in the praise, as in 2. The line on the teacher (தேசிகர்) of the three cities and the poem in triple Tamil may refer to Siva or to a saint, and the reading is tentative. மகாபிணி after the courtesans is a disease caught from them.

title: திருவீழிமிழலை
theme: One song at Thiruveezhimizhalai (திருவீழிமிழலை): the endless round of births, from womb to crop to harvest, with mothers by the crore, and the plea to say once 'Muruga, save my life'.
source_issues: Song 847: the source writes ஓரு for ஒரு (ஓருதா, ஓருகால்) and splits உ யிர் with a space.

reading: The poet traces the round of birth, a form taking shape in the womb as from manure, growing as a crop to harvest, this one going and becoming that one and that one becoming this, a chain like madness, with one mother, two mothers and many crores of them, and asks not to perish in vain but to be given the grace to say once 'Muruga, supreme Kumara, save my life'. The praise names Murugan who sets his feet on the heads of devotees who say 'Muruga' once, who threw the vel at old Sura when the sages and gods cried for justice, the son of the one Vishnu and Brahma could not find, and nephew of Vishnu, at Thiruveezhi.
nuance: ஒருதாய் இருதாய் பலகோடியதாய்: the mothers multiply with the births, a compact image of samsara. The plea and the praise turn on one word: the poet asks to say 'Muruga' once (ஒருகால்), and the praise says Murugan gives his feet to those who say it once (ஓர் தரம்).

title: திருவாவடுதுறை
theme: One song at Thiruvavaduthurai (திருவாவடுதுறை): the poet confesses that instead of praising Murugan he sank into courtesans and then into flattering wicked rich men in verse to escape poverty, and asks not to be left to that weariness.

reading: The poet confesses that, failing to praise Murugan without a slip of speech, he whirled in the pot of birth, delighted in the way of the seed and set his mind on the coral lips of price-women, then went to evil, cruel men of the earth, set them in verse as a kalpaka king of wealth and an Arjuna in battle, and recited his learning loudly to end his poverty; he asks whether Murugan will let him be worn out by this fancy, empty-handed and confused. The praise tells of Krishna who trampled the hooded serpent, tore the crocodile that seized the elephant and drank the breast of the deceiving demoness until she died, and of Rama, and describes the peacock adorned with gold and gems, at Thiruvavaduthurai.
nuance: The confession is double: the courtesans, and the court poet's trade, praising துற்சனர் (the wicked) as கற்பக ராசன் and அர்ச்சுனன் for money. The proper object of praise (உனைக் கனக்கத் துதித்து) is set against the false one. The praise of the peacock's jewelled trappings is hard to divide.

title: மருத்துவக்குடி
theme: One song at Maruthuvakkudi (மருத்துவக்குடி): a plea against deceitful courtesans and the poet's own deafness to good counsel, asking for the feet that give realization of the meaning of the ancient sayings; Murugan is praised as the jnana guru of Siva.

reading: The poet speaks of vain women who pursue the arts of lust, deceitful tricksters and sweet-talkers with cloud-dark hair, in whose sidelong glance he turned and was ruined, and calls himself a low man who will not hear wise counsel, full of craving and bonds, a fool who does not grasp the true thing; he asks for the feet so that he may gain the great realization that gives the good meaning of the lofty old sayings. The praise names the vel against Sura and the arrogant demons, Murugan who loves the triple-Tamil garland sung by the pure who reached Siva, the jnana guru in the mind of Siva the trident-bearer, at Maruthuvakkudi where jackfruit juice floods the fields.
nuance: உரைத்த புத்திகள் கேளா நீசன் ... உளத்தில் மெய்ப்பொருள் ஓரா மூடன்: the poet blames himself for not heeding counsel, and asks for the feet so that the sense of the மூதுரை, the old sayings, may become his own experience (உணர்ச்சி). அரர் மனத்து இயல்படு ஞான தேசிக: Murugan as the jnana teacher in Siva's mind.

title: திருப்பந்தணை நல்லூர்
theme: Seven songs at Tiruppandanainallur (திருப்பந்தணை நல்லூர்): courtesans of the street who ask first whether a man has money, the poet's mala and deeds, and pleas for the jnana teaching, the feet, the gift of rhythmic Tamil, and for remembering Murugan even in pleasure; the praise names the goddess as Sivai, Sambhavi and Parai, bindu and sound.
structure_note: Courtesan songs (850, 852, 853, 854, 856); a chant of Murugan's names (851); and 855, which promises to hold Murugan's feet and arms in mind even while sporting with women.
source_issues: Song 850: குயில்பொலே (line 3) for குயில்போலே.
Song 855: corrupt characters in புண்டா£கம் (line 6, புண்டரீகம்) and நலு¡ர (line 18, நல்லூர்); also the garble இன்ப்முடே (line 9), probably இன்பமூடே.
Song 856: corrupt character in த¨ழைய (line 18), probably தழைய.

tamil: சிலசெம்புள்கள் கழுகுஞ் சிறு நரியுங்கொடி யாடப் ...... பொரும்வேலா
reading: The poet describes the courtesans of the street, scented with sandal and civet, cloud-haired, cuckoo-voiced, walking like peacocks with anklets ringing and lisping like parrots, whose first thought is 'is there money?', who change the minds and deeds of those who see them, and asks Murugan to end the sorrow of the maya of these deceivers who sleep by day and some nights. The praise, in drum syllables, shows the battle with Sura's army and the birds and jackals feeding, names the goddess Sivai, Sundari, Sambhavi and Parai, Siva's left half, as his mother, and Murugan with Valli and Devayanai as the pure guru of Pandanai.
nuance: பணம் உண்டென தவலம்படு நினைவு: the women's thought turns at once to money, the mark of the price-woman. The goddess's names (சிவை, சுந்தரி, சம்பவி, பரை) are a litany of Sakti; the song gives them to Murugan's mother.

reading: The poet asks that his two deeds fear, coming deeds plead, the dark disease sleep and mala and maya fade, that Murugan's grace swell, and that, singing his lofty praise and calling 'moon-faced Muruga, Kadamba, son of Siva, Kandha, Guha, Vela' and 'Siva Siva' with a clear heart, he be given the dancing anklets. The praise names the nephew of Vishnu who took the life of the marutha trees and Kamsa, the hero on the golden peacock who circles the demons' hill, the son loved by the pure Lord who rides the bull with his consort, and the lord of Pandanai with his two consorts.
nuance: The plea is a string of names, a chant within the song; சிவசிவ என்று தெளிவுறு நெஞ்சு makes the clarity of heart come through repeating Siva's name. The first lines personify deeds and disease: past deeds fear, coming deeds beg.

reading: The poet describes the price-women who shame swans in gait, play dramas, sing, run up debts, fall for anyone with great show of passion and cast the net of deceit, and asks that he, a dog of a servant who fell into infatuation and gained passion, disease and illness, wander no more but be given the nectar of mantra and jnana teaching and the anklets, so that grace enters when he calls 'Muruga' with love. The praise names the vel that burned seas and islands, Siva clothed in elephant and tiger skin who took the poet as his servant, Sadasiva whose side Uma never leaves, Vishnu who bears Lakshmi on his chest, and Valli's lord at Pandanai.
nuance: அமுத மந்திர ஞானோபதேசமும் அருளி: the plea is for initiation, a mantra given as teaching. கரி நெடும் புலி தோல் உடையார் எனை அடிமை கொண்ட சுவாமி: the poet calls Siva the one who made him his servant, a rare first-person claim on the father rather than the son.

reading: The poet speaks of women with pot-like breasts and parrot speech, musk in their hair, with whom he stirs up mischief and gives friendship, and asks not to wither in hell but to be given the mind to worship the feet that came round Kailasa. The praise names Murugan son of the goddess who shares half of the river-bearer, born of her old tapas, dweller at cloud-wrapped Pandanai, lord even to Sankara who came down under the jambu tree's shade, who ended the fear of the gods.
nuance: சம்பு நிழலுக்குள் வந்து அவதரித்த சங்கரர் points to Siva under the jambu tree, the form worshipped at Thiruvanaikka, and Murugan is called lord even to him. வண்கயிலை சுற்றி வந்திடு பதம may recall Murugan circling the world or Kailasa, but the allusion is unclear.

reading: The poet tells how fish-eyed women with flowered hair coax him to bed, scent him with powder and embrace him with sweet words, and asks that the sorrow of that infatuation end through the fragrant lotus feet, with thandai, kinkini and anklets ringing, coming always to him so that his cruel deeds, anxiety and mala perish. The praise names Murugan to whom devotees cry 'refuge', who wed Devayanai and the Kurava girl, whose vel crushed the arms of the gods' enemies, and Saravana at Pandanai among monkeys, champak, agil, sandal and konrai.
nuance: The ringing of the anklets is sung in sound (கலின் கலின், கிணின் கிணின்), the feet arriving audibly; the plea is that they come to him (வந்திரும்), not that he go to them.

reading: The poet lists the beauty of women from honey lips and crystal smile to lotus feet, and says that even if he plays in sorrow in the pleasure of union with them, he will lovingly hold in his heart Murugan's lotus feet, his twelve arms and his chest with its garland. The praise names his mother as the Siva-form of 'Om Namah', five-faced, Neeli, Kalyani, the light of bindu and the dwelling of sound, Abhirami Ambika; Murugan whose vel made the demons' blood run while gandharvas sang, the lover of Valli and Devayanai, the lord of Pandanai where Siva wears karanthai, konrai, the moon and the river.
nuance: The song does not ask to leave the women: விளையாடினும் ... பரிவுளங்கொள்வேனே, 'even if I play, I will hold you in mind', makes remembrance the vow, as in 153. The mother's names ஓநமந்த சிவரூபி ... விந்து ஒளி ஓசை தங்கும் make the goddess bindu and nada, the Tirumanthiram's terms.

reading: The poet speaks of women with moon faces and parrot voices, like Menaka and Rati, like sea-goddesses, who stay daily in the street while men bring wealth and gold jewels and go, and asks not to wander under their sway but, with wealth abundant through many tapas, to know the wisdom of speaking of Murugan and to pour out rhythmic Tamil fit to sing him. The praise names Siva of the spreading matted hair who rejoiced in Uma's worship, the city that flourishes on a river equal to the nine Gangas, Murugan who blessed the ganas, gods, Hari, Brahma, Mukunda and the poets, and the vel that split Krauncha.
nuance: நிகர் சந்தத் தமிழ் சொரிந்து பாட: the gift asked is the rhythmic Tamil of the Thiruppugazh itself. நதிபங்கில் ... கந்துகாபுரி, the name of the city by the river, is unclear.

title: திருப்பனந்தாள்
theme: One song at Thiruppanandal (திருப்பனந்தாள்): a plea against women whose speech is sugar, asking Murugan to hand over the unfading good thing; the praise shows the vel playing ball with Sura's head.

reading: The poet speaks of women with clustered dark hair whose speech is called sugar, whose breasts under pearl strings rise like mountains, and asks that his petty mind not wander as they surround him, but that Murugan say to him 'here is the unfading good thing, the wonder'. The praise shows the moon and sun fleeing and the ascetics' homes emptied before Sura, who came asking 'where is that hill, where is this one', his head played like a ball by the vel, the battlefield given to the Kali of war, and Kandha of Panandal.
nuance: மங்கா நற்பொருள் இந்தா அற்புதம் என்றே இப்படி அருள்வாயே: the plea imagines the Lord handing over the truth with a word, 'here, take it'. The praise gives a share of the field to ரணகாளி, the battle-goddess.

title: திருவிடைமருதூர்
theme: Four songs at Thiruvidaimarudur (திருவிடைமருதூர்): a whole life from a dewdrop of seed to the cremation fire, the miser who mocks the next world and dies despised, ending in a plea for union in which 'you and I' become one enjoyment; pleas for the gift of sweet Tamil, for the will to share and sing, and for the teaching of Siva-jnana against courtesans.
structure_note: 858 is a long biography of a worldly life; 859 and 861 are courtesan songs asking for song and for jnana teaching; 860 confesses the failure to sing and share.
source_issues: Song 858: உ றவின்முறை and உ மிழுமது (lines 18, 22) are split by a space after உ.

tamil: ஆளு மேளமாய் வால ரூபமாய் ...... அவரொரு பெரியோராய்
ஆசை யாளராய் ஊசி வாசியாய் ...... அவியுறு சுடர்போலே
வீணி யார்சொலே மேல தாயிடா ...... விதிதனை நினையாதே
மேள மேசொலா யாளி வாயராய் ...... மிடையுற வருநாளில்
வாடி யூனெலாம் நாடி பேதமாய் ...... மனையவள் மனம்வேறாய்
வாயு மேலிடா ஆவி போகுநாள் ...... மனதர்கள் பலபேச
ஈம தேசமே பேய்கள் சூழ்வதாய் ...... எரிதனி லிடும்வாழ்வே
ஏக நாயகா லோக நாயகா ...... இமையவர் பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet traces a life: a drop small as dew on a grass tip becoming a body and a child whose prattle melts its parents, growing into a man with wives, house and halls, a miser who would not let a crumb of husk fall, who sends a poor ascetic asking for food to the upper house and the lower and leaps at him like a dog, follows a vain woman's word, serves vain men, mocks those who say there is a next world and scolds renunciants and brahmins; then poverty and diseases come, his eyes run, phlegm rises, his wife's mind changes and women and children say 'chee', he dreams of chariot and horse and the burning ground, his speech fails and breath leaves while kin wail and drums beat at the cremation ground among ghosts, and he is put into the fire. Against this he asks Murugan, destroyer of bonds, to grant the supreme bliss in which the two deeds, the three malas, death and birth end and 'you and I' become one enjoyment, at Idaimarudur, lord of the world and the gods.
nuance: The miser's sin is refusal, sending the begging ascetic from door to door (மேலை வீடு கேள் கீழை வீடு கேள்), and the denial of the next world (மறுமை உளதெனுமவரை ... வருவார்கள் போகுவார் காணுமோ எனா). The end is not escape to the feet but union: நீயும் நானுமாய் ஏக போகமாய், 'you and I as one enjoyment'. The line on what the devotees of the feet obtain (பெறுவதுவும் ஏசிடார்களோ) is hard to read.

reading: The poet describes women whose eyes reach their earrings as nets for young men's lives, whose lips he drinks and whose breasts he embraces in growing passion, and asks whether Murugan will not grant him the grace to sing sweet poems in order, with knowledge of release ripening, in rare Tamil sound, joined to a worship of bright speech. The praise tells how the vel shattered Meru and the sea, how Murugan rode the peacock to restore the gods and destroy cruel deeds, spoke silent teaching into the ear of his father who dances with ghosts, married the hunter girl, and as Kumara guru sought debate so that the Jains played on the stakes, lord of the great sages of Idaimarudur.
nuance: தாதை செவி நிறைய மவுன உரையாடு: Murugan fills his father's ear with a 'silent' teaching, the Om story without naming Om. அமணர் கழுவில் விளையாட வாது படை கருது குமரகுருநாத: the impaling of the Jains, the Sambandar story, given to Murugan as Kumaraguru.

reading: The poet confesses that he never once went to sing calmly 'Kumara, six-faced one of sweet red speech, the first who came in Saravana, Kandha', the one whom Sankara himself worships, Sankara whom Vishnu, Brahma, the Vedas and the gods cannot praise and who wears serpents, Ganga, moon, konrai and thumbai in his hair; that he never came near with the grace to share even a millet grain; and asks whether he will not think of the vow of walking in the way of tapas. The praise shows the vel splitting the demons skilled in mantra and tantra while vultures, foxes and ghosts feast and dance, names Murugan the great guru of Idaimarudur, lover of the forest maiden, whose lotus feet with ruby anklets, raining compassion, the gods stroke in service as their final refuge.
nuance: The confession is of three omissions: not singing, not sharing (பகிர ஒரு தினையளவு), not keeping to tapas, so the remedy is the same as in 23, sharing even a millet grain. சங்கரன் கும்பிடும் குமரன்: Siva worships Murugan. The opening list of who cannot praise Siva is long and its division tentative.

tamil: புழுகொடுபனி நீர்ச வாதுட னிருகரமிகு மார்பி லேபன
பொதுவினில்விலை கூறு மாதர்கள் மணியணிகுழை மீது தாவடி
மெழுகெனவுரு காவ னார்தம திதயகலக மோடு மோகன
மிடைபடுமல மாயை யால்மிக கலவிய அறி வேக சாமிநின்
எழுகிரிநிலை யோட வாரிதி மொகுமொகுவென வீச மேதினி
இமையவர்சிறை மீள நாய்நரி கழுகுகள்கக ராசன் மேலிட
செழுமதகரி நீல கோமள அபிநவமயி லேறு சேவக
திரைபொருகரை மோது காவிரி வருபுனல்வயல் வாவி சூழ்தரு
reading: The poet speaks of the women who sell themselves in public with civet- and rose-water-scented breasts and arrow eyes, says that he, a dog who does not melt like wax, suffers confusion, delusion and anguish and is entangled in mala and maya, and asks Murugan to come and give his bountiful teaching of Siva-jnana. The praise shows the seven hills fleeing, the sea roaring, the demon army broken and the gods freed while dogs, jackals and vultures feast, names the hero on the elephant and the young peacock, 'victory, Muruga, Guha, Kandavel', and the lord of Idaimarudur where the Kaveri beats its banks.
nuance: பொதுவினில் விலைகூறு மாதர்: women who name their price in public. மெழுகென உருகாவனார் turns the usual image round: he does not melt like wax for the Lord. சிவஞான போதகம், the teaching asked for, is also the name of Meykandar's Saiva Siddhanta text; whether the poet means the book is uncertain.

title: திரிபுவனம்
theme: One song at Tribhuvanam (திரிபுவனம்): the poet caught in the net of union that he enjoys even in dreams asks for Murugan's small red lotus feet; the praise names Murugan who taught his father the one thing and is lord of the siddhas of the shrine.

reading: The poet describes the women whose brows sweat and eyes sink as they speak sweet love and embrace, the lips' moisture sweeter than sugar, and says his life is caught and perishing in the net of a union he enjoys even in dreams; a man without fate or wit, he asks whether he will not gain the small red lotus feet that bring release. The praise names Devayanai, daughter of the thunderbolt-bearer, the sea crying out and the demons turning tail before the lion-like hero, Murugan who offered the one thing that gives experience to his father and received his worship, lord of the siddhas of Tribhuvanam who remain even when all the world perishes.
nuance: கனவிலும் நுகர்தரு கலவி: the union is enjoyed even in dreams, desire outlasting waking. அனுபவம் அளிதரும் ஒரு பொருள் அப்பர்க்கு அப்படி ஒப்பித்து அர்ச்சனை கொண்ட நாதா: the teaching of Siva again, here as 'the one thing that gives experience', after which the father worships the son.

title: கும்பகோணம்
theme: Seven songs at Kumbakonam (கும்பகோணம், Kudanthai): a yogic vision of the dancing Lord of eight qualities in the jewelled hall within, pleas against women and their union, for jnana teaching and the sight of the space of knowledge, and two songs on the body, one on its ageing and one on its filth, asking for Sivayoga and jnana.
structure_note: 863 is a song of inner vision with no confession; 864 to 867 are courtesan songs (866 a short one); 868 is an ageing song and 869 a song of the body's impurity.
source_issues: Song 865: corrupt characters in கிம்பு¡£ச (line 3, unclear) and நெஞ்சிலு¡றி (line 10, நெஞ்சிலூறி).
Song 866: corrupt character in குஞ்சா£ (line 7, குஞ்சரி).
Song 869: corrupt character in உடலு¡டே (line 3, உடலூடே).

reading: The poet asks for the grace to see, where the light of moon and sun strikes the central pillar and the sweet taste of nectar-milk flows, the Lord of eight qualities dancing on the moon-bright seat in the jewelled hall, to see and rejoice in the fragrant petal of the letters, bathe in the sea of nectar, and behold the thousand and eight worlds. The praise, in drum syllables, shows the vel scattering Sura's crown as the seven seas surge, and names Murugan whom the daughter of the cloud-hued Vishnu, the golden doll, worships with hand-cymbals and praises, the six-faced lord of Kumbakonam.
nuance: The plea is a yogic vision in the Tirumanthiram's terms: moon and sun (இந்து, கதிர்), the central pillar (நடுத்தூண்), likely the central channel, the nectar, and the dance in the inner hall (மணிச்சபை). எண்குணமுற்றோன் is the Kural's எண்குணத்தான். கந்த எழுத்து, the fragrant letter, may mean the mystic syllable on a lotus petal, but the line is hard to divide.

reading: The poet asks whether he must wander for the women whose breasts leap like the tusks of an elephant, whose hair is like a cloud-dark night and a peacock's plumes, whose speech is molten gold and whose fish eyes shoot arrows that shatter the mind. The praise tells of Vishnu: as Rama, with his brother and Sita, who was drawn off by the forest deer and imprisoned until he broke the demons' crowns and freed her; as Krishna, blowing the horn and dancing as he gathered the herds; and names Murugan who delights in the breasts of the parrot-like girl, six-faced lord of Kumbakonam.
nuance: The plea is a single question; most of the song is the description and the praise of Vishnu's two avatars. The lines on Rama and the deer are hard to divide.

reading: The poet tells how at a glimpse of a woman's scented breasts he swells with desire, sinks into deceptive union and melts as a rogue, and asks not to wander thus but for Murugan to come, teach him the one thing in the meaning of jnana and give his fair feet daily. The praise names the vel that shattered Meru so the gods might live, and Murugan who cut the heads of those who imprisoned the loving ascetics of the Lord of the five gates, sending them to the stake while vultures pecked, lord of Kumbakonam among fields where conches crawl.
nuance: The praise seems to tell of enemies who harmed devotees of Siva being impaled, which recalls the Jains of the Sambandar story, though here they are called அசுரோர்; அஞ்சுவாயில் பரன், the Lord of the five gates, may mean the Lord reached through the five senses or the five letters. The reading is tentative.

reading: A short song: the poet asks whether, instead of sinking into the foul skin of dancing women with cotton-soft feet, he will gain Murugan's golden love through colourful Tamil of fine words. The praise names Murugan son of the Sakti who lives at the side of the god who fought Kama of the five arrows, lover of Devayanai's breasts, lord of Kumbakonam.
nuance: பங்கமார் தொக்கு, the soiled skin, reduces the women to their surface; the remedy is செஞ்சொல் சேர் சித்ரத் தமிழ், the poet's own art.

reading: The poet describes women who stand in the street at evening combing their scented hair, breasts and ornaments swaying, so that those passing on the road stagger at the sight, and asks that instead of suffering in thirst and dark delusion he may rise at dawn, recite Murugan's names, calling him son of loving Uma, know the right times and gain the grace for his eyes to see the space of knowledge. The praise names Kumaresa who stood in anger before Sura's army and the lord of Kumbakonam with a consort on either side.
nuance: The evening street and the morning worship are set against each other: மாலைதனில் ... காலையில் எழுந்து. ஞானவெளி கண்கள் காண, to see with the eyes the open space of knowledge, is the goal of the daily discipline.

reading: The poet pictures old age, black hair whitening, teeth falling, the mind clouded, dizziness and disease, the back bent, cough in the throat, the body shrunk and a stick shaking in the hand, the wife reviling him and the sons abusing him until he is a corpse, and asks when, the sea of birth of this filthy suffering body ended, he will reach the holy feet. The praise names the hero of the peacock-steed who churned the great sea, the vel that crushed the demons, Murugan proud on the breasts of the Kurava girl of the millet field, rider of the peacock, Kandha of Kudanthai.
nuance: The ageing is told through the household's scorn as much as the body: மனைவியும் நிந்தித்து அடுத்த மைந்தரும் வசைகள் விளம்ப. The praise line on the peacock as a steed (விரக துரங்கம்) is tentative.

reading: The poet speaks of the body born of water and phlegm, guts, flesh, rheum and cough, over which castes and disputants clamour about lineage, which all say is a disease of birth, of which they cry 'this is the Kali age' and 'take it to the burning ground', and which falls to dust, and asks that, instead of cherishing it with earrings, ornaments, clothes, arts and many desires, he be given the Sivayoga and jnana that remove them. The praise, in drum syllables, shows the vel against the Danava army, names Murugan who graces the great ascetics who know equanimity, who took refuge at the feet of the peacock-like girl in the millet field, the child who came through the tapas of Siva's bright flame, at Kudanthai.
nuance: பல சாதியும் வாதியும் இரைத்திடும் குலமே may say that the castes and sects quarrel over a body that is only filth, a rare social note, but the line is hard to read. சமத்து உணர்ந்திடு மாதவர், ascetics who know equanimity, are the model held up.

title: சோமீச்சுரம்
theme: One song at Someechuram (சோமீச்சுரம்): after a full description of lovemaking the poet asks for the jnana to recite Murugan's youth, beauty, arms, feet and faces even in union, in sleep and in every conversation; the praise tells Prahlada's story.
source_issues: Song 870: corrupt character in §ல்முழ்கி (line 7), probably a word for flood or sea with மூழ்கி; உ ரிய, உ ரமுடைய, உ கிர், உ வணபதி (lines 11 to 14) are split by a space after உ.

tamil: உ வணபதி நெடியவனும் வேதாவும் நான்மறையு ...... முயர்வாக
reading: The poet describes lovemaking in detail, hair loosened, face sweating, breasts thrilling, lips like nectar, bangles ringing, two bodies made one without shame, and asks that even while he sinks in union with young women, without a blink, while he sleeps at night or talks with anyone, he be given the knowledge to recite Murugan's youth, beauty, twelve arms, two feet and six faces. The praise tells how, when a child chanted 'Nama Narayanaya' and his father raged 'where is your god?', Vishnu burst from the pillar as a lion and tore Hiranya's chest with his claws, and names Murugan who dwells gladly in the Somesar temple among dancing peacocks and areca groves, by the camp of the Marutha kings.
nuance: As in 855, the plea is not to stop but to remember in every state: in union, in sleep, in speech (கலவிதனில் மூழ்கி ஆழுகினும் இமையாதே இரவினிடை துயிலுகினும் யாரோடு பேசுகினும்). Prahlada is unnamed but the story is unmistakable: the child's நமநாராயணாய, the father's question, the pillar and the claws. மருதரசர் படைவிடுதி, the camp of the Marutha kings, is an allusion not identified here.

title: கொட்டையூர்
theme: One song at Kottaiyur (கொட்டையூர்): the poet, called wicked, troublesome, mad and fallen for his surrender to women, asks for the golden lotus feet and a place among the purified devotees; the praise tells of Sita's abduction and Ravana's ten heads cut.

reading: The poet tells how, falling into the hands of parrot-like women whose silk bodices loosen over pearl strings, he melted under their sway and by ruined deeds wanders called wicked, troublesome, mad, fallen and cruel-minded, and asks Murugan to cut his sorrow, set his golden lotus feet on him and place him among the devotees of the purified state. The praise tells how Ravana carried the golden creeper of the lotus off in his chariot to a grove in the far south and imprisoned her, and how the victor cut his ten crowned heads and many arms, ending his pride, and names the lord of Kottaiyur whom the victorious worship.
nuance: துட்டனெனக் கட்டனெனப் பித்தனெனப் ப்ரட்டனென: the names are what others call him, a public shame. The praise piles up அற ('cut off, ended') through the line on Ravana, a sound-play. பதவிச் சுத்தி அணைப் பத்தர் is hard to divide.

title: சிவபுரம்
theme: A song at Sivapuram (சிவபுரம்): the poet asks that his mind, wandering in the joys and sorrows of a body made of the elements, be conquered and joined to grace on the path of supreme knowledge; the praise is a litany of Parvati and the Man-Lion as Murugan's uncle.

reading: The poet speaks of the one body made of mind and the five elements, in which he wanders in pleasure, sorrow and desire, and asks Murugan to conquer that mind and join him, a dog of a servant, to grace so that he gains the good path of supreme knowledge. The praise calls Murugan the son of Parvati, named as Janani, Sankari, Narani, the spotless one full of the eight qualities, the cause, Siva's consort; the vel that freed the imprisoned gods and uprooted the asuras; the nephew of Vishnu who came as the Man-Lion from the pillar Hiranya struck and drank his blood; and the lord praised by gods and sages at Sivapuram, whose houses are filled with gold by the eight Lakshmis.
nuance: மனமெனும் பொருள் ... கூடியதோர் உடல்: mind is counted with sky, wind, fire, water and earth as what makes up the body, and the plea is to conquer the mind (மதியை வென்று), not the body. பதி மூணெழு வகையாலே is obscure; it may count kinds of birth or constituents. The Narasimha story is told in its detail (the pillar, the claws, the blood drunk like nectar), more fully than usual. திருமடந்தையர் நாலிருவோர் are the eight Lakshmis.

title: திருநாகேச்சுரம்
theme: A song at Thirunageswaram (திருநாகேச்சுரம்): a catalogue of the wicked, from parent-revilers and adulterers to drunkards and hoarders, who will wander in the lowest births; the praise names Vayalur, where the Thiruppugazh was given, and Siva of the shrine as the father who praised his son as guru.
source_issues: Song 873: one corrupt character in வயலு¡ரா (line 18), read as வயலூரா, 'lord of Vayalur'.

reading: Without any plea of his own, the poet lists the wicked who will wander in the lowest births like dogs: those who have no conduct and argue perversely, revile mother and father, kill the cow for its flesh, enjoy other men's wives without a qualm, live by every trick, drink intoxicating liquor, snatch the goods of the helpless without shame, babble their desire for what belongs to others, swagger with club, sword and bow, do sinful austerities without serving a guru, and hoard and bury wealth without giving. The praise names the vel that felled the one mango in the roaring sea, Murugan of Vayalur who received the true Thiruppugazh, the famed true guru whose teaching cuts the delusion of maya for those suffering from past deeds, praised by his father named Nagesa.
nuance: The song is a list of துட்டர்கள் rather than a confession, close to a moral code: the faults named are those the Kural also names (other men's wives, liquor, theft from the helpless, hoarding), with refusal of guru-service (குருசேவை கூடாத) among them. கோமாள நாயிற் கடைப்பிறப்பு: the punishment is birth as the lowest of dogs. மெய்த் திருப்புகழ் பெறு வயலூரா recalls Vayalur as the place of the Thiruppugazh itself. நாகேச நாமத் தகப்பன் is Siva of this shrine. The lines on ப்ராரத்த துக்கம் and புவி ஆதாரமாய்கைக்கு are hard to divide.

title: கூந்தலூர்
theme: A song at Koonthalur (கூந்தலூர்): the poet heaps abuse on himself as a fool bound to women and asks that, even with one flower or leaf, he may fall at Murugan's feet in love; the praise names Rama, the peacock that lifts devotees, and Siva who calls Murugan guru.
source_issues: Song 874: one corrupt character in கூந்தலு¡ருறை (line 24), read as கூந்தலூருறை, 'dwelling at Koonthalur'.

tamil: உ யர்கதி பெறஅரு ளோங்கு மாமயி ...... லுறைவோனே
reading: The poet calls himself a fool who has gone many ways on earth, a madman, a proud lump of a body without patience, an empty one fallen from greatness, a vagabond who left the path of penance, a sinner joined to scented-haired, moon-faced, net-eyed women, and asks for grace that, if not with many flowers then with one flower or one leaf, he may fall with love and worship Murugan's feet. The praise names Vishnu who with one arrow cut Ravana's ten heads and twenty arms as uncle, Murugan who dwells on the great peacock and gives the high state to devotees, poets, gods, sages and children, who raged until the whole clan of Suras who would not bow fell to dust, and whom Siva, holding the poison in his throat, calls guru, at Koonthalur.
nuance: வெகுமலர் அது கொடு வேண்டியாகிலும் ஒரு மலர் இலை கொடும்: the plea scales worship down to one flower or leaf offered with love, so the measure is love, not the offering. குருபரன் என வரு: Siva himself names Murugan guru. One word in the self-abuse (மீகுகேள்வி) is unclear.

title: திருச்சத்திமுத்தம்
theme: A song at Thiruchaththimuththam (திருச்சத்திமுத்தம்): the poet describes women's breasts and wandering eyes and asks to stop suffering in their grip; the praise names Murugan who taught the meaning of the Veda to Siva and confounds the fools who live by lies and plunder of the simple.

reading: The poet describes women's breasts, compared to elephant tusks, golden pots and lotus buds and smeared with fragrant paste, and their kayal-fish eyes leaping to the earrings and their hard words, and asks whether he will not cease to suffer, pressed in the grip of these women. The praise names Murugan who told the meaning of the rare Veda to three-eyed Siva and drove the peacock round the world in an instant, the hero who confounds and cuts down the fools who tell lies, heap up wealth and frighten simple people to make their living, the nephew of Vishnu who sleeps on the serpent and came swiftly on Garuda, and the lord who cut the one in the sea with his shakti, at Thiruchaththimuththam.
nuance: அபகடம் உரைத்து அத்தம் மெத்தப் படைத்து உலகில் எளியரை மருட்டி ... அசடர்: an unusual target for Murugan's wrath, not demons but men who grow rich by deceiving the simple. அடலை புனை முக்கண் பரற்குப் பொருள் சொல் அருமறை: the teaching of Siva, here of the Veda's meaning without naming Om. The second half of the plea (கணியினில் அகப்பட்டு) is hard to divide.

title: திருவலஞ்சுழி
theme: A song at Thiruvalanjuzhi (திருவலஞ்சுழி): a long catalogue of questions about women's eyes, spear, lotus, Kama's arrow, fish, Death, deer, poison, ending in women who plunder like demons; the praise names Rama with Hanuman's army and the yogis and Saiva rites of the shrine.
source_issues: Song 876: corrupt characters in மா¡£ சாதிகள் (line 13), read as மாரீசாதிகள், 'Maricha and the rest'.

reading: The poet asks what the women's eyes are: spears striking the makara earrings, red lotus or lily, Murugan's own vel, Kama's arrows, swords, kayal and kendai fish, Death the killer, deer, humming bees, the bird that drinks moonlight, the old poison Siva ate, split tender mango, the sea that ends the world; and asks whether kinship is possible with women who roam with such eyes and plunder openly, like demons who know the way. The praise names Rama, who with Hanuman and the monkey armies destroyed Maricha and the countless demons of the ten-faced one, as uncle, and the lord at Thiruvalanjuzhi among gods, Bhagiratha and others, the Saiva rites of the Isana mantras, the silent ones of Siva and yogis who know the mantras.
nuance: The figure is the doubting comparison (ஐய உவமம்): each guess names one power of the look, to wound, to charm, to kill. மறலி என்பவனோ ... மானோ puts Death and the deer side by side as the Kural does. The list of Siva's worshippers in the praise (பிராசாதாதிகள், ஈசானாதிகள், மந்த்ரகலாப யோகிகள்) is partly obscure.

title: திருப்பழையாறை
theme: A song at Thiruppazhaiyarai (திருப்பழையாறை): the poet, a slave to women he serves for love, asks Murugan to scold him like a mother and speak one word of teaching so he gains the feet; the praise names the hero of the sea-battle and the son of Siva who is half Uma, at the golden temple of Pazhaiyarai.

reading: The poet describes women whose eyes run to the ears like spears and whose camphor-scented breasts are like lotus buds, and calls himself a rubbish-minded slave and sinner who, caught by them, took up their service and ran after them with love; he asks Murugan to be angry with him like a mother and speak one word of teaching, so that by that grace he gains the feet. The praise names the playful, generous hero who sent the vel at Sura in the sea, the younger brother of the elephant-faced one, the son of Siva who dances with Uma as his half and wears the Vedas as his loincloth, at the golden temple of Pazhaiyarai with its towers and walls like mirrors.
nuance: கோபித்துத் தாயென நீ ஒரு போதத்தைப் பேச: the plea asks for a mother's scolding and a single teaching (போதம்), grace that corrects. ஊழியமே பற்றி: the poet's service has gone to women instead of to the Lord. வேதப் பொற் கோவண ஆடையர் gives Siva the Vedas as his loincloth. A few words (கூளச் சித்தாளன், மூளன்) are uncertain.

title: திருச்சக்கிரப்பள்ளி
theme: A song at Thiruchakkarappalli (திருச்சக்கிரப்பள்ளி): hyperbole on the breasts of women who sell them, and a plea to be freed from attachment to their false union; the praise, in Sanskrit epithets, identifies Murugan with Sambandar, the king of Pugali, and the teacher of Agastya.

reading: The poet lists what the women's breasts do, outshine vessels, break golden pots, drive away the northern mountain, snap elephants' tusks, put bubbles to shame in a blink, rock lotuses in the field, send the paired birds into the sky, split tender coconuts, and asks when Murugan will grant that his mind's attachment to the false union and the hair of those who seal and sell those breasts will end. The praise, mostly in Sanskrit compounds, names Murugan the destroyer of the wicked who bears the shakti, master of the three Tamils, known by the name of the king of Pugali, the teacher who gave Agastya grammar in the south, the six-faced lord, who graced Parvati, she who grows the faiths, and rides the peacock at Seyppathi and dwells at Chakkarappalli, son of the three-eyed one.
nuance: முத்திரையிட்ட தனத்தை விற்பவர்: the breasts are sealed goods sold for money, which makes these courtesans. துட்கரக் கவிதைப் புகலிக் கரசு எனும் நாமம்: Murugan bears the name of the king of Pugali (Sirkazhi) of hard poems, that is Sambandar. சொல்லட்சண ... அகத்தியனுக்கருள் சொற்குரு: the teacher of grammar to Agastya. Some compounds in the praise are hard to divide.

title: திருக்குரங்காடுதுறை
theme: Three songs at Thirukkurangaduthurai (திருக்குரங்காடுதுறை), where monkeys play in the fields: a song only of Murugan's beauty and dance, a catalogue of courtesans who make ascetics falter, and the bent, staff-bound body in which the poet asks the feet even if he is born again.
structure_note: 879 is praise alone; 880 is a courtesan catalogue; 881 moves from women's glances to old age and rebirth.

reading: The poet asks whether he will tell of anything but the beauty of Murugan's crowned six faces, his earringed shoulders, the garlands and gems, the flaming vel, the red flower feet with anklets, and his dance each day to drum syllables. The praise names Rama, who sent the forest monkey into Ravana's grove to set fire and freed Sita, and who walked the great forest with bow and arrows, as the one to whom Murugan is dear, the hero whose vel ended the asuras' army, and the lord at Kurangaduthurai where cane mills hum in flowering groves.
nuance: The first half has no confession: it is a description of Murugan's form and dance (திமிந்தோதி திமித்திமி ... தினந்தோறு நடிப்பது), and the question புகல்வேனோ may mean 'shall I tell of it?' or 'shall I tell of anything else?'. The drum syllables are rhythm. கொடுந்தாரை வெயில் கயிலைத் தொடும் is obscure.

reading: The poet lists the women of scheming desire: singers, dancers who leap onto the stage, coaxers whose love falls short with anyone, who name a price of half a coin, with killing glances, nail-marked breasts and bitten lips, cheats who seek money every day, forms of sin who make ascetics falter, who melt men in pleasure, and asks whether he will give up the delusion of celebrating union with them. The praise names Murugan the bridegroom of the forest girl with dark scented hair, the great life of devotees like himself whom Indra and the gods remember, at Kurangaduthurai where the river's waves cast up the nine gems on the fields.
nuance: அரைப்பணம் கூறு விலையினர் and பொருட்டினம் தேடு கபடிகள் name the price and the greed. தவர் சோரப் புரித்திடும் பாவ சொருபிகள்: their power reaches even ascetics. நினைக்கும் என் போலும் அடியவர்: the poet counts himself among the devotees despite the confession.

reading: The poet speaks of women with pot-like breasts and garlands, caught in the net of their cool-faced glance, and then of the body bent and stooping, walking unsteadily, withered, never without its staff, sleeping and waking, being born and born again; even so, he asks, give the golden feet to wear on his chest. The praise names Vishnu who danced on the poisonous hoods, sleeps on the first serpent-bed, and broke his shackles and ran, the dark cloud, as uncle, and the lord of the shrine where peahens cry on the slopes, bees swarm, and monkeys leap in the fields.
nuance: பிறந்து பிறப்பேனும் ... பொற்பாதம் அருள்வாயே: the plea does not ask to end birth but for the feet even if he is born again. The move from the glance to the stooping body with its staff (கூனி, கோலும் அகலாதே) makes old age the sequel of desire. The Vishnu lines point to Krishna on Kaliya's hoods and his chains breaking at birth, but the reading of விலங்கை முறித்தோடி is mine.

title: காவ்ளுர்
theme: A song at Kavalur (காவளூர்): the poet describes lovemaking with women versed in Kama's arts and asks to escape the ruin of that delusion and reach Murugan; the praise tells Rama's war for Sita and the slaying of Vali.
source_issues: Heading of chapter 181 reads காவ்ளுர்; song 882 names the place காவளூர் (line 24).

tamil: ஆடை சோரநெ கிழ்த்தியி ரங்கவும் ...... உ றவாடி
reading: The poet describes deer-eyed women with milk-sweet speech and pearl-strung breasts, bangles crying as they make love, shame dropped and garments loosened, reciting the texts of Kama, and asks whether, escaping the ruin of that delusion, he will reach Murugan. The praise names Rama who, in anger at Janaki's captivity, destroyed Lanka, gave Sugriva the kingdom and Tara and felled Vali with an arrow, as uncle, the lover of the kura girl who kept watch on the platform in the hunters' millet field, and the lord at Kavalur of areca groves where the three Tamils are known.
nuance: வேளின் நூல்களைக் கற்ற விளம்பவும்: the women recite Kama's texts, love as a learned art. ஆகும் மோக விபத்து: the delusion is called a calamity. The headword is printed காவ்ளுர் and the last line reads காவளூர்.

title: தஞ்சை
theme: Three songs at Thanjai (தஞ்சை): a short plea not to wander in women's maya, a plea to end the illusion and be given the true substance that is everywhere, and a courtesan scene with a plea for knowledge; the praise names Murugan as Siva's teacher and the great towered city.
structure_note: 883 is a short song; 884 asks for the pervading truth; 885 is a courtesan catalogue.

reading: A short song: the poet asks whether he will wander in the maya of women with kohl-dark spear eyes, and whether grace will not come in visible form so that he may reach Murugan's feet. The praise names him the son of Hara who ate poison as nectar and of Uma, dwelling at Thanjai so that devotees who take refuge may live.
nuance: தஞ்சென ... தஞ்சையில்: a pun on the place name and தஞ்சம், refuge. விம்பமதாய் அருள் may mean grace taking an image or form; the sense is not certain.

reading: The poet confesses that in the wish to sink in the sea of pleasure with women whose eyes are like kendai fish hiding in the sea, he left off thinking of Murugan, and asks that, to end this conjuror's illusion, Murugan call him kindly 'come here' and give the true substance that is everywhere. The praise names Valli with her twig-waist and cloud-dark hair, Murugan the teacher of Sambhu whose fire-eye killed Kama, and the lord of great Thanjai with its towering gopuram and golden mansions.
nuance: இந்த்ரசால இப்ப்ரமை: the world of desire is a magic show (indrajala) and a delusion. எங்குமான மெய்ப்பொருள் தாராய்: the remedy is the pervading reality, given by the call 'come here' (எங்கு வா). சம்பராரியைக் கொன்ற தீவிழிச் சம்பு போதகக் குருநாதா: Murugan as guru to Siva who burned Kama.

மஞ்ச ளாலழ காக மேனி யிற்றி மிர்ந்து

மங்கி யேகிடு மாறு ஞான வித்தை தந்து
வண்டு லாவிய நீப மாலை சற்றி லங்க ...... வருவாயே

னென்று வாழ்மணி மார்பன் வீர விக்ர மன்றன் ...... மருகோனே
எண்டி சாமுக வேலை ஞால முற்று மண்டு
கந்த தாருக சேனை நீறு பட்டொ துங்க
வென்று பேரொளி சேர்ப்ர காசம் விட்டி லங்கு ...... கதிர்வேலா
சந்த்ர சேகரி நாக பூஷ ணத்தி யண்ட
முண்ட நாரணி யால போஜ னத்தி யம்பை
தந்த பூரண ஞான வேள்கு றத்தி துஞ்சு ...... மணிமார்பா
சண்ட நீலக லாப வாசி யிற்றி கழ்ந்து
கஞ்சன் வாசவன் மேவி வாழ்ப திக்கு யர்ந்த
தஞ்சை மாநகர் ராஜ கோபு ரத்த மர்ந்த ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet describes courtesans who comb their hair, smear turmeric, wear pearls, draw in everyone they see on the street, bare their breasts, throw the spears of their eyes, name a price and take those who come to bed, and asks that the evil deeds and births of pleasure with them fade away, that Murugan give the knowledge of jnana and come with his kadamba garland. The praise names Vishnu who brought Indra's tree to earth, the conch-bearer Kesava, as uncle, the vel that dusted Taraka's armies in the eight directions, Parvati, moon-crowned, serpent-adorned, who swallowed the poison, as the mother who gave Murugan, and the lord on the peacock at the royal gopuram of great Thanjai.
nuance: விலைகூறி: the price is named. அநுபோக தீவினைப் பவங்கள்: the pleasures are counted as evil deeds that make births, and the cure asked is ஞான வித்தை. இந்த்ர தாருவை ஞாலமீதினிற் கொணர்ந்த is Krishna bringing the parijata tree. தஞ்சைமாநகர் ராஜகோபுரம்: the great gopuram of Thanjavur.

title: சப்தஸ்தானம்
theme: A song for the seven shrines (சப்தஸ்தானம்) around Thiruvaiyaru: the poet asks not to approach scheming courtesans and to be given the joy of singing again the Thiruppugazh he sang at Arunai; the praise names the seven shrines one by one.
source_issues: Song 886: one corrupt character in நி¨த்துமுன் (line 10), read as நினைத்துமுன், 'thinking (on the feet)'.

reading: The poet describes courtesans with deceit in their hearts, spear eyes and sweet words, who call everyone on the street, spread their desire for money and read every trick of maya, and asks not to approach them but, thinking on the lotus feet, to sing in calm joy the Thiruppugazh he sang before at Arunai. The praise names Murugan the bridegroom of Valli, with whom he stayed on her platform and wandered every forest, at whose thought the asuras' houses fell to dust and the gods' land rained gold, and the lord of the seven shrines of Thiruvaiyaru: Pazhanam, Chotruthurai, Vedikudi, Kandiyur where Brahma's head fell, Poonthuruthi, Neyththanam and Thiruvaiyaru itself.
nuance: முன் அருணை நாடதில் ஓது திருப்புகழ்: the poet refers to his own earlier songs at Tiruvannamalai, where the book's tradition places the start of the Thiruppugazh. The seven shrines are named by allusion: அயிலு சோறு for Chotruthurai, மறை தேடிய ... குடி for Vedikudi, விதி ஆதிச் சிரமும் மாநிலம் வீழ்தரு for Kandiyur, நெய்ப்பதி for Neyththanam. The asura line (உழவர் சாகரமோடி ஒளித்திட) is obscure.

title: திருவையாறு
theme: A song at Thiruvaiyaru (திருவையாறு): the poet asks whether the day will come when, leaving the sea of illusion where he praises women part by part, he joins the praise that jnanis sing and reaches the supreme release; the praise names Vishnu's avatars and Siva who is half woman and without caste.

tamil: துணைகொள் மாமலை யோமுலை தானென ...... உ ரையாடிப்
reading: The poet gives the lover's questions, is her hair a raining cloud or darkness, are her eyes swords or does, is her speech the gods' nectar or the cuckoo, her gait a swan's or a she-elephant's, her breasts a mountain, and confesses that he talks thus to bright-browed women, saying 'rule me in love, I am without fault', and suffers; he asks whether one day, not perishing in that sea of illusion, he will reach the long praise that jnanis sing, which is the supreme release. The praise names Vishnu the cowherd on the serpent-bed, the Man-Lion who tore Hiranya's chest and Rama who felled Ravana's ten heads with one arrow, as uncle, and Murugan the son of Siva who burned the three cities, has a woman as his half and has no caste, the vel that turned the peak to ash, at Thiruvaiyaru.
nuance: ஞானிகள் பரவு நீள்புகழே அது ஆம் மிகு பரம வீடு: the praise itself is equated with release. சாதியிலாதவர்: Siva is named as one without caste or birth. The doubting comparisons of the first half are the stock of akam praise of a woman.

title: திருப்பூந்துருத்தி
theme: A song at Thiruppoonthuruthi (திருப்பூந்துருத்தி): after a frank picture of lovemaking, the poet asks that the cravings of food, union and maya end and that he be given the conduct of true knowledge; the praise is a run of epithets for Murugan as commander, teacher and healer of devotees.
source_issues: Song 888: corrupt characters in க்¡£டா (line 9), read as க்ரீடா, 'play', and in ¡£பகி ரண்ட்ருபா (line 21), which I cannot restore with confidence (perhaps ஸ்ரீ ... ரூபா).

tamil: வேண்டு சர்க்கரை பால்தே னேரிதழ் ...... உ ண்டுதோயா
reading: The poet describes the embrace, breasts like tender coconuts, lips sweet as sugar, milk and honey, garments parted, eyes striking the earrings, love-cries and Kama's many kinds of play, and asks that, with the cravings of food, union and maya ended, Murugan give him the conduct of true knowledge that makes him easy to reach. The praise calls Murugan commander of the gods' army, Rudra's son, rider of the peacock, praised by sages and Indra, the calm wise teacher wearing the kadamba garland, lord of Seyppathi, the hero with a mountain-like form, who grants grace so that his devotees' diseases leave them, at Poonthuruthi.
nuance: ஊண் புணர்ச்சியுமாயா வாதனை: hunger, union and maya are named together as the vasanas (traces) to end. மெய்ஞ்ஞான ஆசாரம்: knowledge is asked as a conduct, not only a vision. போந்த பத்தர் பொலா நோய் போயிட: Murugan as healer. Several epithets in the praise are corrupt or obscure (சாங்கிபர், சீநாதீசுரர், ¡£பகிரண்ட்ருபா).

title: திருநெய்த்தானம்
theme: A song at Thiruneyththanam (திருநெய்த்தானம்): after a picture of lovemaking, the poet vows that even sleeping in women's embrace he will not forget Murugan's feet; the praise is a battle scene in drum syllables and Siva's dance.

reading: The poet describes the lovemaking, cloud-dark hair loosening, garlands slipping, the lotus face sweating, the eyes striking the earrings, coral lips drunk, the musk-scented breasts pressed, and says that even sleeping so in embrace he will not forget Murugan's feet. The praise shows the battle in drum syllables, ghouls rising, Bhairavas and demons dancing with their hunger ended by the vel, names Murugan the son of the Lord who dances to the drum wearing serpents, who embraced the kura girl of the mountain, at Thiruneyththanam, lord of the gods.
nuance: துயில்கினும் உனதடி மறவேனே: the song does not renounce the embrace but vows remembrance in the middle of it, an unusual turn for the book. The drum syllables (குகுகுக் கூகுக், செகசெச்) are rhythm.

title: திருப்பழுவூர்
theme: A song at Thiruppazhuvur (திருப்பழுவூர்): a catalogue of prostitutes with foul mouths, love-drugs in rice and dancing seductions, and the question whether kinship with them can be; the praise tells Krishna's part in the Bharata war.

reading: The poet lists the price-women who speak crooked troubling words, whose mouths stink, who size up men, kindle their desire, and serve rice mixed with a drug, who bathe in unguents, dance with anklets, and whirl men with seductive eyes and swaying waists, and asks whether kinship with such prostitutes can be. The praise names Krishna, who darkened the sun with his discus and finished the Bharata war, killing brothers, uncles, elders and sons of the Kauravas until foxes and ghouls fed on the field, praised by the devotees and the Pandavas, as uncle, and Murugan with his peacock that shakes mountain and sea, at Pazhuvur.
nuance: இடும் மருந்தொடு சோற்றையே இடு விலைமாதர்: the women feed men rice laced with a drug, a charge of love-medicine (வசிய மருந்து) beyond the usual deceit. திகிரி கொண்டு இருளாக்கி: Krishna hiding the sun with his discus, from the Mahabharata war. The Pandava lines (அரி அருளும் மைந்தர்கள்) are my reading.

title: பெரும்புலியூர்
theme: A song at Perumpuliyur (பெரும்புலியூர்): the poet, sunk in women's beds, asks Murugan to pity him and give his two feet; the praise names him son of Chidambaram and of Sivakami.

reading: The poet describes women with anklets and jingling ornaments, breasts heaving, earrings swinging, peacock-like and laughing, and asks Murugan, who sees him sunk with them on the bed, to pity him a little and give his two feet. The praise names Murugan the son of Chidambaram on the peacock with his kadamba garland, the one at whose anger the asuras were uprooted and vultures fed on heaped corpses, the son of Sivakami, the radiant Abhirami, who went to the millet field and joined the kura girl, at Perumpuliyur.
nuance: சிதம்பரகுமார and சிவகாமி: the praise names Murugan through Chidambaram's dancer and his consort, near Perumpuliyur (புலியூர் is also Chidambaram's old name). பெதும்பை எழு கோலம் may refer to the seven stages of a woman's life.

title: நெடுங்களம்
theme: A song at Nedungalam (நெடுங்களம்): the poet asks that the senses, past deeds and diseases burn like cotton, that he live among the old devotees, and that Murugan come on the peacock and give his feet; the praise describes Murugan's own lovemaking with his consort.

reading: The poet asks that the five senses, the two old deeds and diseases burn to ash like cotton, that he live among the old servants of the Lord, and that Murugan, with the elephant-faced one, come on the peacock with anklets sounding bindu and nada, kill his care and give the full feet today. The praise describes the union of Murugan with his golden consort, waist and eyes whirling, garments slipping, the moon-brow and dark hair tumbling, and names him the lord of Nedungalam, where devotees gather and Brahma and the gods praise him.
nuance: The frank love scene here belongs to the god, not to the poet's confession: மங்கை மணமுண்ட பாலா. பழைய தொண்டர்களுடன் பழகி asks for the company of the old devotees. சிலம்பு கழல் விந்து நாதம்: the anklets sound as bindu and nada. பஞ்சவர் வியன் பதியுடன் குலாவ is obscure; it may name the five (the senses, or Siva's five faces).

title: குறட்டி
theme: Two songs at Kurattai (குறட்டி): the poet asks not to sink in the mud of women's bodies with a mind bound to maya, and not to wander in a ruined body of diseases, filth and carrion; the praise names Siva the beggar of alms and a long litany of Parvati.
structure_note: 893 is a courtesan song; 894 catalogues the body's diseases.
source_issues: Song 893: corrupt characters in உப்ப ¡£கை (line 15), read as உப்பரிகை, 'balcony'.

tamil: கூரிய கடைக்க ணாலு மேருநி கரொப்ப தான
கோபவ தரத்தி னாலு மேவிடு விதத்து ளால
சீரிய வளைக்கை யாலு மேகலை நெகிழ்ச்சி யேசெய்
சேறுத னினித்த மூழ்கி நாளவ மிறைத்து மாயை
சாடுமு வணப்ப தாகை நீடுமு கிலொத்த மேனி
வாரண முரித்து மாதர் மேகலை வளைக்கை நாண
reading: The poet lists the sharp eye-corners, mountain breasts, red lips, belly, speech, bangled hands and loosened girdles of the price-women, and asks whether he will wander with a mind joined to maya, sinking daily in their mud and wasting his days. The praise names Vishnu of the Garuda banner who destroyed Ravana's army, as uncle, and Murugan the son of the Lord who flayed the elephant and took alms while women's girdles and bangles slipped in shame, at Kurattai with its walls and balconies.
nuance: சேறு தனில் நித்தம் மூழ்கி நாள் அவம் இறைத்து: the women are mud and the days are poured away. மாதர் மேகலை வளைக்கை நாண மாபலி முதற்கொள் நாதன் appears to name Siva as the beggar (Bhikshatana) whose beauty made the sages' wives lose their girdles and bangles.

tamil: நீரிழிவு குட்ட மீளை வாதமொடு பித்த மூல
நேருறு புழுக்கள் கூடு நான்முக னெடுத்த வீடு
பாரிய நவத்து வார நாறுமு மலத்தி லாறு
பாறோடு கழுக்கள் கூகை தாமிவை புசிப்ப தான
நாரணி யறத்தி னாரி ஆறுச மயத்தி பூத
நாடக நடத்தி கோல நீலவ ருணத்தி வேத
வாரணி முலைச்சி ஞான பூரணி கலைச்சி நாக
மாடம தில்முத்து மேடை கோபுர மணத்த சோலை
reading: The poet lists the diseases, diabetes, leprosy, phlegm, wind, bile, piles, fever, and the worms of the house Brahma built of blood, brain, flesh, skin and pus, stinking through nine gates, a puppet of disease that foxes, dogs, ghouls, vultures and owls will eat, and asks whether he will wander in vain carrying this ruined body. The praise is a litany of Parvati as Narani, the woman of dharma, lady of the six faiths, Mahamayi, the dancer, the blue one, queen of the Vedas, Uma, Neeli, bearer of the trident, full of jnana, who gave birth to the hero on the peacock, at Kurattai of mansions, towers and groves.
nuance: நான்முகன் எடுத்த வீடு: the body is a house Brahma built, and the inventory runs from disease through its stuff to its scavengers. The praise is given almost wholly to the Mother (ஆறு சமயத்தி, ஞானபூரணி).

title: அத்திப்பட்டு
theme: A song at Aththippattu (அத்திப்பட்டு): the poet follows a death through the bier, the pyre and the mourners' return home, where Kama soon has them laughing again, and asks for the way to heaven and the golden feet; the praise names Parvati's penance at Kanchi and Vishnu as uncle.
source_issues: Song 895: one corrupt character in கக்ஷ¢யவர் (line 6), read as கக்ஷியவர், 'those of the party' (the mourners).

reading: The poet pictures death: sense gone, the life leaves, kin cry, drums beat, the body is set on a golden bier, laid on the pyre with rice from flower hands and cloth, the Vedas recited, and burned in crackling fire; the mourners bathe, go home and forget their grief, and wicked Kama with his flowers makes them laugh and weep again. Thinking of his servant, worn out in women's hands, the poet asks Murugan to tell him 'this is the way to heaven' and give the golden feet. The praise names Murugan the son of the mountain-king's daughter, the green peacock who did her hard penance at Kanchi, the nephew of Vishnu who shot Ravana's ten heads and twenty arms, the one on the emerald peacock who dried the sea and resettled the gods, at Aththippattu of fields where kayal fish leap.
nuance: The funeral is told rite by rite (அரிசி இட்டு, கலை, மறைகள், புனல் முழுகி மனை புக்கு), and the turn is that the mourners' grief ends at the bath and Kama takes them again. கச்சியினில் அரிய தவம்: Parvati's penance at Kanchi. The line on the mourners (உறவுநிலை சுட்டுச் சுட்டி) is hard to divide.

title: அத்திக்கரை
theme: A song at Aththikkarai (அத்திக்கரை): the poet asks to leave the vanity of adornment and mean company, remove the three faults, learn faultlessly, serve the freed who know themselves, and enter the shoreless sea of release; the praise names the shakti that pierced the Suras and Valli rescued from the elephant.

reading: The poet asks not to wander on earth washing and decking the skin with gold and scent, proud, leaving purity and doing what the elders' words forbid among mean kin, but to remove the three faults, learn many arts without error, and, by the knowledge gained in serving the freed ones who know themselves, see the Real and enter the shoreless sea of release. The praise names the one shakti that pierced the Suras who had made the eight directions and the gods serve them, so that Indra's grief ended and he regained his city, Murugan who called the frightened kura girl when the elephant came and embraced her, and the dear son of Siva with water and the crescent in his hair, at Aththikkarai.
nuance: முக்குற்றம் அகற்றி: the three faults are traditionally desire, anger and delusion. தனையுணர் முத்தர்க்கு அடிமைப்பட்டு இலகிய அறிவாலே: knowledge comes through service to the freed, not by study alone. கரையகல் முத்திப்புணரி: release as a sea without a shore. கரி வரும் அத்தத்தில் அழைத்து: the elephant that frightened Valli into Murugan's arms.

title: கந்தனூர்
theme: A song at Kandanur (கந்தனூர்): after births in every form, the poet cries 'give me the state of jnana now' and asks whether Murugan will not come as father and mother run to embrace a leaping child; the praise names the vel against the fire-eyed demons and Siva with the Mother as his half.

reading: The poet speaks of the forms divided from bindu, moving and unmoving lives in every direction, through which he has come and wandered, and of the body that falls away; when he, lower than a dog, cries in pain 'come and give me the state of jnana this instant', he asks whether Murugan will not think of him as a father and mother melt and embrace the child who leaps toward them. The praise names the vel that destroyed the fire-eyed ones who come roaring like thunder in the dark, so the gods returned to Indra's world, and Murugan the son of Siva with the moon in his hair, who helps the poet's life, with the Mother in his half who stands everywhere, at Kandanur.
nuance: மைந்தர் தாவிப் புகழ தந்தை தாய் உற்றுருகி வந்து சேயைத் தழுவல்: grace pictured as parents running to the child who leaps toward them, a tender image rare in the book. விந்து பேதித்த வடிவங்கள்: births as forms differentiated from bindu. The first quatrain's syntax (மிஞ்ச நீ விட்ட வடிவங்களாலே) is uncertain, and the fire-eyed ones may be asuras or Death's servants.

title: வாலிகொண்டபுரம்
theme: A song at Valikondapuram (வாலிகொண்டபுரம்): the poet scorns those who carry a carrion body yet swagger in wealth, with chowries, horns and palanquins, and asks that this desire burn and he be given love as a servant of the feet; the praise names Siva's dance and Murugan's own dance of victory.
source_issues: Song 898: corrupt characters in §ர்¡லெ (line 4), which I cannot restore, and in லு¡த (line 9), read as லூத, 'blowing' (horns and flutes).

reading: The poet describes those who carry a body that flies, ants, foxes, dogs, ghouls, vultures and crows will eat, yet call it fitting and speak arrogantly like a rutting elephant, boasting of their wealth, arms and minds, wearing cool garlands among dancing women, white chowries, horns and flutes, riding in palanquins to the end; he asks that the desire for that great life burn away, that desire for Murugan grow, and that, seeing the service of Siva, he be given love as a servant of the feet. The praise names Murugan who burned the Suras of the dark mountain of deceit, while Siva dances in the hall with Brahma, Indra and the gods worshipping, who danced in victory as the vidyadhara women rejoiced, and who came to guard the millet with Valli, at Valikondapuram.
nuance: The scavenger list opens the song, so the pomp that follows (வெண்கவரி, கொம்பு குழல், தண்டிகை) is seen as carried by a corpse to be. உனது பாத தொண்டனென அன்பு தாராய்: the plea asks for love as service. Two corrupt words in line 4 (§ர்¡லெ) leave a phrase unread.

title: திருமாந்துறை
theme: A song at Thirumanthurai (திருமாந்துறை): the poet pictures old age, bent body, loose teeth, cough, bedridden years and fading sense, and asks Murugan to come on the peacock before life goes and give his planted feet; the praise names Valli's millet field and the mango-rich fields of the shrine.

reading: The poet pictures the body bent, the teeth loose, the mind faltering, years passing on the bed, a cough, a swollen aching belly and sense fading, and asks that before life goes Murugan come on the high peacock and give his firmly planted feet. The praise names Murugan the bridegroom of Valli in the sweet millet field with its vengai trees, who grants those who seek him states beyond what they hold, and the lord of the fertile land where ripe mangoes burst and flow into the paddy fields, at Manthurai where men and the king of the gods praise him.
nuance: The decline is told in a short run of verbs (வளைந்து, நெகிழ்ந்து, தடுமாறி, நொந்து, ஓய்ந்து, அழிந்து). ஆர்ந்துள கடன்கள் வாங்கவும் அறிந்து may mean knowing how to collect what is owed, the old man's mind still on debts; the reading is uncertain. மாங்கனி உடைந்து தேங்க: a play on the shrine's name, mango ford.

title: வயலூர்
theme: First songs at Vayalur (வயலூர், வயலி, 1 of 2), the shrine near Trichy on the Kaveri where the poet places his own call: courtesans who show, sell and swear, the catalogue of a woman's charms, and the body and kin renounced with 'enough, enough'; against them the poet asks for the teaching of pati, pasu and pasam, for jnana beyond sects and rites, and recalls the Lord who called him at Viralimalai and ruled him in a dream.
structure_note: Courtesan songs (901, 902, 903, 914) and songs of women's charms (905, 906, 909, 910, 913); doctrine (900 on pati-pasu-pasam, 907 against sects and the lower paths, 908 renouncing body and kin); and two songs of the poet's own story (911, 912), with a third (904) that asks 'who am I' in all he does. Two songs (901, 914) and 913's Sambandar praise recur in the next chapters.
