Song 976: corrupt character in று¡ர (line 3, for தூர); the line கதத்திற் காயம தாகும (line 13) seems a syllable short of the rhythm (perhaps காதத்திற்), and மத்முறு (line 9) is garbled.

reading: The poet names the courtesans who speak harm, dance for the coins thrown to them, lift a man up and then pull the ladder away, and the lustful men who sink with them, till wind diseases, colic and other ailments take the body and Yama, who never lets go of his noose, drags it to his town and a ruined hell; he asks Murugan to cut away this illusion and give his support. The praise sounds the battle in drum syllables, with ghosts gaping as Sura's armies die before the rider of the golden peacock, and sets Kutralam, thronged with faultless devotees, ascetics and siddhas, above Koodal, Siramalai, Kazhi, Karuvur and other shrines.
nuance: ஏறிட்டிட்டு ஏணியை வீழ்விடு முழுமாயர்: the women raise a man up and kick away the ladder, an image of the bargain's end. The song carries the courtesan's harm through to disease, Yama's noose and hell, one chain of consequence. The list of shrines in the praise ranks Kutralam above Madurai and the other famed centres.

reading: The poet asks to be given, as an honour, the life that is not learned in the Veda, not seen by understanding, has no distance in space, is hard for seekers of salvation to find, is not burned by fire or shaken by wind, the great light within fragrance, and far from those drunk with maya. The praise speaks obscurely of those who recite 'this is evil' yet never see the path, and names Murugan who, mad for the girl, took a hunter's form and came to live among the hunters, the lord of Kutralam among devotees, ascetics and siddhas.
nuance: The whole plea is a string of negations ending in -அது (கேள்வியிலாதது, காணவொணாதது, வேகாதது), the way the Upanishads speak of the Self as what fire does not burn nor wind dry; what is asked for is that state itself (வாழ்வை ... அருள்வாயே), not escape from women or death. The opening of the second half is hard to divide and the reading of it is a guess.

reading: The poet asks whether he must wander daily over breasts that bear nail-marks like palm leaves scored by poets of elaborate verse, captive to women whose eyes tear at their pearl ear-ornaments and fight like spears, and asks for grace to praise truly the golden lotus feet that the gods praise. The praise names Rama, who made the ten-headed king of demons give up his breath, and Siva, who cut off Brahma's extra head and broke the sun's teeth in anger, and ends at Kutralam where jackfruit, plantain and leaping fish fill the little river.
nuance: வித்தார கவித்திறத்தினர் பட்டோலை நிகர்த்து: the poet compares the scored breasts to a poet's written palm leaf, a craftsman's self-aware simile. பற்பாசன் மிகைச் சிரத்தை அறுத்து ஆதவனைச் சினத்துறு பல் போக உடைத்த: Siva cutting Brahma's fifth head and breaking the sun's teeth, the latter a detail of the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice.

title: ஆய்க்குடி
theme: One song at Aykudi (ஆய்க்குடி): seeing that the glory of conquering kings ends in a moment at the burning ground, the poet asks, like the devotees who left household life, to be done with the dance of birth; the praise tells of Siva kicking Death for the boy.
source_issues: Song 978: unflagged garble in வெருபக் (line 6), which seems to have lost a syllable.

reading: Seeing that the great life of kings whose swords put armies to flight goes in a moment to the burning ground, the poet asks whether he may not, like the devotees who left household life and rose, look on the flower feet, rest from his weariness, and end the dance of coming into the world in a karma-strung body. The praise tells of Siva leaping with his anklet to kick the fierce form of Death when its noose struck at a boy, names Indra and the gods bowing, and calls Murugan the guardian of Aykudi who imprisoned Brahma and shattered the demons and the mountain by the sea with his vel.
nuance: The plea draws its lesson from the fall of kings, not from courtesans: மாத்திரைப் போதில் இடுகாட்டினில் போம், gone in an instant to the cremation ground, and its model is the renunciant (இல்வாழ்க்கை விட்டு ஏறும் அடியவர்). The boy and the noose are the story of Markandeya; the kick is Siva's, not Murugan's. The plea's last lines (கோப்புடைத்தாகி அலமாப்பினில் ...) are hard to divide.

title: திருப்புத்தூர்
theme: Two songs at Thiruppuththur (திருப்புத்தூர்): the poet regrets the base work of making praise-songs on women's breasts for patrons and longs for chariyai and kiriyai; and the courtesans who demand the coins promised and drive men out; the praise dwells on Siva as Bhairava and as the archer of the triple city.
source_issues: Song 980: corrupt character in லு¡ர (line 23, for ஊர).

reading: The poet recalls women whose glances bewilder young men and whose breasts he likened to elephant tusks, pots, gem caskets, lotus buds and tender coconuts, and asks when he will cast off the base trade of making praise-songs, as a servant, to please each patron, and live doing chariyai and kiriyai. The praise is all of Siva: the one who kicked Death, Bhairava garlanded with gods' skulls and bones who dances against Kali, the rider on the back of the bull who is the butter-thief, leader of the ghost army, wearing moon, konrai and white erukku, and Murugan his son at Thiruppuththur among the fields.
nuance: புகழ்ச்சிப் பாடல் அடிமை அவரவர் ப்ரியப்பட்டு ஆள உரைசெய் இழிதொழில்: the confession is of the poet's craft, praise poetry made to please patrons, with its stock comparisons of women's breasts, which the song itself first rehearses. The remedy is ritual service (சரியை கிரியை). நவநீதத் திருட்டுப் பாணி இடபம் makes Krishna, the butter-thief, Siva's bull, a Saiva claim of precedence.

reading: The poet describes the courtesans who mock with their eyes, show a house, slip their cloaks and display their breasts, then harass the men who come at the agreed hour, demand the coins named, and drive them out midway when the money is not in hand; he asks whether he will not end the evil of a mind sick with love for these cheats on their golden beds. The praise names Siva of the poison throat, the skull-bearer who danced for Parvati, the archer whose arrow was the earth-swallower, who bears the Ganga in his hair and is praised by ghost armies, and Murugan who came to teach him meaning, at Thiruppuththur of holy waters.
nuance: காசு கேட்டது கைப்பற்றா இடை காதி ஓட்டி: the money is the point, so this is the trade, not desire alone. தாத்திரி பட்சித்தா என உமிழ் வாளி: the arrow that 'ate the earth' is Vishnu, who became the arrow when Siva burned the triple city. சேதனார்த்த ப்ரசித்திக்கே வரு முருகோனே: Murugan teaching Siva, without naming Om.

title: திருவாடனை
theme: One song at Thiruvadanai (திருவாடனை): the diseased body dies, is wailed over, carried on a bier and burned to ash before it stinks, and the poet asks not to seek such a birth again; the praise names Siva who drank the poison, before whom Murugan taught the Agama of knowledge.
source_issues: Song 981: corrupt character in லு¡தாரி (line 2, probably லூதாரி or ஊதாரி; the sense is unclear).

reading: The poet follows the flesh-filled, sickly body to its end: when life goes the townsfolk gather and wail until they tire, lay it on a bier, carry it off before it stinks, and set it in the fire without shame until it is ash; he asks for grace so that he will not seek this birth again. The praise names Vishnu who dances on the serpent's hood, Brahma on the flower, the gods and the eight mountains, saved when Siva ate the halahala as nectar, and Murugan who, before that Siva, gave the Jnana Agama with right conduct and devotion, at Adanai.
nuance: நாணாமல் வைத்துவிட: the kin burn the body 'without shame', with no more regard than for refuse. The remedy is not the body's improvement but an end of birth (இப்பிறவி நாடாது). ஆசார பத்தியுடன் ஞானாகமத்தை அருள் makes Murugan the teacher of the Agama to Siva, the Om story in another dress.

title: உத்தரகோசமங்கை
theme: One song at Uttarakosamangai (உத்தரகோசமங்கை): bowing first to Ganapati of the many sweets, the poet asks to sing Murugan's praise and so gain Siva's state, the vast space of knowledge and the nectar of refuge; the praise is a battle scene.

reading: The poet hails Murugan as younger brother of the elephant god of wish-granting knowledge, lord of the bhuta host, who ate sugarcane, jaggery, sugar, milk, honey, tender coconut, the three fruits and lentils into his belly, and asks whether, bowing at the golden feet and naming the peacock and the jingling anklets with melting heart, he will sing that golden praise and gain Siva's state, the great open space of knowledge, and the nectar of refuge. The praise is a battle scene in drum syllables, horses and elephants heaped up, demons' corpses covering the directions and blood like red cloud, ending with the gods regaining their city and Valli, the hunter girl of inner meaning and knowledge, at Uttarakosamangai.
nuance: The opening is a full offering-list to Ganapati, a rare frame, and Murugan is approached as his brother (தந்திக்கு இளையாய்). The goal is laid out in three steps: சிவபதம், ஞானப் பெருவெளி, and அமுது. உட்பொருள் ஞானக் குறமகள் gives Valli an allegorical title, the hunter girl who is the inner meaning of knowledge.

title: இராமேசுரம்
theme: Two songs at Rameswaram (இராமேசுரம்): a whole life from youth's trade and pleasures among price-women to old age with a stick and a list of diseases, and the endless sweetness of unions that hides the Lord's feet; the praise tells of Brahma beaten for not knowing Om and of Rama's deeds.
source_issues: Song 984: corrupt character in லு¡டே (line 4, for ஊடே).

reading: The poet runs through a life: youth, beauty, play, trade, a worthless life thought to last a hundred years, building mansions and seeking wealth, perfumes and flowers, and whirling for some days in desire for price-women; then wrinkled skin, grey hair, blindness, faltering legs, deafness, a stick, and colic, itch, phlegm, wind, diabetes, anaemia, scrofula, fever and cough, until the body stinks like filth, and he asks whether he must perish so. The praise tells how Murugan struck the four-faced Brahma who could not explain the ground of Om, beating his four heads, names him son of the goddess and bridegroom of the hunter girl of knowledge, and lists Rama's deeds against Tataka, Subahu, the seven trees, Vali, Viradha, the sea and Ravana before ending at Rameswaram where the Vedas are chanted.
nuance: The song is a life in two quatrains, built on chains of -ஆகி and -மாறி (ஆகி ... ஆகி, then மாறி ... மாறி), so that each stage becomes the next and each faculty changes away. ஓம் என அதாரம் உரையாத பிரமாவை விழ மோதி பொருள் ஓதுக என: the Om myth is explicit. பசு பாச பதி சூழ் கதிகள் மாறி may mean that even the soul's paths among bondage and the Lord fail in old age.

reading: Not knowing how to bow at the lotus feet the gods praise, the poet tells of embracing women within the net of their eyes on soft beds, asking 'is it honey, is it cane syrup, what equals it?', and asks whether he will not end the sorrow of countless unions and endless delusion. The praise names the anklets that went against Sura, the fierce peacock, Valli's bridegroom, the great one who told Siva the meaning of Veda and Agama without shyness, and Vishnu's nephew at Rameswaram.
nuance: The poet's question, தேனோ கருப்பில் எழு பாகோ இதற்கிணைகள் ஏதோ, is the lover's own praise of pleasure quoted against himself. ஞானபரற்கு இனிய வேதாகமப் பொருளை நாணாது உரைக்கும் பெரியோனே: the child teaching the father 'without shame', Murugan as guru to Siva.

title: இந்தம்பலம்
theme: One song at Inthampalam (இந்தம்பலம்): a yogic hymn asking for the Sivayoga of nectar in the sky's sushumna, the Absolute of the letters and of light, and for youth and grace at the feet; the praise is a battle in drum syllables.

reading: The poet describes a reality no one can know: the stainless lotus form, the sounding conch and Veda, the supreme space shining everywhere, the fifty-one letters from which the worlds, rivers and cosmic eggs begin, the red light everywhere, beginning and middle, the lotus and turiya where moon and sun spread their rays, and the Sivayoga of nectar enjoyed by the five in the sushumna of the sky; he asks that, knowing it with compassion and calling 'son of Gauri, Kumara, Kumaraguru', he be given youth and grace at the feet. The praise is a battle sounded in drum syllables, the vel sent so that gods, Hari, Brahma and the sages survive, and Murugan embracing Valli, daughter of Hari, at Inthampalam.
nuance: The vocabulary is that of Tirumular's yoga: ககன சுழிமுனை (the sushumna in the sky of the head), துரியம், அமுத சிவயோகம், and ஐம்பந்தொரு அக்ஷரம் (the fifty-one letters). அரியின் மகள் makes Valli the daughter of Vishnu, a story the text names only in these two words. Much of the first half is a list whose syntax is uncertain.

title: எழுகரைநாடு
theme: One song for the lord of Ezhukarai Nadu (எழுகரைநாடு): the poet asks to weep, sing the six-syllable names and become a servant in love night and day, and be given the stainless meaning.

reading: The poet asks that, gazing without guile, melting and praising, eyes full of tears and love growing ever greater night and day with no other distraction, singing 'Kumara, Muruga, six-lettered one, Saravana, who drank the milk of the Krittikas' with faltering speech, worshipping and weeping again and again, he become Murugan's servant and be given the wholly stainless meaning. The praise names Murugan who showed the supreme path, the son of Parvati and of Pasupati who fought Kama with his eye, the vel that set the sea afire and the seven hills roaring, and the lord who settled the gods in their land and rules the people of Ezhukarai Nadu.
nuance: The plea asks for the signs of bhakti themselves, tears, melting, faltering speech (மொழி குழறா), weeping (அழுதழுது), rather than for release from women or death, and only then for the meaning (மலாப் பொருள்). ஷடாக்ஷர names the six-syllable mantra of Murugan.

title: ஒடுக்கத்துச் செறிவாய்
theme: One song at Odukkaththu Cherivay (ஒடுக்கத்துச் செறிவாய்): the courtesans' arts, love potions, smiles with stained teeth, the gold assayed in their hands and the quarrel that sends a man away; the praise names Vishnu at length and Murugan who came as a merchant to esteem Tamil.

tamil: உ றிக்குட் கைத்தல நீட்டு மச்சுதன் ...... மருகோனே
reading: The poet describes courtesans versed in deceitful talk and the arts of Kama, who feed men herbal potions, melt and cheat hard-hearted fools, speak base words, hug a man's neck, laugh showing stained teeth, take the wealth from his hand and assay its gold, count the hours and pick a quarrel to drive him off, and asks whether he will not rid himself of the ruined mind that enters their arts. The praise names Murugan who crushed the demons and wedded the hunter girl, Vishnu who lies on the serpent in the sea and stretched his hand into the butter-pot, and Murugan as the one who came as a merchant to honour Tamil, at Odukkaththu Cherivay.
nuance: மருத்துப் பச்சிலை தீற்று: the women dose their men with herbal love-potions, a rarer charge than flattery. கற்புகர் மாற்று உரைப்பது: they test the touchstone value of the gold they take, the bargain made exact. உரைக்கச் செட்டியனாய்ப் பன் முத்தமிழ் மதித்திட்டு: Murugan coming as a merchant to esteem Tamil points to a local story the text does not tell, and the lines on the Tamil-learned one (தமிழ் தேர்த்த வித்தகர்) are hard to divide.

title: காமத்தூர்
theme: One song at Kamaththur (காமத்தூர்): a short love-lament for a girl scorched by Kama's arrows and the moon on her flower-bed, asking Murugan to come and embrace her.

reading: Speaking for a girl in love, the singer asks that she not be scorched on her bed of flowers by Kama's honeyed arrows and by the crescent moon that burns like poison, and that Murugan come wearing his garland to fill her with joy. The praise names the vel that sent Sura running, the rooster banner that crows to call the dawn, and Murugan the bridegroom of the girl whose speech is like syrup, the lord of Kamaththur.
nuance: The song is in short tight syllables (ஆகத் தேதப் பாமற் சேரிக் ...) and much of it is hard to divide; the reading of the plea as an akam lament for a girl, like 974, rests on the moon, Kama's arrows and the burning flower-bed. ஆலப் பாலைப் போல: the moon is like the halahala poison, though white as milk.

title: முள்வாய்
theme: One song at Mulvai (முள்வாய்): before the quarrelling kin and Death who hides in the sky can take his life, the poet asks Murugan to enter his brief life with anklets, sacred thread and kadamba.

tamil: மின்னார் பயந்த மைந்தர் தன்னா டினங்கு விந்து
விண்மேல் நமன்க ரந்து மண்மே லுடம்பொ ருங்க
பொன்னார் சதங்கை தண்டை முந்நூல் கடம்ப ணிந்து
பொல்லே னிறைஞ்சி ரந்த சொன்னீ தெரிந்த ழுங்கு
பன்னா ளிறைஞ்சு மன்பர் பொன்னா டுறங்கை தந்து
பன்னூல் முழங்க லென்று விண்ணோர் மயங்க நின்று
முன்னாய் மதன்க ரும்பு வின்னேர் தடந்தெ ரிந்து
மொய்வார் நிமிர்ந்த கொங்கை மெய்ம்மாதர் வந்தி றைஞ்சு
reading: The poet asks that before his life goes, while the sons born of women quarrel among their own and speak against each other, Death hides in the sky, and the body wastes on earth knowing its day has come, Murugan, wearing golden anklets, thandai, the sacred thread and kadamba, enter his brief life as honey dwells in unfeigning hearts. The praise names Vishnu, the cloud who gives the heavenly world to devotees and lies on the serpent, and ends at Mulvai, where women whose bodies are bent like Kama's cane bow come to worship.
nuance: The plea sets the quarrel of heirs beside the approach of Death (விண்மேல் நமன் கரந்து), the family already dividing what the dying man leaves. பொய்யார் மனங்கள் தங்கும் மதுபோல: Murugan is asked to enter as he stays in true hearts. The last quatrain and the lines on Vishnu are hard to divide.

title: வாகைமாநகர்
theme: One song at Vagaimanagar (வாகைமாநகர்): the poet's infatuation with women's speech, eyes, breasts and gait, set against Murugan's own love for the hunter girl, whose hair he combed and whose feet he held.
source_issues: Song 990: three corrupt characters, in லு¡றல் (line 7, for ஊறல்), லு¡ர (line 8, for ஊர) and லு¡றல் (line 14, for ஊறல்).

tamil: ஆலை யான மொழிக்கு மாளை யூடு கிழிக்கு
ஆசை மாத ரழைக்கு மோசை யான தொனிக்கு
ஓலை மேவு குழைக்கு மோடை யானை நடைக்கு
ஊறு பாவ வுறுப்பி லு¡றல் தேறு கரிப்பி
வேலை யாக வளைக்கை வேடர் பாவை தனக்கு
மேவு வேடை யளித்து நீடு கோல மளித்து
மாலை யோதி முடித்து மாது தாள்கள் பிடித்து
வாகு தோளி லணைத்து மாக மார்பொழி லுற்ற
reading: The poet lists the women's speech sweet as cane juice, eyes deadly as Death's poison, calling voices, heavy breasts, ear-ornaments, elephant gait and slender waist, and asks whether, in infatuation, he will wander in the bitterness and the moisture of the sinful body. The praise tells how Murugan gave the hunter girl surpassing love, took on the hunter's guise, then on the platform in the field combed her hair, held her feet, drank the nectar of her mouth and embraced her to end her longing, at Vagaimanagar of groves.
nuance: The two halves use the same words: the poet wanders in மயல் and in the ஊறல் of the body, while Murugan drinks the ஊறல் of Valli's mouth so that her மயல் ends. The god's love is told as tenderly and physically as the poet's sin, and the song leaves the contrast unstated.

title: விசுவை
theme: One song at Visuvai (விசுவை): a short plea not to fall into women's net with failing understanding, and to be given the feet with love.

reading: The poet asks not to fall into the net of women who part and deck their curling hair and come with their breasts swaying, losing his understanding and growing weak, and asks for the twin feet that the gods worship, given with love. The praise names the vel that struck the mountain, the hunter girl of sweet speech, Siva of the konrai and the bull as his father, and Visuvai amid fragrant sandal groves.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: The first of the general songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 1 of 21), named for no shrine: litanies of 'namo namah' to Murugan and to the goddess, the poet's long self-condemnations, pleas for the supreme truth beyond kingly pomp and beyond the quarrels of sects, Ganapati's offerings, the funeral drum, and yogic and doctrinal hymns.
structure_note: Litanies (992 to 994, 998, 1005), with 994 and 998 mostly naming the goddess; self-condemnations (993, 1003, 1006); songs against worldly pomp (995, 996, sharing a refrain) and against the sects (1004); pleas against women and death (997, 1001, 1002); and two songs that ask to sing and know the Lord (999, 1000).
source_issues: Song 992: four corrupt characters, in ஜ¨முத (line 15, for ஜீமூத), புண்டா£கா (line 18, for புண்டரீகா) and கி¡£டா (line 20, for கிரீடா).
Song 994: corrupt character in புண்டா£க (line 12, for புண்டரீக).
Song 995: corrupt characters in தீ¨க்ஷப ¡£¨க்ஷக (line 10, for தீக்ஷை பரீக்ஷை).

reading: The poet hails Murugan in a litany of 'namo namah': knowledge beyond the gunas, lord of nada, the partless, the fullness of the kalas, cousin of Kama, kadamba-footed, son of the three Tamils and life of the three worlds, and asks whether, without falling at the lotus feet with that praise, he must drown in the ocean of seven births and whirl in Kama's maya. The praise piles up names: son of Siva who dances with vetalas in the forest, son of the Ganga, master of the elephant-raised maid, lord of the peacock, Visakha, six-faced, sporting with the hunter Lakshmi, slayer of Sura, and Vinayaka's dear brother.
nuance: The plea is short and sits inside the litany: the 'namo namah' is itself what the poet fears he will fail to say (என்று பாத வாரிஜத்தில் விழாதே). பஞ்சபாண பூபன் மைத்துன: Murugan as cousin of Kama, since Kama is Vishnu's son and Vishnu is Murugan's uncle.

tamil: ஆத ரித்தருள் பாலா நமோநம ...... உ ந்தியாமை
reading: The poet condemns himself at length as one who never studied the three Tamils, useless, lustful, a demon of desire without the yoga of the indweller, fool of fools, a ruin who never sought the fruit of penance, a plotter of sin and killing, without justice, the greatest traitor among sinners, angry and greedy, a ruined jester living in the tangle of bonds, and asks when Murugan will take him. The praise is a litany of 'namo namah': the virtuous one with the golden trident, honey of the three Tamils, hard for Brahma to reach, dancer in the hall, the feet that trampled Death's messenger, the true guru of nada, light within the light, lord of the great gods.
nuance: The self-condemnation is formally a string of accusatives ending in -அனை (வ்ருதாவனை, காமாவிகாரனை, மோடாதி மோடனை), each a charge the poet lays on himself, closed by ஆளுவது எந்நாளோ. The second half answers it in the same rhythm with 'namo namah'.

reading: A litany without a plea: 'namo namah' to Murugan, knower of the Veda, hero of the vel, the lotus feet of bindu and nada, the peacock like a cloud, undivided knowledge, the one who became the elements and lives in fullness, twelve-armed. Then it names the goddess whom Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Indrani and the seven mothers serve, the vina-bearer, Siva's support, Adishakti, Parvati, Neeli, wearer of serpents, eternal mother, and hails Murugan as her son, slayer of Sura and life of the Veda-knowers.
nuance: பூதம் மற்றுமே ஆனாய், பூரணத்துளே வாழ்வாய்: Murugan as the elements and as the fullness within them. Nearly half the song is the goddess's names, and Murugan's praise is that he is the son of that Aryai.

tamil: ஆவி காப்பது மேற்பத மாத லாற்புரு டார்த்தமி
ஆனை மேற்பரி மேற்பல சேனை போற்றிட வீட்டொட
பூவை மார்க்குரு காப்புதி தான கூத்தொடு பாட்டொடு
பொக போக்யக லாத்தொடு வாழ்ப ராக்கொடி ராப்பகல்
தேவி பார்ப்பதி சேர்ப்பர பாவ னார்க்கொரு சாக்ரஅ
தேவ பாற்கர நாற்கவி பாடு லாக்ஷண மோக்ஷதி
மேவி னார்க்கருள் தேக்குது வாத சாக்ஷ ஷடாக்ஷர
வீர ராக்கத ரார்ப்பெழ வேத தாக்ஷக னாக்கெட
reading: The poet asks whether he, who never grasped the supreme truth that guarding the soul is the highest state and the true aim of life, but wandered on elephants and horses with armies, houses, lands and forests, and spent night and day with women's dance, song and scented breasts, should lose this body so. The praise names Murugan who taught Siva, Parvati's lord, the initiation beyond waking, the poet of the four kinds of verse, son of the Krittikas, the six-lettered and twelve-eyed one, and the vel that felled Meru and made the demons roar and the sea cry out.
nuance: ஆவி காப்பதுமேற் பதமாதலாற் புருடார்த்தம் இதாம் எனாப் பரமார்த்தம்: the plea is philosophical, the soul's keeping as the true புருஷார்த்தம், against the pomp of rule and pleasure. சாக்ர அதீத தீக்ஷை: the initiation Murugan gives Siva is named as beyond the waking state. Several Sanskrit words in the praise are corrupt.

tamil: ஏக மாய்ப்பல வாய்ச்சிவ போக மாய்த்தெளி வாய்ச்சிவ
ஏழு பார்க்கும்வி யாக்கிரன் யானெ னாப்பரி தேர்க்கரி
தோகை மார்க்கொரு காற்றொலை யாத வேட்கையி னாற்கெடு
சோதி காட்டவ ராச்சுத நாத னார்க்கருள் போற்றிய
நாக மேற்றுயில் வார்க்கய னான பேர்க்கரி யார்க்கொரு
நாத நாட்டமு றாப்பல காலும் வேட்கையி னாற்புகல்
வேக மேற்கொ ளராப்புடை தோகை மேற்கொடு வேற்கொடு
மோல நாட்டவர் பூக்கொடு வேல போற்றியெ னாத்தொழ
reading: The poet asks, before he loses his cruel body through craving for women and the weariness of boasting as a king, 'I am the tiger of the seven worlds', on horse, chariot and elephant, for the supreme truth he never understood in the guru's word that Siva is one and many, Siva-bliss and clarity. The praise names Murugan who became guru by one word of knowledge, hard for Vishnu on the serpent and for Brahma, who gives his state to poets who sing him with longing, and the vel that brought down the mountain of the demons while the sea cried out.
nuance: ஏகமாய்ப் பலவாய்ச் சிவபோகமாய்த் தெளிவாய்ச் சிவமீது எனா: the guru's word quoted is a compact Saiva creed, Siva as one and many. Like 995, which shares its refrain (வேலை கூப்பிட வீக்கிய பெருமாளே), it sets royal pride and desire against the truth not grasped. சோதி காட்ட அராச்சுத நாதனார்க்கு is unclear.

reading: The poet asks that his life not whirl in the fierce sorrow of fate, deluded by women whose kayal-fish eyes fight through their ear-rings and plunder life like spears, and asks for the manhood to worship the feet by Murugan's grace, so that this dog may live. The praise names the sun, moon, worlds and gods who bow, the vel that pierced Sura's chest, and Murugan who in a hunter's guise went to the millet field and said to the cloud-haired girl, 'hear me, you alone are my refuge'.
nuance: ஆண்மை தந்தருள்: the strength asked for is to worship, not to conquer. In the praise the god himself speaks Valli's refuge-formula to her (வேறு தஞ்சமும் நீயே), inverting the devotee's words.

reading: The poet describes the eight-petalled lotus of the world, with the sun on it, the deities set in their places, the yogic mantra of the mooladhara, the crowned seat above, the jewelled mansion known by the texts and countless lights, incense and lamps in a wide hall, and asks Murugan, the hero, pandit and acharya who ascended it, to remove his karma. Then a long list of the goddess's names, Kumari, Pingalai, Mangalai, Abhirami who danced in the hall, Kala-sankari, trident-bearer, dark-throated, skull-bearer, Kalyani, the text of the Vama tantra, Sivakamasundari, ends by hailing Murugan as her son.
nuance: The first half seems to describe the body's lotuses as a temple, with மூலாதாரம், the gods stationed in it and the crown above as the mandapa, but the syntax is a long list and the reading is tentative. The goddess's names include tantric ones (பிங்கலை, காம தந்திர, வாம தந்திர நூல்).

tamil: போதிலி ருந்துவி டாச்சதுர் வேதமொ ழிந்தவ னாற்புளி
போதுயர் செந்தழ லாப்பெரு வானநி றைந்த விடாப்புக
ஆதர வின்பருள் மாக்குரு நாதனெ னும்படி போற்றிட
ஆசையெ ணும்படி மேற்கவி பாடுமி தம்பல பார்த்தடி
காதட ரும்படி போய்ப்பல பூசலி டுங்கய லாற்கனி
காரட ருங்குழ லாற்கிரி யானத னங்களி னாற்கலை
சாதன மென்றுரை யாப்பரி தாபமெ னும்படி வாய்த்திடு
சாகர மன்றெரி யாக்கொடு சூரரு கும்படி யாத்திணி
reading: The poet asks whether a day will come when he too, knowing it, praises Murugan, singing many verses: the one whom Brahma who spoke the Vedas and Vishnu of the bird could not find, the fire filling the sky, Siva of great fame, praised Murugan with love as great guru so that he might think on the feet. The praise lingers on Valli's eyes, lips, hair, breasts, waist and ear-leaf, and names Murugan who, saying 'this is the way', wandered alone and steadfast in her service, and the vel that struck the sea and Sura.
nuance: The first lines tell the column of fire that Brahma and Vishnu could not measure, and then make that Siva praise Murugan as guru. The plea is for the gift of song and knowing, as in 2 and 25. The praise's word சாதனம் is unclear.

tamil: வேடர்செ ழுந்தினை காத்திதண் மீதிலி ருந்தபி ராட்டிவி
மேனித ளர்ந்துரு காப்பரி தாபமு டன்புன மேற்றிரு
நாடறி யும்படி கூப்பிடு நாவலர் தங்களை யார்ப்பதி
நாறுக டம்பணி யாப்பரி வோடுபு ரந்தப ராக்ரம
ஆடக மந்தர நீர்க்கசை யாமலு ரம்பெற நாட்டியொ
ஆழிக டைந்தமு தாக்கிய நேகர்பெ ரும்பசி தீர்த்தரு
வாடைநெ டுங்கிரி கோட்டிய வீரனு மெம்பர மாற்றிய
வாசவன் வன்சிறை மீட்டவ னூரும டங்கலு மீட்டவன்
reading: The poet tells how Valli, guarding the millet on her platform, was stirred by love, and Murugan entered the field, and asks whether a day will come when, singing that valour and calling to the poets so that all the land knows, he gains the rare penance to seek the two feet praised by the fourteen worlds. The praise names Vishnu who churned the sea with Mandara and the serpent for rope and fed the hungry gods, Siva who burned the forts and bent the great mountain as bow, the gods' cry 'you bore our burden', the demons destroyed, Indra freed from prison, and Murugan who resettled heaven.
nuance: அருந்தவம் வாய்ப்பதும் ஒருநாளே: the penance hoped for is to sing Murugan's valour in the Valli story, praise itself as the tapas. The division of the first half's syntax is uncertain.

reading: The poet confesses the infatuation for women's eyes, voice, hair, waist, gait, lips, smile and musk-scented breasts that never abates, and pictures the end: disease, Yama taking the life, mourners fondling, weeping and fainting, someone calling 'take away the old corpse', a drum beating, and the walk to the burning ground, and asks whether that is sweet. The praise names Rama, who cut off ten heads and twenty arms with one arrow, Vishnu who answered the elephant in the pond and drank out the demoness's life with her milk, and who measured the worlds with his feet, and the vel that shattered the northern peak.
nuance: The question இனிதோ தான், 'is that sweet?', turns the lover's word back on him at the funeral. குதறு முதுபிணம் எடும் என: the mourners themselves call the body an old corpse to be taken away.

reading: The poet lists the offerings to Ganapati, chickpeas, lentils, flattened and puffed rice, sweets, vadai, plantain and many fruits, set before the great-bellied elephant god with gladness, and confesses that he has not bowed with folded hands and streaming eyes to the one who comes after him, Muruga, Shanmukha; he asks whether his wandering in cruel karma, poverty, smallness and the pit of women will not end. The praise shows Death and sun and moon afraid as the vel, the peacock that circles the world and the cry 'Hara Hara' of sages and gods, and ends with Murugan grown in the Saravana pool.
nuance: The worship of Ganapati is laid out in full and Murugan is named as the one who comes after (பிறகு வரும் ஒரு முருக), the order of temple worship; the fault confessed is to have stopped short of bowing to him. Poverty (வறுமை) is named among the sufferings, unusual beside the women.

reading: The poet describes the courtesans, proud, foolish, deceitful thieves who draw young men into the net of their quarrelsome eyes and melt them like wax in fire, and confesses that, seeking them, he never even tried to follow the words of the great virtuous ones who teach the ascetic state, so that his kin and all people call him a fool and low-born; he asks, since this servant suffers so, to be given the one rare meaning. The praise shows Siva dancing to the damaru while sages melt crying 'Hara', names Murugan as son of the goddess who dwells with him, Kumara, Saravanabhava, guru on the peacock, who embraced Valli.
nuance: The poet reports what others say of him (அசடன் அறிவிலி இழிகுலன் இவன் என இனமும் மனிதருள் அனைவரும் உரைசெய), a public shame rather than a private confession. The cure asked for is a teaching (ஒரு பொருள்), in keeping with the neglect of the sages' words.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to leave behind the path of those who tend the little hut of a body of flesh, blood and worms bound for the cremation ground: the ritualists, the quarrelling sectarians, and those of half-grown knowledge who call chariyai and kiriyai penance, and to tell him plainly 'this is the thing', so that the two deeds, the malas, night and day, 'mine' and 'yours' all cease, and the experience of that sweet solitude, beyond what the Vedas' end can fix, the greatness of two in one, is revealed. The praise names the goddess, daughter of the mountain king, worshipped by the seven mothers, Abhirami of Arunai who gave the seven nether worlds, and Murugan her son, who gave Pasupati the one word of silence, with his consorts, vel, peacock, poetry, the sweet verse of the Upanishads, generosity and beauty.
nuance: இரவு பகலற எனதற நினதற அநுபூதி: the state asked for is named by what ceases, and the word அநுபூதி (direct experience) is the goal. Chariyai and kiriyai are here among the paths to be left, though in 979 the poet longs for them. மவுனம் அருளிய: the teaching to Siva is given as silence, not as Om.

reading: The poet asks whether a day will come when he can speak without fault all the names that come as 'Muruga, the six-faced', telling the peacock that crushed the northern peak, the seven hills and the serpent king's hoods, the rooster banner, Murugan's compassion, greatness, colour, youth, the two feet, the kadamba crown and the shoulders that embraced Valli. The praise sounds the vel against the demons, the blood river, the sea torn and the mango tree felled, and the hill named for a bird pierced, and names Murugan guru, Saravana, whom the Ganga, the six women and Uma each call 'my child'.
nuance: The plea is the wish to praise rightly (பழுதற மொழிவது), and the list of what is to be praised is the song. குருகு பெயரிய வரை is the Krauncha hill, named for the heron; the mango (அடுமரம்) is Sura.

tamil: உ ரக சுடிகையில் நடநவி லரிதிரு ...... மருகோனே
உ லக முழுதொரு நொடியினில் வலம்வரு ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet condemns himself at length: without a millet-grain's thought of sharing, without compassion, who never sang Arunai, Thanigai, Palani, Swamimalai and the many hills, deceitful of speech, without beauty, caste, goodness or the medicine for birth, a mind that whirls seventy times in one turn of the potter's wheel, who never thought to melt, weep and worship, darkened, graceless, without wealth, a thief, without mind, path or rule, and asks whether a day will come for him to reach Siva's state. The praise names Vishnu at length, Rama who cut Ravana's heads and arms with one arrow, the royal envoy, the giver to the elephant in the pond, the one who fought the twin marutha trees, the man-lion who tore Hiranya when his child prattled the Veda, the dancer on the serpent's hood, and Murugan the sun of devotees who circled the world in an instant.
nuance: The list is built of words in -இலி (one without): கருணையிலி, அழகிலி, குலமிலி, அருளிலி, விதியிலி, and the first lack named is sharing (பகிர நினைவு ஒரு தினையளவிலும் இலி). திகிரி வரும் ஒரு செலவினில் எழுபது செலவு வரு மன பவுரி: the mind spins seventy times while the potter's wheel turns once.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 2 of 21), named for no shrine: most confess the poet's bondage to women and their embraces and ask for the feet, two face the funeral pyre and Death's messengers, one sets the Lord's form beyond what all the sects and scriptures know, and one appears to give the lovesickness of women who watch the god pass in the street; the praise leans heavily on Vishnu's avatars as Murugan's uncle and on the ghouls feasting on the battlefield.
structure_note: Courtesan and lovemaking songs (1007 to 1010, 1012, 1015, 1017 to 1020); the body and the pyre (1014, 1019, 1021); the scriptures' limits (1011, 1016); a love-lament probably in another voice (1013). Songs 1012 to 1015 and 1018 to 1021 are in markedly harder, denser rhythms.
source_issues: 1010, 1013, 1019: the glyph ஡ stands for ஊ (இலங்கலூடுறு, முன்றிலூடே, தூர்த்த/றூர்த்த).
1007, 1010, 1011, 1019, 1020: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ ததி, உ ழலுகினும், உ ளதென, உ ரைதரு, உ ற்றார், உ க்காரித்து, உ ருத்திரரை, உ டுத்த).
1011: இருந்ந நாளும probably for இருந்த நாளும.

reading: After a frank picture of lovemaking with women who swear 'you are my very life', the poet does not ask to be pulled out: he vows that whether he sinks, rises or tosses in that ocean of passion he will never forget to think and say that Murugan's two feet are his life's help. The praise shows the battlefield of vultures, ghouls and dancing Bhairavi, Rama's one arrow felling the ten crowns and twenty arms, and Murugan, nephew of that Vishnu, the guru and Saravana who rides the peacock so that Indra regains his city.
nuance: அநுராக உததியதனிடை விழுகினும் எழுகினும் உழலுகினும் உனது அடியிணை எனது உயிர் உதவி என ... மறவேனே: the song ends its plea with a vow (மறவேனே) rather than a request, setting remembrance of the feet inside the passion instead of after escape from it.

reading: The poet describes women whose eyes are spears and whose music oozes blame, who strike young men without pause like Death himself with his net of karma's darkness, and asks not to capsize in the shoreless sea of fate through infatuation with them, but to have the lotus feet of the Kumara who melted for the hunter girl in mind even in dreams. The praise names Vishnu who sleeps on the serpent and measured the earth, Murugan the great one who told Siva on the bull 'this is the supreme knowledge', and the vel that turned the asuras' chests to mire.
nuance: இடைவிடாது எறு நடுவனும் என: the women are likened to நடுவன், Yama, the impartial killer, so desire and death are one figure. கரையிலா விதி எனும் ஒரு கடல்: fate is a sea without shore. The line about learning and knowledge that sages despise (கலைகளும் அறிவொடு கருதொணாதென முனிவுற) is hard to construe.

reading: Infatuated by women's hair, waist, gait, eyes, speech and breasts as by a deadly poison, the poet calls himself a fool falling into hell, a thief who never worshipped, a deceiver and a sinner sunk in lying talk, and asks to be shown one way to reach the lotus feet. The praise is almost wholly of Vishnu: dancer on the serpent's head, measurer of the worlds, splitter of Hiranya, Rama of the single arrow, Krishna who fought the marutha trees and played the flute to the cattle; Murugan is his nephew and the lover of the dark hunters' girl.
nuance: The self-abuse is a pileup of rhymed nouns (அவலனை, அசடனை, திருடனை, மருடனை, கபடனை, விகடனை), its rhythm part of the confession. The praise spends nearly all its length on Vishnu's avatars before naming Murugan in the last line.

reading: The poet confesses playing day and night with women whose breasts imprison the hearts of a crore of young men, drinking their lips as nectar and sinking in a sea of infatuation, and asks whether there will be a day when he forgets that ruinous karma and lives thinking of the long flower feet. The praise shows the gods and sages hailing Murugan as the demons die, and the ghouls on mountains of fat tasting the flesh, 'this is astringent, this sour, this rotten, this good', and eating until their hunger ends; he is Ganga's son, the hunter girl's husband, the vel that pierced the mountain.
nuance: The ghouls' tasting talk (துவரிது புளியிது தொய்ந்ததீதிது ... உளதென) is a comic set piece inside the battle scene, not stock drum syllables. பகிரதி சிறுவ names Murugan as Ganga's child.

reading: The poet asks when, hearing what the rival sects call the ultimate (form, the formless, a light that is neither, space, heaven, the pillar holding the worlds) and seeing the reality itself, he will rest in awareness and silence, strive for the highest state, not be bewildered by the pleasures of touch, sight, smell and sound, and be freed from the pit of deceitful women into which he, guilty of the five great sins, has fallen. The praise shows the gods crying 'Hara Hara, Siva's son Skanda, refuge!' and Murugan saying 'fear not', the vel that tore the asura's chest, the emerald peacock, and Brahma, Vishnu and Siva praising him.
nuance: உரைதரு பரசமயங்கள் ஓதுவது ... அது பொருள் கண்டு மோனமொடு உணர்வுற: the definitions of the other sects are listed, then passed beyond by seeing the thing itself in silence. Whether the definitions are rejected or taken as partial pointers depends on the syntax, which is unclear. பஞ்ச பாதகன்: the five great sins.

reading: The poet likens women's eyes to the poison that rose when the gods churned the sea with the mountain and the serpent rope, eyes that outdo Kama's five arrows, and asks whether, his mind no longer fixed and faltering on their breasts and troubled in their lies, he will not be given Murugan's red feet like a hundred-petalled lotus. The praise tells of Rama crossing the bridged sea with the monkey army and felling the ten heads and twenty arms, Siva wearing konrai, thumbai, moon and Ganga with the goddess at his side, and Murugan following the parrot-like hunter girl.
nuance: இமையவர் பற்றிக் கடைந்த அன்றெழு நஞ்சுபோலே: the eyes are the halahala poison of the churning, an image that makes the woman's glance as world-threatening as the poison Siva had to swallow.

reading: Women brighten their faces, loose and refill their hair with flowers, adjust their dress and come out through the street courtyards in a line with knowing smiles; then Kama stands, the white crescent burns like the undersea fire, the bees hum and the Malaya breeze wounds the body, and the song asks whether the mind should melt and be troubled by this infatuation. The praise shows the peacock's flight splitting the sky and whirling Mandara, Murugan dear to the three-eyed Self-born, victor of the hunters' war, and the child whom Sankari Gauri took up and fed from her breast.
nuance: The plea has no first person. The women dressing and coming into the street, then afflicted by Kama, the moon, bees and the south wind, look like the ula convention of women who fall in love watching the god's procession; if so the song is in their voice or about them, not the poet's confession. This is an inference from the imagery.

reading: The poet pictures kin wailing at his side, the body on the palm-wood pyre with drums beating, and Death with fire-spitting eyes tying the life tight to take it, and asks that before then he be given to learn, entering their discipline, with the understanding of those who think of Murugan as the giver of the goal. The praise names the vel that pierced the northern mountain, dried the sea and struck down the mango, the teacher of the meaning to Siva of the moon and Ganga, and the Lord of the eternal pure ones who hold fast to the silence that endures when the ages end.
nuance: கதிதரு முருகனும் என நினைபவர் கற்பிற் புக்கு அறிவு ஒக்கக் கற்பது: the remedy for death is to learn in the company and discipline of those who know Murugan as the goal; கற்பு here seems to mean their way or learning, not chastity, but the line is compressed. மவுனத்திற் பற்றுறு நித்தச் சுத்தர்கள்: silence as the refuge of the pure.

tamil: விடமென அயிலென அடுவன நடுவன மிளிர்வன சுழல்விழி
விரகுடை வனிதைய ரணைமிசை யுருகிய வெகுமுக கலவியில்
நடலையில் வழிமிக அழிபடு தமியனை நமன்விடு திரளது
நரகதில் விடுமெனு மளவினி லிலகிய நறைகமழ் திருவடி
இடியென அதிர்குரல் நிசிசரர் குலபதி யிருபது திரள்புய
எரியெழ முடுகிய சிலையின ரழகொழு கியல்சிறு வினைமகள்
வடவரை யிடிபட அலைகடல் சுவறிட மகவரை பொடிபட
மணிமுடி சிதறிட அலகைகள் பலவுடன் வயிரவர் நடமிட
reading: The poet, ruined alone by passion for women who flatter a man's skill and melt in many-sided union, asks whether, when Death's host binds him tight and drags him off to hell, the fragrant holy feet, the eternal reality that is release, will not come. The praise tells of Rama's arrow scattering Ravana's twenty arms and golden heads, Murugan who takes Valli with her green parrot, and the vel that shattered Sura's crown while the Bhairavas danced.
nuance: திருவடி முத்திக்குட்படு நித்யத் தத்துவம்: the feet are named as the eternal tattva within release itself. இயல் சிறு வினைமகள் and the vocative இந்த்ரலோகா are unclear: the first seems to be Valli, the second may make Murugan lord of Indra's heaven.

reading: The poet lists who and what cannot know the Lord: the nine siddhas in their caves, Brahma, the asura lords, Siva who burned the cities, Vishnu, Indra with the thunderbolt, the codes of dharma, the Puranas, all the arts and the many Vedas; and asks when, knowing that the Lord's holy form is the knowledge beyond both knowing and not knowing, he will reach the red lotus feet. The praise tells of Vinayaka who, as Vyasa dictated, wrote the Bharata war on the mountain with his broken tusk, the coral elephant after whom Murugan came, and his union with Devayanai.
nuance: அறிவும் அறியாமையும் கடந்த அறிவு திருமேனி: the form of the Lord is itself a knowledge beyond the pair of knowing and ignorance. The myth of Ganesha writing the Mahabharata with his tusk at Vyasa's dictation is named outright (பழுதற வியாசன் அன்று இயம்ப எழுதிய விநாயகன்), with Murugan as his younger brother.

reading: The poet describes lovemaking in detail, hair loosened, face sweating, breasts shaking, the self lost in union, and the love-arts learned from the books of passion, and asks whether he may waste away wandering with young women. The praise shows Murugan going to Sura's battlefield and taking the peacock from his enemy, then going to the hill, bowing even at the hunter girl's feet, wandering unseen by the hunters in the millet field, resolving even to mount the palmyra-stem horse, and at last uniting with her.
nuance: மதனகலை ஆகமங்கள்: the poet calls the manuals of love 'agamas', a mocking echo of scripture. In the praise the god himself takes on the lover's humiliations of Tamil akam poetry: bowing at the girl's feet and resolving to ride the madal (புதிய மடல் ஏறவும் துணிந்த அரிய பரிதாபம்).

reading: The poet confesses becoming the slave of women who stray from the learned path, show sweet talk, musk-smeared breasts, eyes, hair and arms, ask for coins through a broker and stand in the street like peacocks, and asks whether he will cast off that long desire and, going with the devotees, melt and praise and bow at the feet. The praise recalls the churning, Siva who bent the mountain into a bow and smiled the cities into flame and called Murugan the guru of the true meaning, and Murugan, who melted at the speech of the golden myna guarding the millet on the hill.
nuance: தரகொடு கைக்காசைக் கேட்டு: a broker (தரகு) negotiates the price, an unusually concrete detail of the trade. தத்வார்த்தக் குருபரன் என ஓதும்: Siva himself names Murugan guru. The opening lines of the praise (மைச்சாவிக் காக்கைக் கடவுளை ...) are obscure.

reading: The poet tells of a life spent: sent on small errands by sly-eyed women and robbed by them in youth, then bound by the rope of kin and parents and stumbling in bodily toil, then coughing, spitting and losing breath, the body burned in fire, and asks whether there will be a day he escapes this forest of a body. The praise names Murugan the son of the peacock of Kamakottam who gives her breast milk, nephew of Krishna who danced for the cowherd women's curds and milk, the one who came alone on the road so the learned could hear, and the giver of the meaning to Siva who burned Kama.
nuance: The plea moves through three stages of life (சிறுகாலை, the rope of kin, the cough and the pyre), a compressed biography. மெய்க்காடு: the body as a wilderness. காமக் கோட்டக் குலமயில் points to the goddess of Kamakottam at Kanchi. கற்றாவிற் காட்டி ... நற்றாயிற் காட்டி is hard to construe.

reading: The poet describes women who dress their hair, roll their eyes, half-hide their breasts, call, catch and smile, praise a man for money and make love in elaborate postures, and asks Murugan to bear with him who wallowed in that worm-hole of infatuation, call him out at once and protect him. The praise shows the sinner Sura who mocked the Rudras, burst the mountains, sent the gods fleeing and shook the three worlds, and the Kumara whose spear revelled in the sea of his blood.
nuance: பொருட்கு மிகத் துதித்து: the praise is for money. மோகப் புழுத்தொளை, the worm-hole of passion, is among the harshest images for the courtesan. பொறுத்தருளி ... அப்புறத்தில் அழைத்து: the plea is for forbearance and to be called out, not for knowledge.

reading: The poet asks Murugan not to leave him in this body, a hut that houses his heap of karma and the fruit of maya, unable to seek the truth, nor wearied by men who boast 'who can match me, who is so able?' and slight him, but in his grace to set him where he may reach the lotus feet with the taste of Tamil and end death. The praise shows the vel opening a sea of blood from Sura's head, arms and chest, and Murugan joyfully marrying the prattling cuckoo Valli in the hunters' town where she sang in the millet field.
nuance: தமிழ்ச்சுவையிட்டு இறப்பற எய்த்திட: Tamil song is the means of reaching the feet. The first quatrain (இசைக்கும் இடற் குடில், விளைப்பகுதிப் பயப்பளவுற்று) is very compressed and its split into words is a guess.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 3 of 21), mostly short and grouped in pairs or sets that share a closing refrain: the poet asks to be freed from the lure of women, from disease and from Death, and to sing and serve the feet; one song judges arguers and hoarders bound for Death's town, one is a love-lament, and one asks for the yoga that would bring back the departing breath.
structure_note: Songs sharing a final refrain: 1024 to 1027 (the gods freed from the asuras' prison), 1028 to 1030 (தேவ தேவ தேவாதி தேவப் பெருமாளே), 1031 and 1032 (the dancing peacock steed), 1033 and 1034 (devotees of blameless justice), 1035 and 1036 (the sword-fight with Sura). Disease is the subject of 1025 and 1027, Death of 1028 and 1034, the body of 1034 to 1036.
source_issues: 1022: பாயற் கிநட்முழ்கிப் is garbled (perhaps பாயற்கிடை மூழ்கி).
1023, 1025, 1034: the glyph ஡ stands for ஊ (களிறூரும், உடலூடே, குடிலூடே).
1033: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ ழலாதே).

reading: The poet confesses being entranced by bejewelled women, and also wandering with a cunning mind, trusting men without understanding and singing them as golden-handed great patrons, and asks to be told how to sing the lotus feet in fresh and fitting verse instead of living in lies. The praise names the green-cloud Vishnu who as Rama felled ten heads and twenty arms with one arrow, one who wandered singing sweet songs of wisdom in devotion at the feet of the dancer whom Vishnu and Brahma cannot grasp, the vel thrown at Sura, and the Velaikkaran of the hill of millet and bamboo pearls.
nuance: அறிவிலாரைத் தேறிப் பொற்கை புகழ் பெரியராகப் பாடி: the poet confesses the court poet's sin of praising undeserving patrons as generous, and asks instead for song for the Lord. The figure who wanders singing ஞானப் பாடல் at the dancer's feet may be Murugan as Sambandar, but the text does not name him.

reading: The poet describes women who price their musk-smeared breasts for coins and sell love on camphor-scented beds, and asks whether, caught in the net of their kohl eyes that outdo Kama's arrows and Yama himself, he must go deluded to ruin. The praise is a chain of epithets ending in -kara: the one with the holy name Chetti, the glorious thrower of the vel, who circled the world in a moment on the peacock, the bridegroom with red flowers on his chest, plunderer of the asura lord, guardian of the gods' king, rider of the elephant, giver of release, and the Velaikkaran of the pure hunters' daughter.
nuance: முலையை விலை கூறிக் காசுக்கு அளவே: the price is stated outright. செட்டி எனும் ஒர் திருநாமக்கார: Murugan bears the name Chetti, the merchant, presumably from a guise taken to approach Valli; the song names the title, not the story. The -kara chain is a rhythmic device.

reading: The poet asks whether, deluded by women whose eyes scorn Kama's arrows, caring for neither land, town, house, wealth, children, wife nor kin, and without true knowledge, he must search through seven births and fall into hell. The praise names the green peacock that pecks the dancing serpent, Murugan who stands so all may be saved where the Veda speaks silence, Valli's bridegroom in the hunters' field, and the one who cut the prison where the asuras held the gods and set them free.
nuance: நாடு நகர் ... சுற்றம் இவை பேணா: the poet's fault includes neglecting worldly duties for women, not only neglecting God. ஆரணம் உரைக்கும் மோன கவிடத்தில் is unclear; it may mean the place of silence the Veda points to.

reading: The poet asks that when disease of cold, phlegm, fever, wind and bile surrounds the body and brings the life to slip away, before he perishes in a sea of grief with father and children around him, Murugan think to come and give the feet that taught the Veda on earth. The praise names Murugan who comes daily on the peacock to those who pine in love, who taught the Veda to the deluded brahmins before Vishnu and Brahma, and who freed the gods.
nuance: The diseases are named by the humoral scheme (வாதம், பித்தம், with சீதம் and மலம்). மாதர் மயலுற்று வாட ... வருவோனே: here the pining is of women in love with Murugan, a reversal of the poet's usual infatuation.

reading: The poet asks not to wander in the delusion of peacock-like women whose eyes and breasts crush young men's strength, and that a mind which thinks on Murugan's name, with sin gone, come into his hands: Murugan is the great life of devotees who think of him with song, music, dance and devotion. The praise names the dancing peacock, the teacher of the Veda's word to Siva, and the hero who stood as the hunter girl's servant.
nuance: பாடல் இசை மிக்க ஆடல்கொடு பத்தியோடு நினை பத்தர்: devotion is pictured as performance, song, music and dance, the setting the poet asks to join.

reading: The poet lists the diseases (spirit possession, colic, fever, swelling, the great belly, cough, anaemia, leprosy, wind, bile and piles) and asks that none of them come near him as he wastes, and that he be set to live in the high state of release. The praise names Valli's husband, the peacock that measured the whole earth in its running, and Murugan who removes the sufferings of devotees who chant the Veda.
nuance: The plea is a medical catalogue; the cure asked for is release (முத்தி நீடிய பதம்) rather than health alone.

reading: Those who learn books to quarrel and win arguments, those who seek money and live without giving, and those who never melt saying 'life of the Lord who shares his body with the woman' all go to the town of great Death and wander there. The praise names Murugan the Lord of the form of nada who dwells in the heart, ruler of the serpent world and the fourteen worlds, bearer of the vel and the cock banner, God of the gods.
nuance: The song has no plea: it is a judgement on three kinds of men, setting disputatious learning and ungiving wealth beside lovelessness. மாதுபாகர் வாழ்வே, the life of Siva the half-woman, is the address Murugan is given by those who do melt.

reading: The song asks whether it is fitting that the girl, deluded by love, should waste away under Kama's arrows, the roaring sea, the cuckoo whose anger never ends and her own mother's harsh enmity. The praise names Murugan who rides the peacock in joy, the cock banner by which the seven worlds live, and the vel that fought Sura to ashes.
nuance: An akam love-lament, not the poet's confession: the speaker (a companion, the mother or the girl herself; the text does not say) presents the classical afflictors of the lovesick girl, adding the mother's scolding (மாதாவின் வார்மைப் பகை).

reading: The poet, who cannot speak truth while great craving remains, who suffered by joining ignorant women and learned only noisy books, a dog of a servant, asks Murugan to show him a little grace so that his life does not become empty chaff. The praise names him easy to reach for the bravest of heroes, the Kumara of the peacock, husband of the hunter creeper, and the steadfast God of gods.
nuance: ஆவி சாவி யாகாமல்: சாவி is grain without a kernel, so the life is pictured as a husk. ஆரவாரம் மாறாத நூல்: learning that is only noise, as in 1028.

tamil: காதி லோலை கிழிக்குங் காம பாண விழிக்குங்
காணொ ணாத இடைக்கும் பூணு லாவு முலைக்குங்
கோதி லாத கருப்பஞ் சாறு போல ருசிக்குங்
கூருவே னொரு வர்க்குந் தேடொ ணாததொ ரர்த்தங்
பூதி பூஷணர் கற்பின் பேதை பாகர் துதிக்கும்
போக பூமி புரக்குந் த்யாக மோக குறப்பெண்
சோதி வேலை யெடுத்தன் றோத வேலையில் நிற்குஞ்
சூரர் சேனை யனைத்துந் தூளி யாக நடிக்குந்
reading: The poet, never sated by women's spear-eyes that reach their ears, their yazh-like speech, unseen waists, breasts and lips sweet as fresh cane juice, asks whether Murugan will not think even a little of letting him reach the meaning that no one can find by searching. The praise names Murugan the teacher of wisdom praised by Siva of the ash and his consort, the arms that embrace Valli, the vel that fought the mango tree and the hill in the sea, and the rider who makes the peacock dance as Sura's armies turn to dust.
nuance: ஒருவர்க்கும் தேடொணாததொர் அர்த்தம்: the goal is a meaning beyond anyone's search, given only by grace. போத தேசிகன், the teacher of knowledge, is a title of Murugan here.

tamil: காவி சேர்பவ ளத்தின் கோவை வாயித ழுக்குங்
நீத மான அடிக்கும் மாலு றாத படிக்குன்
பார மேரு வளைக்கும் பாணி யார்சடை யிற்செம்
பால காஎன நித்தம் பாடு நாவலர் துக்கம்
சூரர் சேனை தனைக்கொன் றார வார மிகுத்தெண்
reading: The poet asks Murugan to look on him so that, not infatuated with women's hair, eyes, lips, breasts and dancing feet, he may praise him with love. The praise names Murugan the child whom poets daily sing as 'Bala' and whose sorrow and sin he cuts away, giving the state of joy, son of Siva who bent Meru and wears the half moon, and the rider of the peacock while Kali dances in the blood sea of Sura's army.
nuance: பாலகா என நித்தம் பாடு நாவலர்: the reward the praise names goes to poets who sing the god as a child, which is what the plea asks to become.

reading: The poet asks not to wander in love with the sulking and noise of women whose eyes, brows and arms sell infatuation and make good men faint, and asks Murugan to understand him a little so that he may hold the feet that are his town, his mother and his kin. The praise names him the bridegroom of the girl on the hill who gave the hunters heaven, the one who speaks the name of safety kept by Siva, whom Vishnu and Brahma could not find, and the one who gives life to devotees of blameless justice.
nuance: ஊர் பெற்ற தாய் சுற்றமாய் உற்ற தாள்: the feet take the place of home, mother and kin. ஊடற்குள்ளே புக்கு: the courtesan's sulk (ஊடல்) is a trap. Which name is meant in சேமத்தின் நாமத்தை மொழிவோனே is not said.

reading: The poet asks that before the trident-bearer comes to seize the life from this hut of skin, bone and flesh, Murugan give him a mind keen in devotion to the flawless feet. The praise names the vel that struck down Sura who hid in the sea, Murugan who gave knowledge to the Primal one who swallowed the poison that would have killed the world and the gods, and the bridegroom of the doe-eyed girl.
nuance: சூலத்தன்: here Death is the bearer of the trident, a weapon usually Siva's. The lines on the poison (ஆலத்தை ... ஆம் வித்தையாமத்தை அருள்வோனே) are compressed and their split into words is uncertain.

reading: The poet, in a body of flesh with nine openings and a crore of womb-paths behind it, asks to sing Murugan's grace so as to grasp all learning and music, to seek his feet morning and evening without forgetting, and to worship the feet of those who praise his name. The praise names the vel by which the sun, moon, time, wind, cloud, sea, mountain and water, the gods who worship Siva's feet, Indra, Vishnu and Brahma live, and the sword-fight with Sura of many magics.
nuance: நாமம் புகழ்பவர் பாதம் தொழ: the plea reaches beyond the Lord's feet to the devotees' feet. ஒன்பது வழி: the body's nine gates.

reading: The poet, not knowing the strong act that ends the two karmas of this body of five elements bound as pasu and pasam, asks whether he will not attain the good yoga by which the little life that runs out in hundreds and thousands of breaths may be turned back. The praise names Valli of the millet field, the seas set on fire, the Vedas crying out, and the sword that cut Sura's chest and arms.
nuance: அறுநூறும் பதினுறழ் நூறும் பதினிருபது நூறும் ஓடும் சிறுவுயிர்: the numbers seem to count the breaths a life spends, and the yoga asked for would make the breath return (மீளும்படி). Whether they add up to the traditional daily count of breaths is a guess. The plea is in the language of Saiva Siddhanta (பசுபாசத் தேகம், இருவினை).

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 4 of 21): pleas against disease, birth and the decaying body, against flattering patrons and courtesans, and above all for the inner way (silence as temple, breath and the six centres, the self lost so that all becomes one, the abode of supreme wisdom that no fire, wind or weapon touches), set to praise that calls Murugan the Meru of compassion.
structure_note: Two rhythm groups. 1038 to 1042 run in long syllables (தானா) and share the refrain சேயே வேளே பூவே கோவே தேவே தேவப் பெருமாளே; 1043 to 1051 run in a Sanskrit-heavy metre ending கருணை மேருவே தேவர் பெருமாளே. The yogic and non-dual songs (1043 to 1045, 1047, 1049, 1050) are the chapter's core; 1046 and 1051 confess women, 1041 and 1048 the funeral and Death's messengers.
source_issues: 1038: ஡ in the second line stands for ஊ (ஊசாடு ஊசல்).
1040: lines 11 and 12 are garbled (பர்ழு டேவா னூடே பர்ரு டேயூர்).
1041: line 13 is corrupt (தீயு ஧ட்முள்).
1044: வா஡ணச in line 11 is corrupt, perhaps வாரீச.
1045: line 2 is corrupt (பான ஧ம்முல), perhaps பானம் மூல.
1050: a stray ** ends line 2 (மெதிர்கூறத்**).
1051: ஡ stands for ஊ in lines 1 and 5 (ஊதை, ஊறு), and பி஧ல்முழ்க in line 7 is corrupt for பில் மூழ்க.

reading: The poet asks that wind-disease, headache, colic and swollen belly not come near, that he not enter the womb-path again in this body packed with illusion, nor whirl in births like waves beating on the sea, and asks whether he will gain Murugan's paired anklets so that the many devotees who recite may also reach the goal. The praise calls Murugan kin to those who sing the Vedas with music so that their ruin perishes, the hero whose feet Vishnu and Brahma seek, and the Lord whose vel powdered Sura.
nuance: The plea names diseases one by one (வாதம், தலைவலி, சூலம், பெருவயிறு), the body's own failings before birth's cycle. ஓதும் பல அடியாரும் கதி பெற யான் உன் கழலிணை பெறுவேனோ seems to ask the feet not only for himself but so that other devotees reach the goal, though the clause could also mean 'as many devotees have'.

reading: The poet asks whether he, a dog, must die without being saved, not tending the swinging hut of flesh with its ceaseless disease, his mind apart from worldly custom, unreached by the liberation in which 'I am you and you are I' that the many Vedas' meanings cannot search out. The praise calls Murugan sky, wind, fire, water and earth and their owner, life of the doe-like Valli, bearer of the cock banner, the honey of the hill where honey falls in long forest streams.
nuance: நானே நீயாய் நீயே நானாய் is the non-dual goal stated in four words; the Vedas' meanings cannot seek it (நாடா வீடு). The praise reuses the five-element formula of Murugan as everything and its owner. The rhythm of long syllables makes several splits uncertain, and ஡ in the second line stands for ஊ (ஊசாடு ஊசல் குடில).

reading: The poet seems to recite the flattery poets give patrons: 'you are like the deathless, ageless Kama, a giver who pours grace, a knower and king, life to those who depend on you, like Mal with his arrow, like the rain cloud', and asks whether he must go in vain to such people who neither fit the praise nor sing. The praise names Siva, lord who rides the bull, whose feet in the depth of the netherworld Vishnu lying on the serpent in the ocean could not find, and calls Murugan his treasure, wearing the vetchi garland.
nuance: The opening string of comparisons (வேளே போல்வாய், தாதாவே, மாலே போல்வாய், காரே போல்வாய்) is the stock language of praise-poems to patrons, and யான் வீணே ஏகத்திடலாமோ regrets carrying it to unworthy men; the same complaint returns in 1062. The rhythm hides word breaks, so whether the comparisons are the poet's flattery or addressed to Murugan is not certain.

reading: Before the hut of many doors made of sinew, skin and water becomes a place for dogs and ghouls to crowd round, the poet asks Murugan of the twelve garlanded shoulders, life of the gods who take refuge, to give him, a dog, without delay the strength to sing his feet with his tongue. The praise names Vishnu who rules the seven worlds with one step and Brahma of the Vedas, who could not reach the feet through earth and sky, and Siva of the golden hair who rides the bull and lives with his lady.
nuance: நானா வாசல் குடில், the hut of many doors, is the body with its openings, food for dogs and ghouls once dead. Two lines of the praise (பர்ழு டேவா னூடே பர்ரு டேயூர்) are garbled; the sense of Vishnu and Brahma searching the feet through earth and sky is a guess from what survives.

reading: The poet pictures mother, uncles, women and cousins turned to strangers throwing this hut of illusion and infatuation into the long fire, then going down to bathe in the water, and asks Murugan, whose form is knowledge, to look on him and give grace at his flower feet before life leaves in that anguish. The praise names the vel that relieved the gods' fear and Siva who destroyed the wicked, whose son Murugan is.
nuance: மாறானார் போல் neatly says the kin act as if they were strangers once the body is ash. போதாகாரா, 'whose form is knowledge', is the address of the plea. A line of the praise (தீயு ஧ட்முள்) is corrupt.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to rule him by saying, as a teacher: 'Come, fool, listen: do not play in the filth of desire and infatuation for women; look within; the unchanging flame of wisdom stands, find it without searching; see the endless meaning of the Vedas that is the true gain', for who else on earth is fit to rule him. The praise calls Murugan the commander of the gods' army, whose twelve shoulders embrace the millet-field girl, and whose arrow, sword and vel cut Sura to dust.
nuance: The plea is cast as the guru's own words the poet wants to hear, beginning வாராய் பேதாய் கேளாய். ஆராயாதே ஆராய், 'investigate without investigating', points to knowledge not won by effort. The word splits are often doubtful in this rhythm.

tamil: அகல நீளம் யாதாலு மொருவ ராலு மாராய
சகல வேத னாதீத சகல வாச காதீத
சகல சாத காதீத சகல வாச னாதீத
விகட தார சூதான நிகள பாத போதூள
விபுத மாலி காநீல முகப டாக மாயூர
ககன கூட பாடீர தவள சோபி தாளான
களப காம வீர்வீசு கரமு கார வேல்வீர
reading: The poet asks whether, taking as his temple the silence that no one can measure in breadth or length, strewing flowers of the joy of great knowledge on the seat of ritual, he will perform the great worship of the Siva-form beyond all Vedas, all words, all action, all disciplines and all residual impressions. The praise is a run of Sanskrit epithets for Murugan of the peacock and the vel, pure and all-pervading, delight of poets, ending in the Meru of compassion.
nuance: அரிய மோனமே கோயில்: the temple is silence, and the worship is inward, offered to what is beyond Vedas, words, actions and vasanas (சகல வேதனாதீத, சகல வாசகாதீத, சகல வாசனாதீத). The praise packs Sanskrit compounds whose splits are hard to fix.

tamil: அடைப டாது நாடோ றும் இடைவிடாது போம்வாயு
அருள்பெ றாவ னாசார கரும யோகி யாகாமல்
உ டலம் வேறு யான்வேறு கரணம் வேறு வேறாக
உ ருகி ஆரியாசார பரம யோகி யாமாறுன்
வடப ராரை மாமேரு கிரியெ டாந டாமோது
மகுட வாள ராநோவ மதிய நோவ வா஡ணச
கடையு மாதி கோபாலன் மருக சூலி காபாலி
கனக லோக பூபால சகல லோக ஆதார
reading: The poet asks not to become a graceless karma-yogi of improper conduct who, thinking that the breath that leaves daily without pause will give liberation if turned back, stumbles endlessly on earth, but to be given Murugan's lotus feet so that, shaking off body, self and the instruments as separate things and melting into the feet beyond words, he may become a supreme yogi of noble conduct. The praise tells of the churning of the ocean with Meru, the serpent and the moon pained, by Gopala, whose nephew Murugan is, and of Siva with trident and skull, whose son he is.
nuance: The song distinguishes two yogis: one who relies on stopping the breath (வாயு அடைய மீளில் வீடாகும் என நாடி) but lacks grace, and the one who melts into the feet. உடலம் வேறு யான் வேறு கரணம் வேறு: body, self and faculties are seen apart and shaken off. In the praise வா஡ணச is corrupt, perhaps for வாரீச, the sea-born Lakshmi.

tamil: அமல வாயு வோடாத கமல நாபி மேல்மூல
அசைவு றாது பேராத விதமு மேவி யோவாது
எமனை மோதி யாகாச கமன மாம னோபாவ
எனதி யானும் வேறாகி எவரும் யாதும் யானாகும்
விமலை தோடி மீதொடு யமுனை போல வோரேழு
விரிவு காணு மாமாயன் முடிய நீளு மாபோல
கமல யோனி வீடான ககன கோள மீதோடு
reading: The poet asks for the state beyond the heart's imagining in which 'mine' and 'I' fall away and everyone and everything becomes himself, reached as the pure breath stops, the fire is kindled at the root above the lotus navel and the nectar drunk, step by step without wavering, striking Yama and gaining the power to travel the sky. The praise compares Murugan's peacock racing over the spheres to Vishnu stretching over the seven worlds, and calls him cloud, ocean and Meru of compassion.
nuance: The yogic steps (breath held, fire at மூலம், nectar drunk, ascent by சோபானம், a ladder) and their powers (எமனை மோதி, ஆகாச கமனம்) lead to the stated goal: எனது யானும் வேறாகி எவரும் யாதும் யானாகும், loss of ego and identity with all. A line near the start is corrupt (பான ஧ம்முல), and the river names in the praise are unclear.

tamil: அறவு நீளி தாய்மீள அகலி தாய வார்காதி
துயில்கொ ளாத வானோரு மயல்கொ ளாத ஆவேத
துணியு மாறு லாநீல நயன மாத ராரோடு
பயிலு மேக நீகார சயில ராசன் வாழ்வான
பரிபு ரார பாதார சரணி சாம ளாகார
கயிலை யாள ரோர்பாதி கடவு ளாளி லோகாயி
கமழு மார ணாகீத கவிதை வாண வேல்வீர
reading: The poet describes women whose blue eyes, sharper than arrow and vel, maddening like intoxicating drink, long and reaching to the ears, make even sleepless gods and Vedic ascetics free of infatuation resolve to ride the palm-stem horse, and asks Murugan to show a path by which he, drooping with such women, may be saved. The praise is a hymn to Uma, daughter of the Himalaya, Abhirami, Syamala, supreme yogini, Mahamayi, half of the lord of Kailasa, and calls Murugan the poet of Vedic songs fragrant with the nectar of her breast.
nuance: மடலேற, mounting the palm-stem horse, is the akam lover's public declaration of desperate love; here even ascetics are driven to it by the women's eyes. கனதனாசல அமுதூறல் கமழும் ஆரணா கீத கவிதை வாண points to Sambandar, fed by Uma's milk and singing the hymns, identified with Murugan.

tamil: இரத மான வாயூறல் பருகி டாவி டாய்போக
இதயம் வேறு போகாம லுருகி யேக மாய்நாளு
சகள மோச டாதார முகுள மோநி ராதார
பரத நீல மாயூர வரத நாக கேயூர
பரமர் தேசி காவேட பதிவ்ரு தாசு சீபாத
கரத லாவி சாகாச கலக லாத ராபோத
கடவுள் தாதை சூழ்போதில் உ லக மேழு சூழ்போது
reading: Having described drinking a woman's mouth until thirst goes, sinking in the sea of pleasure with a heart that melts and does not stray, the poet asks what Murugan's form is: the sum of Veda, chariyai, yoga, kriyai and gnanam, the world with form beginning with the elements, the bud of the six supports, the support-less, or the formless. The praise calls Murugan guru to Siva, who wears on his head the lotus feet of the chaste hunter girl, and who circled the seven worlds when the elephant-faced god on his mouse circled their father.
nuance: The two halves of the plea are joined by the word வடிவேயோ, and it is unclear whether the poet asks what Murugan's form is or contrasts the lovers' oneness with it. சடாதார முகுளம், the bud of the six centres, and நிராதாரம், the support-less, name yogic levels. The last line alludes to the contest in which Ganapati circled his parents and Murugan circled the world.

tamil: குருதி தோலி னால்மேவு குடிலி லேத மாமாவி
கொடிய பாச மோர்சூல படையி னோடு கூசாத
பருதி சோமன் வானாடர் படியு ளோர்கள் பாலாழி
பழுது றா பாவாண ரெழுதொ ணாத தோள்வீர
மருது நீற தாய்வீழ வலிசெய் மாயன் வேயூதி
கருதொ ணாத ஞானாதி எருதி லேறு காபாலி
கனலில் மூழ்க வேநாடி புதல்வ கார ணாதீத
reading: Before Death, sent by Yama to break the life in the hut of blood and skin, comes with his cruel noose and trident and his diseases, the poet asks Murugan, whose vel freed sun, moon, gods and the milk ocean from fear, to grant him grace to sing his feet with love. The praise names Krishna who felled the marutha trees and played the flute, who ran when the elephant cried 'Root!', husband of the cowherd women and Rama obedient to his mother's word, whose nephew Murugan is, and Siva the skull-bearer who dances with ghosts, whose son he is.
nuance: காலன் is here Yama's servant (ஏமனால் ஏவி விடு காலன்), coming with பாசம், சூலம் and diseases as weapons. பழுது றா பாவாணர் எழுதொணாத தோள்: the shoulders flawless poets cannot write, the praise admitting its limit.

tamil: சுருதி யூடு கேளாது சரியை யாளர் காணாது
தொடரொ ணாது மாமாயை யிடைபு காது ஆனாத
பருதி காயில் வாடாது வடவை மூளில் வேகாது
பரவை சூழி லாழாது படைகள் மோதில் மாயாது
நிருதர் பூமி பாழாக மகர பூமி தநமுள
நிகர பார நீகார சிகர மீது வேலேவு
reading: The poet asks Murugan to tell him where the abode of supreme wisdom is: unheard through scripture, unseen by those of ritual conduct, not reached above turiya, followed by no one, untouched by great maya, unending bliss that does not die in fire, wither in the sun, burn in the undersea fire, fall in the wind, sink in the ocean or perish when weapons strike. The praise calls Murugan the vel-thrower on the snowy peak, teacher whom Brahma and Vishnu esteem, and treasure of Siva of the golden bow who moves in sky and earth and dances in Kailasa.
nuance: The list of negations (fire, sun, wind, ocean, weapons) recalls the Gita's description of the self that weapons do not cut nor fire burn, though the text does not name it; here it describes the abode of wisdom. துரிய மீது சாராது: even turiya, the fourth state, does not reach it. The question பரம ஞான வீடு ஏது புகல்வாயே recurs in 1054.

tamil: தொடஅ டாது நேராக வடிவு காண வாராது
துறையி லாத தோராசை யிறைவ னாகி யோரேக
நெடிய கால்கை யோடாடு முடலின் மேவி நீநானு
அடல்கெ டாத சூர்கோடி மடிய வாகை வேலேவி
அழகி னோடு மானீனு மரிவை காவ லாவேதன்
கடுவி டாக ளர்ருப நடவி நோத தாடாளர்
கடவு ளேறு மீதேறி புதல்வ கார ணாவேத
reading: The poet asks whether Murugan, who cannot be touched or seen directly or answered by those who recite scripture, who is lord of the directions, the one turiya, other than all and knowledge itself, and who entered the body of long arms and legs saying 'you and I', will not tell him the one truth by which he may go before the fierce messenger sent by Death arrives. The praise names the vel that killed crores of Suras, the guardian of the girl born of a doe, and Siva the poison-throated dancer riding the bull.
nuance: நீ நானும் என நேர்மை நூல் கூறி: the Lord entering the body and teaching 'you and I' may point to the non-dual teaching of 1038. மான் ஈனும் அரிவை is Valli, born of a doe. The plea's last clause is hard to split, and the line has a stray ** in the source.

tamil: நிலவில் மார னேறு஡தை யசைய வீசு மாராம
நிலையில் வாச மாறாத அணையில் மாத ராரோடு
இலவி லு஡று தேனூறல் பருகி யார வாமீறி
குலவி யோம பாகீர திமிலை நாதர் மாதேவர்
குடில கோம ளாகார சடில மோலி மீதேறு
கலவி கூரு மீராறு கனக வாகு வேசூரர்
கடக போல மால்யானை வனிதை பாக வேல்வீர
reading: The poet describes lovemaking in moonlight as Kama's wind blows, in garden shade and on the mansion's upper floor, on a fragrant bed, drinking the honey of lips like silk-cotton flowers and pressing breasts to his chest, and vows that even as infatuation grows he will not forget Murugan's kadamba-garlanded feet. The praise shows the child Kumara climbing onto Siva's matted crown with Ganga and the serpent, never parting from the hunter girl, and the vel that turned Sura's army to dust, consort of the elephant's girl.
nuance: Unusually, the plea does not ask to be freed from women: மால் கூரினும் உன் நீப சீர்பாதம் மறவேனே, even in growing infatuation he will not forget the feet. The child climbing the father's matted crown (சடில மோலி மீது ஏறு குமர) is a tender image. ஡ stands for ஊ (ஊதை, ஊறு), and பி஧ல்முழ்க is corrupt for பில் மூழ்க.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 5 of 21): the rotting body, the funeral and Death's men, women's eyes and the poet's wasted verse, false promisers, and the miser who gives not even bran, set against pleas for the abode of supreme wisdom, the word of grace already received, and the feet; the praise leans on the Mahabharata and Krishna as Murugan's uncle.
structure_note: Three refrain groups: 1052 and 1053 close the கருணை மேருவே run; 1054 to 1058 end in சிகரி தகர வீக்கிய or முதிய மூர்த்திகள் தம்பிரானே; 1059 to 1063 share the refrain குலிச பார்த்திபன் உலகு காத்தருள் கோவே தேவே வேளே வானோர் பெருமாளே, with Kurukshetra and Gajendra in the praise; 1064 to 1066 are short songs ending அறிவும் உரமும் அறமும் நிறமும் அழகும் உடைய பெருமாளே.
source_issues: 1053: கேர்டுதி in line 12 is corrupt.
1056: ஡ stands for ஊ in line 2 (உடலூடே).
1059: கனகேர்டு in line 14 is corrupt, perhaps for a word naming Garuda.
1060: line 12 is corrupt (஧த்ருர் கோமான்).
1061: பா஡ண in line 14 is corrupt, perhaps பூரண.

tamil: மனக பாட பாடீர தனத ராத ரர்ருப
வருண பாத காலோக தருண சோபி தாகார
குனகு வேனை நாணாது தனகு வேனை வீணான
கொடிய னேனை யொதாத குதலை யேனை நாடாத
அநக வாம னாகார முநி ராக மால்தேட
அரிய சார தாபீட மதனி லேறி யீடேற
கனக பாவ னாகார பவள கோம ளாகார
கடவு ளேக்ரு பாகார கமல வேத னாகார
reading: After playing with women of sandal-smeared breasts and Kama's arrows, the poet heaps names on himself: one who fawns shamelessly, dallies, is worthless, a dog, sinful, cruel, a babbler without learning, blind and seeking nothing, and asks whether there will be a day when Murugan rules him. The praise says that, sent by the father whom Vishnu could not find, Murugan as Madurai's lord mounted the seat of learning and examined all four, and calls him Meru of compassion, rider of the peacock.
nuance: The run of self-names (குனகுவேனை, குறையனேனை, நாயேனை, வினையேனை, கொடியனேனை, குதலையேனை, குருடனேனை) makes the confession. மதுரேசன் அரிய சாரதா பீடம் அதனில் ஏறி அகில நாலும் ஆராயும் may allude to Murugan judging the poems of the Madurai academy, but which story and what 'all four' means is not clear from the text.

tamil: அதல சேட னாராட அகில மேரு மீதாட
றதிர வீசி வாதாடும் விடையி லேறு வாராட
மதுர வாணி தானாட மலரில் வேத னாராட
வனச மாமி யாராட நெடிய மாம னாராட
கதைவி டாத தோள்வீம னெதிர்கொள் வாளி யால்நீடு
கதறு காலி போய்மீள விஜய னேறு தேர்மீது
உ ததி மீதி லேசாயு முலக மூடு சீர்பாத
உ தய தாம மார்பான ப்ரபுட தேவ மாராஜ
reading: The poet asks Murugan to come dancing on his peacock while all dance: the serpent Adisesha below, Meru, Kali and Siva on his bull who danced against her, ghosts and vetalas, Sarasvati and Brahma, the gods, the moon, and Lakshmi and tall Vishnu as Murugan's in-laws. The praise recalls Bhima with his mace and Arjuna's arrows reducing the enemy armies, the bellowing cattle brought back, and Vishnu who reclines on the ocean and rides Garuda, Murugan's uncle, and names him Lord who dwells in the heart of the great king Prabhuda Deva.
