nuance: வறுமை தந்திடு பாழ் மூதேவிகள், 'ruinous Misfortune-goddesses who bring poverty', ties the women to loss of wealth, and பேய் நீராகிய உணவு to drink. The abuse is a list of plural nouns ending in -கள் with no verb until the plea.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள்), not tied to a shrine: most confess the poet's bondage to courtesans and union with them and ask for Murugan's feet or teaching; others set out the body's frailty, a list of sinners bound for hell, the poet's past as a court poet of women's bodies, and a satire on the boasts of the Kali age turned into the poet's own modesty; the praise draws on the Ramayana, the Bharata war, Prahlada, Siva burning Kama and Murugan teaching Siva.
structure_note: Courtesans and union: 1142, 1144, 1145, 1147, 1148, 1151, 1152, 1153, 1154, 1156. 1143 and 1149 ask for the knowledge beyond the body and the sects; 1146 is a catalogue of sinners with a praise sung almost wholly in drum syllables; 1150 is a long self-accusation; 1155 is satire and modesty. Vishnu's avatars fill much of the praise (Ramayana in 1144, 1147, 1151, 1153; Bharata war in 1144; Gajendra in 1142; Prahlada in 1150).
source_issues: Song 1145: garbled line 3 (....... ; ந்த்ரகோபம்), probably இந்த்ரகோபம், the red velvet insect.
Song 1149: corrupt று஡டொரு (line 16), probably ஆற்றூடொரு (஡ for ஊ).
Song 1153: corrupt மா஡ணச (line 16), probably மாரீச (Maricha); unflagged ஆரமுநல்முழ்கி (line 6), probably ஆரமும் உழ்கி or மூழ்கி.

reading: The poet confesses that in this ruined, swaying hut of flesh he has been a wastrel driven by infatuation, nursing endless desire, quarrelling through the town, and standing like a dog in the power of honey-tongued courtesans, and asks when the day will come that Murugan grants the feet that devotees adorn with kadamba flowers. The praise names Vishnu who sleeps on the serpent, churned the sea with Meru, herded cattle and hurled the discus to cut down the crocodile when the elephant cried out, Murugan as his sister's treasure, who fell at the feet of the hunter girl in the millet field, and the lord who shattered the seven mountains and stirred the seven seas.
nuance: பரத்தையர்க்கு ஒரு நாய்போலவே அவர் வசத்தில் நிற்பது: the courtesans are named by the Tamil word, and the poet's image for himself is a dog. சிறுப்பிள்ளைத்தனம், childishness, sums up the life. The elephant and crocodile are the Gajendra story (வாய் நாகம் ஓலமிட ... கர வினைத் தறித்தவர்).

reading: The poet calls the body a raw clay pot with nine openings, soaked in two kinds of deed and disease, and asks that, not falling into the path of fools who never think how to reach the high state but sink in the sea of craving, he be taught one day from Murugan's Tamil-knowing mouth the dawning light of knowledge beyond the thirty-six, in which the three qualities and the seal of 'I' are destroyed. The praise names Siva who danced against Kali and asked to be told, and Murugan who whispered into his right ear that this was the supreme space of the bliss of consciousness, and Indra's son-in-law who killed Sura with the vel.
nuance: முப்பதின் அறுபதின் மேலாம் may count the thirty-six tattvas and what lies beyond them, and நான் ஆ என வரு முத்திரை is the stamp of the ego; both readings depend on how the syllables split. The guru story has a new detail: the teaching is given into Siva's right ear (தெக்ஷண செவி), and what is taught is சிற்சுக பரவெளி, the space of conscious bliss, not Om by name.

reading: The poet describes courtesans whose dark eyes, like Death's messengers, warriors' swords and the vel, take young men's lives for Kama's kingdom, how he melted in their arts until the wealth in his hand was gone, and how they then said 'no shame? go, go now, mother, call the others'; he asks that his love for these deceivers end. The praise names Krishna, charioteer of Dharma, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva against the king of Hastinapura, and Rama who felled Ravana's ten heads and twenty arms with one arrow, as Murugan's uncle.
nuance: The dismissal is given in the courtesans' own words (வெட்கமிலை நட ஏகும் ஏகும் இனி மற்றவரை அழையும் மாதரே), so the turn comes exactly when the money is gone (பொருளான ஆகும் வரை). படிறிகள், deceivers, is the poet's last word for them.

tamil: உ ற்ப லங்கள்சி வந்துக விந்திட ....... ; ந்த்ரகோபம்
reading: The poet describes union, loosened hair, pressed breasts, reddened eyes, lips like the red indragopa insect, coos like the cuckoo and the dove, nail marks, and asks when he will leave this hut of a body, worn out in that pit, and reach Murugan's lotus feet. The praise tells how the sea burned and the Krauncha hill was split, how Indra regained his place and Devayanai her bridegroom, and names Murugan with the rooster banner, wearing kadamba and loved by the hunter girl.
nuance: குரம்பை, a hut, for the body, is the word that turns the scene: the poet asks to leave it (விட்டு அகன்று) for the feet. One line is garbled (see source issues).

reading: The song lists sinners: those who do not pay the teacher who taught them, who wrong great ascetics, Brahmins who harm their own town, those who give nothing to the beggar, who are partial, who mock those who serve Siva and Vishnu, who have no single-minded meditation, who are steeped in lust; all of them, it says, will suffer in the seven hells. The praise is almost wholly drum syllables (தாதத, தூதுது, சாசச, டுட்டுடு ...) for Murugan's dance, praised by the learned.
nuance: There is no first-person plea: the first half is a moral catalogue ending in ஏழ் நரகு உழல்வாரே. ஈசர் விஷ்ணுவை சேவை செய்வோர் protects the devotees of both Siva and Vishnu. Several items in the list (ஊசலிற் கனலாய் எரி காளையர், ஆர் தனக்கும் உதாசின தாரிகள்) are hard to construe, so the list is only roughly read.

reading: The poet describes courtesans whose eyes reach their palm-leaf earrings, who trouble even ascetics learned in wisdom with the poison set in their eye-arrows, catch good wealth at their fragrant breasts and lead a man in with 'come', and asks that their illusion be ended and he be given the true akshara that was given to the gods. The praise tells how Nala threw mountains into the sea for Rama's bridge, Vibhishana received grace and the demons died, names Siva who destroyed Kama's body, and Murugan who fell in love in the millet field.
nuance: ஞானம் ஓதி மிகுத்த தவத்தவர்க்கு இடர் ஓகை செலுத்தி: the women's eyes threaten even ascetics, a point the confession uses against itself. வானவருக்கு அருளுற்ற அக்ஷர வாய்மை may mean an imperishable truth or a sacred syllable; I cannot tell which.

reading: The poet describes women whose eyes reach their earrings, their loosened cloth and hair, their lips and play, and asks whether one day the frenzy of ripe lust will subside and, knowing Murugan, he will reach the blissful state practised in the cage of silence and abide in grace. The praise tells how the northern mountains wailed, the earth rejoiced, Indra regained his city, the sea shrank and Sura's mango tree was torn up by the root, and names Murugan who embraced the daughter raised by the elephant.
nuance: மவுன பஞ்சரம், the cage of silence, turns the image of a caged bird into the goal: the silence where knowing Murugan (உனை உணர்ந்து) brings bliss (சுக பதம்). The plea grows directly out of lust subsiding (காம பரவசம் தணிந்து).

reading: The poet speaks of the One that the clamouring arts cannot point to and the warring sects cannot reach, the great light seen when birth and the two deeds end, which the Vedas melt toward and which is reached by letting go of everything, and confesses that, not knowing it, he is caught in the net of women's eyes, musk and brow-marks; he asks whether he must suffer. The praise names Murugan as the child with anklets whose feet the Vedas worship, nursed by the stars, born on the hundred-petalled lotus bed in the pond, who crushed Sura and the golden mountain, lord of the gods.
nuance: The opening is a negative theology: ஏகம் is what the பதறிய சமயிகள் cannot reach and is found only by leaving all (முழுதையும் விட்டால் சேர்வது). The praise's pond and lotus (பாசடை, டாமரை, சததள அமளி) seem to describe the birth in the Saravana pool, though the pool is not named; one word is corrupt.

tamil: கவிஞ னாய்த்திரிவேனைக் காமக் ரோதத் ...... தூர்த்தனை யபராதக்
ப்ரமிக்கு நெஞ்சனை உ ருவ மாறி முறை முறை
களவு சாத்திர மோதிச் சாதித் தேனைச் ...... சாத்திர நெறிபோயைம்
தனிற் பிறந் தொரு நொடியின் மீள அழிதரு
புவியின் மேற்பசு பாசத் தேபட் டேனைப் ...... பூக்கழ லிணைசேரப்
பொருளின் மேற்சிறி தாசைப் பாடற் றேனைக் ...... காப்பது மொருநாளே
குலைய வீக்கிய வேளைக் கோபித் தேறப் ...... பார்த்தரு ளியபார்வைக்
குதலை வாய்ச்சிறி யோனுக் காகத் தூணிற் ...... றோற்றிய வசபாணிப்
பரவி வாழ்த்திட வேகற்றாரச் சோதிப் ...... பாற்பணி யிறைவாகைப்
பரவை கூப்பிட மோதிச் சூர்கெட் டோ டத் ...... தாக்கிய பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet accuses himself at length: he was a poet who sang women's bodies from foot to head, a lustful, angry rogue, a deceiver, unsettled, who argued for shastras in every sect without discipline, followed the five senses, took this passing life as lasting and was caught in the bonds of the bound soul; he asks to be guarded and brought to the flowered feet, having at least a little desire for the reality that destroys the qualities, deeds and maya. The praise names Siva who burned Kama with a look when he broke his yoga, Narasimha who came from the pillar for the child who said 'namo Narayana', and Murugan who freed Indra from fear and drove off Sura.
nuance: பாதாதிகேசம் அளவும் பாடும் கவிஞனாய்த் திரிவேனை: the poet confesses the very genre of praising women limb by limb, which his own confessions resemble. ஆசாரவீன சமயம் தோறும் களவு சாத்திரம் ஓதி may mean he argued false doctrines in every sect; the phrase is uncertain, as is மூகம் தனிற் பிறந்து.

tamil: உ டுத்த ஆடையும் வேறாயு ழன்றுக ...... ழன்றுவீழ
reading: The poet describes women with eyes darker than a vel, drinking their lips, embracing them, nail marks and slipping cloth, and confesses that he sees no way to end it and no companion to help. The praise turns the same gaze on Valli, her anklets, peacock-feather dress, breasts and spear-like eyes that drove Murugan to longing until he joined her, and names Rama who killed Ravana, Siva who bent Meru as a bow, and Murugan as the servant-hero honoured by both.
nuance: The second half describes Valli's body in the same terms as the courtesans' (கண்கள், தனங்கள், ஓதி), and has the Lord's mind tremble (மனம் பரதவிக்க), so the desire the poet cannot end is shown sanctified in Murugan's love. ஒன்றுகாணேன் twice, 'I see none', is the plea's whole force. Who is மாயான் whose mind is troubled (line 12) is not certain.

reading: The poet runs through a woman's hair, brow, ears, eyes, nose, lips, teeth, breasts, gait, waist and feet, and asks that his heart not weaken at them, and that Murugan grant the meaning he told Agastya and the lotus feet that Hari and Brahma could not measure. The praise names the vel that killed the demons and restored the gods to their cities, and Murugan who embraced the hunter girl in the forest where the hunters wrest the tusks from elephant herds.
nuance: அகத்தியனொடு உரைத்த பொருள் makes Murugan Agastya's teacher; the text gives the 'meaning', not Tamil by name. The catalogue of the woman's parts in -க்கும் is answered by the feet that cannot be measured (அளப்பரிய பதக்கமலம்).

reading: The poet tells how, caught by peacock-like women's games in an unrighteous mind, he climbed on their flowered bed and drowned in a sea of passion, and asks that even he, a dog in their power, be raised. The praise tells the Ramayana: Rama going to the forest at his mother's word with Sita and Lakshmana, the golden deer Maricha, Khara and Dushana, the seven trees and Vali, Hanuman and the bridge, and the single arrow that felled Ravana's ten heads, with Murugan as his nephew.
nuance: The poet calls himself கொடிய மனது அநியாய மாபாதகா போதி, a great sinner of crooked mind. The Ramayana is told in order and at unusual length, but as stock praise of the uncle. The word for the deer is corrupt (see source issues).

tamil: கொலைவிழி சுழலச் சுழலச் சிலைநுதல் குவியக் குவியக்
குறியணி சிதறச் சிதறக் கரவளை கதறக் கதறக்
கலவியி லொருமித் தொருமித் திலவிதழ் பருகிப் பருகிக்
கையிலுள பொருள்கெட் டருள்கெட் டனைவரும் விடுசிச் சியெனக்
சலநிதி சுவறச் சவறத் திசைநிலை பெயரப் பெயரத்
தமனிய நெடுவெற் பதிரப் பணிமணி சிரம்விட் டகலச்
பெலமது குறையக் குறையக் கருவிகள் பறையப் பறையப்
பெடையொடு குழறக் குழறச் சுரபதி பரவப் பரவப்
reading: The poet describes union in doubled words, eyes rolling, waist bending, bangles crying out, lips drunk again and again, and how after a few days, his wealth and good name gone, everyone drove him off with 'chi, chi', and asks whether he must wander the world. The praise is a battle in doubled words, the sea drying, mountains shattering, Sura's strength failing and jackals and owls following, ending with the vel.
nuance: The doubling (சுழலச் சுழல, குவியக் குவிய ...) runs through both halves, so the union and the war share one rhythm. கையிலுள பொருள்கெட்டு அருள்கெட்டு is the turn: money and grace go together.

tamil: கோழையா ணவமி குத்த வீரமே புகல்வர் அற்பர்
கூறியே நடுவி ருப்பர் சோறிடார் தரும புத்ர
ஆழுவார் நிதியு டைக்கு பேரனா மெனஇ சைப்பர்
ஆயுநூ லறிவு கெட்ட நானும் வேறல அதற்கு
ஏழைவா னவர ழைக்க ஆனைவா சவனு ருத்ர
ஈசனார் தமதி டுக்க மாறியே கயிலை வெற்பில்
வேழமீ துறையும் வஜ்ர தேவர்கோ சிறைவி டுத்து
வீரசூ ரவன் முடிக்கு ளேறியே கழுகு கொத்த
reading: The poet mocks the boasts of the age: cowards proclaim their valour, men of low birth claim high lineage and sit in the middle, those who feed no one call themselves Dharmaputra, the poor call themselves Kubera; this, he says, is the way of the Kali age, and he, without real knowledge, is no different, so this song is his apology to the assembly. The praise names Murugan who came to Kailas to end the gods' distress, freed Indra from prison and released Brahma, and took up the bow while vultures pecked at Sura's crown.
nuance: அவையடக்க உரையீதே: the song names itself as the convention by which a poet abases himself before the learned. The satire turns on the poet in one line (நானும் வேறல அதற்குள் ஆகையால்). The opening of the praise (ஆனை வாசவன் உருத்ர ஈசன் மேல் வெயில் எறிக்க) I cannot construe with confidence.

tamil: சந்தனங் கலந்த குங்கு மம்புனைந் தணிந்த கொங்கை
சங்கினங் குலங்க செங்கை யெங்கிலும் பணிந்து டம்பு
கொந்தளங் குலுங்க வண்சி லம்புபொங்க இன்சு கங்கள்
கொங்கைபைங் கரம் புணர்ந்த ழிந்துணங் கலுந்த விர்ந்து
தந்தனந் தசெஞ்சி லம்பு கிண்கிணின் குலங்கள் கொஞ்ச
சந்தனம் புனைந்த கொங்கை கண்களுஞ் சிவந்து பொங்க
வந்தநஞ் சுகந் தமைந்த கந்தரன் புணர்ந்த வஞ்சி
மைந்தனென் றுகந்து விஞ்சு மன்பணிந் தசிந்தை யன்பர்
reading: The poet describes adorned women swaying through the street, their bangles, hair and anklets, and asks to be freed from their embraces and given Murugan's feet. The praise names the anklets on Murugan's own feet as he comes, the hunter girl of the champak field whose breasts he embraced, the son of Uma who shares Siva's body, and the lord who enters the hearts of loving devotees.
nuance: The women's anklets (வண்சிலம்பு பொங்க) are answered by Murugan's (செஞ்சிலம்பு கிண்கிணி ... தண்டை), the same sound turned to the Lord's coming.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 12 of 21), sung at no named shrine: the poet confesses his bondage to women and courtesans who take a man's wealth, pictures old age, the funeral and Death's servants, traces a life from the womb to the pyre, and asks for the feet, for knowledge beyond the scriptures and sects, and for a place among the devotees; the praise turns on Krishna's boyhood, Siva's deeds, the freeing of the gods and Murugan as teacher of Siva.
structure_note: Death and the body: 1158 (the funeral), 1163 (womb to pyre), 1166 and 1167 (old age), 1169 (Death's servants), 1170 (the body and Yama's noose). Women: 1160, 1161, 1164, 1171. Knowledge and the feet: 1157 (the reality beyond scriptures and sects), 1159, 1162, 1165 (the five letters and Om), 1168 (the sea of births and the devotees' assembly).
source_issues: Throughout: the source splits உ from the following letters with a space (உ ரையாடி, உ ததி, உ றைந்த), apparently a font conversion fault.
Song 1163: corrupt character in சிறைவை஢ட (line 163, probably சிறைவீட, 'free from prison'); unflagged slip அரவங்ளுந் (line 166) for அரவங்களும்.
Song 1167: corrupt character in ருத஧முழ்க (line 244, probably குருதி முழ்க, 'sinking in blood').
Song 1168: corrupt character in லு஡டே (line 259, probably ஊடே, 'through').
Song 1169: corrupt character in வீழ்வ஡ணது (line 286); the intended word is unclear.
Song 1170: corrupt character in உய஧ருறி (line 299, probably உயிருறி, 'life entering').
Song 1171: unflagged garble '....... ; த்ழுறல்' at line 319, probably for a word ending in ஊறல் (the lips' moisture).

reading: The poet says the reality that the Vedas, the crores of Puranas, those infatuated with chariyai, kiriyai, sacrifice and yoga, and the debaters of rival sects chase and cannot know, is far off; he asks whether his mind will not one day melt in the Lord's light, join the compassionate devotees in the ocean of bliss, dance and rejoice, and sing without forgetting the jewelled lotus feet. The praise names Murugan as nephew of the cloud-dark Krishna who felled the marutha trees, sucked the demoness's breast, made the elephant scream and kicked the cart, and as the hero of the peacock, lord of Devayanai and the hunter girl and of crores of gods.
nuance: The opening list sets the four Saiva paths (சரியை கிரியை ... யோக) beside the Vedas and the quarrelling sects (பரசமய பேத வாதிகள்) as things that run after the truth without reaching it; what is asked for instead is melting (உருகி), the company of devotees and song. மகோததி, great ocean, recurs in 1175 for the same bliss. The Krishna deeds (மருது, அலகை முலை, சகடு) are stock praise of the uncle.

tamil: தப்பிற் றவறுறு மத்திப நடையென ...... உ ரையாடிச்
reading: The poet pictures his own funeral: kin, children and his sweet-spoken wife say it is over and he is cold, wail and beat their heads asking how this mistake happened, the fire-pot is carried, the drum sounds and the corpse is covered; he asks that at the hour his body is left Murugan give his two feet. The praise names the mountain daughter who rejoices while old ghouls dance to the drum, Siva in the tiger skin, the elephant-faced Ganapati who eats sugarcane and flattened rice as Murugan's elder brother, and the battle in which the night-walkers' clans fell.
nuance: The funeral is told through the mourners' talk, which is hard to split in places (சலமிது சுத்தச் சலம், 'it is cold, quite cold'; மத்திப நடை): the reading of those lines is a guess. The plea is narrow: only at that moment (அப்பொழுது இருசரண் அருள்வாயே). The drum phrase தொக்குத் தொகுதொகு is rhythm, not words.

tamil: செங்கை னற்புகை யோமாதிகள் குண்ட மிட்டெழு சோமாசிகள்
றங்கம் வெட்டிய கூர்வாள்விழி மங்கை யர்க்கற மாலாய்மன
அந்த நிற்குண ஞானோதய சுந்த ரச்சுட ராராயந
கொங்க டுத்தகு ராமாலிகை தண்க டுக்கைது ழாய்தாதகி
கொண்ட சித்ரக லாசூடிகை யிண்டெ ருக்கணி காகோதர
சங்கு சக்ரக தாபாணியு மெங்க ளுக்கொரு வாழ்வேசுரர்
தஞ்ச மற்றிட வேதாகர னஞ்ச வெற்புக வீராகர
reading: The poet says that while fire-priests and Soma-sacrificers fall prostrate at the pair of feet, he struggles with delusion and the senses, and his monkey mind is caught by women's sword-sharp eyes; he asks that darkness not cover it and that, in the dawn of attributeless knowledge, Murugan give him with love one of his feet. The praise has Siva, crowned with konrai, tulasi, datura, Ganga and the moon, and Vishnu with conch, discus and mace, beg Murugan to free the gods from prison, and names the vel he sent at the mountain.
nuance: நிற்குண ஞானோதயம், the rising of knowledge without attributes, is the gift asked. The contrast between the ritualists (ஓமாதிகள், சோமாசிகள்) who already bow at the feet and the poet distracted by women is my reading of an opening whose syntax is not clear, especially திண்டிறல் தவ வாள்வீரரொடு இகலா.

reading: The poet lists the arrows of women's eyes, sharper than carp, deadlier than poison, angrier than a deer, their speech of honey and syrup, their banyan-leaf bellies, hair, lips and smiles, and asks that he put desire for them far away and reach Murugan's feet with praise. The praise is of Siva, who kicked Death, burned Kama, begged at Kasi in Brahma's skull, rode the bull, held the poison, wore the elephant's hide and danced in the cremation fire with Uma at his side, and of Murugan his child, who sent the vel at the sea, Sura and the seven hills.
nuance: The eye that wounds (விழிக் கணை) and speech like nectar are the usual weapons; the plea is simply to send desire far off (ஆசையினைத் தூரவிடுத்து). ஆதுலருக்கு at the end means the helpless or destitute: Murugan as lord of those without support.

reading: The poet tells of cheating women who use love-powder, take the wealth in a man's hand by trickery, deck their breasts in silk and talk like parrots, and of his own madness in their bites and kisses; he asks for the wonder that cuts his attachment. The praise names the vel that pierced the demon army to battle drums, the vel that gives wealth to pure devotees who melt in grief, the lord of the green peacock, and Murugan who pointed out the meaning to Chokkar, Siva of Madurai.
nuance: சொக்குப்பொடி is a love-drug and கைப்பொருளைக் கெத்தில் பற்றி is wealth seized by cunning, so these are the paid women. சொக்கர்க்கு அர்த்தத்தைச் சுட்டிய is the teaching of Siva again, with Siva named by his Madurai name. Lines 101 to 103 (திக்குக்கெட்டு ஒட்டுச் சிட்டென பட்டத்துற) are obscure.

tamil: மாமாயி பார்வதி தேவிகு ணாதரி...... உ மையாள்தன்
reading: The song opens with a string of names for Uma (giver of knowledge, cause of causes, the great Maya, Parvati) and names Murugan her son, guru of gurus, Valli's lord and the bridegroom of the heavenly deer-girl; the poet, calling himself a dog, asks to wear Murugan's feet on his head, to be rid of the fever of delusion, and to praise him rightly through learning. The praise names him as the one who came to Koodal and had the Jains who would not wear ash impaled so that the hunchbacked Pandya rose, as nephew of Rama who split Ravana, and as the lord beyond word and mind who destroys bonds.
nuance: நீறு இடா அமணோர் ... கழுமீதினில் ஏறிட, கூனான மீனன் இடு ஏறிட, கூடலில் வருவோனே is the story of Sambandar at Madurai, here told of Murugan himself, with holy ash as the mark that divides the two faiths. சீர்பாத சேகரன், one who wears the feet as a crown, is what the poet asks to become. பாசவிநாசகன் names Murugan as the destroyer of the bonds.

reading: The poet traces a life from the drop placed in the mother, growing like a pea into flesh, blood, limbs and nine openings, through ten months, birth and first steps, to falling under a woman's spell, walking bent with a stick, lying bedridden, Death coming first, the corpse lifted by weary sons and kin and burned on the pyre; he asks for the anklet feet so that this birth may end. The praise is a battle in which vultures and ghouls feast to drums, Indra and Brahma praise the vel that freed the gods, and Murugan is the son of Sankara who wears the moon, Ganga, konrai and serpents.
nuance: The life runs without a pause from womb to woman to stick to pyre, so that the plea is against birth itself (செனனமிது தவிர), not only death. அந்தகன் is Death. சிங்கி, the woman's power over him, is literally a poison.

reading: The poet describes women with shaking breasts, golden ornaments, anklets and a vina in hand, child-like speech and arrow eyes, who daily make love to a man and daily cheat him and seize his goods as debts; he asks for the feet so that, turning from their tricks and his own worthless ways, he may gain Sivam and hold to austerity. The praise is a battle sung in drum syllables in which the vel splits the demons and grinds the mountain to dust, and names Murugan the beautiful lord.
nuance: கடன்பற்றிக் கொளும் மாதர், women who seize things as if collecting a debt, makes these the paid women. The goal is named in Saiva terms, சிவம் பெற்றுத் தவம் பற்ற. Most of the second half (தனந்தத்தத் தனந்தத்தத் ...) is rhythm.

tamil: நகரமிரு பாத மாகி மகரவயி றாகி மார்பு
நதிமுடிய சார மாகி உ தயதிரு மேனி யாகி
அகரவுக ரேத ரோம சகர வுணர் வான சூரன்
அதனைஅடி யேனும் ஓதி இதயகம லாலை யாகி
குகனுமரு ளாண்மை கூர மகரமெனு சாப தாரி
குழவிவடி வாக வேநம் பரதர்தவ மாக மீறு
அகிலவுல கோர்கள் காண அதிசயம தாக மேவி
அறுமுகவன் மீக ரான பிறவியம ராசை வீசும்
reading: The poet describes the Lord's form as made of the five letters, na the feet, ma the belly, si the chest, va the mouth, ya the crown, and of the syllables a and u of Om, the fullness that is knowledge within knowledge, and asks that he too recite it, make the lotus of his heart a temple and receive attentive knowledge. The praise appears to tell how Siva went to sea as a fisherman to seek and marry the fisher-girl, with Guha and the one cursed to be a makara in the story, and ends at the lord of light of the ajapa.
nuance: நகரம் இரு பாதமாகி ... வாய் வகரமாகி lays the letters of நமசிவய on the body, and அகர உகர ... ஓம் adds the pranava; இதய கமல ஆலயம் makes the heart the shrine. The fishing story is my identification from the net (வலை), the fisher folk (பரதர்), the girl of the waves and the makara curse, as in the Tiruvilaiyadal tale; the syntax of the second half and the word அசபை (ajapa, the unspoken mantra) are uncertain.

reading: The poet pictures old age, grey hair, fallen teeth, dried skin, failing legs, dim eyes and the staff, the body a slipping lump of flesh, and the illusion of a life called 'ours' that only brings grief; he asks whether his mind, still bound to women's musk-scented hair and kohl-dark eyes, will not turn to singing Murugan's golden feet. The praise is a long portrait of Siva, who taught the three poets, keeps the green lady at his side, begged alms, swallowed the sea's poison, burned the three cities and wears snake, Ganga, moon and herbs, and whom Vishnu and Brahma worship daily; Murugan taught the good to that Hara.
nuance: The force of the song is that the old body and the lust come in the same breath: the mind is still tied to women (மிடைபடு சித்தம்) when the teeth are gone. உரையொடு சொல் தெரிந்த மூவர்க்கும் ... போதித்து may point to the three Tevaram poets, and நகையாதே may mean 'without seeing through (laughing at) this illusion'; both are uncertain.

tamil: நிமிர்ந்த முதுகுங் குனிந்து சிறந்த முகமுந் திரங்கி
நெகிழ்ந்து சடலந் தளர்ந்து விளங்கு விழியங் கிருண்டு
டுமிழ்ந்து பலருங் கடிந்து சிறந்த வியலும் பெயர்ந்து
உ றைந்த உ யிருங் கழன்று ...... விடுநாள்முன்
உ கந்து மனமுங் குளிர்ந்து பயன்கொள் தருமம் புரிந்து
திமிந்தி யெனவெங் கணங்கள் குணங்கர் பலவுங் குழும்பி
சிரங்கை முழுதுங் குடைந்து நிணங்கொள் குடலுந் தொளைந்து
அமிழ்ந்தி மிகவும் பிணங்கள் அயின்று மகிழ்கொண்டு மண்ட
அலங்க லெனவெண் கடம்பு புனைந்து புணருங் குறிஞ்சி
reading: The poet pictures the straight back bent, the face wrinkled, the belly sagging, the stick, the dim eyes and wandering mind, the wife spitting at the sight, others scolding and life slipping away, and asks whether before that day he will do dharma that bears fruit with a glad, cool heart, humbly bow to Murugan and rejoice. The praise is the battle with old Sura, the vultures and ghouls in the blood, and Murugan who wore white kadamba and married the goddess of the kurinji hills.
nuance: Unlike most death songs, the plea is not for Murugan to come at the hour but for the poet to act before it: பயன்கொள் தருமம் புரிந்து, doing fruitful dharma, beside worship. The wife who spits (மனையாள் கண்டு உமிழ்ந்து) is the harshest touch in the picture.

reading: The poet cries jaya to the Death of the Nirutar, the vel praised by the gods and the son of the pure one, worshipping the feet night and day, and asks that Murugan end his weariness in the sea of births that rises like seven seas, set him in the assembly of his devotees, give him knowledge and take him as his own: when will that day come? The praise tells how, after Indra's long penance in the form of a bamboo, Siva sent Murugan to free the gods, and how he went with his host, overthrew the mountain and Sura, freed the gods and returned to Hara.
nuance: உனது அடியார் வாழ் சபையின் ஏற்றி, lifting him into the assembly where the devotees live, is the goal beside the ending of births. வேணுவின் உருவமாய் ... தவசினால் may allude to Indra hiding as a bamboo at Venupuram (Sirkazhi); I offer that identification as a guess.

tamil: ஆர வார மாயி ருந்து ஏம தூத ரோடி வந்து
ஆக மீதி லேசி வந்து ஊசி தானு மேநு ழைந்து
வீர மான சூரிகொண்டு நேரை நேரை யேபி ளந்து
வீடு வாச லான பெண்டிர் ஆசை யான மாதர் வந்து
நாடி யோடி வாற அன்பர் காண வேண தேபு கழ்ந்து
நீரின் மீதி லேயி ருந்த நீலி சூலி வாழ்வு மைந்த
நீல னாக வோடி வந்த சூரை வேறு வேறு கண்ட
reading: The poet pictures Death's messengers coming with a roar like the sea, piercing the body, crushing it like sugarcane in the mill and cutting it with daggers while people cry out, and the women of the house and the women he loved falling on him weeping; he asks Murugan to see this and come. The praise names the Goddess by many names, Nari, Suli, Ambai, Mahamayi, Neeli, the mountain daughter beside the Lord the Vedas praise, and Murugan her son, wearing kadamba, the child who cut Sura apart.
nuance: ஏமதூதர், Yama's messengers, here torture the body (ஆலைமீதிலே கரும்பு எனவே) rather than simply bind it, and the plea is the familiar one, கண்டு வருவாயே. Most of the praise is of the Goddess, not of Murugan.

tamil: நீரு மென்பு தோலி னாலு மாவ தென்கை கால்க ளோடு
நேச மொன்று தாதை தாய ராசை கொண்ட போதில் மேவி
தூரு மின்ப வாழ்வு மாகி யூன மொன்றி லாது மாத
ரோடு சிந்தை வேடை கூர ...... உ றவாகி
ஊழி யைந்த கால மேதி யோனும் வந்து பாசம் வீச
சூர னண்ட லோக மேன்மை சூறை கொண்டு போய் விடாது
தோளி லென்பு மாலை வேணி மீது கங்கை சூடி யாடு
பாரை யுண்ட மாயன் வேயை யூதி பண்டு பாவ லோர்கள்
பாத கங்கள் வேறி நூறி நீதி யின்சொல் வேத வாய்மை
reading: The poet says the body of water, bone and skin takes life when father and mother desire, grows as a child into the joys of youth and lust for women, and at the end the buffalo-rider comes and throws his noose; he asks whether the illusion by which this flesh perishes will not end. The praise names the vel against Sura, Siva wearing bones and Ganga with his peacock-like consort, Vishnu who swallowed the earth, played the flute and walked after the poets' song, and Murugan as the life of devotees who sing the truth of the Veda.
nuance: மேதியோன், the buffalo-rider, is Yama, and பாசம் வீச is his noose. பாவலோர்கள் பாடல் கண்டு ஏகும் மால is the story of Vishnu following a poet, as in 14. சூது மொழிவோனே, 'who speaks சூது' to Siva and his consort, I cannot place: it may mean subtle or secret words.

reading: The poet describes lovemaking in detail, the gem string snapped by nails, the drinking of lips, faltering speech, sounding bangles, the perfumed bed and the tight embrace, in which he gives his mind and knowledge over to women, and asks whether he will ever give one moment to worship. The praise names the vel, the peacock, the cock banner and the hunter girl as what the poets who compose flawless Tamil set at the centre of their verse, and Murugan as the guru who made bloom for the three-eyed father the meaning of the teaching that the quarrelling six sects cannot reach.
nuance: சட்சமயிகள், the six sects, deluded and quarrelling, cannot grasp the உபதேசப் பொருள் that Murugan gave Siva: the teaching story is set against sectarian argument. The Tamil poets who 'write and teach' (எழுதிக் கற்பித்துத் திரிபவர்) of the vel and the peacock are a self-portrait of the poet's own craft.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 13 of 21), sung at no named shrine: most confess the poet's bondage to courtesans who rob, drug and discard a man, and ask Murugan to end the infatuation; others ask for the reality beyond sects and scriptures, for the feet before Death or the scribe's fate comes, and for knowledge that roots out the bonds; the praise turns on Krishna, Rama and Siva, Murugan's own love-sickness for Valli, and Murugan as teacher of Siva.
structure_note: Courtesan songs: 1172, 1173, 1176, 1178, 1180, 1181, 1182, 1183, 1185; 1176 and 1183 share a 'showing' (காட்டி, காட்டுவர்) refrain. 1174 asks whether the ascetic's fall is fate or grace. 1175 and 1177 ask for the reality the sects cannot reach; 1179 is a litany of சாமி; 1184 is the householder's cares before Death; 1186 asks for knowledge that roots out the malas.
source_issues: Song 1172: the last word is spelt பெறுமாளே for பெருமாளே.
Song 1174: corrupt character in மடலு஡ர்தற்கு (line 398, probably மடலூர்தற்கு, 'to ride the palmyra horse').
Song 1180: the first half has five lines where the pattern needs six; a line seems lost after line 524.
Song 1181: unflagged garble '....... ; ளையோனே' at line 563, probably இளையோனே.
Song 1182: several lines look garbled (பெங்கும் line 573, பூன்கண் line 574, lines 576 to 578).
Song 1185: corrupt character in தசக்஡ண (line 658, probably தசக்ரீவ, Ravana); the ஡ண for ரீ pattern.
Song 1186: unflagged garble யற்முதுடை at line 671.

reading: The poet describes dancing women with pearl strings on their breasts, harsh eyes and a great appetite for wealth, who give their lips' nectar to young men struck by Kama's sugarcane bow, and asks whether his wandering, caught in their cheating and lost to grace, will not end so that he may cling to Murugan's feet. The praise names the war on the mad elephant-faced demon where ghouls play in blood and the eighteen hosts dance, Murugan's love for the kuravar girl born to a sage absorbed in tapas, and the guru who named a stubborn poet 'egg' and won a poem from him.
nuance: மெத்தத் திரவிய பட்சத்தியர், women very fond of money, makes them the paid women. முற்பட்ட முரட்டுப் புலவனை முட்டைப் பெயர் செப்பிக் கவிபெறு refers to a story of Murugan mocking a proud poet that I cannot identify with confidence; the deer (உழை) and the sage point to Valli's birth.

tamil: பலர்பொருள்க வர்ந்திடைக லாமிட் டோ ட்டிகள் ...... கொடிதாய
யுடனுருவு பங்குடைய நாகக் காப்பனும் ...... உ றிதாவும்
உ ரலொடுத வழ்ந்தநவ நீதக் கூற்றனு ...... மதிகோபக்
reading: The poet describes women who dance and sing, rob many men and then pick quarrels to drive them out, weep and rub their eyes as if in love, and are Death in the shape of desire with glances like arrows; perfumed with lilies, musk and rosewater in the south wind, he falls on their breasts and melts till dawn, and asks whether a day will come when Murugan protects him. The praise names Siva with Parvati at his side, Krishna bound to the mortar by the cowherd women for stealing butter, Indra on his elephant who came to worship, and Murugan who was angry with Brahma, guarded the gods' city, toppled Krauncha and routed the demons.
nuance: பலர் பொருள் கவர்ந்து இடை கலாமிட்டு ஓட்டிகள, they take many men's wealth and drive them out with a quarrel, is the Naladiyar's picture of the courtesan. ஆசைக் கூற்றிகள் and பார்வைக் கூற்றினர் call the women Death. விபுதர்பதி அங்கதலம் மேவிச் சாற்றிய தமிழ்நூல் seems to tie the south wind to a hill where Tamil was first told, perhaps Pothigai; that is uncertain.

tamil: பழுதற வோதிக் கடந்து பகைவினை தீரத் துறந்து
பரிமள பாணத் தயர்ந்து பனைமட லு஡ர்தற் கிசைந்து
அழுதழு தாசைப் படுங்க ணபிநய மாதர்க் கிரங்கி
எழுதரு வேதத்து மன்றி முழுதினு மாய்நிற்கு மெந்தை
இருவுரு வாகித் துலங்கி யொருகன தூணிற் பிறந்து
பொழுதிசை யாவிக்ர மன்தன் மருகபு ராரிக்கு மைந்த
reading: The poet says that though he studied without fault, renounced to end hostile karma and sat in many yogas, Kama's fragrant arrows wore him down until he was ready to ride the palmyra horse, and he melted for women weeping with acting eyes; he asks whether this ruin is the fate of his former deeds or the will of Murugan's grace, for in his confusion he cannot tell. The praise names the father present in the Veda and in all things, Vishnu who came from the pillar in two forms and split Hiranya's chest, Murugan as his nephew and as son of Siva, and the lord who ran into the millet field for the forest deer-girl.
nuance: The song's question is explicit: முற்பயந்த விதிவசமோ, மற்றை உன்றன் அருள்வசமோ, fate of past deeds or your grace's will? It is left unanswered. That the renouncer and yogi is the one who agrees to ride the madal (பனைமடல் ஊர்தற்கு இசைந்து) turns the akam lover's last resort into an ascetic's fall. ஞானக் குருந்து may recall the kuruntham tree of 7.

tamil: பாணிக்குட் படாது சாதகர் காணச்சற் றொணாது வாதிகள்
ஏணிக்கெட் லொணாது மீதுயர் சேணுக்குச் சமான நூல்வழி
ஏதுச்செப் பொணாத தோர்பொருள் சேரத்துக் கமாம கோததி
ஆணிப்பொற் ப்ரதாப மேருவை வேலிட்டுக் கடாவி வாசவன்
ஆழிச்சத் ரசாயை நீழலி லாதித்தப் ப்ரகாச நேர்தர
வாசிக்கப் படாத வாசகம் ஈசர்க்குச் சுவாமி யாய்முதல்
reading: The poet describes a reality that cannot be held, cannot be glimpsed by practitioners or spoken by debaters, is not caught in the five elements, is not reached by other means, by imagined meditation, by the ladder of the desiring mind or by the path of books, nor stated by reasons, a great ocean of bliss, and asks whether he will bow to Murugan's sandal-scented feet. The praise names the vel driven into golden Meru to end Indra's danger, the rule of the world's circle under the shade of a single umbrella, Murugan who wears on his head the jewelled anklet feet of the hunter girl, and the teacher who first made Siva read the word that cannot be read.
nuance: The plea is built from negatives (படாது, ஒணாது, தகாது, பெறாது), a way of naming the One by what cannot reach it. வாசிக்கப் படாத வாசகம், the unread word, taught to Siva is the Om story, though Om is not named. கிராதை நூபுர ... பாதசேகர, he who wears Valli's feet as a crown, reverses the usual devotee's posture.

tamil: பால்மொழி படித்துக் காட்டி ஆடையை நெகிழ்த்துக் காட்டி
மேல்நக மழுத்திக் காட்டி தோதக விதத்தைக் காட்டி
மேவிடு மயக்கைத் தீர்த்து சீர்பத நினைப்பைக் கூட்டு
காலனை யுதைத்துக் காட்டி யாவியை வதைத்துக் காட்டி
கானினில் நடித்துக் காட்டி யாலமு மிடற்றிற் காட்டி
மாலுற நிறத்தைக் காட்டி வேடுவர் புனத்திற் காட்டில்
மான்மகள் தனத்தைச் சூட்டி ஏனென அழைத்துக் கேட்டு
reading: The poet lists what women show a man, reading milky speech, loosening their clothes, seating him on the bed, giving their lips, opening the books of love, rolling their eyes, pressing their nails and showing their tricks, and asks that Murugan end his delusion for them and show him the greatness of thinking of his feet. The praise uses the same refrain of showing for Siva, who kicked Death, danced in the forest at the end of time, held the poison and burned Kama, and for Murugan, who in the hunters' millet field showed himself worn with love, embraced the deer-girl and showed the skill of a happy life.
nuance: The verb காட்டி ends almost every phrase on both sides of the song: the women display their arts, Siva displays his deeds, and the poet asks Murugan to display (காட்டி) the eminence of the feet. தோதகம் is deceit. Some phrases of the Valli part (வாலிபம் இளைத்து) are hard to construe.

reading: Calling on the lord of the cock banner who fought the Nirutar and Krauncha and wed the kuravar girl, the poet asks that with tears pouring from both eyes and a mind brimming with love, as the body of elements, the life within it and the inner faculties fall away and he himself is lost, he may know by awareness what the debaters and sects call 'it is' and 'it is not'. The praise names Kama with his makara banner, Tamil breeze from the Malaya hills, flower arrows and sugarcane bow, burned by the eye of Siva, and Murugan as the son given by Abhirami, Sankari, the mountain daughter, delight of the gods' elephant-girl.
nuance: யானும் இழந்த இடந்தனில் உணர்வாலே, by awareness in the place where I too am lost, puts knowledge after the loss of body, breath, faculties and self, not after argument. ஆமென அன்றென நின்றதை, that which stands as both 'yes' and 'no', is what the sects dispute.

reading: The poet describes women who knit their brows, flash carp eyes, spread their hair, wave bangled hands, lead a man to an aloe-scented bed in a crystal chamber, embrace him, mark him with nails and give the nectar of their lips, and asks whether, rid of the madness these melting women give, he will strive to worship Murugan. The praise is a long portrait of Siva, the dancer, burner of Tripura, holder of the poison, Ganga on his head, Uma's lord on the mountain, who cuts birth, smears cremation ash, rides the bull and burned Madana, and names Murugan as born of his boundless grace.
nuance: உருக்கிகள், the women who melt a man, and தருபித்து, the madness they give, frame the plea, which is only to try (முயல்வேனோ) to worship. Murugan is called the one who arose within Siva's compassion (க்ருபைக்குள் உதித்தருள்).

tamil: புவிக்குன் பாத மதைநினை பவர்க்குங் கால தரிசனை
புரட்டும் பாத சமயிகள் நெறிக்கண் பூது படிறரை
கவிக்கொண் டாடு புகழினை படிக்கும் பாடு திறமிலி
கலக்குண் டாகு புவிதனி லெனக்குண் டாகு பணிவிடை
சிவத்தின் சாமி மயில்மிசை நடிக்குஞ் சாமி யெமதுளெ
செழிக்குஞ் சாமி பிறவியை யொழிக்குஞ் சாமி பவமதை
தவத்தின் சாமி புரிபிழை பொறுக்குஞ் சாமி குடிநிலை
சதைக்குஞ் சாமி யெமைபணி விதிக்குஞ் சாமி சரவண
reading: The poet confesses that he does not know the sight that those who think of Murugan's feet attain, falls in with the deceiving sectarians who twist the path, has no skill to sing his praise and whirls in sin like a lazy dog, and asks whether Murugan does not know the account of service due to him in this troubled world. The praise is a litany of சாமி: the lord of Sivam, who dances on the peacock, shines within us, ends birth, forgives faults, grinds the demons to dust, ordains our service, and the one of Saravana who is called 'the father's Swami'.
nuance: தகப்பன் சாமி, his father's lord, is the title from the story of Murugan teaching Siva. எனக்கு உண்டாகு பணிவிடை கணக்கு, the reckoning of service that falls to me, asks to be given work rather than release. The first lines (காலதரிசனை, புலக்கண், புழுக்கண் பாவம்) are hard to construe.

reading: The poet says he gives no thought to what would end the pleasure he takes in women's carp eyes, fragrant hair and pot-like breasts, but quarrels with all, spends his days and whirls like a spun top until he falls; he asks Murugan to end his fear of the hour life leaves. The praise names the destruction of the Sura clans so that Indra and the gods were freed, the sea trembling and Meru crumbling, and Murugan who, pained by the south wind, evening and Kama's attack, went to the hunters' millet field and bowed to the dark-eyed Valli.
nuance: The same south wind and Kama that drive the poet to women make Murugan himself love-sick (வேடை எனும்படி சிந்தை நொந்திட) for Valli: the song puts the god in the lover's place. The top (பம்பரம்) spinning and falling is the poet's life.

reading: The poet says he cannot cross the ocean of desire for proud pleasure-women with carp eyes and ear-studs, or the ocean of tantra, ritual, Veda and Agama whose shore he never sees; he has not sung the anklet feet and has no love, yet asks the guru for grace. The praise names the saving of Indra's city, the end of the night-walkers, the mountain split and the sea roaring as the vel broke the mango, and Murugan in the millet field begging the hunter's girl to save his life from the south wind and Kama's flower arrows.
nuance: The two oceans are set side by side: desire (ஆசை என்கிற பாராவாரம்) and the endless scriptures (தந்த்ர க்ரியா வேதாகம கலையாய ஆழி); neither can be crossed, and the poet admits even love is lacking (நேசிலன்). Murugan's own plea to Valli, காமவிடாய் கெடும்படி காவாய் ஆவியை, echoes the poet's.

tamil: பொங்குங் கொடிய கூற்றனு நஞ்சும் பொதுவில் நோக்கிய
பொன்கண் டிளகு கூத்திகள் பூன்கண் கலவி வேட்டுயிர்
குன்றங் கதிரை பூப்பர முன்துன் றமரர் போற்றிய
எங்கும் பகர மாய்க்கெடி விஞ்சும் பகழி வீக்கிய
விந்தம் பணிய வாய்த்தரு ளந்தண் புவன நோற்பவை
எங்குங் கலுமி யார்த்தெழ எங்குஞ் சுருதி கூப்பிட
என்றென் றவச மாய்த்தொழு தென்றும் புதிய கூட்டமொ
reading: The poet speaks of dancing women who cast nets of eyes that look like Death and poison and melt only at the sight of gold, and of his enslavement in their embrace, and asks whether, his infatuation ended, there will be a day when he praises the sacred hills, among them Sonagiri, Kathirai and the Kundram. The praise names the hunters with their bows who bow at the lotus feet, and the deer-girl who scared the birds from the millet field, with whom Murugan spends his days with ever-new companions.
nuance: பொன்கண்டு இளகு கூத்திகள், dancing girls who soften at the sight of gold, makes them the paid women. The list of hills in lines 576 to 579 is too garbled to read with confidence; சோண (Sonagiri, Tiruvannamalai) and கதிரை (Kathirkamam) are the clearest names.

tamil: உ ததி யமுதென நிகழ்த்திக் கேட்பவர் ...... பொடிமாயம்
உ றவு கலவியை விடுத்திட் டாட்கொள ...... நினையாதோ
reading: The poet lists what common women show young men, rolled eyes, swaying breast-chains, loosened hair, smiles, slipping clothes, dancing feet, and how they embrace them till they melt, strip them of all they own, give drugs that burn the belly and draw out their very life; he asks whether Murugan will not free him from that union and take him. The praise names Krishna who kicked the marutha trees, broke the cowherd women's pots, was beaten with a rope and wept, split Hiranya's chest and held up the hill against the rain, and Murugan his nephew whose vel tore Sura's kin and whose lotus feet are praised.
nuance: பொதுமாதர், women common to all, and உடைமை அடையவே பறித்து, stripping a man of everything he owns, are explicit; பொடிமாயம் and மருத்திட்டு ஆட்டிகள் add the love-drug, as in 1161. காட்டுவர் closes every phrase of the first half, as காட்டி does in 1176.

reading: The poet speaks of the children he must support and the wife who must be fed, the toil of seeking gold and the mind's great agitation, all as the chain Brahma writes decrees, and asks that before Death comes to the burning ground to take his life, he may praise 'Kanda of the sandal shoulders' and Murugan end his torment and give his feet. The praise names Siva the skull-bearer who took blows from Arjuna, rode the bull, burned Kama with his eye, danced in the fire and swallowed the poison, and Murugan who gave him the meaning, and who gives his loving devotees release from sin and a fearless heart.
nuance: வண்போதன் தீட்டும் தொடரது படியே, according to the chain the lotus-born writes, makes the householder's cares Brahma's script for him. பார்த்தன் கையில் அடி உண்டு is the story of Siva as the hunter struck by Arjuna. The first half is hard to construe in places (வம்பாருந் தேக்குண் டிட).

reading: The poet runs through a woman's charms, the waist like Kama's bow, the elephant gait, the lotus feet, the musk-scented hair, the makara earrings, the bud-like breasts, the honey lips, the ear-long eyes, the jasmine smile and the moon forehead, and asks whether a day will come when Murugan ends the swooning infatuation he feels for every limb and takes him. The praise names Rama who bridged the sea, burned the city, ended Sita's grief and rolled the ten heads of Ravana with one arrow, Siva who burned the three cities with Meru for a bow, and Murugan who restored the gods to their city and smashed Sura and the mountain.
nuance: The catalogue, each item ending in -க்கே (for the waist, for the gait ...), is itself the infatuation: அவயவம் அனைத்தூடினும் அவசமுறு மயல், a swoon at every limb. Rama and Siva are praised as Murugan's kin in one sweep.

reading: The poet says that by Kama's arrows and the two kinds of deeds his body of earth and sea dances on, and asks that the maya of the mind and the hard deeds be cut away with the old impurity at its root, that he gain the joy of knowledge in experience, and play with the devotees at the feet; he asks Murugan to come before him on his steed, full of compassion and knowledge, with the gods raining flowers, bright as crores of white moons. The praise names the countless women waving fans, sun and moon as lamps, the matted sages and Vedic chanters around Siva, and Murugan his son, lord of Valli, Vishnu's nephew, the lord of Tamil.
nuance: மனமாயை, இருகாழ்வினை, மலம் வேரற names the three bonds of Saiva Siddhanta (maya, karma, anava) and asks for them to be cut at the root, followed by ஞான அநுபூதி, knowledge as lived experience. The garbled யற்முதுடை (line 671) leaves one word unread.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 14 of 21), named for no shrine: most confess the poet's bondage to courtesans and their embraces and ask for the feet, the gift of song or knowledge; others give the funeral and Death's crowd, a clause-by-clause inventory of old age, a mother's lament for her lovesick daughter, and in 1200 Murugan selling himself as Valli's slave. The praise turns on the churning of the ocean, the Mahabharata told almost whole, and Murugan as Siva's teacher.
structure_note: Courtesan and lovemaking songs (1190, 1191, 1193, 1195, 1197 to 1201); the funeral and death (1187, 1196); old age (1194); an akam lament in a mother's voice (1189); a plea for the One beyond the elements (1188); 1192 mixes the plea for mind's dissolution with Nakkirar's Tamil. Several songs (1191, 1194, 1201) end on Murugan as the one who taught Tamil or the silent Veda.
source_issues: 1187: the line before the last ends with a stray '....... ;' before ளையோனே (probably இளையோனே).
1188: the glyph ஡ stands for ஊ in ஞான்று஡து (ஞான்றூது, line 17); வீழந்தாவல் for வீழ்ந்தாவல் (line 9).
1189: the glyph ஡ stands for ஊ in குழலு஡தி (குழலூதி, line 3); சூரர்அகாடு (line 15) appears garbled.
1193: lines 5 and 6 (விநன்முசிப், வன்சர மென்முவா) appear garbled.
1197: ஆகாஎ நாளினில் probably for ஆக எந்நாளினில்.
1195: initial உ split from its word (உ ற்பித்து).

reading: The poet pictures a life of walled mansions, gold in the house and many women around him, lived drunk and deluded, until on the last day the body is tied to the bier, friends wail and beat their chests and the limbed doll is given to the fire; he asks whether grace will not end this misery and set him holding Murugan's two sandals. The praise tells the churning of the sea with the golden mountain and the serpent rope, the poison that sent the gods into hiding, and Siva who held it, Murugan's father; it ends with his wooing of the hunter girl while the seven worlds laughed, and the heads of Sura cut off.
nuance: இருபாதுகையைப் பற்றி நிற்க: the poet asks to hold Murugan's sandals (பாதுகை), not his feet, a humbler image of refuge. பாவை, 'doll', for the corpse makes the body a puppet once its life is gone. The line on the hunter girl and the laughing worlds is hard to divide, and its end is corrupt.

reading: The poet asks for the One that Murugan spoke when Siva, who wears the bones of the dead, bowed to him, the thing that shines when the five elements, the inner instruments and the 'I' all subside; having reached desirelessness and fallen melting at the feet, he asks whether Murugan will not know that the cry 'Sentha, refuge, refuge' is never in vain. The praise tells of Vishnu who measured the worlds coming alone with the discus when the elephant in the pond cried 'Lord, my life is going', and ends with the peacock-like girl of the hills in the fragrant grove.
nuance: நான்போய் ஒடுங்க அடங்கலும் மாய்ந்தால் விளங்கும் அது ஒன்றினை: the plea is for what appears only when the elements, the கரணங்கள் and the self are gone, a doctrinal request rather than a confession. வேண்டாமை, desirelessness, is named as already reached. The elephant's cry is Gajendra's.

tamil: மாறுபொரு கால னொக்கும் வானிலெழு மாம திக்கும்
மாயமட வார்த மக்கும் ஆயர்குழ லு஡தி சைக்கும்
வேறுபடு பாய லுக்கு மேயெனது பேதை யெய்த்து
வேடர்குல மாதி னுக்கு வேடைகெட வேந டித்து
ஆறுமிடை வாள ரக்கர் நீறுபட வேலெ டுத்த
ஆழியுல கேழ டக்கி வாசுகியை வாய டக்கி
சீறுபட மேரு வெற்பை நீறுபட வேசி னத்த
சேருமட லால்மி குத்த சூரர்அகாடு போய டைத்த
reading: In a mother's voice, the singer says her innocent girl is worn down by love: by the moon that rises like Death, the sleepless sea, the deceitful women who speak blame, the cowherd's flute, the cold north wind, Kama, and the bed that has turned strange; she asks Murugan, who once played the hunter to end the hunter girl's longing, to come on his two feet before her changed body wastes away. The praise names the six-faced lord of the vel, the peacock that holds Vasuki in its beak, and the release of the gods from Sura's prison.
nuance: This is akam, the classical pangs of the lovesick girl spoken by her mother, as in 24: the moon, the sea, the wind and the herdsman's flute all wound her, and வசையே சொல் மாய மடவார், the gossiping women, are the town's blame (alar). The daughter's lover is the god himself.

tamil: மின்னினில்ந டுக்க முற்ற நுண்ணியநு சுப்பில் முத்த
விம்மியிள கிக்க தித்த கொம்மைமுலை யிற்கு னித்த
கன்னல்மொழி யிற்சி றக்கு மன்னநடை யிற்க றுத்த
கண்ணழிவு வைத்த புத்தி ஷண்முகநி னைக்க வைத்த
அன்னநடை யைப்ப ழித்த மஞ்ஞைமலை யிற்கு றத்தி
அன்னையிறு கப்பி ணித்த பன்னிருதி ருப்பு யத்தில்
பொன்னுலகி னைப்பு ரக்கு மன்னநல்வ்ர தத்தை விட்ட
பொன்மலைவ ளைத்தெ ரித்த கண்ணுதலி டத்தி லுற்ற
reading: The poet lists the charms of women who sell themselves, the trembling waist, pearl smile, curved brow, sugared speech, swan's walk, dark eyes and red mouth, and says that the karma which, while his mind lay degraded in them, made him think of the six-faced one is something he will never forget. The praise has Valli playing in the millet field, binding Murugan's twelve arms, and the golden mountain bent as a bow to burn the three cities of those who abandoned their vow.
nuance: கண்ணழிவு வைத்த புத்தி ஷண்முக நினைக்க வைத்த கன்மவசம்: the poet appears to thank karma itself for turning his fallen mind toward Murugan, an unusual twist where the song ends in a vow (மறவேனே) rather than a request. The Tripura dwellers are called those who left the good vow (நல்வ்ரதத்தை விட்ட புன்மையர்).

tamil: முத்தமு லாவு தனத்தியர் சித்தச னாணை செலுத்திகள்
முட்டவி லாவி மருட்டிகள் நெட்டிலை வேலின் விழிச்சியர்
தத்தைக ளாசை விதத்தியர் கற்புர தோளின் மினுக்கிகள்
தட்டழி யாது திருப்புகழ் கற்கவு மோதவு முத்தமிழ்
மத்தக யானை யுரித்தவர் பெற்றகு மார இலட்சுமி
வற்றிட வாரிதி முற்றிய வெற்றிகொள் சூரர் பதைப்புற
சித்திர மான குறத்தியை யுற்றொரு போது புனத்திடை
செச்சையு லாவு பதத்தின மெய்த்தவர் வாழ்வு பெறத்தரு
reading: The poet describes women who enforce Kama's command, melt young men, have spear eyes and 'thirty crore minds', and asks that, not ruined by them, he be granted to learn and recite Thiruppugazh and the knowledge of the tattvas in threefold Tamil. The praise names Siva who flayed the elephant, Vishnu as uncle, the vel that dried the sea against Sura, Valli embraced in the field, and Murugan who gives the true ascetics their life.
nuance: திருப்புகழ் கற்கவும் ஓதவும்: the song asks for the book's own name, the praise of the Lord as a thing to learn and recite. முப்பது கோடி மனத்தியர், women of thirty crore minds, is the poet's figure for their fickleness.

reading: The poet describes women whose hair, lips and spear eyes undo men, who drive them like the sea and make them seem mad, and whose embrace melts body and life like wax in fire, and asks that, with craving for the world removed, Murugan keep him and rule him at the golden feet where the mind is dissolved. The praise recalls the vel that stretched out for the Tamil of Nakkirar at the Madurai Koodal hill, Murugan's search for the hunter girl, and the moment when, to please moon-crowned Siva, he sent his peacock round the world.
nuance: மனோலயம், dissolution of the mind, occurs twice: first in the women's embrace, then at the feet the poet asks for, as if the same melting were sought in its true place. நக்கீரர் ஓதிய தமிழுக்காக நீடிய கரவோனே: the hand stretched out for Nakkirar's Tamil, the poet of Murugan's own praise. The peacock sent round the world in an instant points to the contest for the fruit, though the fruit is not named. Several runs in the first half are hard to divide.

reading: The poet describes women with cloth over their breasts, crescent brows and eyes blacked with collyrium, whom he sought out until his heart, infatuated and scattered, could not join Murugan's work, and asks whether this deceit will never leave him. The praise names Murugan as companion of the devotees who praise him steadily through tapas, bridegroom of Devayanai born for the gods' welfare, and the vel that broke the mountain and defeated Sura who came hidden in a deceiving form.
nuance: நின்செயல் மருவாமல் கலங்கும் வஞ்சகம்: the deceit is the poet's own, a heart that will not join the Lord's work. Lines 5 and 6 (விநன்முசிப், வன்சர மென்முவா) appear garbled.

reading: The poet sets out old age clause by clause: strength gone, pride broken, years spent, teeth fallen, back bent like a bow, face dimmed, sight darkened, cough come, sleep gone, speech failing, tongue fallen, mind fading, limbs that will not stretch, diseases lodged, the mat reached and the stench of filth risen, and says 'now it is a matter of a moment, come before me in grace'. The praise has the vel thrown against the demons who imprisoned Indra, Valli wooed in the millet field and married in the sight of the world, and Murugan who expounded clear Sentamil to his devotees.
nuance: Each clause ends in அது (ஒழிந்தது, உதிர்ந்தது, வளைந்தது), so the decay is told as a running inventory, one verb at a time. நிமிஷம் இங்கு இனி ஆச்சுது: the plea is for grace at the very last minute, with no confession of women.

reading: The poet confesses wandering round the lies of petty women who teach Kama's arts with their carp eyes and draw men to perfumed golden beds, calls himself base, and asks for the one day when Murugan will make him fit, teach him to worship his feet and grant his mind grace. The praise, in drum syllables, shows Siva's dance and calls Murugan the guru who gave grace to siddhas, the pure freed ones and devotees, the destroyer of Tripura's demons who freed the gods, with the cock banner.
nuance: உனதடி அர்ச்சிக்க: what the poet asks to be taught is ritual worship of the feet. The battle lines (திக்குக்குத் திகுதிகு, டுட்டுட்டு) are rhythm, not words.

reading: The poet pictures Death with a crore of spears pressing to waste his life while the women he loved still cling, and the elders and young saying 'what's left to do, is he dead?', carrying him to the burning ground and saying he will fall into the seven hells, a wretch without fortune; he asks Murugan to come with the Vedas sounding while the worlds, the gods and the sages praise him. The praise retells the Mahabharata: Dharma losing the land at dice, twelve years in the forest, the stay at Virata's court and the cattle raid, the embassy, Duryodhana's death in the war, and Vishnu who drove Arjuna's chariot, Murugan's uncle.
nuance: ஏது கருமம் இவர் சாவெனா: the kin's words over the dying man are quoted, coldly practical. இருவாறு வருஷம், two sixes of years, is the Pandavas' twelve-year exile; the praise gives the epic in sequence rather than as single epithets.

reading: The poet, beaten about by women whose mouths drip honey and whose sulks are their gift, calls himself a sinful utter fool and asks on what day, before he becomes the work of misfortune, Murugan will grant him the work of his service. The praise names Vishnu whose arrows scattered Ravana's crowns, Murugan's uncle, and the lord who lived with the hunter girl in the small hut of the forest people.
nuance: முகடித் தொழில் against அடிமைத் தொழில்: the work of Mudevi, goddess of ill fortune, set against the work of service to the Lord, if முகடி is read so. ஆகாஎ நாளினில் is probably a garble of ஆக எந்நாளினில்.

reading: The poet describes plainly his nights with common women, the necklace, the betel-reddened lips, the loosened silk, and says that even while his mind practises the arts of love he will not forget the sword in Murugan's hand, the protection of his golden feet adorned with vetchi flowers, and his jewelled anklets. The praise is a battlefield: demon cities burned, asuras pierced, and countless ghouls dragging corpses, drumming and laughing while birds fly.
nuance: மறவேனே: as in 1007 the song ends with a vow of remembrance inside the passion, not a plea for escape from it.

tamil: வளைகர மாட்டி வேட்டி னிடைதுயில் வாட்டி யீட்டி
மழைகுழல் காட்டி வேட்கை வளர்முலை காட்டி நோக்கின்
புளகித வார்த்தை யேற்றி வரிகலை வாழ்த்தி யீழ்த்து
பொதுமட வார்க்கு ஏற்ற வழியுறு வாழ்க்கை வேட்கை
தொளையொழு கேற்ற நோக்கி பலவகை வாச்சி தூர்த்து
துணைவன்மை நோக்கி னிடைமுறை யாய்ச்சி மார்ச் சொல்
இளநகை யோட்டி மூட்டர் குலம்விழ வாட்டி யேட்டை
இயல்புவி வாழ்த்தி யேத்த எனதிடர் நோக்கி நோக்க
reading: The poet describes the common women who show their hair, breasts and peacock walk and kindle infatuation with thrilling words, and asks Murugan to drive out and change the base nature that craves a life fit for them. The praise names the devotees who praise his radiant feet with instruments, the women who fed and played with the child Murugan, the god who scattered the fools' clan with a smile and restored the gods' song, and the guru who saw the poet's trouble and rescued him by showing him his two deeds.
nuance: இருவினை காட்டி மீட்ட: rescue comes by being shown one's own two kinds of deed. ஆய்ச்சிமார், cowherd women, who feed and bathe the child are hard to identify; they may be the foster-mothers of Murugan's birth or a borrowing from Krishna's story.

reading: The poet asks whether he should be caught in the deceiving net of play-acting dancing women, called a madman by the whole world, losing shame, custom, conduct, justice and sense, and become the slave of the slaves of dogs. The praise answers with Murugan's own servitude: to the hunter girl dressed in peacock feathers and leaves on the platform with her sling, he said 'I am your hereditary slave', clasped her feet again and again, and with the Vedas, the gods and the world's rim as witness sold himself and had it written on Meru.
nuance: The two halves mirror each other: the poet fears becoming a slave (நாயடிமையும் அடிமைப்பட்டு) to women of deceit, while the god freely declares himself Valli's வழியடிமை, sold (விலைப்பட்டு) by a deed inscribed on Meru. Bondage to desire and bondage in love are set side by side.

reading: After a long and frank picture of lovemaking until the two seem one, the poet asks that even in the days when his mind is lost in that passion he be given ways to praise Murugan's two feet, the vel hand that casts out karma, his holy face beyond depicting, and his grace. The praise has Vishnu and Brahma pressing his feet, a battlefield of ghouls, vultures and Bhairavas, and calls Murugan the supreme guru who showed the Lord of the matted hair the silent way that the ancient Veda gives.
nuance: எனது மனது அழியும் நாட்களினும் ... ஏத்தும் வகை தரவேணும்: praise is asked for within the passion, not after it. பழய மறை தரு மவுன வழி: what Murugan teaches Siva is named here as the silent way of the Veda, without Om.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 15 of 21), named for no shrine: most confess bondage to courtesans who seek money and ask for the feet, knowledge or release; others ask to be freed from the round of wombs, picture the corpse carried to the pyre and Yama's summons, and offer a garland of letters; a long litany of the Goddess, Sambandar's impaling of the Jains and Kannappar's offering appear in the praise.
structure_note: Courtesan and lovemaking songs (1202, 1206 to 1208, 1210, 1213, 1214, 1216); the corpse and death (1203, 1204, 1215); rebirth (1205); self-abuse and the plea for non-dual knowledge (1209, 1211); a song offered as a garland (1212).
source_issues: 1203: corrupt glyph in பிண஧முடி (line 1); புர்முணும் (line 10) probably for புரமூணும்.
1211: corrupt glyph in மோகாச஡ணத (line 3); விபாணதன் and மாறாம காரிலெனையினி are obscure, possibly garbled.
1214: the glyph ஡ stands for ஊ in வாயிலு஡றல் (வாயிலூறல், line 7); initial உ split from its word (உ மையாயி).
1207: initial உ split from its word (உ ருக்கி, உ ழைக்கும்).

tamil: வேலொத்து வென்றி யங்கை வேளுக்கு வெஞ்ச ரங்க
கோலத்தை விஞ்ச வெஞ்சொல் கோடித்து வஞ்ச நெஞ்சர்
கோதற்ற நின்ப தங்கள் நேர்பற்றி யின்ப மன்பு
ஞாலத்தை யன்ற ளந்து வேலைக்கு ளுந்து யின்று
நாடத்த டஞ்சி லம்பை மாவைப்பி ளந்த டர்ந்து
ஆலித்தெ ழுந்த டர்ந்த ஆலத்தை யுண்ட கண்ட
ஆதிக்கு மைந்த னென்று நீதிக்குள் நின்ற அன்பர்
reading: The poet describes women whose eyes are Kama's arrows, arms bamboo, breasts hills and hair darker than clouds, and asks that he no longer stand again and again in the houses of the deceitful-hearted, but that his mind come near Murugan's flawless feet with joy and love. The praise has Vishnu who measured the earth, the vel that split the hill and the mango and shook the serpents' world, Siva who drank the poison and dances with his consort, and Murugan who says 'fear not' in danger to the devotees who stand in justice.
nuance: வஞ்ச நெஞ்சர் கூடத்தில் நின்று நின்று: the repeated நின்று gives the poet's loitering at the women's doors.

tamil: அனைவோரும் வந்து சிச்சி யெனநால்வ ருஞ்சி ரிக்க
கடையேன்ம லங்கள் முற்று மிருநோயு டன்பி டித்த
களிகூர என்ற னுக்கு மயிலேறி வந்து முத்தி
சடைமீது கங்கை வைத்து விடையேறு மெந்தை சுத்த
தவிடாக வந்தெ திர்த்த மதனாக முஞ்சி தைத்த
மிடிதீர அண்ட ருக்கு மயிலேறி வஞ்சர் கொட்டம்
மினநூல்ம ருங்குல் பொற்பு முலைமாதி ளங்கு றத்தி
reading: The poet takes the corpse of one ruined by offence, whom all mock with 'chi, chi' while even the four bearers laugh and which burns to nothing in the fire, and asks that in the same way his impurities, with the two diseases and the Kali age, die, so that he becomes pure space and Murugan comes on the peacock to give release. The praise names Siva of the Ganga and the bull who laughed the three cities to husk and burned Kama with his eye, whose guru Murugan is, and his dance on the peacock for the gods.
nuance: அடியார் மனம் சலிக்க ... அபராதம் வந்து கெட்ட பிணம்: the image seems to be the corpse of one who grieved the devotees, made the model for the death the poet wants for his own malas. சுத்த வெளியாகி, becoming pure space, names the goal. The first line has a corrupt glyph and the division of the opening clauses is uncertain.

reading: The first half is the talk of mourners over a body: don't leave the corpse at the threshold, raise a tall bier before it rots, deck it, call the drummers, stop the weeping, lift it before it stinks; and the poet asks that on the day his kin carry him to the burning ground, Murugan come quickly on the peacock with the hunters' daughter to guard his life. The praise tells of the elephant seized by the crocodile in the pond and Vishnu who came on Garuda blowing the conch, the vel thrown against the demons, and the gods resettled in their golden land.
nuance: As in 21 the confession is made through quoted speech: the kin's instructions over the body (எடுமின் யாக்கையை) show how quickly the person becomes a thing to be disposed of.

tamil: அப்படி யேழு மேழும்வ குத்துவ ழாது போதினி
அக்ஷர தேவி கோவின்வி திப்படி மாறி மாறிய
டிப்படி யோனி வாய்தொறு முற்பவி யாவி ழாவுல
கற்பக வேழ மேய்வன பச்சிள ஏனல் மீதுறை
கற்புர தூளி லேபன மற்புய பாக சாதன
விப்ரச மூக வேதன பச்சிம பூமி காவல
மெத்திய ஆழி சேறெழ வெற்பொடு சூர னீறெழ
reading: The poet says that, by the decree of Brahma, consort of the goddess of letters, he has taken every form of body again and again, born at the mouth of every womb and stumbling through the world for aeons he cannot count, and asks Murugan to grant that he not be born again. The praise names the hunter girl of the green millet field where the elephant came, Indra's world upheld, the guardian of the western land, and the vel hurled so that the sea turned to mud and Sura and the mountain to ash.
nuance: அக்ஷர தேவி கோவின் விதிப்படி: birth is assigned by Brahma's writ, the lord of Sarasvati. The opening (அப்படி ஏழும் ஏழும் வகுத்து, அக்ரம் வியோம கோளகை) and the Sanskrit run of epithets in the praise are hard to divide.

reading: The poet describes lovemaking with women whose eyes close and speech falters, and admits that alone he cannot give up the embrace, so asks for Murugan's young feet rich in compassion. The praise has Siva of Kailas, Indra of the thunderbolt, Brahma and Vishnu on Garuda who tears the serpent's hoods, and the vel buried in clouds, sky, sea, mountain and the demon's chest.
nuance: தமியேனால் தவிரொணாது: the poet confesses he cannot leave it by his own strength, so the feet must be given.

reading: The poet describes women who call young men, draw out a great deal of money, embrace them on beds and melt them, and says he is drained, his tongue dry, living in fear and shame; he asks Murugan to end this labour and give the feet that lead to release. The praise names Siva, whom even Vishnu could not reach, dancing the great dance, to whom Murugan gave the teaching that made his devotion overflow, and the vel that pierced Sura's chest and let the friendly survive.
nuance: மிக்க காசு இழைத்து: money is named, the courtesan's trade. சுகத்தில் அத்தர் தாம் மிகுத்த பத்தி கூர் சுரக்க வித்தை தான் அருள்வோனே: Siva, the father, receives the teaching and overflows with devotion.

reading: The poet, worn out by Kama who shoots the bud arrows from his sugarcane bow, calls himself a vessel at the door of women like Rambha and a wandering lecher who seeks breasts that plot death like Death himself, and asks Murugan to give him virtues and join him to the good anklets. The praise names Rama who burned Lanka with his monkey army and Krishna who in one chariot sided with Arjuna against the hundred, and the vel that split the hill of Sura.
nuance: கூற்றெனக் கொலைசூழும் குயங்கள்: desire is again Death. Several runs in the praise (பெருங்குறோட்டைவிட்டு உறங்கு காற்றென) are obscure.

reading: Calling his body a bundle of flesh and filth, the poet asks whether, failing to reach release and wearing himself out in union with women, he should be slandered by men on earth as a buffoon, a rogue and a loudmouth. The praise names the Lord who knocked Brahma, the potter of the Veda, on the forehead, and the Tamil verses with the tala beat that sent the Jains in their mats onto rows of sharp stakes, with the victorious vel and unfailing compassion.
nuance: கலைதலை கெட்ட பாய்ச் சமணரை நட்ட கூர்க் கழுநிரை ... ஏற்றிய தாளக் கவிதை: Murugan is identified with Sambandar, whose Tamil hymns sent the Jains to the stake. குயவனை ... குட்டினால்: Brahma struck as a potter, the punishment in the story of Om, though Om is not named here.

tamil: அளக பார முங்கு லைந்து அரிய பார்வை யுஞ்சி வந்து
அதர பான மும்நு கர்ந்து அறிவு சோர வும்மொ ழிந்து
பளக னாவி யுந்த ளர்ந்து பதறு மாக மும்ப யந்து
பரம ஞான முந்தெ ளிந்து பரிவு நேச முங்கி ளர்ந்து
துளப மாய னுஞ்சி றந்த கமல வேத னும்பு கழ்ந்து
சுரர்கள் நாய கன்ப யந்த திருவை மாம ணம்பு ணர்ந்து
களப மார்பு டன்த யங்கு குறவர் மாது டன்செ றிந்து
கடிய பாத கந்த விர்ந்து கழலை நாடொ றுங்கி ளர்ந்து
reading: The poet describes the embrace of women plainly, until reason fails and day and night are forgotten, and asks to be given Murugan's red feet so that, with supreme knowledge made clear and love rising, he may speak his praise. The praise names Siva whom Vishnu and Brahma could not find, Devayanai the daughter of the gods' king, Valli in love's play, and Murugan who enters the minds of those who daily think on his anklets and leave their sins.

tamil: ஆசார வீன னறிவிலி கோபாப ராதி யவகுண
மாசான நாலெண் வகைதனை நீநானெ னாத அறிவுளம்
வீசால வேலை சுவறிட மாசூரர் மார்பு தொளைபட
மேகார வார மெனஅதிர் போர்யாது தான ரெமபுர
கூசாது வேட னுமிழ்தரு நீராடி யூனு ணெனுமுரை
கோதாமெ னாம லமுதுசெய் வேதாக மாதி முதல்தரு
reading: The poet heaps names on himself, without conduct, witless, angry, an offender, base, unfit, carried away by desire, a sinner whose mind never gained the knowledge that says neither 'you' nor 'I', and asks Murugan not to think so of him but, with a mother's and father's grace, to grant great knowledge. The praise has the vel that dried the sea, fed the ghouls and sent the demons to Yama's city, and the Lord who, not shrinking when the hunter bathed him with water from his mouth and said 'eat this flesh', ate what he had tasted as nectar.
nuance: நீ நான் எனாத அறிவு: the knowledge the poet lacks is non-dual. The hunter's mouth-water bath and tasted flesh are Kannappar's offering, usually told of Siva at Kalahasti; here the praise seems to give it to the Lord the song addresses. The first lines have a corrupt glyph and obscure words (விபாணதன், மாறாம காரிலெனையினி).

reading: The poet, a devotee full of longing, asks whether he will set his heart's lotus as the flower, thread love through it, tie it on his tongue with art so that it spreads the fragrance of knowledge, with a pure mind as the singing bee, and so adorn Murugan's radiant feet with a garland of the flowers of the letters. The praise names the hunter girl of the forest, Devayanai of the great elephant, and the vel that brought down Sura, who came out of the fish-filled sea.
nuance: மாத்ருகா புஷ்ப மாலை: the garland is made of the மாத்ருகா, the letters of the alphabet held to be mother-powers, so the song itself is the offering; heart, love, tongue and mind each become part of the garland.

reading: The poet describes women who kindle desire, ask for cloth and money, sway their breasts and mimic peacocks and parrots, and lead a man by their foul passage, and asks whether the infatuation that torments him will not end. The praise names the peacock that seizes and shakes the serpent, Hari's nephew whose feet fill devotees' minds, the vel thrown at Sura who harmed the gods, and the lord who rejoices with the hunter girl in the golden land of the Ponni river.
nuance: ஆடைப் பணத்தை எடு: the women's demand is quoted. பொனி நீர் பொற்புவி: the Ponni, the Kaveri, is named, a pointer to a Chola-country shrine though the song is filed among the general songs.

tamil: ஆசை நேச மயக்கிகள் காசு தேடு மனத்திகள்
யாவ ரோடு நகைப்பவர் வேறு கூறு விளைப்பவர்
மாசி லாத தனத்தியர் ஆடை சோர நடப்பவர்
வாயி லு஡ற லளிப்பவர் நாளு நாளு மினுக்கிகள்
ஓசை யான திரைக்கடல் ஏழு ஞால முமுற்றருள்
யோகி ஞானி பரப்ரமி நீலி நாரணி யுத்தமி
ஏசி லாத மலைக்கொடி தாய்ம னோமணி சற்குணி
ஏறு மேனி யொருத்தனும் வேத னான சமர்த்தனும்
reading: The poet describes women who bewitch with desire, whose minds seek money, who melt men's life, laugh with anyone in the street and make quarrels, with poison eyes, and asks whether he will stop walking to their doors. The praise is a litany of the Goddess, Uma, mother of the seas and seven worlds: yogi, jnani, supreme Brahmi, Neeli, Narani, the excellent one, Abhirami of the Veda, mountain creeper, Manonmani; Murugan is her son, dear to Siva and Brahma.
nuance: காசு தேடு மனத்திகள்: money is named. The praise gives almost all its space to the Goddess's names, so Murugan is praised as அருள்பாலா, child of her grace.

tamil: ஆல மேற்ற விழியினர் சால நீட்டி யழுதழு
ஆடல் பார்க்க நிலையெழு பாடை கூட்டி விரையம
கால மாச்சு வருகென ஓலை காட்டி யமபடர்
காம வாழ்க்கை பொடிபட ஞானம் வாய்த்த கழலிணை
வேல கீர்த்தி விதரண சீலர் வாழ்த்து சரவண
வேடர் நாட்டில் விளைபுன ஏனல் காத்த சிறுமியை
ஞால மேத்தி வழிபடு மாறு பேர்க்கு மகவென
நாத போற்றி யெனமுது தாதை கேட்க அநுபவ
reading: When eyes of poison weep, drums beat, the bier is raised, kin stand apart and Yama's servants show the palm leaf saying 'the time has come, come' and carry off the life, the poet asks first to be given the awareness to think with love on the anklets that crush the life of lust and give knowledge. The praise names Saravana, Valli's devotee in disguise, the child who came in the reed-bed as son to the six, and the one who spoke the word of lived knowledge when his old father asked, saying 'Lord, praise'.
nuance: நாத போற்றி என முது தாதை கேட்க அநுபவ ஞான வார்த்தை அருளிய: Siva as the old father asks and Murugan teaches, Om not named. காலமாச்சு வருக என ஓலை காட்டி: the summons is quoted. வியாழ கோத்ர is obscure.

reading: The poet describes women standing in the street with garlands and thin cloth on their breasts, and asks that, not speaking even a little with them, he speak daily of Murugan's vel, his blue peacock, his six lotus faces and the two consorts on either side. The praise names him son of the Lord whom Brahma and Vishnu could not find, husband of the hunter girl, younger brother of the elephant-faced one, and the vel thrown at Sura's chest.
nuance: உரையாதே ... உரையேனோ: the poet turns his speech from the women to the Lord; the plea is about what the tongue does.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 16 of 21): confessions of courtesans who price love, of praising patrons and of wealth hoarded without sharing, the funeral and the rotting body, set against pleas for the feet, for Saiva knowledge of Lord, soul and bond, and in 1221 the poet's disowning of every act as his own.
structure_note: The general songs run in order of their first letter (இ, உ, ஊ, எ, ஏ, க). Courtesans and price: 1229 to 1231; women's eyes and infatuation: 1217, 1218, 1223, 1225, 1228; the poet's trade of praising patrons: 1224, 1226, 1231; the funeral: 1227. 1219 and 1221 are doctrinal, and 1222 sets the mantra against Death's servants.
source_issues: 1221: line 10 is garbled (மகிழ்ந்து ...... அ ளுறித்), with initial அ split from its word.
1228: யாயையு in line 15 is probably மாயையு.
1231: ஡ is corrupt three times: சுக்஡ணவ and தசக்஡ணவ for சுக்ரீவ and தசக்ரீவ (஡ண for ரீ), and கடற்று஡ளி for கடல் தூளி (஡ for ஊ).
1217, 1218, 1219, 1220, 1221, 1231: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ டன்மற்கடை, உ ணருப, உ பதேசி, உ னதருளை, உ டலது, உ னையோத, உ ளநெ, உ பய).

reading: The poet confesses his enjoyment of slender-waisted women, their lips and camphor-smeared breasts, and asks for even a little grace so that, his base qualities gone through awareness of the attributeless, he may enter the one partless form. The praise tells of Brahma thrown into prison, names Vishnu as eater of curd, ghee and the world and brother-in-law of Siva who ate the poison, and calls Murugan the victor whose vel struck the gods' foes and felled the eight mountains.
nuance: நிற்குண உணர்வாலே ஒரு நிஷ்கள வடிவில் புக: the goal is put in Sanskrit doctrinal terms, entry into the nirguna, nishkala form, against the துற்குணம் of the first lines. Brahma's imprisonment is named without its cause. The run of lines 5 to 7 (who fears whom) is hard to divide.

tamil: இருகுழை மீது தாவடி யிடுவன வோதி நீழலி
இழிவன காம வேதமு மொழிவன தாரை வேலென
கருகிய நீல லோசன அபிநய மாத ரார்தரு
கதிபெற ஈட றாதன பதிபசு பாச மானவை
ஒருபது பார மோலியு மிருபது வாகு மேருவு
றொருகணை யேவு ராகவன் மருகவி பூதி பூஷணர்
பரவிய கான வேடுவர் தருமபி ராம நாயகி
பதிகுடி யேற வேல்தொடு முருகம யூர வாகன
reading: The poet describes women's dark eyes that leap to the earrings, roam in the hair's shade, speak the Veda of love and strike like spears and poison, and asks that he, who withered in their embrace, be set on the way by having Pati, pasu and pasam separated each from each without stain. The praise names Rama who went with the monkeys and felled the ten crowns with one arrow, calls Murugan the teacher whose instruction ash-adorned Siva understood, Valli's lord, the one who resettled Indra, and lord of yogis rapt in jnana.
nuance: பதி பசு பாசம் ஆனவை கசடற வேறு வேறு செய்தருள்வாயே: the plea is in the terms of Saiva Siddhanta, asking for the discrimination of Lord, soul and bond. The praise has விபூதி பூஷணர் உணர் உபதேச தேசிக, Siva learning from Murugan, without naming Om.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to drive off his twofold disease of impurity with Siva's light, call him kindly, set the paired feet on his head, seat him on the peacock, give him the vel, and grant him the place of a teacher whom the Vedas, gods and earth would praise. The praise calls Murugan younger brother of the elephant-faced god who cuts the disease of birth and poverty, wearer of kadamba, embracer of the wise wife Vishnu gave, and the one who powdered the hill, cut down the asuras and freed the gods.
nuance: The plea is unusually bold: not only the feet on the head (முடிமேலே இணைதாள்) but the peacock, the vel and உபதேசிகப் பதம், the rank of a teacher. இருவோரும் ஒருவாக, 'the two as one', given by the lord of Kailasa, is obscure; it may mean Siva and Uma joined. Ganapati is praised at length in the second half.

reading: The poet asks whether his mind will not think day and night on the feet with little anklet bells that prattle the Vedas, adorned with the lotus of his heart and with flowers, and whether Murugan will not take pity on a deceiver with no help but his grace, who carries a body of five elements from world to world.
