The praise is of battle, an elephant and the golden hill, the sea set on fire, and Siva and Uma praising the child Kandan while all worlds, gods, Vishnu and Brahma bow.
nuance: பஞ்சபூத உடலது சுமந்து அலைந்து உலகுதொறும் வந்துவந்து: rebirth is told as carrying the five-element body from world to world. The poet calls himself வஞ்சகன், a deceiver. The battle lines (கனநிவத... கடகசயிலம்) are hard to divide.

reading: The poet calls his body flesh, bone, filth and nerves, eaten by fated disease, and himself the lowest dog, and asks who he is to subside, to bow, to sing Murugan in joy, to melt, to wither, to walk and fall. The praise answers with Siva, who himself united, knew, rejoiced, pitied like a mother, became Siva, grew and remained by himself, and calls Murugan his son and lord of the devotees of salokam, samipam and sarupam.
nuance: The repeated நானார் ('who am I') is set against the repeated தானே ('he himself'): the poet disowns every act of devotion as his own and gives all agency to the Lord who does everything by himself. The three devotee classes in the refrain are the graded releases short of union; sayujyam is not named. The word after மகிழ்ந்து in line 10 is garbled.

reading: The poet asks whether he will worship the red feet adorned with kadamba, jasmine, kuvalai and vetchi, having won manhood by cutting down with the sword of mantra, which the sects, rites and all sixty-four arts cannot reach, the cruel servants of Yama who come by fate's path to take his life, and which those who wander raising banners that say none is their equal never find. The praise calls Murugan the red-handed vel that fought Diti's sons and bathed in a river of blood, rider of the bright peacock, and lord of the thirty-three gods, which it counts out.
nuance: மந்த்ர வாளால் ... யமபடரை வெட்டித் துணித்து: the mantra is a sword against Death's servants, and it lies beyond the boasting sects and arts. The refrain lists the thirty-three: eleven on bulls (the Rudras), twelve in chariots (the Adityas), two Ashvins and eight Vasus. The opening lines' split is uncertain.

reading: The poet asks whether he must wander, worn out with a heart sore and burning, after women whose young-coconut breasts draw young men's eyes, who cling with love and then leave without attachment by deceit. The praise calls Murugan younger brother of the pot-bellied elephant god who gathers fruit, sugarcane and cakes in his trunk and is kind to devotees, and the beautiful one whose vel split the sea and pursued and cut down the great mango.
nuance: அணைந்து பின் பற்றற்று அகல் மாயம்: the deceit is the women's leaving once attached, not a price named. கொக்கு is the mango, the form Sura took, a detail the song names by its word only.

reading: The poet asks whether his dying will not end: a body for crows, dogs, jackals and ghosts, whether in forest, country or house, after seeking what is sweet in writings and songs, piling great wealth and eating it without sharing, and boasting of high lineage. The praise names Murugan lord of the daughter of thousand-eyed Indra, the peacock-rider whose vel fought Sura, the Vel of Kongu, partner of the hunters' girl, and lord of the gods who offer flowers at his feet.
nuance: பாத்து உணாது: eating without dividing it with others, the Kural's own phrase for sharing, here named as the poet's fault. கொங்கில் வேளே places the song in Kongu without naming a shrine. The opening search in ஏட்டிலே ... பாட்டிலே ... நீட்டிலே may be of a poet's trade; its sense is uncertain.

reading: The poet asks whether, infatuated by bodiced breasts and red-veined carp eyes that spit poison like Death, he should go about without fear or shame, called a rake by all who hear, mad after wealth. The praise is a dense string of epithets naming the green dancer, the one who dwells in the lotus, the bearer of the discus and conch and the gods of the sky, and calls Murugan the one who cut down the great mango in the sea.
nuance: அச்சக் கூச்சமற்று ... தூர்த்தன் என: the confession is of public shame, being named a rake (தூர்த்தன்). The praise's clipped syllables are very hard to divide and only its last line is clear.

reading: The poet confesses stealing the old poets' phrases (eyes bigger than the sea, breasts bigger than mountains, lips redder than coral, shoulders softer than bamboo) and singing them on a man, calling him strong, peerless, gracious and fearless in hope of gain, and says 'enough, enough' of this restless birth, asking for the red lotus feet. The praise likens the must of the white elephant to two rivers falling from the silver mountain, and calls Murugan the one who took the vel so Indra and the worlds might stand, set the sea crying for refuge and fought the asuras with the hill.
nuance: பழங் கிளவி பல களவுகொண்டு: the poet calls his borrowed stock comparisons theft, and the praise of a patron (அடல் அசஞ்சலன் அதுலன் அநுபமன்) begging. அலமலம், 'enough, enough', turns from the patron to the feet.

reading: The poet describes the funeral: drums beat, young men of the clan bind the body, wrap it in a torn cloth on the bier, burn it, bathe and go home to sit, and says life is pure falsehood; he asks for the high state of Siva so that sorrowful birth may go. The praise calls Murugan the vel that bored through the eight mountains and eased the gods, the one who beguiled the hill girl and embraced her, wearer of kadamba and vetchi, and the one who cut down his foe in the sea.
nuance: சுத்தப் பொய் ஒப்பது உயிர்வாழ்வு: the funeral is told without comment until this judgement. மிக்கச் சிவத்ததொரு சொர்க்கப் பதம் may mean 'a heavenly state that is wholly Siva' or 'very red', a pun on சிவம்.

reading: The poet asks whether the illusion in which his heart goes and dies in the deceitful love of women, sweet-spoken, bee-haired, carp-eyed and moon-faced, will not end. The praise calls Murugan the one who went with love to the hill where the cloud-haired, cuckoo-voiced hill girl lives, who made Sura's sea boil, and who conquered both maya and Kama.
nuance: வென்று மாயையும் அன்றி வேளையும் வென்று: in the refrain Murugan conquers maya and Vel (Kama), so the praise answers the plea's மாயம். The source has யாயை, read as மாயை; the reading is tentative.

reading: The poet describes women who leave men with a begging bowl, catch young men with kohl-eyes, stained teeth and painted faces, and asks whether it is not enough, now that he who clung to them has suffered, to be set at the lotus feet. The praise calls Murugan one who was born as a child to a line it names and removed a fault, the one who meets the breasts of the creeper girl born of the deer to the Brahmin sage, and who crushed the seven hills with his arms.
nuance: கப்பரை கைக்கொள வைப்பவர்: the women reduce men to the beggar's bowl, so the loss of wealth is named in the first words. The lines on முத்தரையர்க்கு ஒரு மகவாகி point to a birth story I cannot identify; they may allude to Murugan as a saint, but the text does not say.

reading: The poet asks for the red feet, praised by the ancient Veda and adorned with jasmine and kuravam, while life lasts in a body that wilts among women who show their price and men of false learning and liquor. The praise calls Murugan the child who longed for the breasts of the parrot girl guarding millet, the peacock hero who freed the prisoners, the vel that felled the mountain, and the good lord of devotees who crown his feet with lilies.
nuance: விலை காட்டு ... அரிவைமார்: the women show a price. Most of the first four lines, in a clipped rhyme on -ல்ல, are hard to divide, so the company the poet lists is uncertain.

tamil: களவு கொண்டு கைக்காசி னளவ றிந்து கர்ப்பூர
கலவி யின்பம் விற்பார்க ளவய வங்க ளைப்பாடு
உ ளநெ கிழ்ந்த சத்தான வுரைம றந்து சத்தான
உ பய பங்க யத்தாளி லபய மென்று னைப்பாடி
அளவில் வன்க விச்சேனை பரவ வந்த சுக்஡ணவ
அடலி லங்கை சுட்டாடி நிசிச ரன்த சக்஡ணவ
வளரு மந்த ரச்சோலை மிசைசெ றிந்த முற்பாலை
வடிவு கொண்டு பித்தாகி யுருகி வெந்த றக்கானில்
reading: The poet says some sell the pleasure of love after reckoning the coins in a man's hand, and some learn and make poems on these women's limbs; he asks whether it would be shameful if he forgot such speech, knew Murugan as the true, sang 'refuge' to his musk-scented feet and melted. The praise names Rama, who with Sugriva's army raised dust from the sea, burned Lanka and shot the one arrow at ten-headed Ravana, as Murugan's uncle, and tells of Murugan taking a hunter's form, mad with love, to find Valli in the hills.
nuance: கைக்காசின் அளவறிந்து: the price is measured to the coin. The poet sets two trades side by side, the women who sell love and the poets who sing their bodies, and offers his song to the feet instead.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 17 of 21): the household, wealth and kin left at the burning ground or seized at Death's coming, courtesans who take money, and pleas for the name and feet at the last hour, beside songs of inner yoga, of Siva-knowledge as a bride, of experience over scripture and sect, and of the threefold Tamil.
structure_note: Songs in order of their first letter (க, கி, கு, கோ, ச, சா, சி, சீ, சூ, செ, த). Household and wealth: 1235, 1238, 1239, 1245; Death: 1236, 1243, 1244; courtesans: 1233, 1237, 1242, 1243; the inner way: 1240, 1241, 1242, 1246. Five praises (1232, 1236, 1237, 1245 and, less clearly, 1233) have Murugan instruct Siva or call him guru to Siva.
source_issues: 1244: ஡ stands for ஊ in line 2 (யாதிலு஡மாசை, perhaps யாதிலும் ஊமாசை), and ஧வ்முழ்க in line 5 is corrupt for மூழ்க.
1237: சாவியது in line 10 is unclear.
1240: line 15 (பூங்குற மாதினுட வாடியிருள்) is short of syllables.
1235, 1241: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ டையமுனி, உ வகாரியன்பர்).

reading: The poet asks whether a day will come when, crossing the sea of birth with its deceitful fish and sharks in the boat of true speech, he will lay many flowers (kuravu, vetchi, mullai, utpalam, kadamba, vilvam and others) on Murugan and recite his words. The praise calls Murugan the one who spoke love to Valli born of the deer, guru to the lord whose limit Brahma and Vishnu could not see, and, with wordplay on தெய்வயானை, younger brother of the divine elephant, lord of the white elephant and dear to Devayanai.
nuance: The plea is for flower worship and recitation (உனது சொல்லை ஓதிப் பணிவது), an outward worship rare in these songs. The refrain plays on தெய்வ யானை: Ganapati, Airavata and Devayanai. The first lines (கல்விடாது ... மெய்கள் தோணி) are hard to divide.

reading: The poet, infatuated by young women's poison carp eyes and breasts and by Kama's bodiless form, asks not to be born again into this world in the hut of suffering, and to be let worship at the feet that the devotees reach. The praise names Murugan the hero who embraced the hill girl, the vel that fought the eight mountains, the one who knows sweet Tamil set to music that the lord with matted hair praises, and the beautiful six-faced one with twelve eyes.
nuance: இன்னிசை உறு தமிழ் தெரிவோனே: Murugan is the knower of Tamil with music, perhaps alluding to his teaching Siva, but the line (தன் நிறை சடை இறை என் முனி பரவரு) is unclear.

tamil: கிஞ்சுகமெ னச்சி வத்த தொண்டையள்மி கக்க றுத்த
கிம்புரிம ருப்பை யொத்த குங்குமமு லைக்கு றத்தி
நெஞ்சுருகி நெக்கு நெக்கு நின்றுதொழு நிர்க்கு ணத்தர்
நின்பதயு கப்ர சித்தி யென்பனவ குத்து ரைக்க
கஞ்சன்வர விட்ட துட்ட குஞ்சரம ருப்பொ சித்த
கந்தெறிக ளிற்று ரித்து வென்றுதிரு நட்ட மிட்ட
டஞ்சியஜ கத்ர யத்தை யஞ்சலென விக்ர மித்து
அன்றவுண ரைக்க ளத்தில் வென்றுததி யைக்க லக்கி
reading: The poet asks for the threefold Tamil in Murugan's service, so that he may tell in parts the fame of the two feet that melting devotees beyond the gunas and faultless bhaktas strew with vetchi, and speak the name Murugan took as servant of the hill girl with coral lips and dark eyes. The praise names Krishna, who broke the tusks of the elephant Kamsa sent, and Siva who flayed the elephant and danced, and calls Murugan the one whose fierce vel calmed the three worlds, fought the asuras, churned the sea and freed the gods.
nuance: த்ரயத் தமிழ், the three Tamils of prose, music and drama, is what the poet asks for. குறத்தி கிங்கரன் எனப் படைத்த பெயர் is Murugan's own title as Valli's servant. Whether பேசா means 'so as to speak' or 'not speaking' is unclear.

reading: The poet describes a life of wife, servants, clan, pride and gathered wealth ending when the body falls like a broken pot, is wrapped in a small old rag and left at the burning ground, and asks to be given the red feet before the body is destroyed. The praise is a battle in drum syllables: trees fall roaring, the asuras' army flees, the mountains roar, the sage of four Vedas is made servant, the gods rise, and Indra of the thunderbolt is resettled in his world.
nuance: சிறு பழைய துணி போர்த்தி: the rich man of the first lines is covered with a small old rag at the end, the reversal the song turns on. மறைநாலும் உடைய முனி ஆட்பட may be Brahma brought low, but he is not named. மொளமொளமொளாச் is drum syllable.

tamil: குறைவ தின்றி மிக்க சலமெ லும்பு துற்ற
குலைகு லைந்து தெர்ப்பை யிடைநி னைந்து நிற்ப
மறலி வந்து துட்ட வினைகள் கொண்ட லைத்து
மனமி டைஞ்ச லற்று னடிநி னைந்து நிற்க
அறுக மிந்து மத்த மலையெ றிந்த அப்பு
அருந டஞ்செ யப்ப ரருளி ரங்கு கைக்கு
சிறுகு லந்த னக்கு ளறிவு வந்து தித்த
திசைமு கன்தி கைக்க அசுர ரன்ற டைத்த
reading: The poet asks that, before Death comes like a dark cloud, harrows him with his evil deeds and the sorrow of death draws near while he lies on darbha grass, he may stand with untroubled mind thinking of Murugan's feet, and that Murugan come on the peacock and give release. The praise calls Murugan the one who spoke a rare sweet word to the father who dances wearing arugu grass, moon, datura and river, who embraced the girl of a small clan in whom wisdom dawned, and who opened the asuras' prison while Brahma stood bewildered.
nuance: தெர்ப்பை இடை: the dying man laid on darbha grass. மறலி ... துட்ட வினைகள் கொண்டு அலைத்து: Death torments with one's own deeds. சிறுகுலம் தனக்குள் அறிவு வந்து உதித்த சிறுமி praises Valli's wisdom, not only her beauty.

tamil: கோக னகமு கிழ்த்த போக புளகி தத்த
கூட வரவ ழைக்கு மாடு குழைய டர்த்த
ஆக முறவ ணைத்து காசை யபக ரித்து
ஆசை யதுகொ ளுத்து மால மதுகு டித்த
மாக நதிம திப்ர தாப மவுலி யர்க்கு
வாகு வலைய சித்ர ஆறி ருபுய வெற்பில்
வேக வுரக ரத்ந நாக சயன சக்ர
வீசு திரைய லைத்த வேலை சுவற வெற்றி
reading: The poet describes women with lotus-bud breasts who call men to come, embrace them, take their money and then bite their lips again, and asks whether he must still suffer, drunk on the poison of desire. The praise calls Murugan the one who told a meaning to Siva of the crowned river and moon, the twelve-armed bridegroom of the hill girl, nephew of the emerald Vishnu lying on the serpent with the discus, and the one whose vel dried the sea.
nuance: காசை அபகரித்து மீள இதழ் கடிப்பது: the theft of money comes between the embraces, which is the deceit. The word after மவுலியர்க்கு is unclear (சாவியது), but ஓர் அர்த்தம் மொழிவோனே gives Murugan telling Siva 'a meaning'.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to clear away the pleasure of living proud of a sandal-adorned wife and children with anklets, called 'my wealth', so that sorrows fade, and to give his feet today. The praise calls Murugan the dweller of Kurinji with kadamba shoulders, the vel that split the hill, the beautiful one who dwells in the bodies of devotees who conquered the five senses, and the one who said 'fear not' when the worlds shook.
nuance: எந்தன் தனங்கள் என்றென்று: wife and children are named as 'my wealth', so the plea is against possessiveness more than the household itself. ஐந்திந்த்ரியங்கள் வென்று ஒன்றும் அன்பர் அங்கம் பொருந்தும்: Murugan's dwelling is the body of the self-controlled devotee.

tamil: சலமல மசுத்த மிக்க தசைகுரு தியத்தி மொய்த்த
சகலமு மியற்றி மத்த மிகுமிரு தடக்கை யத்தி
கலனணி துகிற்கள் கற்பி னொடுகுல மனைத்து முற்றி
கலைபல பிடித்து நித்த மலைபடு மநர்த்த முற்ற
மலைமக ளிடத்து வைத்து மதிபுனல் சடைக்குள் வைத்து
மடிவுற நினைத்து வெற்பை வரிசிலை யிடக்கை வைத்து
பலதிசை நடுக்க முற்று நிலைகெட அடற்கை யுற்ற
பழுதறு தவத்தி லுற்று வழிமொழி யுரைத்த பத்தர்
reading: The poet asks whether his harsh karma will not end: in a body of water, filth, flesh, blood and bone, he does everything for maya, gathers elephants, children, wife, jewels, clothes and clan, rejoices in the womb's way, and studies arts, suffering daily without meaning. The praise calls Murugan the great life of the father who keeps the mountain's daughter at his side, the moon and river in his hair, axe and fire in his hand, the mountain as a bow, and who laughed down his foes, and the one who looks with grace on devotees in faultless tapas.
nuance: கலைபல பிடித்து நித்தம் அலைபடும் அநர்த்தம்: learning is listed among the attachments, not set against them. மறைதொழ நகைத்த: Siva destroying his foes (Tripura) by a laugh, told in the text's own details.

reading: The poet asks whether Murugan will not grant him, as those who know peace beyond have gained wisdom, a way to live in stillness with gaze half-closed, breath held, the light appearing, and Sivayoga stirring the soul, in the dance-form of the one who danced the dance of jnana and bliss while Uma sang. The praise pictures the hill of plantains like elephant trunks, mango honey and bees on vengai, and Murugan dwelling in the grove with the hill girl.
nuance: தூங்கிய பார்வை ... தாங்கிய வாயு ... தோன்றிய சோதி ... சிவயோகம்: the plea is a compact list of yoga's stages, and சோம்பினில் வாழும் வகை, living in 'idleness', means the stillness of the yogi. Line 15 seems short of syllables.

reading: The poet asks whether he must perish, not knowing how to drink the Siva-bliss of union with the lady of the lotus of Siva-knowledge, wandering as a form of impurity and panting after common women; he asks Murugan to come before him daily so he may play with the hosts of devotees and his impurities and twin deeds break. The praise names Uma, the bride, Gauri and Sivakami at Siva's side, who one day shared a pomegranate in the elephant's hand, and asks Murugan, her son, to grant the deathless abode of nectar to one born in vain.
nuance: சிவஞான புண்டரிக மலர்மாது: Siva-knowledge is personified as a lady to be embraced, set against the common women (பொது மாதர்). The pomegranate shared by Uma is named but its story is not told.

tamil: சீறிட்டு லாவு கண்கள் மாதர்க்கு நாள்ம ருண்டு
சீரிட்ட மாக நின்ற காசைக்கொ டாத பின்பு
ஆறெட்டு மாய்வி ரிந்து மாறெட்டு மாகி நின்று
ஆகத்து ளேம கிழ்ந்த ஜோதிப்ர காச இன்பம்
மாறிட்டு வான டுங்க மேலிட்டு மேல கண்டம்
வாள்தொட்டு நேர்ந டந்த சூர்வஜ்ர மார்பு நெஞ்சும்
கூறிட்ட வேல பங்க வீரர்க்கு வீர கந்த
கோலப்பெண் வாகு கண்டு மாலுற்று வேளை கொண்டு
reading: The poet asks that the wretchedness of being cast off, after he served women of darting eyes and stopped giving the money they wanted, not harm him, and asks whether the light shining as bliss in the body and in the soul will not appear, the one spread out as six and eight that no one can describe. The praise is of the vel that split Sura's diamond chest and the golden hill, and of Murugan, hero of heroes, who saw the hunters' beautiful girl and joined her in love.
nuance: காசைக் கொடாத பின்பு சீரற்று: when the money stops the man is ruined, the courtesan's logic. ஆறெட்டுமாய் விரிந்தும் may count the tattvas, but the number is unclear.

reading: The poet, caught by women seeking wealth like a fish on the hook, asks that when Death comes by fate to seek his life he be given the thought to call 'Adi Muruga, Adi Muruga'. The praise calls Murugan the one who fought with the vel while the asuras cried out, the yoga peacock who bows at the feet of the guru of Om Namasivaya, Uma's son, nephew of Rama and Hari, dweller in devotees' hearts, and Devayanai's husband.
nuance: ஆதிமுருகா ஆதிமுருகா ஆதிமுருகா என: the plea at the hour of death is simply for the name, repeated. ஓநமசிவாய குரு பாதம் makes Siva's mantra itself the guru at whose feet Murugan bows.

reading: The poet, a ghoul for gold, land and women, a diseased doer of crores of sins, asks that when Death comes to drop him into the seven hells Murugan come fast on his steed, speaking the word of wisdom, so his sins go. The praise calls Murugan the vel that made the sea quake and Death fall and run, nephew of Krishna who climbed the kurundha tree with the women's saris, and the one who lives with the hill girl.
nuance: செழுந்தாது பார் மாது: gold, earth and woman, the triple desire. விழுந்தோடவே காலன் in the praise answers the plea: Death himself falls. Several words are corrupt.

reading: The poet asks to be given, before the failing time comes for wealth, servants, kin, sons and house, the thought of grace to melt in devotion and hold Murugan's feet daily. The praise names Rama who rolled the ten heads, calls Murugan the one whom the pot-bellied elephant god, eating cakes, puffed rice and honey, helped to embrace the hunter girl in the forest, and the one who told the Veda's word to the three-eyed lord who gives release.
nuance: மொய்ப்பன் உதவ அடவிக்குள் மறமகளை அணைவோனே: Ganapati's help in the Valli story is named outright. முத்தி தரு முதல்வர் ... மறைமொழியை மொழிவோனே: Murugan teaching Siva, without naming Om.

reading: The poet asks whether one should speak without end as the Puranas and Srutis, without seeking the one cause known by experience by those who rose saying 'enough' to pleasures, delusion, lust, fire-like anger, greed and the many forms of the sects. The praise tells of Murugan who, taking a form and feigning distress, judged the time and joined the hunter girl, armed with Kama's two arrows and bow, and whose vel resettled Indra and powdered the demon.
nuance: அநுபூதி கொண்டு அறியும் ஒரு காரணம்: experience, not scripture or sect, knows the one cause. The question (விளம்புவதோதான்) may be the poet's self-rebuke or a jab at scholars; the sentence's subject is unclear.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 18 of 21): the poet asks to be lifted above the quarrels of sects and the lure of women, out of the body seen as self and the bubble of life, and to be given the true word, the teaching Murugan gave Siva, and the feet; one song is a love-lament, one a vow that in kingship or poverty he will speak only of the feet, and one a frank account of love answered by a plea for Vedanta's lamp.
structure_note: Several songs ask for a word or teaching rather than escape alone: 1247 (the Lord beyond he, she and it), 1248, 1251, 1252, 1253 and 1261. Women are the confession of 1248, 1256 to 1261; the body and its end of 1250. 1249 is a vision of union at the Sivaganga tank; 1254 an akam lament in the girl's voice; 1255 a vow. 1251 has the ghost-troupe singing Thiruppugazh itself.
source_issues: 1250: the glyph ஡ stands for ஊ (சேறூறு).
1258: ஡ stands for ஊ in மடலூர and ஡ண for ரீ in உயிரீர்வார் (printed மடலு஡ர, உயி஡ணர்வார்).
1253: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ ள்ள).
1250, 1256, 1261: a syllable is lost before the refrain marker '....... ;' (ளையோனே for இளையோனே in 1250 and 1256; ருபார்வை in 1261).

tamil: தவநெறி தவறிய குருடுகள் தலைபறி கதறிய ...... பரபாதத்
தருமிகள் கருமிகள் வெகுவித சமயிக ளவரொடு ...... சருவாநின்
றவனிவ னுவனுட னவளிவ ளுவளது இதுவுது ...... வெனுமாறற்
றருவுரு வொழிதரு வுருவுடை யதுபதி தமியனு ...... முணர்வேனோ
குவலய முழுவதும் மதிர்பட வடகுவ டிடிபட ...... வுரகேசன்
துவல்கொடு முறையிடு சுரர்பதி துயரது கெடநிசி ...... சரர்சேனை
துகளெழ நடநவில் மரகத துரகதம் வரவல ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet asks whether he, a lonely one, will come to know the Lord whose form passes beyond both form and the formless and beyond all talk of he, she and it, without being drawn into dispute with the blind who left the path of austerity, the hair-plucking ascetics, ritualists and sectarians of many kinds. The praise shows the earth shaken, the northern peak shattered, the serpent king's crests crushed and the ancient sea dried as Murugan answers the appeal of the gods' king and turns the demon army to dust, riding the dancing emerald steed.
nuance: அவன் இவன் உவன் உடன் அவள் இவள் உவள் அது இது உது எனும் ஆறு அற்று: the Lord is beyond the threefold grammar of person and distance, a formula that also opens Saiva and Vaishnava doctrinal works. தலைபறி, those who pluck out their hair, are Jain ascetics; பரபாதத் தருமிகள் is less clear. The plea is not to defeat the sects but to stop quarrelling (சருவா நின்று) and know.

reading: The poet describes the breasts of women, likened to the tusks of rutting elephants, to radiant peaks and to tender coconuts, and the creeper-like women who exhaust young men, and asks that the nights and days he spends in their net end and he be set to praise Murugan. The praise names him the one who first told the subtle, supreme truth to Brahma, Vishnu and Siva who did not know it, the vel that struck the rakshasa hiding in the sea, and the companion of great poets who find the best word in an instant.
nuance: சததள பார்த்திபற்கு அரி புருஷோத்தமற்கு எரிகனல் ஏற்றவற்கு: Brahma of the hundred-petalled lotus, Vishnu and Siva who holds fire all receive the teaching; Om is not named. கவிஞர் உசாத்துணை: Murugan as the poets' confidant, a role the poet claims for his own songs. The Sanskrit compounds of the praise are hard to divide.

reading: The poet asks that, with wrinkles, grey hair, the body's suffering and the two deceitful deeds destroyed, he bathe and play in the Sivaganga tank, that Sivam leap into him so that his inner form becomes Murugan's form, and that, with gods, sages, Brahma and Vishnu calling him Hara's son and Ganapati 'my younger brother', Murugan come on the peacock with the vel, join his father in the holy dance, and give the precious meaning. The praise names Siva, the dancer of Madurai who made foxes into horses for a Pandya king, and Murugan the vel that burns to powder the dark hill, the asuras and our two deeds, who dwells in the poet's love with Valli.
nuance: The plea is a vision, not a confession: bath, possession by Sivam, transformation into the god's form (அக வடிவு உன்றன் வடிவம் என), and the dance. பரி என்ப நரிகள் தமை and மதுரை நடராஜன் name the foxes turned to horses, a Madurai sacred game of Siva. பழியஞ்சி may be the Madurai Siva's name 'who feared blame', and புண்டரிக வடிவ may point to Chidambaram; both are unclear. The same vel burns the asuras and 'our two deeds'.

reading: The poet confesses that, not knowing how to end the great maya that takes as 'I' a leather bag of the five elements oozing the mire of desire, he tends a body that ghosts, vultures, jackals and crows will tear and drag, and asks Murugan to uproot him from this clown's life driven as if by a madman and give his feet. The praise tells of Murugan changing form to court the hunter girl in the bamboo forest, riding the peacock, striking golden Meru to its roots and burning hostile beings to ash to guard heaven.
nuance: தோற்பை யான் ஆக நோக்கும் மா மாயை: the delusion named is taking the body for oneself, not only lust. தீ, உதை, தாத்ரி, பானீயம், வான்: the five elements in mixed Tamil and Sanskrit. பேயோன் நடாத்து கோமாளி வாழ்க்கை, a buffoon's life run by a madman, is the song's sharpest image.

reading: Against sophist sectarians who rise quivering to argue and plant flag against flag, the poet asks to be wholly Murugan's servant and given, without fault, the meaning of the one word that makes plain the first principle unknown to the Vedas. The praise shows a trained troupe of ghosts drinking, dancing and bathing in a sea of blood, smashing hills, and reciting, beginning and ending Thiruppugazh songs, as Murugan crushes the demons in a blink.
nuance: படிப்பன திருப்புகழ் எடுப்பன முடிப்பன: the book names itself, sung by the ghosts of the battlefield. ஒரு மொழிப்பொருள், the meaning of one word, likely points to Om but does not name it. The first half's chain of -ன verbs (துகைப்பன, அறுப்பன, துணிப்பன, விழுப்பன), trampling and cutting heads, is hard to assign: it may describe the poet's victory over the debaters in argument or the vel's work.

tamil: துத்தி நச்ச ராவிளம் பிச்சி நொச்சி கூவிளஞ்
சுத்த ரத்த பாடலம் பொற்க டுக்கை யேடலஞ்
புத்தெ ருக்கு பாழிகங் கொத்தெ டுத்த தாளிதண்
புத்தி சித்தி வாய்கனஞ் சுத்த சத்ய வாசகம்
பத்தி யுற்ற தோகையம் பச்சை வெற்றி வாகனம்
பக்க விட்டு வாய்நிணங் கக்க வெட்டி வாய்தரும்
கைத்த லைப்ர வாகையுந் தத்த ளிக்க மாமுறிந்
கைக்க ளிற்று வாரணம் புக்கொ ளிக்க வாரணங்
reading: The poet lists the adornments of Siva's matted hair (the hooded serpent, jasmine, nochi, vilva, the crescent of nectar, the red patali, golden konrai, the waves of the Ganga, the blue lily, erukku, dhatura) and asks Murugan to give him, whose life is a bubble, the pure true word of weighty wisdom he gave in grace to that Siva. The praise shows Murugan on the peacock, killing the asuras, the sea heaving, Sura as the mango split, Indra's elephant fleeing to hide, and the cock held in his hand.
nuance: புற்புதப் பிராணன், a life like a bubble (budbuda), is the plea's whole self-description, set against the long catalogue of Siva's flowers. வாரணம் returns in the last lines as sea, elephant and cock, a play the rhythm hides. Several flower names and the praise's compounds are uncertain.

tamil: தெரிவை மக்கள் செல்வ முரிமை மிக்க வுண்மை
சினமி குத்த திண்ணர் தனிவ ளைத்து வெய்ய
பரவை புக்கு தொய்யு மரவ ணைக்குள் வைகு
பழுதில் நிற்சொல் சொல்லி யெழுதி நித்த முண்மை
இருகி ரிக்க ளுள்ள வரைத டிக்கு மின்னு
எழுக டற்கு ளுள்ளு முழுகு வித்து விண்ணு
அரிவை பக்க முய்ய வுருகி வைக்கு மைய
அறிவி னுக்கு ளென்னை நெறியில் வைக்க வல்ல
reading: Before his heart can grasp the truth about wife, children, wealth and kin, and before fierce, strong ones surround him, kick him with cruel troubles and break his strength, the poet asks to be given the good of speaking and writing faultless words of Murugan and telling the truth daily. The praise names him Vishnu's nephew, the one who drowned Sura in the seven seas and gave the gods strength, who gave the great truth to Siva, and who is good to the devotees able to keep the poet on the path within knowledge.
nuance: சினமிகுத்த திண்ணர் are likely Death's servants, though the song does not name Yama. நிற்சொல் சொல்லி எழுதி: the plea is for speaking and writing praise, a poet's petition. The last line credits devotees (அடியவர்) with keeping the poet on the path.

reading: In the voice of a love-sick girl, the singer says that the south wind, the pounding sea, the moon scattering fire, the anril bird and the five arrows close in at dusk, and asks the lover to give his garland lovingly so that her heart does not perish. The praise names Murugan whose chest embraces Valli, whose anklets are hung with pearls and bells, whom konrai-wearing Siva once came to worship, and who struck the hill.
nuance: This is akam poetry, not the poet's confession: the request for the hero's garland (அலங்கல்) is the heroine's classical plea. The machinery is that of 24: wind, sea, moon, anril and Kama's arrows at evening.

reading: The poet vows that whether he lives as a king, with drums at a festooned golden gate, young women waving chowries, bards praising his arms and elephants, chariots, banners and horses filling the land, or whether poverty grows, he will speak of nothing but Murugan's feet. The praise names him the cause of the worlds, adorned by the hill-like breasts of the hunter girl, scourge of the asuras who resettled the gods' king in his city, who frightened Brahma and rides the peacock, with supreme wisdom, beauty and manliness.
nuance: There is no confession and no request: வாழினும் வறுமை கூரினும் ... ஒழிய மொழியேனே is a vow of constancy in either fortune. The royal pomp is described at length only to be set aside.

reading: The poet confesses giving his mind willingly to women who strike with poison-sword eyes and covet wealth, a dam built in the conch-filled sea, and asks whether a day will come when he, a wretch packed with shame, will think of Murugan so that the seven troubled births leave and the books he learned rejoice. The praise names him Vishnu's nephew, the young one who crushed the long hill in the sea, and the one who took up the vel to stand beside the hunter woman with pearl-hung breasts and cutting eyes.
nuance: தனத்தை நத்துவார் may mean 'who covet wealth' or refer to breasts; the reading of courtesans rests on that word. கற்ற நூல் உகக்க: the poet's learning is shamed by his life and would be fulfilled by thinking of the Lord. The marker before ளையோனே has lost a syllable.

tamil: நற்குணமு ளார்த மைப்பொல் மைக்குழலி லேசி றக்க
நச்சுவிழி யால்ம யக்கி யிச்சைபல பேசி யுற்று
வெற்பனைய மாத னத்தை பொற்புறவு றாவ ணைத்து
வெட்சிகமழ் நீப புஷ்ப வெற்றிசிறு பாத பத்ம
ரத்தினப ணாதி ருத்தன் மெய்ச்சுதனு நாடு மிக்க
நற்றிசையு மேறி யிட்ட பொய்ச்சமணை வேர றுத்து
சற்சனகு மார வ்ருத்தி அற்புதசி வாய னுக்கொர்
சக்ரதரன் மார்ப கத்தி லுக்ரமுட னேத ரித்த
reading: The poet describes women with flower-decked, fragrant hair who enchant with poison eyes and speak desires, their minds set on wealth, and asks whether, instead of wasting daily in infatuation with them, a day will come when Murugan gives the true grace of his small lotus feet fragrant with vetchi and kadamba. The praise names him the son of Rudra, the Kumara who uprooted the false Jains spread in all directions and spread the holy ash, the true guru of Siva, and the one who set the mark of his spear on the chest of discus-bearing Vishnu.
nuance: பொய்ச் சமணை வேர் அறுத்து நல் திருநீறே பரப்பி: Murugan identified with Sambandar, who drove out the Jains and spread the holy ash. சக்ரதரன் மார்பகத்தில் சத்தி அடையாளம் இட்ட, the vel's mark on Vishnu's chest, is an allusion I cannot identify.

tamil: நாகாங்க ரோமங் காட்டி வாரேந்து நாகங் காட்டி
நானாங்க ராகங் காட்டி நாகேந்த்ர நீலங் காட்டி
மேகாங்க கேசங் காட்டி வாயாம்பல் வாசங் காட்டி
மேல்வீழ்ந்து தோயுந் தூர்த்தன் மோகாந்த காரந் தீர்க்க
ஏகாந்த வீரம் போற்றி நீலாங்க யானம் போற்றி
ஏறோங்க லேழுஞ் சாய்த்த நான்மூன்று தோளும் போற்றி
த்யாகாங்க சீலம் போற்றி வாயோந்தி டாதன் றார்த்து
சேவேந்தி தேசம் பார்க்க வேலேந்தி மீனம் பூத்த
reading: The poet lists what women show, their hair-line like serpents, bodiced breasts, marked foreheads, cosmetics, dark eyes, cloud-black hair and lily-scented mouths, until he would ride the madal and falls upon those who drag out his life, and asks Murugan to show the lamp of Vedanta to end this rogue's darkness of delusion. The praise is a chain of 'hail': to his lone valour, his blue steed, his kadamba garland, his twelve arms that toppled the seven hills, his generosity that gives what anyone asks; he defeated Sura and guarded Indra's starry world.
nuance: The refrain காட்டி, 'showing', runs through both halves: the women show their bodies, and the poet asks the Lord to show (காட்டி) the lamp of Vedanta instead. மடல் ஊர, to ride the palmyra horse, is the akam lover's public last resort, here turned on the poet himself. போற்றி is the praise's refrain.

reading: Melting like wax in fire before women with musk-scented, flower-decked hair and carp-eyes that fight like weapons by their earrings, the poet asks Murugan to end the suffering in which the two deeds torment him and he loses strength and sense. The praise names him younger brother of the elephant-faced one, the hero whose golden arms embrace Valli, and the six-faced one who fought with the vel while drums sounded and countless ghosts danced.

The poet seems to confess going to vel-eyed women for money, losing his settled hold like a weed in a crop, and the pride of learned verse in which the inner self perishes, and asks Murugan to end that trouble, let him hold the feet and grant him the thought of release. The praise names Vishnu who dried the round sea to fight, Siva beyond reach whose great life Murugan is, the vel that struck the long hill in rage, and the Tamil of release that siddhas hold in their minds and praise.
nuance: The song is set in doubled hard consonants (பற்றநெட் டைப்படைத் துட்டிருட் டை...), and most of the first half resists division into words; the reading is a guess at its outline. கவிக் கொட்டம், the arrogance of poets, would make this a confession of the poet's own pride. முத்தித் தமிழ், the Tamil of release, closes the song.

tamil: பாதக மான யாக்கை வாதுசெய் பாவி கோத்த
பாரப டிர மாப்ப யோதர மாதர் வாய்த்த
தோதக மாய வார்த்தை போதக மாக நோக்கு
சூழும னாதி நீத்த யானொடு தானி லாச்சு
சாதன வேத நூற்பு ராதன பூண நூற்ப்ர
சாகர சூர வேட்டை யாடிய வீர வேற்ப்ர
மாதவன் மாது பூத்த பாகர னேக நாட்ட
மாமலர் தூவி வாழ்த்த யானையை மாலை சூட்டி
reading: The poet calls himself an impure dog who takes as instruction the deceitful words of women who cheat on their beds, with eyes sharper than Kama's arrows and swords, and asks for the word of wisdom, rising bliss without 'I' and 'mine', that will end his deeds and the beginningless bond that surrounds him. The praise shows Brahma of the Vedas and sacred thread humbled, the hill struck, Sura hunted in the sea, Indra praising and restored, and Murugan garlanding Devayanai and guarding the gods' army.
nuance: தோதகமாய வார்த்தை போதகமாக நோக்கு: the poet takes the women's deceit (தோதகம்) as teaching (போதகம்), a rhyme that is the song's point. யானொடு தானிலா, without I and self, and சூழும் அநாதி, the beginningless that surrounds, point to the Saiva idea of beginningless bondage. A syllable before ருபார்வை is lost.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 19 of 21): the poet traces the body from the womb to the burning ground, sets kin and Death's rope against the feet, confesses the lure of women and calls himself every name of fault, and asks for steady wisdom, the yogic ascent to the thousand-petalled lotus, the company of devotees and release; one song is a love-lament and one a vow not to forget the feet even in lovemaking.
structure_note: Life-cycle songs: 1263 (Brahma shaping the body), 1265 (born, crawled, walked, became a corpse), 1270 (the body of filth and bone), 1272 (from conception to the harlot's net). Kin and Death: 1266 and 1267. Yoga: 1264 and 1275. Women: 1262, 1271, 1273, 1276. Self-reproach: 1269. Akam lament: 1268. 1274 asks to join the devotees, with a Krishna praise.
source_issues: 1262: line 274 (ஆக நகம்பட ஆர முயங்கிய) has no beat marker and may have lost words.
1269: மிகுமுனருபதானம் and நடைபெறு க்டுர are garbled.
1271: விநன்முடி is garbled.
1275: நநடு doubles a syllable.
1276: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ யர்தலங், உ லகமும்).

reading: The poet describes lovemaking with women, hair loosening, breasts thrilled, the drinking of mouths and the nail-marks of passion on the bed, and asks whether he will forget that desire and know Murugan. The praise tells the Valli story at length: at Narada's word Murugan went seeking his lady in the millet field, lost his shame, changed his form in deceit, walked till his lotus feet ached, struck by Kama's arrows, up the hunters' hill, and married the girl born of the deer the great sage joined.
nuance: The praise matches the confession: நாணம் அழிந்து, மார சரம்பட மோகமுடன், the god himself is shamed and struck by Kama for Valli. Line 274 lacks its beat marker and may have lost a word.

reading: Before the waves of suffering of this body arise, the body that Brahma skilfully fashions with disease, deeds and troubles, a hut with hands and two legs into which life enters and which is sent into the world and ends in fire, the poet asks for a love for life that says 'Murugan who comes on the emerald peacock'. The praise names the vel that pierced the hill and dried the sea, the Tamil-mouthed one who gave sweet Tamil to Siva so the two deeds would leave, and the Lord who pities the poor more than those who sing with many arts.
nuance: பிரமனும் விரகொடு பிணி வினை இடர் கொடு: Brahma builds the body out of disease and deeds themselves. இசை மொழிபவரினும் ஏழைக்கு இரங்கும்: the Lord prefers the helpless to the accomplished singers, a striking claim from a poet.

tamil: பூதக லாதிகள் கொண்டு யோகமு மாகம கிழ்ந்து
போம்வழி யேதுதெ ரிந்து ஆதிய நாதியி ரண்டு
நாதப ராபர மென்ற யோகியு லாசம றிந்து
நாடியொ ராயிரம் வந்த தாமரை மீதில மர்ந்த
வேதபு ராணம்வி ளம்பி நீலமு ராரியர் தங்கை
வேடமெ லாமுக சங்க பாடலொ டாடல்ப யின்ற
reading: The poet asks whether, knowing the elements and kalas, rejoicing in yoga and worship and the way faults go, knowing the yogi's delight called Nada-Paraparam that came out of Bindu and the full and causal power, feeling the breath of wisdom and seeing the light, he will reach the two feet of the Lord seated on the lotus where a thousand nadis meet. The praise is a litany of the Goddess, Sarvesvari, Kali, Pidari, Vani, Varahi, Abhirami, Sivakami, Uma, sister of Vishnu, mother of the worlds, consort of the matted-haired dancer, who bore Murugan.
nuance: நாடி ஒராயிரம் வந்த தாமரை is the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown, where the Lord's feet are to be reached. The sequence பூரணி காரணி விந்து வெளியான நாத பராபரம் sets Shakti, Bindu and Nada in the yogic order, and the praise turns entirely to the Goddess. How the opening (பூதகலாதிகள்) divides is uncertain.

reading: The poet traces the body: they came in love, formed in the womb, were born, lay, sat, crawled, walked, weakened and became corpses, carried to the burning forest and burned; and he, worn out by this ruined body that falls when desire goes, asks Murugan to say 'fear not'. The praise tells of Rama going into the forest with his younger brother, crying 'where is my lady?', and of the monkey that burned Lanka, names Murugan his nephew, and Valli's partner whom the gods praise.
nuance: பிறந்தார் கிடந்தார் இருந்தார் தவழ்ந்தார் நடந்தார் தளர்ந்து பிணமானார்: a life told as a list of verbs, in the plural of what others did. The plea asks only for reassurance (அஞ்சல்).

reading: Before Death, the wicked punisher, throws his long rope and seizes his life while brothers born with him, kin and wife gather in the house quarrelling daily and his attachment to wealth grows, the poet asks to melt with devotion to the guru and be given words of Murugan's truth to speak of his feet. The praise names him the one whose victory in beautiful Tamil is praised beyond the directions, Valli's bridegroom who loves the sweetness of her words in the hut, the teacher who gave the three-eyed Siva the beginning of release, and the piercer of Krauncha.
nuance: The household is pictured as a daily quarrel over property (நித்தப் பிணக்கிட்டு ... பொருட்பற்று). நிற் தத்துவச் சொற்கள்: the plea is for doctrine as speech. குருப் பத்தி may be devotion to Murugan as guru or to a human teacher.

reading: Before Yama comes on his black buffalo seeking him and twists out his life, while the great illusory grief, deeper than the sea, for children, mothers, in-laws, wife and dependents withers him, the poet asks for a little of Murugan's lotus feet so that he may live with his mind stilled. The praise recalls Siva burning Kama with his third eye before the gods in yoga, and names Murugan the one who gave unattainable knowledge to Vishnu, who melts at the songs of devotees and is sweet to Devayanai and Valli.
nuance: மாயத் துயரம்: the grief for kin is called illusory, and the list of relatives is the burden. சித்தம் ஓவித் துயிலும் அற்று: the stilling of mind and end of sleep is the life asked for. Who receives the 'knowledge beyond reach' (எட்டொணா வித்தை) is unclear.

reading: In the voice of someone watching a love-sick girl, the singer says that the moon-faced creeper, wounded by Kama's fresh lotus arrow and the pearl-and-shell sea, frightened on her fragrant bed, her clothes and hair in disorder, is wasting away, and asks the lover to send his kura blossoms quickly. The praise names Murugan whose feet are worshipped by Brahma and Vishnu, Valli's bridegroom, dweller in the lotus of Saravana pool, who fought the asura armies.
nuance: This is akam poetry, not the poet's confession; the speaker is likely the mother or friend. The request for the hero's flowers (குரவு அலர்) matches the garland asked for in 1254. புதனை in the praise is obscure.

tamil: மதிதனை யிலாத பாவி குருநெற யிலாத கோபி
வகையது விடாத பேடி தவநினை விலாத மோடி
விதியிலி பொலாத லோபி சபைதனில் வராத கோழை
மிகுபர மதான ஞான நெறிதனை விசார மாக
எதிர்வரு முதார சூர னிருபிள வதாக வேலை
இனியசொல் மறாத சீலர் கருவழி வராமல் நாளும்
நதியுட னராவு பூணு பரமர்குரு நாத னான
நகைமுக விநோத ஞான குறமினுட னேகு லாவு
reading: The poet calls himself a chain of names, senseless sinner, angry man without a guru's path, ghost whose mind won't settle, coward who will not leave maya, idler who never thinks of penance, miser, one who shuns the assembly, wretch who will not leave the quarrel of deeds, and asks to be given the path of supreme wisdom to reflect on. The praise names the Kumara whose vel split Sura in two, who keeps sweet-spoken virtuous people from the womb and ever young, the guru of Siva who wears the river and serpent, and Valli's lover.
nuance: The self-abuse is the song's whole first half: each epithet ends in a noun of contempt (பாவி, கோபி, பேயன், பேடி, மோடி, லோபி, கோழை, கூளன்). இனிய சொல் மறாத சீலர் கருவழி வராமல்: those who keep sweet speech are spared rebirth. மிகுமுனருபதானம் and நடைபெறு க்டுர are garbled.

reading: Before the breath leaves this cage made of filth, skin, water and bone and father, wife, mother and kin cry out at the burning ground, the poet asks to become Murugan's servant who worships him. The praise names Murugan the great life who proclaims the sastras while Siva the dancer watches and praises, the vel that struck Sura in the sea, and the Lord who gives to those who guard dharma without sleeping.
nuance: The song is set in doubled hard syllables (மலந்தோற் சலந்தேற் றெலும்பாற்), and the body as கூடு of filth and bone is clear while much else is a guess. Murugan teaching sastra with Siva as delighted listener repeats the teacher-of-Siva theme.

tamil: மனநூறு கோடி துன்ப நொடிமீதி லேநி னைந்து
மடமாத ராசை கொண்டு புவிமீதி லேம யங்கி
விநன்முடி யேதி ரிந்து புவிமீதி லேயு ழன்று
விசையான தோகை துங்க மயிலேறி யோடி வந்து
தினைவேடர் காவல் தங்கு மலைகாடெ லாமு ழன்று
திரையாழி சேது கண்டு பொருராவ ணேசை வென்ற
முனிவோர்கள் தேவ ரும்பர் சிறையாக வேவ ளைந்த
முடிகோடி தூளெ ழுந்து கழுகோடு பாற ருந்த
reading: The poet confesses a mind that thinks a hundred crore sorrows in an instant, embracing in Kama's sulks, desire for women that deluded him and wasted his sense, and a body weakened by lust, and asks that on the day it falls Murugan come running on his peacock and give the house of open wisdom. The praise names him the Kumara who wandered the hunters' hills and bowed at the girl's feet, nephew of Vishnu who as Rama built the bridge and defeated Ravana, and the vel that crushed the demons who imprisoned sages and gods, leaving them to vultures.
nuance: வெளி ஞான வீடு, the house of open (spacious) wisdom, is the release asked for. சிறுபேதை கால் பணிந்த: Murugan bowing at Valli's feet. விநன்முடி in line 3 is garbled.

reading: The poet traces his life from conception in passion through the womb, the months and birth, to crawling, wearing jewels, walking, wandering as he pleased, smearing on stinking civet and mixing in the harlot's net, and asks whether he must die so. The praise tells of Vishnu splitting the crocodile when the elephant cried 'First one, refuge!', names his tortoise, fish, boar, dwarf and man-lion forms, and Siva as the column of light at Arunai, and ends with Murugan embracing Valli.
nuance: The life comes full circle: it begins in மாதர் மயல் and ends in வேசி வலை. The images of gestation (தேனுகுடம் எனத் திரண்டு, a gathering like a honey pot) are hard to read exactly. The Gajendra story and the avatars are named outright.

reading: The poet describes women whose pearl-hung breasts are like an elephant's tusks and whose spear eyes wound, so that his mind is clouded, his pure sense gone and he whirls in grief, and asks instead to worship the two feet with many words on his tongue and be given a little of the life of the lotus. The praise names Vishnu who in wrath felled the ten heads, Murugan's courtship of Valli, the meaning of the Veda that frees devotees from deeds, and the Lord praised by those learned in devotion and wisdom.
nuance: சொற்கமல வாழ்வு may mean the life of the lotus feet won by words, or a 'lotus of speech'; the plea is again for praise as the way.

tamil: முருகம யூரச் சேவக சரவண ஏனற் பூதரி
முழுகிய காதற் காமுக பதிபசு பாசத் தீர்வினை
றுருகியு மாடிப் பாடியு மிருகழல் நாடிச் சூடியு
றுலகினொ ராசைப் பாடற நிலைபெறு ஞானத் தாலினி
மருகனெ னாமற் சூழ்கொலை கருதிய மாமப் பாதகன்
வருமத யானைக் கோடவை திருகிவி ளாவிற் காய்கனி
பொருதிரு கோரப் பாரிய மருதிடை போயப் போதொரு
பொதுவியர் சேரிக் கேவளர் புயல்மரு காவஜ் ராயுத
reading: Calling Murugan peacock warrior, Saravana, lover immersed in Valli's breasts, and guru who taught old Siva the end of the bonds of Lord, soul and bond, melting, dancing, singing, seeking and wearing his feet, the poet asks whether a day will come when, with worldly desire gone, he joins Murugan's devotees through steady wisdom. The praise is a Krishna catalogue: the demoness's breast drunk, the elephant's tusks wrenched, the wood-apple demon struck, the bird, the twin marutha trees and the cart, the child reared in the cowherds' settlement, and names Murugan his nephew.
nuance: பதி பசு பாசத் தீர்வினை: the Saiva Siddhanta triad of pati, pasu and pasa is the teaching Murugan gives Siva here. உணர்வினோடு ஊடிக் கூடியும், sulking and reuniting, brings the lover's quarrel into worship. The goal is the company of devotees, not release alone.

reading: The poet asks for the light sought above the root centre in the forest of the mind's delusion, the state of silence, the secret instruction by which Murugan's play teaches a way not given in the many paths, and the steady, unfading gem-light in the middle channel. The praise names him Vishnu's nephew, guru to Siva the lord of the trident whose foot kicked Yama, and the light dancing to drum syllables.
nuance: மூலா நிலமதின் மேலே and நடு வழி point to the muladhara and the central channel of yoga; வாடா மணி ஒளி is the light at its end. ரகசிய உபதேசம், secret instruction, makes Murugan the yogi's guru. நநடு doubles a syllable, and நாலா ருசி அமுது is obscure.

reading: The poet describes lovemaking frankly, reddened eyes, sweat, ringing anklets, loosened hair, shaking breasts and bending waist, and says that even if he embraces women and his mind is deluded, he will not forget Murugan's shining feet. The praise recalls the churning of the sea when poison rose and the gods begged in fear, and Murugan on the great peacock that shook the heights and protected the world.
nuance: மதிமயங்கினும் ... நின் பதங்கள் மறவேனே: unlike most songs, this one does not ask to be freed from women but vows remembrance in the midst of them.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 20 of 21): after two long songs on lovemaking and on women's eyes, the chapter turns to short songs that ask not to be born again, for the experience of the feet, for the word beyond the quarrelling scriptures, and against singing for deceitful patrons; Murugan appears as Sambandar who impaled the Jains, and three akam songs give the lovesick girl's plight under Kama, the sea, the cuckoo and the moon.
structure_note: Four long songs (1277 to 1280), then short eight-line songs (1281 to 1291, with 1289 longer). 1285 and 1291 are two versions of one akam song (Kama's arrows, the blue sea, the cuckoo, 'embrace the deer'), and 1290 is a third on the moon and the south wind. 1282 and 1287 both end with Murugan as Sambandar.
source_issues: 1279: corrupt glyph in மிடறு஡ட்டு, read மிடறூட்டு (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS).
1280: ஞான்ரு பத்தின் in line 8 should probably be ஞானரூபத்தின்.
1283: corrupt glyph in கருப்பற்று஡றி, read கருப்பற்றூறி (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS).
1287: a stray space after the vowel உ splits words at line starts (உ மைமுலை, உ ரிய).

tamil: வரிவிழி பூச லாட இருகுழை யூச லாட
மணிவட மாலை யாட முருகவி ழோதி யாட
இருவரு மேக போக மொருவர்த மாக மாக
இருகர மாறு மாறு மறுமுக நீப மார்பு
திருநட மாடு காளி பயிரவி மோடி சூலி
குருபர நாத னாகி யரனொரு காதி லோது
குறமக ளார பார முகிழ்முலை மீது தாது
reading: The poet describes lovemaking in full motion, eyes battling, earrings, breasts, bangles and garlands swaying, honey dripping from the flowered hair, two becoming one body in maya, and vows that even then he will not forget Murugan's twelve arms, six faces, kadamba-garlanded chest and two feet. The praise calls him the child of grace of the dancing Kali, Bhairavi and trident-bearer who burned Tripura, Sivai of Kailasa, daughter of the mountain, and the guru who spoke into Siva's ear, whose garland rests on the Kuratti's breasts.
nuance: Unusually the plea does not ask to escape the embrace: மாயை படுபோதும் ... மறவேனே, 'even when I fall into maya I will not forget', makes remembrance of the Lord hold within the act itself. அரன் ஒரு காதில் ஓது: Murugan teaching Siva in the ear, Om not named. The goddess is given a run of fierce names (காளி, பயிரவி, மோடி, சூலி) before the gentle ones.

reading: The poet lists women's red spear-eyes that cut the lives of men and sages, their fragrant hair, smiles, musk-painted breasts, sweet lips, navel and waist, and asks whether Murugan will not lovingly think to grant, beyond that union, the cruel miry life and endless births, the great pure state of silent supreme bliss. The praise is a head-to-foot picture of Murugan: six faces, jewelled forehead ornament, twelve eyes of compassion and twelve earrings, lotus hands, sacred thread, waist-bells, anklets, peacock and vel, the beautiful Kumara, son of three-eyed Siva who melts with the mountain's daughter.
nuance: The song sets two catalogues against each other: the woman's body part by part in the plea, and Murugan's form part by part in the praise, so that beauty is redirected rather than renounced. ஒரு மவுன பரமசுக சுத்தப் பெரும்பதம் names the goal as silence and bliss. புண்டாணகச் சுழிமடு is hard to divide.

reading: The poet asks not to wander sharpening infatuation, caught in the torment of women whose voices are like the vina and whose eyes are poison and spear-points, nor to perish greedily piling up house and wealth, but that Murugan feed the scripture of knowledge into the nest where life dwells and show him the true state. The praise calls him the one who dwells in the land of the Veda, the gracious Vel who heard Nakkirar's composition set to song, who embraces the hunter girl of the high forest, and who set fire to the demons' land and freed the gods from prison.
nuance: ஆவியுறை கூட்டில் ஞானமறை ஊட்டி: the body is the nest of the life, to be fed with knowledge rather than with women and wealth. கீரர் இயல் கேட்ட names Nakkirar, the poet of the Tirumurugatruppadai, as one whose poem Murugan received. The line on hunters of the knowledge path who sought a tank (கேணியுற வேட்ட ஞானநெறி வேட்டர்) is obscure, and ஆணியுள வீட்டை is unclear.

reading: The poet, wandering infatuated in the danger of women whose tormenting eyes equal the sea, the sword, the halahala poison and Kama's arrows, asks to leave that tumult, have the distortion of the gunas run off and grow clear, and be given the greatness of joining the path of the unspeakable supreme form of knowledge. The praise names Rama who loosed the arrow that split Vali's chest and the seven sal trees, the blue-bodied Vishnu who blew the conch, Murugan as his nephew who uproots the base, and the lord who unites with the hunters' peacock-like girl.
nuance: குணவிகாரம் ஓட: the disturbance of the qualities must run away before clarity (தெளிய) comes, and the goal is கூறொணா தற்பரம ஞானரூபம், the supreme knowledge-form that cannot be spoken. The conch episode (அமரேசன் ஒலிக்க வளை ஊதி மோகித்து விழ) is not clear to me, nor வெருப at the end of line 2.

reading: The poet asks not to be born on this earth, not to mix with cheats, not to grow weary reciting the three Tamils, and to be given release. The praise calls Murugan the guru of true knowledge of the tattvas, the one whose form is sound, the eternal good life, and the light of the world who dances.
nuance: முத்தமிழை ஓதித் தளராதே seems to set even the recitation of Tamil among the things that wear one out, perhaps poems recited for patrons as in 1284; the plain sense is uncertain. சத்த சொரூபா: Murugan as sound itself.

reading: The poet asks that the chain of his binding deeds be removed and that he be given the state that, triumphant and in bliss, overflowing with love like the nectar of the milk ocean, desires that end. The praise says Murugan, having resolved it in mind, took a small form and danced the bharata to the beat, and as Sambandar filled the land with Tamil so that those who do penance to end their bonds had their want removed.
nuance: சம்பந்தன் எனத் தமிழ் தேக்கிய: Murugan identified with the child-saint Sambandar, whose small form (சிறுவடிவு) and dancing are those of the boy. The second half of the plea (அந்தந்தனில் இச்சைகொள் ஆற்பதம்) is hard to construe.

reading: The poet asks not to be born again oozing out of a womb, not to wander in heavy suffering, and that Murugan protect him so that the experience of his holy golden feet may flourish. The praise calls him the one who belongs to those free of attachment, the ornament of the beyond, holder of the cock banner, the light of the world.
nuance: அநுபூதி, direct experience of the feet, is the goal, a word that recurs in 1293 and 1294. பரப்பற்றாருக்கு உரியோனே: he belongs to those who have cut their clinging. The glyph ஡ in line 1 stands for ஊ (கருப்பற்றூறி).

tamil: கருப்பை யிற்சுக் கிலத் துலைத்துற் பவித்து ...... மறுகாதே
கபட்ட சட்டர்க் கிதத்த சித்ரத் தமிழ்க்க ...... ளுரையாதே
விருப்ப முற்றுத் துதித்தெ னைப்பற் றெனக்க ...... ருதுநீயே
வெளிப்ப டப்பற் றிடப்ப டுத்தத் தருக்கி ...... மகிழ்வோனே
பருப்ப தத்தைத் தொளைத்த சத்திப் படைச்ச ...... மரவேளே
பணிக்கு லத்தைக் கவர்ப்ப தத்துக் களித்த ...... மயிலோனே
செருப்பு றத்துச் சினத்தை முற்றப் பரப்பு ...... மிசையோனே
தினைப்பு னத்துக் குறத்தி யைக்கைப் பிடித்த ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet asks not to be churned about, born from seed in the womb, and not to recite colourful Tamil poems that please deceitful scoundrels; he says Murugan regards him as one who praised him longing to be held. The praise names the Vel whose Sakti weapon pierced the mountain, the peacock delighting in seizing serpents, the one whose fame spreads in battle, and the lord who took the Kuratti's hand in the millet field.
nuance: கபட்ட சட்டர்க்கு இதத்த சித்ரத் தமிழ்கள் உரையாதே: the refusal to spend Tamil on flattering false patrons, so that praise is kept for the Lord. The line வெளிப்படப் பற்றிடப்படுத்தத் தருக்கி மகிழ்வோனே is obscure and my reading of the plea's second half is tentative.

reading: An akam plea in the voice of the girl's mother or friend: tormented by the arrows of cruel Kama, the roaring blue sea and the cuckoo of the grove, the deer-like girl has lost her composure, so let Murugan embrace her. The praise calls him dear to Siva who wears the serpent, the learned poet who knows the arts, Vela, harbour of his devotees' love, the six-faced lord.
nuance: நிலைமை கெடு மானைத் தழுவாயே: the plea is not for release but for the god's embrace of the lovesick girl. The sea's roar and the cuckoo's call are the classical tormentors of separation. Nearly the same song stands at 1291.

reading: The poet asks not to wander in the great net of women with Meru-like breasts, and whether Murugan cannot think to rule this dog so that he may rise each day. The praise names the one who taught knowledge so that souls may be saved, who bears twelve shoulders, who is dear to Siva who rides the bull, and the six-faced lord of the elephant-maiden.
nuance: நாயேனை ஆள: the plea is to be taken as servant. மாதானை may be மாது ஆனை, Devayanai, or a great army; I take the first.

reading: The poet asks to leave the vain devotion of the sects and, seeking the worship of Siva at the lotus feet, to be given grace through the true guru's scriptures and teaching. The praise names Murugan as the one who drank the milk of Uma's breast and spoke grace, made true penance his own, showed the farther shore of Tamil teaching, and impaled the Jains, that is, as Sambandar.
nuance: சமய பத்தி வ்ருதா: devotion within the sects is vain, but Siva-worship (சிவார்ச்சனை) is not counted a sect. உமைமுலைத் தரு பால், சமணரைக் கழுவேற்றிய: the unmistakable details of Sambandar, given here to Murugan.

reading: The poet asks whether he will gain the word of the heart that is not settled in the mass of quarrelling scriptures nor in the six-fold seat, and that is hard to gain even by the rare Vedas. The praise calls Murugan the one who fought the demons as the seven seas roared, and the close companion of poets who sing to gain wealth from his feet.
nuance: சருவிய சாத்திரத் திரள்: the scriptures that quarrel, as in 1287's vain sects. சடுதிகழ் ஆஸ்பதம் may be the six systems, and அனிதய வார்த்தை, perhaps a word from the heart or beyond it, is obscure. பொருள் அடியால் பெறக் கவிபாடும் புலவர் can also mean poets who seek the meaning through the feet.

reading: The poet asks whether he will escape the road to the deceit of women who rage and hiss, laugh and talk to bind him in infatuation, flaunt their breasts and half hide them in cloth, tend him until his mind is soothed, and then plunder his wealth. The praise recalls Murugan seeking a way to unite with the Kuratti guarding the millet field while bees sang, coaxing her unseen by her clansmen, and asks him for his feet as the one who fought until Sura died.
nuance: தனத்தைச் சூறைகொள் மடவார்: the wealth taken is named, and சதி (deceit) closes the list. The praise sets Murugan's own secret courtship of Valli, hidden from her kin, against the women's false intimacy.

reading: An akam plea: should the innocent girl suffer because of the moon that rises to harm her, the south wind that scatters fire, and Kama who dances with his flowers? The praise names the king who punished Brahma of the Veda, the chest the hunter's doll desires, the Vel that struck the mango in the sea, the lord of the speechless gods.
nuance: The tormentors are the stock of the evening of separation: moon, south wind, Kama (அநங்கன்). ஓதச் சூதம் எறிந்த வேலா: Sura as the mango tree in the sea. ஊமைத் தேவர்கள் may be the gods struck dumb, perhaps for not knowing Om; I cannot place it.

reading: A variant of 1285: by Kama's leaping arrows, the long blue sea and the cuckoo coming softly from the grove, the girl's body melts, and Murugan is asked to embrace her. The praise calls him the one clear in singing lucid Tamil, the valiant Kumaresa, whose anklets of knowledge Valli worships, Valli's bridegroom.
nuance: Line for line the same frame as 1285 with different adjectives (துள்ளும், தொல்லை, மெள்ள, மெய்யுருகு), as if two drafts of one song survive. வள்ளல் தொழு may refer to Valli or to a generous devotee.

title: பொதுப்பாடல்கள்
theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 21 of 21): short songs that ask for the knowledge that cuts 'I' and 'mine', for the experience (அநுபூதி) and dance of knowledge, for the vision of the feet beyond the river of births, the net of family and the women who want gold, and for knowledge no book can hold; three akam songs give the lovesick girl under Kama, the moon and the town's gossip, and the book ends on a fragmentary song of Murugan's hill and battle.
structure_note: Thirteen eight-line songs (1292 to 1304), of which 1296, 1297 and 1303 are akam; 1303 repeats the frame of 1290 in the previous chapter. 1305 is a long song printed with gaps (marked ...), apparently incomplete.
source_issues: 1305: the song is printed with gaps marked ... and a broken line structure; parts of the text are missing.
1299 and 1305: a stray space after the vowel உ splits words at line starts (உ றுதி, உ னது, உ ழுவைகள், உ லவு, உ லகர்கள்).

reading: The poet asks not to think of serving women whose words are sweet as honey, and that he be given to know the understanding in which 'I' and 'mine' are cut away. The praise calls Murugan dear to Indra, king of the gods, younger brother of the elephant-faced one, the six-faced lord.
nuance: யான் எனது அற்றிடு போதம்: the same pair of 'I' and 'mine' that the Kural names as the root of bondage; here its cutting is asked as a gift of knowledge, not achieved by effort.

reading: The poet asks not to think of desire for women but to seek Murugan's two lotus feet, and to be given the experience that is nectar, sugar and honey. The praise names him the cause of all, of excellent nature, who unites with the forest Kuratti, whose vel fought Sura's kin to dust, rider of the peacock.
nuance: The sweetness the poet turns from (women) returns as the sweetness of அநுபூதி, nectar, sugar and honey (ஆரமுதமான சர்க்கரை தேனே). காரணமதான: Murugan as the cause.

reading: The poet asks that to him, a poor one who seeks the dance of knowledge with a melting that grows every day, the wealth of experience may flourish. The praise calls Murugan the child given by Siva who wears poolai and erukku flowers, the moon and the snake, and the lord who called the elephant at the right moment.
nuance: நாளும் மிகுத்த கசிவு: devotion as a melting that grows daily. ஞான நிருத்தம், the dance of knowledge, is the object sought. வேளை தனக்கு உசிதமாக வேழம் அழைத்த likely alludes to Murugan calling the elephant (Ganesa) to frighten Valli into his arms, but the text gives only the elephant and the timing.

reading: The poet, thinking of and seeking Murugan daily, asks that with those who have attained nishtha as his companions, and by the path of their high austerity, he be given the dance of the aim and its marks. The praise calls him nephew of the conch-bearer Vishnu who sent destruction on the kin of the victorious rakshasas, dweller in the hearts of the faultless, bearer of the cock banner.
nuance: நிட்டை பெற்று இயல் கருத்தர் துணையாக: the company of those established in contemplation is the means. லக்ய லக்கண நிருத்தம் may mean the dance that is both the goal and its sign; நத்தியு தமதவத்தின் is hard to split.

reading: An akam plea, in the voice of the girl's mother or friend: having seen Murugan come in glory on his peacock like a dark blue cloud, the girl is infatuated, so let him give her the fragrant garland on his chest. The praise names the Vel who once hurled the vel at the sea, death to the clan of valiant Suras, meaning of the four Vedas, the lord who strikes his chest saying 'It is I'.
nuance: மால்கொண்ட பேதை: the girl's infatuation began with a sight of the god's procession, and what is asked is his garland (தார்), the classical token of the hero's acceptance. நான் என்று மார் தட்டும் gives Murugan a warrior's boast.

reading: An akam plea: is it right that the girl sink in sorrow because of Kama, who died yet did not die, the reproach of the women nearby, and moonlight that burns without burning? The praise calls Murugan the hero of unchecked strength, death to the arguing Sura clan, rider of the unrestrained peacock, the peerless lord.
nuance: The plea is built on paradoxes: பட்டுப் படாத மதன், Kama burned by Siva yet alive, and சுட்டுச் சுடாத நிலவு, moonlight that scorches without fire. பக்கத்து மாதர் வசை is the town's gossip of akam poetry.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to come and grant boons in plenty, so that he may become a master fit for Murugan's line, as his father was found fit to carry a message to Paravai again and again. The praise names him younger brother of the karpaka-like elephant god, husband of the Kuratti whose eyes are bows, the one who told Siva what was fitting, and who knocked Brahma on the head.
nuance: பரவைக்கு எத்தனை விசை தூது: Paravai is the wife of the saint Sundarar, to whom Siva went as messenger at his devotee's bidding, and the plea asks for grace on that scale. அரனுக்கு உற்றது புகல்வோனே, அயனைக் குட்டிய: the teaching of Siva and the punishing of Brahma, the story elsewhere told of Om, which is not named here. The construction of the plea's first two lines is uncertain.

reading: The poet asks not to enter the river of births with its waves nor wander on the path of nature, but by the meaning of the guru's sure word to be given the vision of Murugan's feet. The praise calls him the meaning of the scriptures of the six creeds, an ocean of virtue to those who know the knowledge within knowledge, the lord of the three Tamils whom the short sage Agastya praises, Kumaraguru of the Krittikas.
nuance: பிரகிருதி மார்க்கம்: the path of nature, of the body and its tattvas, set against the guru's word (குரு வாக்கியப் பொருள்). அறுசமய சாத்திரப் பொருளோனே: here Murugan is the meaning the six creeds share, where 1287 and 1288 call sectarian devotion vain. குறுமுனிவன் ஏத்தும் முத்தமிழோனே: Murugan as Tamil, praised by Agastya.

reading: The poet asks Murugan to think of revealing in grace the wise attainment of knowledge that cannot be completed by writing on the leaves of books, and of gently gathering him in and guarding him. The praise names him the one who won fame by honouring and praising the girl who dwells in the forest where parrots play, and who guarded the karpaka grove.
nuance: புத்தகத்து ஏட்டில் தீட்டி முடியாது: the knowledge sought is beyond what can be written in a book, so it must be given by grace (அருளாலே). The line கைத்தலத் தீக்குப் பார்த்து நுழையாத is obscure; it may say the grove was one that (the demons) feared to enter.

reading: The poet, who wavers desiring the meanness of public women who desire gold, asks that Murugan, desiring him, grant him once to desire to think of Murugan. The praise calls him the guru desired truly by Siva of the lightning-bright matted hair, who drew near and desired the Kuratti whom the mother desired.
nuance: Every line turns on விரும்பு, desire: the women desire gold, the poet desires their meanness, Murugan is asked to desire the poet so that the poet may desire him, and Siva and Murugan desire in turn. The wordplay moves desire from gold to grace. பொதுமாதர் and பொன்னை விரும்பிய name the courtesans' trade.

reading: Not knowing how to cross the net of maya called house, children and kin, swollen with his deeds, the poet, a dog of a servant, asks whether he must pour water on weeds. The praise calls Murugan bridegroom of the Kuratti who plays stirring up the spring, and the lord who cut the gods free from prison.
nuance: மனை மக்கள் சுற்றம் எனும் மாயா வலை: the household itself is the net. விழலுக்கு இறைத்தல், watering useless grass, is a proverb for wasted effort, here the poet's whole life.

reading: The girl speaks for herself: must this sinner's life faint because of the moon rising over the sea, the arrows Kama shot, and the reproach that has spread over the whole earth? The praise names the Vel that pierced Sura's broad chest, the light, the king seated on the peacock, the chest that wedded the elephant-maiden, the lord of the three gods and all the gods.
nuance: பாவியேன் ஆவி மயங்கலாமோ is the girl's own voice, where 1290 speaks of her. பாரெலாம் ஏசிய: the gossip has spread over the whole world. மூரி மால் யானை may be Devayanai.

reading: The poet asks not to be born into the deceptive false hut that sky, earth, wind, water and fire inhabit, but to learn Murugan's name with the Tamil of knowledge and attainment and to be given praise in his hand. The praise calls him the one bound to the forest Kuratti of rustic speech, the Vel that fought the golden mountain, wearer of the fragrant vetchi garland, emperor of the gods' heaven.
nuance: மாயத் தெற்றிப் பொய்க்குடில்: the body as a false hut of the five elements. புகழ் கைக்குப் புரிவாயே may be read as asking for the gift of praise-songs, புகழ், the name of the book itself. The split of the first line (வானப் புக்குப் பற்றும் மருத்து) is uncertain.

tamil: ... வனச மலர்நிகர், செம்பொற் சதங்கையடி யன்பர்க்கு வந்துதவு ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: The surviving lines invoke Murugan as guru, Saravanabhava, Shanmukha and Guha, delight of the hunter's daughter, lord of the kurinji hills where tigers, bears, boars, buffaloes and deer roam, and ask for his grace; then they describe drums, conches, horns and trumpets thundering as at the world's end while the world cries 'Hara Hara, Siva Siva, refuge', and end on the anklet-bearing feet that come to help devotees.
nuance: The text is incomplete, so no plea survives beyond அருள் தருவாயே; the rest is a battle scene in instrument names and the closing image of the feet that come to the devotees (அன்பர்க்கு வந்து உதவு).

title: க்ஷேத்திரக் கோவை
theme: The catalogue of shrines (க்ஷேத்திரக் கோவை): a single song that strings together the names of Siva's and Murugan's shrines across the Tamil country, from Kumbakonam, Arur and Chidambaram to Senthil, Eragam, Avinankudi and Vayalur, and ends with Murugan dwelling in every temple in the world.
structure_note: One song with no plea: the whole first and second halves are a list of places, each line ending in an address to Murugan (வாழ்வே, செகநாதம், வருதேவே, வயலூரா, மணிமார்பா), closing on the goddesses who praise him and his two consorts.
source_issues: 1306: corrupt glyph ஧ in ஧வ்ளுர் (probably எவ்வுளூர், Tiruvallur), and ஡ in வயலு஡ரா, read வயலூரா (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS: 2).
1306: செங்சோ லேரக looks corrupt (perhaps செங்கோடு, ஏரகம்); a stray space after உ splits உம்பர் at two line starts.

reading: The song is a garland of shrine names: Kumbakonam, Arur, Chidambaram, Sirkazhi, Mayuram, Sivakasi, Rameswaram where the Veda-knowing one came alone to worship, Evvulur, Parangiri, Thiruvadanai, Senthil, Edakam, Solaimalai, Eragam, Avinankudi, the hills one by one, Virinjai, Kanchi, Vayalur, Perur, Kandiyur and others, each a place where Murugan lives. It closes with the women who contend with Siva, Vani, Lakshmi and the beautiful one, praising him every day, and with Murugan who married Indrani's daughter and the hunter girl, the lord in every temple throughout the world.
nuance: The song has no confession: its devotion is the naming of places, and the last line (உலகெங்கு மேவிய தேவாலயந்தொறு பெருமாளே) turns the list into a claim that the Lord is in every temple, not only these. குன்று தோறுடன் echoes the 'every hill' (குன்றுதோறாடல்) of Murugan's worship. Several names are hard to identify because the rhythm splits them (செம்பு கேசுரம், செங்சோ லேரகம், கம்பை மாவடி, தென்சி வாயமு), and the reading of these is tentative.

title: பழமுதிர்சோலை
theme: Pazhamudircholai (பழமுதிர்சோலை, 1 of 2): Murugan of the hill of Solaimalai is hymned as the letter A and the form above the three gods, and as the guru who teaches Siva; the poet confesses courtesans who sell their love and polish brass for gold, the life from womb to old age taken as eternal, the old body coughing over its medicines and the sick body fattened on food, and asks for the feet, for servanthood, for the yogic ascent and for the knowledge that he is Siva.
structure_note: Courtesan songs (1308, 1311, 1312, 1315, 1317, 1319, 1320); songs on attachment, the life-course and the body (1310, 1314, 1316, 1321); doctrinal songs (1307 on Murugan as all, 1313 on the yogic ascent through the centres, 1318 on nada, bindu and Siva). 1309 is a short plea for the dance of knowledge. The hill is also called குலகிரி (1321, and 1322 in the next chapter) and அலையாமலை (1314); 1312's praise describes the town with its stream and towers.
source_issues: 1313: corrupt glyphs ஧ in ஧வ்ளுர் (probably எவ்வுளூர்) and ஡ in நாவலு஡ர், read நாவலூர் (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS: 2); எருர், தெவுர், மூதுர are probably ஏரூர், தேவூர், மூதூர் with lost vowel signs.
1316: corrupt glyph in இகலு஡ர், read இகலூர் (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS: 1).
1315: two line ends are damaged: '....... ; ளையோனே' (probably இளையோனே) and 'வேத ரு ரு பர', where syllables are missing; தமீழ் தமீழ் is a stretched spelling for the rhythm.
Across the chapter a stray space after the vowel உ splits words at line starts (உ லக, உ டல்செய், உ ருவி லாத, உ லவு, உ ருகு, உ பய, உ யிரை); read as one word.

இருநில மீதி லெளியனும் வாழ எனதுமு னோடி ...... வரவேணும்

reading: Murugan is hymned as the letter A, the lord, the excess and the within; as Brahma, Vishnu and Hara and the one above them; as the letter I, as all things and as sweetness; and the poet asks him to run ahead of him so that even a lowly one may live on this wide earth. The praise names the form that delights Indra, the lord who rejoices in the worship the forest hunter offered at Kathirkamam, and the peacock that dances to the drum syllables, at Pazhamudircholai.
nuance: அகரமுமாகி ... இகரமுமாகி: Murugan as the first letters, the image the Kural opens with; here he is also அவர்மேலாய், above the three gods he becomes. The plea is small and tender: எனது முன் ஓடி வரவேணும், run ahead of me. The praise names கதிர்காமம், the shrine in Lanka, and the hunter's worship there.

பலிகொள்க பாலி யோகி பரமகல் யாணி லோக பதிவ்ரதை வேத ஞானி ...... புதல்வோனே
படையொடு சூரன் மாள முடுகிய சூர தீர பழமுதிர் சோலை மேவு ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: The poet describes the musk-smeared breasts, laughing play and many kinds of pleasure of women in love-union, and asks whether he, sunk in that union and given to low deeds, will ever reach the wisdom of jnana he has thought of. The praise is a long litany of the Goddess, Kali, the trident-bearer, Bhairavi, Nili, Varahi, Bhagavati, the poison-eater, Abhirami, Kapali who takes offerings, the yogini, the supremely auspicious, the chaste wife of the world, the knower of the Veda, whose son Murugan is, the hero who rushed at Sura and his army, at Pazhamudircholai.
nuance: The praise is almost wholly the Goddess's names (கொலைபுரி காளி சூலி ... வேத ஞானி), fierce and gentle together, before புதல்வோனே makes Murugan her son. மதராஜன் கலவி: the union is called Kama's own.

reading: A short song: the poet asks Murugan to come on earth for a purpose, so that Death does not come near and he may see the way, and to come performing the dance of knowledge that Narayana and Brahma never knew. The praise names him the bridegroom of the elephant-raised girl, the six-faced one with twelve eyes, the vel that destroyed Sura's kin, at Solaimalai.
nuance: நாரணனும் வேதன் முன்பு தெரியாத ஞான நடம்: the dance that Vishnu and Brahma could not see is the idiom of Siva's unseen form, here given to Murugan's dance. ஆரமுதமான தந்தி மணவாளா: Devayanai, raised by the elephant.

tamil: சீலமுள தாயர் தந்தை மாதுமனை யான மைந்தர்
தீமையுறு மாயை கொண்டு வாழ்வுசத மாமி தென்று
வாலவய தான கொங்கை மேருநுத லான திங்கள்
வாழுமயில் மீது வந்து தாளிணைகள் தாழு மென்றன்
சேலவள நாட னங்கள் ஆரவயல் சூழ மிஞ்சி
சேருமம ரேசர் தங்க ளூரிதென வாழ்வு கந்த
ஆலவிட மேவு கண்டர் கோலமுட னீடு மன்று
ஆனமொழி யேப கர்ந்து சோலைமலை மேவு கந்த
reading: The poet confesses that his heart wavered in desire for mother, father, wife, house, children and wealth, that through evil maya he took this life for permanent, and that, his earnings gone, he wandered the streets wasting away for women; he asks Murugan to come on the living peacock so that he may bow at the feet, and to show love that ends his deluding karma. The praise names the hero who defeated Sura, honoured in a land of fields and golden terraces like the gods' own town, who spoke the fitting word so that his father, the poison-throated dancer of the hall, rejoiced, at Solaimalai.
nuance: The attachments come in order, kin and household and wealth before women: மாதுமனை யான மைந்தர் சேருபொருள் ஆசை. வாழ்வு சதமாம் இது: the error is to take life as eternal. ஆனமொழியே பகர்ந்து, the word that delighted Siva, points to the teaching of Siva without naming Om.
