சோலைதனி லேப றந்து லாவுமயி லேறி வந்து
reading: The poet confesses he was deluded by the spear eyes of women versed in the love-texts, did their bidding at their sweet words, grew mad with love, and when his great wealth had gone to them stood a sinner; he asks when he will seek and bow at the flower feet with anklets and kadamba. The praise names Murugan raised by the grace of Uma who holds the left of Siva, the nephew of the dark one who measured the earth with one step, and the vel that ground Sura's kin to dust, on the peacock that flies over the groves to Solaimalai.
nuance: நீடு பொருள் போன பின்பு பாதகனுமாகி: the wealth spent on the women leaves him not only poor but a sinner. வீரமதனூல் விளம்பு போக மடமாதர்: the women are cast as teachers of Kama's treatise. Vishnu measuring the world (ஓரடியினால் அளந்த) is the Trivikrama story.

tamil: வாரண முகங்கி ழிந்து வீழவு மரும்ப லர்ந்து
பூரண குடங்க டிந்து சிதகள பம்பு னைந்து
போக சயனந் தவிர்ந்து னாடக பதம்ப ணிந்து
ஆரண முழங்கு கின்ற ஆயிர மடந்த வங்கள்
ஆயிர முகங்கள் கொண்ட நூபுர மிரங்கு கங்கை
தோரண மலங்கு துங்க கோபுர நெருங்கு கின்ற
reading: The poet describes breasts that outdo an elephant's temples, shake the great mountain, bow Kama's head and make ascetics forget their penance, and asks whether a day will come when, leaving those women's beds, he bows at the golden feet and is called a servant who performs worship. The praise is a picture of Solaimalai: streets ringing with the Vedas and full of sacrificial fires, the thousand-faced stream of the anklet (நூபுர) Ganga at its bathing ghats, towers hung with festoons, gem-set halls and golden mansions bright as the sun.
nuance: பூசனைசெய் தொண்டன் என்பது ஒருநாளே: the wish is to be named a servant who worships, a public identity rather than an inner state. The praise is a rare town-portrait; நூபுரம் இரங்கு கங்கை names the hill's stream as the Ganga of the anklet. The first lines of the plea are hard to divide.

reading: In the language of yoga the poet traces an ascent: from the four-petalled lotus with the breath running on both sides, through the centres of earth and the others, the three regions, the light of a hundred and eight petals, bindu and nada and the sound beyond, through the sacred Nandi; he asks Murugan to make him, a mute one, shine, to send him out by the root gate into the light on Murugan's breast, and give him today the way the eight kinds of yoga join in this. The praise names Siva who sold horses as a horse-merchant and took Vadavurar as his servant, Gauri on his left who cut the seven births, and a long list of shrines, Kasi, Rameswaram, Ratnagiri, Kanchi, Madurai, Thiruthani, Senthil, Nagai, Kazhi, Palani and Navalur, with the hill of Solaimalai.
nuance: The terms are those of the yogic body: நாலு சதுரக் கமலம் (the four-petalled root centre), இரு பக்கம் செல் வளி (the two breaths), விந்து நாத, மூல வாசல், யோக பேதவகை எட்டு (the eight limbs). The splitting of the numbers (ஆர மூணு பதி, நுறு பத்தினுடன் எட்டு இதழ்) is unsure. வாசி வாணிகன் எனக் குதிரை விற்று ... வாதவூரன்: Siva as horse-dealer for Manikkavasagar, named by his town. The shrine list repeats the device of the catalogue song 1306.

reading: The poet traces his life: formed in the mother's womb with limbs, mouth, eyes, nose and ears, falling into the hands of grey-haired women, laid to sleep and fed on the mother's breast, then taking wife, kin, a life that does not last and wealth as permanent, never thinking of Murugan; he asks whether a day will come when this utter fool, who never learned to worship the feet, is made to sing Murugan's praise and reach true knowledge. The praise shows the battlefield where ghosts with jackals drink the demons' blood and owls dance, and names Murugan who embraces the girl raised by the elephant and the hunter girl, lord of the devotees at the hill of golden terraces and cloud-touched groves.
nuance: The life is told from conception (கருவாகியெ தாய் உதரத்தினில் உருவாகவெ) through birth and nursing to the household, so that the whole course becomes the delusion: சதமாம் இது தானென. நரைமாதர் are the old women, midwives, whose hands first receive the child. The hill is called அலையாமலை.

பானி றக்க ணேசர் குவா குவா கனர் ....... ; ளையோனே
பாசமற்ற வேத ரு ரு பர ...... குமரோசா
போர்மிகுத்த சூரன் விடோ ம் விடோ மென
போயறுத்த போது குபீர் குபீ ரென ...... வெகுசோரி
பூணியிச்சை யாறு புயா புயா றுள ...... பெருமாளே.
reading: Built on doubled cries, the song describes women coming with anklets jingling, youths seeking them in endless infatuation, breasts gleaming and the poet's heart lurching, and asks that, at the hour when this seizes him, Murugan say 'Hey, hey! what delusion is this, tell me', and give grace saying 'here, here are the feet you love'. The praise names Murugan younger brother of Ganesha who broke his tusk to write the Bharata on Meru, the guru who taught Tamil in the ear of the great sage, and the Guha whose vel cut Sura as he cried 'we will not yield', with blood gushing, at Solaimalai, with Devayanai's shoulders and twelve arms.
nuance: The whole song is made of doubled exclamations (கலீர் கலீர், பகீர் பகீர், அடா அடா, இதோ இதோ, குபீர் குபீர்), so the grace is imagined as a scolding and a showing in the god's own voice. பாரதத்தை மேரு ... கோடொடித்த: Ganesha's broken tusk used to write the Mahabharata. மாமுநிக்கு காதில் உணர்வு: Tamil taught to Agastya. வாடை பற்று வேளை may be the hour of love's wind or of death; the plea is unsure.

tamil: உ னது ஞான பாத பத்ம ...... முறுவேனோ
reading: The poet speaks of the body wasted by fevers, phlegm, cough, wheezing and the humours, and asks whether, fattening the dreadful wretched belly with food every day, one can gain the yogic power that prolongs life, or whether, freed from the torment of worldly books and given blissful experience, he will reach Murugan's lotus feet of knowledge that dance the dance of nada in the formless void. The praise names Rama, for whom the son of the wind and Vali's son threw hills to bridge the sea, and who killed the ten-headed one with an arrow, as Murugan's uncle, the peacock that danced on Sura's crushed brains, and Murugan son of Tyagar at Solaimalai where sages and gods gained knowledge.
nuance: உருவிலாத பாழில் வெட்டவெளியில் ஆடு நாத நிர்த்த ... ஞான பாதம்: the feet dance in the formless void, the open space of the yogis. The question on yoga siddhi gained by feeding the body seems ironic. How the halves of the plea join (what is before the diseases come, and what is asked) is unclear. தலைகள் ஆறு நாலு: six and four, ten heads.

reading: The poet lists the courtesans who set a price on their affection, unsettle the minds of those who love them, take bodies through sin, comb and knot their hair, cast infatuation with a look, polish tarnished brass ornaments with ash to make them shine, flaunt jewels at breast and ear, speak lavish lies and cheat and drain even those who love them, and asks whether he will set his mind on their maya and suffer daily. The praise names Valli guarding the millet field with her sling, Siva who went as messenger for the poet who sang him and who was beaten for pittu as a labourer at the Vaigai bank in Koodal, and Murugan who came at the holy town of Pugali, at the ancient Solaimalai thick with sandal and agil trees.
nuance: பாசத்தால் விலை கட்டிய பொட்டிகள் and பித்தளையிற் பணி நீறிட்டே ஒளி பற்ற விளக்கிகள்: love with a price on it, and brass passed off as gold, the fraud put in one picture. திருப்புகலிப் பதி வருவோனே: Murugan who came at Pugali (Sirkazhi), the identification with Sambandar. The Siva stories are Sundarar's messenger and the Madurai pittu labourer. How அடிபடுவோனோ டாரத்தோடு divides is unsure.

reading: In a run of confessions the poet says he has not seen through the illusion of spear-eyed women, has not worshipped with garlands, has not known that the goods that are beginning and end are the six faces, nor that the dancing peacock is the form of the one mantra, that he wanders the world in a body made of nada and bindu and has not stood worshipping in the state of nada; he asks Murugan to rule him by giving the 'I am He' that the life which knows the light is Siva. The praise names Murugan who won over Sura's clan and stands at Solaimalai.
nuance: The plea is all negations (தெளியேனே, பணியேனே, தெரியேனே, அறியேனே). சோதி உணர்கின்ற வாழ்வு சிவம் என்ற சோகம் அது தந்து: சோகம் is likely सोऽहम् 'I am He', the meditation of identity with Siva, though it can also read as grief. The peacock as மந்த்ர ரூபம் makes Murugan's mount a mantra.

reading: The poet describes women whose earrings reach their eyes, who bewilder Kama and are kin even to Death, who destroy great penance, with eyes like mango slices, who call sweetly, give their honey lips and pleasure, then work betrayal and ruin a man's good name, and asks whether their kinship is fit. The praise describes Uma with breasts like golden pots that burst their bodice, the yogini skilled in all things, the peacock-like Uma who bore Murugan, and Murugan who took up the vel and cut down Sura's kin, at Solaimalai.
nuance: மாய நமனுக்கும் உறவாகி: the women are kin to Death himself, desire and death in one person. The praise answers the plea with the same body: Uma's breasts described in the plea's terms, now as the mother's.

tamil: உ லவு முடைதனை நெகிழ்த்திக் காட்டி ...... யுறவாடி
உ யிரை விலைகொளு மவர்க்குத் தேட்ட ...... மொழிவேனோ
reading: With the refrain 'showing', the poet lists the courtesans' displays, loosened hair, rolling eye corners, earrings, love-talk, pale lips, nail marks, swaying breasts, bent waist, loosened clothes and anklet feet, and asks whether he will stop earning for those who buy a man's life for a price. The praise names Murugan who cut off the tuft of Brahma, husband of Saraswati of the Veda face, the Siva who made the crocodile give back the swallowed boy and heard Tamil expounded, the matted-haired lord with the elephant skin and Ganga who bowed to receive grace, and the one who showed him the nature of Siva and made the peacock dance.
nuance: உயிரை விலைகொளும் அவர்க்குத் தேட்டம்: not wealth alone but life is the price. The praise refrain takes the same verb, காட்டி turning to காட்டு: the women show their bodies, Murugan shows Siva his own nature (சிவமயத்தைக் காட்டு). The crocodile story is Sundarar's at Avinashi. The phrases முதல்வ குகைபடு திருப்பொற் கோட்டு முனிநாடா and குலமலை are obscure.

reading: The poet pictures old age: hair grey as a crane, teeth rattling loose, faltering steps with a stick, coughing and hiccupping, vomiting phlegm and bile, then sesame oil boiled with triphala, dry ginger and long pepper, strained and taken, until the body dies; before life goes, he asks to learn Murugan's praise, hold and worship his feet, and be given the supreme release that cuts birth. The praise shows Murugan saddling his mount to ride against Sura's hosts, making the peacock dance in battle, escaping Indra's daughter to give his heart to the hunters' daughter in the millet field, and piercing the cruel hill, the fierce lord who dwells on Kulagiri.
nuance: The remedies (திலதயிலம், திரிபலை, சுக்கு, திப்பிலி) are listed with a physician's care, only to end in உடல் செத்திட்டு: medicine prolongs nothing. The cure asked for is song and the feet. குலிசன் மகட்குத் தப்பியும்: a playful turn, Murugan slipping away from Devayanai to Valli.

title: பழமுதிர்சோலை
theme: Pazhamudircholai (பழமுதிர்சோலை, 2 of 2): one song in which the poet, describing lovemaking, vows that even sunk in that old infatuation he will not forget Murugan's garlanded crown and the vel in his hand; the praise names Uma's son, the vel of knowledge thrown at Sura's hill and sea, and the lord of Kulagiri.
source_issues: 1322: a line end is damaged ('....... ; ளநீரின்'), probably for இளநீரின் with syllables lost.

tamil: மலரணை ததும்ப மேக குழல்முடி சரிந்து வீழ
வழிபட இடங்க ணாட பிறைநுதல் புரண்டு மாழ்க
முலையிணை ததும்ப நூலின் வகிரிடை சுழன்று வாட
முதுமயல் கலந்து மூழ்கி மகிழ்கினும் அலங்க லாடு
சிலைநுத லிளம்பெண் மோகி சடையழகி யெந்தை பாதி
சிறுநகை புரிந்து சூரர் கிரிகட லெரிந்து போக
கொலைமிக பயின்ற வேடர் மகள்வளி மணந்த தோள
கொடிமின லடைந்த சோதி மழகதிர் தவழ்ந்த ஞான
reading: The poet describes lovemaking on a flower bed, cloud-dark hair loosened, scent and sweat mingling, crescent brows turning, garments slipping, breasts heaving and faces pressed together, and says that even while he is sunk and rejoicing in that old infatuation he will not forget Murugan's crown swaying with garlands, his form and the vel in his hand. The praise names him son of Uma of the bow brows, half of Siva, green-gold of body, the Murugan of knowledge who with a small smile hurled the vel so that Sura's hill and sea burned, Valli's bridegroom with the kadamba garland, at Kulagiri.
nuance: Unusually there is no plea to be freed from desire: மகிழ்கினும் ... மறவேனே, 'even while I rejoice, I will not forget'. The remembrance of the god is held inside the confession rather than set against it. The vel is called ஞான, knowledge, as it is elsewhere.

title: புதிய பாடல்கள்
theme: New songs (புதிய பாடல்கள்): two songs without a shrine. In one the poet confesses a life spent learning arts, singing poems and running after wealth and women; in the other, the courtesans' binding arts; the praise names Murugan the guru who spoke supreme knowledge into Siva's ears and the vel that cut down Singamukha.
source_issues: 1323 and 1324: a stray space after the vowel உ splits words (உ ருவினில், உ ன், உ றவாமோ); read as one word.
The heading 'புதிய பாடல்கள்' names no shrine; these appear to be songs added to the collection later.

reading: The poet confesses that, sunk in the maya called the womb and grown up on earth, he learned many arts and books from scholars, sang many kinds of poems, went along the streets running far after wealth, and sank in infatuation with bow-browed women, and asks whether he must wander in such petty ways. The praise names Murugan the guru of gracious experience who keeps his devotees alive, the son who recited supreme knowledge in both of Hara's ears, the son of the eternal Goddess who felled the roots of Sura's clan, the lord of the peacock and vel.
nuance: The confession is of a learned poet: the arts and the poems themselves served the hunt for wealth (பொருளெனும் ஆசை). அரன் இரு காதில் அருள் பரஞான அடைவினை ஓதி: the teaching of Siva, given here as knowledge whispered into his ears; Om is not named.

tamil: கொஞ்சி மகிழ்ந்த வறட்டு வீணியர் ...... உ றவாமோ
reading: The poet describes courtesans with gold-laden breasts and pearl strings who twist men with their words, delude them on the couch, and with swaying waists, kissing lips and cuckoo cries bind them as with chains, and asks whether the kinship of such barren, useless women is fit. The praise shows Murugan mounting the peacock while even the one unafraid of the sea's poison trembled, cutting off Singamukha's head and leaving the great-faced Sura limbless with a vel sent like the Sarabha bird, the son of Sankari who bore the elephant-faced one, who dances daily so that yogis of mantra and tantra join their palms.
nuance: The women are named வேசியர், courtesans, but the song speaks of their arts, not of money, and calls them வறட்டு வீணியர், barren and useless. சிம்புள் is the Sarabha, the bird-beast that subdued the man-lion, apt for a vel sent against the lion-faced Singamukha. The line on the poison (திங்கள் அரும்பு சலத்திலே விடம் வந்தது கண்டு பயப்படாதவர் சிந்தை நடுங்கி) is unclear.

title: புனவாயில்
theme: Punavayil (புனவாயில்): one song of the death-bed, speech gone, eyes dim, milk spilling from the mouth, the physician giving up and wives and kin falling and wailing, with the plea that on the day Death comes Murugan appear with the peacock, his twelve arms and his two consorts; the praise tells of Hanuman bringing Sita's tokens to Rama, whose nephew dwells at Punavayil.
source_issues: 1325: a line end is damaged ('....... ; யல்தோகை'), with syllables lost before the word for the peacock.
1325: a stray space after the vowel உ splits words at line starts (உ ரையும், உ லர்ந்தது, உ ழலும், உ டலும், உ றவும்); read as one word.

tamil: உ ரையுஞ் சென்றது நாவும் உ லர்ந்தது
உ ழலுஞ் சிந்துறு பால்கடை நின்றது ...... கடைவாயால்
உ டலுந் தொந்தியும் ஓடிவ டிந்தது ...... பரிகாரி
reading: The poet pictures his own death: speech gone, tongue dry, eyes like cotton, the milk given him standing and dribbling from the corner of the mouth, the body chilled, hands and legs stiff, flesh and belly shrunk, the physician saying no remedy will work now, kin and wives beating themselves and falling in tears; he asks that on the day Death comes to take his life Murugan appear before him with the peacock, the twelve strong arms, the garlands and his two consorts. The praise tells how Hanuman, son of the wind, brought tokens to Rama, and how Rama, seeing along the path Sita's earrings, ring, anklets, bracelets and the ball she had thrown, grieved; Murugan is Narayana's nephew at southern Punavayil.
nuance: The death is told sign by sign from inside the dying body, then from the bedside: the physician's verdict (பரிகாரி வரவொன்றும் பலியாது இனி) and the women's wailing. The plea asks not to escape death but for a vision at the hour. In the praise Sita's ornaments scattered along the road are listed as fully as the dying body's signs; the reading of these lines is tentative.

title: திருவெழுகூற்றிருக்கை
theme: Thiruvezhukutrirukkai (திருவெழுகூற்றிருக்கை): the closing number-poem, in which the numbers one to seven rise and fall through the lines while the praise tells Murugan's story: the one form of the Taraka Brahman, the release of Brahma, the circling of the world, the marriage to Devayanai, the teaching of Siva, the birth at Kazhumalam as master of three Tamils, the vel at Krauncha, and the lord of Eragam on the Kaveri's north bank.
structure_note: A single song in the form of the ezhukutrirukkai, where numbers are woven in ascending and descending order (ஒன்று, இரண்டு, மூன்று ... ஏழு and back); it is all praise, with no confession.
source_issues: 1326: the number pattern is broken in places by run-together words (குடிமி for குடுமி, அன்றி லங்கிரியிருபிள வாக, காவிரிவடகரை ... குருகிரிஇருந்த), probably transcription spacing.

tamil: ஒன்றா யொன்றி யிருவரிற் றோன்றி மூவா தாயினை
முந்நீ ருடுத்த நானிலம் அஞ்ச நீவலஞ் செய்தனை
reading: All praise, counted out in numbers: Murugan, the one form of the Taraka Brahman, born in the one line from the two and never ageing, once lifted Brahma's tuft in a blink and freed him from prison when the three gods begged at his feet, circled the four-fold sea-girt land in an instant on the two-winged peacock, married the daughter of the one-trunked, four-tusked elephant, became younger brother of the five-armed, arugu-wearing Ganesha, and guru to the three-eyed Siva who teaches the Vedas in the five letters. He was born at Kazhumalam, drinking Uma's milk, as the master of three Tamils and king of four kinds of poetry, born of six stars, split the Krauncha hill with one vel, and dwells as lord of Eragam, the hill on the Kaveri's north bank where Brahmins of the six letters praise his feet.
nuance: The numbers carry the form, not the sense: the device is the classical ezhukutrirukkai, a chariot-shaped number poem. தாரகப் பிரமம், the 'saving Brahman', is the pranava, and Murugan's guruship over Siva (முக்கட் சுடரினை ... ஒருகுரு வாயினை) is set inside it. கழுமலத்து உதித்தனை ... முத்தமிழ் விரகன்: Murugan identified with Sambandar, born at Sirkazhi and fed by Uma. ஆறெழுத்து அந்தணர்: the six-letter mantra of Murugan. Some number-phrases (இருபிறப்பாளரின் ஒருவன், ஒருவகை வடிவினில் இருவகைத்தாகிய மும்மதன்) are obscure.
